Storyline essentially non existent, they make things up as they go along and disregard many of the story arcs building in the previous two films and replace them with sloppy and lazy character choices and story resolutions.

The film is visually entertaining in parts and I'm sure a 8 year old child will love this movie but overall it's cringey, heartless, boring, insults the intelligence of the audience, requires almost 0 brain engagement, ruins the point of the original movies, over Disneyfies the hell out of the sets.

I was close to walking out the screening on several occasions! But found myself just laughing in shock at how ridiculously bad it was.

It's pretentious, uninteresting, messy, full of plot holes, essentially just an advert for toys and it plays it FAR FAR too safe.

Don't bother paying to see this movie. Even if you LOVE Star Wars like I do. It's not worth it. You'll likely leave the cinema feeling frustrated wishing you could delete it from your mind.

It gets a 2/10 and not a 0/10 only because the cinematography is pleasant and for a younger audience up to 11-12 years old I guess they'll enjoy it. And wanna buy all the toys....

title: What happened to Star Wars being fun?
review:
The original trilogy had a style, wit, and charm that unfortunately all subsequent films in the franchise are drastically devoid of.
This addition is no exception, and honestly does a pretty horrible job of "wrapping up" the storyline. The explanations and resolutions are either really reaching, or make no real sense...they certainly lack any sort of surprise, and don't really DO anything for the audience. Yes, the visuals are incredible and you'll get plenty of "oooo's and ahhhh's" if that's what you're looking for. It's an entertaining popcorn flick, but how anyone can care about any of the characters at this point is beyond me.
But, it will sell a lot of tickets..just like it's predecessors. And ultimately THAT is the only goal of the film. So, in that regard, it's a success.

title: Joyless, chaotic, un-suspensful nonsense
review: I can't believe JJ Abrams directed this (although there was his trademark, requisite lens flare in at least one shot). The movie starts out rushed and chaotic, segues into pointlessness, and completely jumps the shark at the finale. The only redeeming feature of the movie was little Babu Frick (and perhaps the little D-O droid). Worst of all, the movie lacked any sense of that magical Star Wars space drama feel that made the franchise what it is.

title: Too bad that the story ended this way
review:
The Mandalorian beats this movie with one hand tied behind back.

They totally misunderstood the whole Force idea.

Many people say that the prequels are bad, but these three movies were much much much... much worse. Too bad that they finished the saga that way.

The only thing i liked in this is movie is the small tech guy that rebooted ****. Reminds me of old Yoda.

title: Forgettable
review: Nothing special, not interesting, a mess. Why do they still go to J. J. Abrams to direct!? He is that good.

title: The roots for this mess started way back with TFA.
review: What started as something possibly good (but which had problems from the start, specifically the writing revolving around Rey the Mary Sue) - TFA - went off the rails in TLJ, and by the time this last one came around, it wasn't enough to save this mess of a trilogy. It would have been better if it hadn't even been made to begin with. I'm not going to count this as canon.

title: doesn't make sense
review: Looks cool tho, but for 200,000,000 budget they could have made something better.

title: You Want Star Wars? We'll Give You Star Wars!
review: This movie seems to be a direct response to any criticism that fans had with The Last Jedi, and everything comes together in a completely incoherent mess. While watching The Rise of Skywalker, I felt like I was watching a 2+ hour long advertisement for sweet sweet merchandise. Retcons were made for the sake of restoring icons to the franchise, characters were boiled down to their stereotypes, and expanded universe material sprinkled in to please the dire hards. When you try to pander to everyone, you impress no one.

title: Worst movie ever.
review: Honestly terrible. Do not waste your time. Do not buy the toys. Make Disney pay for putting out this absolute turd!!!

title: Abrams killed Star Wars
review:
This film could possible be the worse of the franchise. There were big battles, little battles, some chasing, more fighting, but not a lot of story. What little story there was, was contrived and made no sense. It did not fit in with the eight chapters that came before it.
Great science fiction, like Star Wars, is created and developed with a specific paradigm in mind. For Star Wars it is all based on a balance of good and evil. If one side is in charge, everything is chaos. Abrams ignored the previous story lines, the need for balance, and obviously doesn't understand basic human emotion. If the movie had been chaotic, it would have been more interesting.

title: The Disney Star Wars trilogy is very, very bad.
review:
This hollow charade does not deserve a review nor my time.

Luckily I got my ticket for free.

If you decide to go and see this, please get a lobotomy first.

title: A Royal Mess
review:
Imagine you made yourself some spaghetti bolognese and openned some fine wine. You're walking with it to the dining table when you suddenly stumble. The plate goes crashing into the wall and spaghetti splats everywhere. The wine seeps into the sofa and floor. You're left bleeding with shattered glass everywhere. You look up and wonder, wtf just happened? This is the perfect analogy for this movie.- it's a mess.

The story is everywhere and there is absolutely no character progression. Any sense of character progression is actually characters suddenly switching from one mindset to another, with little to no context. The story is so fast paced that there's little time to enjoy or get a sense of what's happening. I suspect it's because they're trying to fill in any plot holes and inconsistencies from the other movies. Even by the third movie, none of the characters are likeable and I couldn't care what happens to any of them. This movie is such a mish-mash of different scenes and plots that it becomes just plain boring. When we walked out of the cinema, someone said to their partner, "it's so bad, there wasn't one wow moment." Yes, I agree, there was not a single wow moment. I'm afraid every sense of nuance has been removed from the latest edition of the Star Wars saga and they try to make up for it by cramming a million special effects into every scene possible. It's like the writers had no idea how to write complex characters or characters that acted... well... human. The original Star Wars characters were based off Jung's archetypes, which were also based of stories from mythology, religion and tales. This is why Luke, Anakin and so on, held such strong ties to the viewers. There was a lot of history and literature around the making of the hero and the characters within. However, the writer, for these editions, seem to want to make their own unique tale without giving and credence to what made Star Wars popular. It has now become a shallow shell of what Star Wars was. Rey is a n unlikable Marry Sue and all the other characters are trying to forge a nostalgia bond with any of the original characters they didn't kill off. It's so sad to watch.

There was one thing that was improved upon however. I went into the movie expecting the worst, and I got what I came for.

title: One word: disappointing.
review: I so wanted to like it. I've tried to convince myself to like it. I found myself sighing at parts of it and others were simply cringe-worthy. Overall, it is simply one disappointment after another and you could probably skip the whole film and just guess how it ends instead - it would probable be more satisfying :)

title: Cliche fest with a rip-off scenario
review: Copy-paste of whole sections from Avengers: Endgame, with every cliche you can possibly think filling the gaps. Most disappointing movie of the year for me.

title: Boring
review:
I am so sorry to say this bot it was more boring than TLJ.
It was better but boring.

title: George Lucas life's work lies in ruins
review: There's so much going on in this movie that your senses are just overloaded. This movie could be made into three movies easily. Little of it makes any sense, though. Everybody and their dog show up. Even John Williams (the composer) makes a 2 seconds appearance. Everything predicted by vloggers and bloggers came true. George Lucas life's work lies in ruins.

title: Stop giving them your money: Bad writing strikes again
review:
Incredible levels of audio-visual effects and reasonably talented actors let down by bad writing. This seems to be the main problem with most high budget movies these days and its such a shame since many of the scripts are so bad that its frankly incomprehensible how they got green-lit for production.
Even though this movie will most likely make money it will depreciate the Star Wars brand even further and if this trend continues it will loose its value completely within the next decade.

title: Worst star war movie yet
review:
If you are fine with 2.5 hours of things happening for the sake of happening then you would probably like this movie. Despite being 2.5 hours long, there is little plot or character development.

There are so many moments where my reaction was "really, just like that?". Older movies still had a plot that you could follow and had a sense of originality. You knew where the movies were going. Here things happened because they needed to happen for the plot to go in a certain direction.

I gave up trying to understand the last part of the movie. I empathize with star war fans who feel this is just made because they want money by recycling the same cliches.

title: oi
review: There is a moment in the film where the entire theater i was in collectively groaned in disappointment bordering disgust. u all will know when u see this film. ðŸ™„

title: No finale
review:
If it was a stand alone movie it would be okay, but unfortunately it's not only supposed to tie up the sequel trilogy but the whole 9. Sadly it fails especially the latter.

There is some good in it. Can't fault Driver's performance, C-3PO gets a few cracking lines and there's a little more chemistry between the main 3. It's fast paced and there's a lot in it (probably too fast and too full) and as a result it's not until you digest it that the plot holes really start to stand out. You can tell there was no clear structure between the 3 films and the story certainly feels forced.

ROTJ was a perfect ending and it's The Rise of Skywalker's effect on this which is its biggest flaw. The film may be fun enough on the surface but playing it safe and going down the route of nostalgia opened up a potential can of worms and the resultant lack of care for the whole story really leaves a sour taste.

title: The Death of Star Wars!
review: Kathleen Kennedy said in an interview when Disney acquired LucasFilms and I quote "The main thing is to protect these characters and make sure they continue to live in the way George created them". Well that was a lie and just wait till you see this movie and the middle finger Disney is giving the fans!

title: They have no clue, just a remake of Episode 4-6
review:
Our hero would dethrone his own blood. Luke detrhoned his father, and now Rey will detrhrone her grand father. Some of nostalgia with the old characters came out of nowhere.

A Naive boy Kylo who is the main villain suddenly becoming a hero after seeing his mother is dead. Its like a "Martha" moment on BvS, and why dont he feels the same when Leia almost died in the ship? Makes no sense.

Then again there is any sense in this plot, they will keep telling us 'its the feeling' again and again in the film.

Palpatine said he wants to kill his grand daughter, then wants to be killed by his grand daughter, then wants to killed her again, then finally be killed. Its a very lazy writing for a legendary supervillain.

The acting and cinematography is ok, but ghost of old characters looks awful. The title shoud be "Star Wars Episode 6B: The Rise of Palpatine"

title: What a letdown!! Was hoping for a far better movie!!
review:
So I just saw this movie today. I went in with an open mind hoping for a great delivery as per usual for a Star Wars film... but this starts with a HUGE REVEAL, Palpatine is alive... I was facepalming at that point "The Dead Speak!!" Why on Earth/Space would you put such a reveal exactly in the title roll??

I decided to ignore that thinking that it might be just a one off... to my dismay it wasn't. The ENTIRE FIRST HALF was RUSHED and full of flat and wooden dialogue which made me lose my apetite for any popcorn I had!

At this point I was asking myself if buying a ticket let alone popcorn was even worth it.

I did like the C3PO moments they were hilarious. But still did not make up for all the overwhelmingly underwhelming mess that I was witnessing!!

Finn... yeah we heard ya, no need to shout like that, it was annoying as hell and cringeworthy!! I loved those Millennium Falcon stunts tho they were cool.

Rey, Palpatine's Granddaughter!?!? Wtf? That was really stupid, I get it though, JJ Abrams was given the duty to clean up TLJ's mess which is frankly impossible to do in a 2.5hr runtime!!! Disney, What were you thinking?? Ah of course... money.

I give up at this point... they ruined Leia which is disgusting and inappropriate to do in memory of someone who died! You should be ashamed!!

Too many new and quick unnoticeable characters were included unnecessarily!

Hats off to some of the actors who still tried to do their best.. but hey, let's face it they worked with what they were given.

The cinematography was spectacular and mesmerizing, the only major positive in this movie in my opinion.

Overall rating is an F

title: one of the worst movies I have ever seen
review: Absolute trash. Do not see this movie. Meaningless trash that treats the audience like an idiot.

title: Enjoyable film slandered by an entitled community
review:
I'm sick and tried of bad reviews for what isn't a bad movie given by people who only highlight the bad points. It feels like people believe they're entitled to a movie with a story told exactly how they want it and so refuse to enjoy it. The 1 star reviews are not from true Star Wars fans in my opinion.

Star Wars storytelling has never been incredible or even that original. The whole sagas story is as old as time, one of good vs evil. Star Wars has always been fun, sometimes dark and entertaining with a clear message of finding hope in the darkest of times. This movie was just that.

I'm more than happy with this latest entry from the Galaxy Far Far Away

title: Haters gonna hate, but I loved it
review: Movie that in my view saved the new trilogy. It takes you on an intense journey in the Star Wars universe, loved it. Let's see if it passea the test of time, but as of now - an awesome episode in the Star Wars saga!

title: Sorry Mom, Star Wars is dead...
review:
One of my earliest happy memories in life is going to see The Empire Strikes Back with my mom. I remember how utterly fascinated I was with the experience, magical. Years later when I was old enough to understand what was going on in the Original Trilogy I knew I was a lifelong Star Wars fan.

Every single movie that came out later, even the Phantom Menace reminded me of the magic of that 1st movie going experience, some of the magic was still intact. Up until this movie...

It is an excel sheet masquerading as a movie. A struggle between jj abrams vs rian johnson. Like a tug of war is how I'd describe this new trilogy. As much as I hated some choices Rian made in the previous movie, I almost wish he was at the helm on this one so at least one vision got realized.

What happened is the damn rope breaks due to all this course correcting. Other reviewers have gone into painstaking detail about the issues so I won't go into them but most are true.

Today I simply mourn because The Force is gone, the magic is gone, the story is gone, our Jedis are now truly extinct. At least I still have that distant memory of the 1st ever movie I went to see in my life where Star Wars really did take me to a Galaxy far, far away...

title: Retcons Anakin and Luke
review: A disaster of epic proportions. There is almost nothing the film gets right apart from audio and visuals. Plot feels rushed and the main characters development are non existent

title: An amazing journey
review: I'll start off to say that I am biased. In 1977 I went to see A New Hope as a 10 year old boy. From the opening score I was hooked and transported into a world that would stay with me now into my early 50s. As a young boy I imagined being part of that world - the trading cards, models of the Falcon and Red 5 X-Wing. As each moving came I could hardly wait in excruciating anticipation. In my 30s the prequels came out. Yes, they were not the same...new characters and the building of the story of Obi-wan and Anakin. Understandably, many felt these movies did not measure up to the nearly impossible expectations of episodes 4-6. Then comes The Force Awakens. Again, new characters introduced and we're led through essentially a passing of e wand to a new generation. So now we close with The Rise of Skywalker. I was blown away. I truly feel it was an epic adventure. I can't adequately relate the excitement and emotions felt through the entire movie. At once a 52 year old man and a 10 year old boy reliving every moment of the galaxy far far away. Tears of joy.

title: Wasted potential ruined by its predecessor
review:
I'm not going to make this review about TLJ, because that topic has been shredded to bits many times over, but I can't help but notice how much this film suffers from the reckless decisions made by the writers of Episode VIII. A good lot of time in this film is dedicated to turning back the clock and reversing many plot points etc. and the rest of the movie suffers for it.

Now exactly what I'm saying here is that while ROS is far from a satisfying ending, I don't believe it's entirely its fault. That does not mean that similar, or worse story decisions weren't made in this film. Because on many occasions it was very apparent.

I went in to this film with two friends, ready to have a good laugh at the movie's expense. Yes, that is what TLJ did to me... It made me see Star Wars as a joke, and I have loved this franchise for almost all of my life.

However, I remember entering the theatre and sitting down before I glimpsed a smaller man with what I assume were his friends enter. The man was dressed as an X-wing pilot and I remember in that moment thinking that I would try and give this movie a chance. So I and the rest of the audience sat in silence and then 30 minutes in, the movie started to fall apart. I specifically think of the Hux-scene because in that moment, the entire audience laughed - and from that moment on, the laughter never really stopped.

I feel so bad for this man all dressed up in his outfit, going to the theatre, wanting to be amazed, and then the audience laughs at the movie just as you would laugh at a person tripping and falling on an ice covered sidewalk. But as I feel bad for laughing, I wholeheartedly believe that the movie is to blame, because it's a mess. It's embarrassing and its deus ex machina plot solutions are pathetic.

Don't go see this movie, don't go and give away your money for something this embarrassing.

I give this movie a score of 4, and here's why: Everyone's notion of what numbers mean in this context differ in some capacity and to me, a 5 or anything higher is a movie that I quite enjoyed, for one reason or another. I hold Star Wars movies to a higher standard than say, The Hangover, and therefore I could not enjoy this movie for what it was.

title: Don't believe the negative reviews
review: I went knowing all of the spoilers, anticipating this to be a disaster, and boy was I wrong. Yes, it was very busy, but it needed to be after the last jedi, and definitely made up for it.

title: Underwhelming
review: There is never a dull moment in this movie, there is always something happening constantly evolving the plot which makes this a dramaturgical nightmare in my opinion. The movie feels rushed and should've been longer with time dedicated towards explaining deep lore to less hardcore fans. Delivers an ending that fans can live with and some will be happy with.

title: The kids bloody loved it and so did I
review: Ignore the negative reviews this film is amazing, my kids all wanna see it again they thought it was fantastic, loads of nostalgia for me and plenty of action and excitement for them, won't spoil anything but there's a bit in the final battle that trumps the end game finale for me. Loved it, go see it you won't be disappointed

title: Good entertainment but set your expectation to low
review:
Other reviewers are right: this is no classic Starwars we knew and love. I won't repeat the same language but it strongly reminds me of what happens at work: some dude produces a design document and send for stakeholder review. There are generally too many of them and they all put in their own selfish and parochial comments. The weak-minded author tries to close all the comments by catering to all of them, ending up with a meandering, soulless, and fragmented design.... In art as in engineering, you need a decisive and visionary leader to control the narrative. Inundated yourself in pipedream system engineering fantasy land and you get this design by committee.
Visuals are good tho... Looks like after 2000 the only dudes who worked hard in the film industry were the visual effect crews.

title: Pompous anticlimax
review:
I was quite defensive about the trilogy until now. The Force Awakens was decently entertaining reboot. The Last Jedi, although corny, was somewhat interesting to sit through. Outside of the main saga, Rogue One, I considered to be a good movie per se. And while I never expected a masterpiece here, I hoped last episode of the 42 year old saga would at least be: entertaining.

Well, the longest episode of the saga manages to offer the least (apart from Episode II). The movie is bombarded with crammed visual topping. Literally every second of it's length is filled with a flashy action, yet none of it is memorable. The Last Jedi had memorable moments, whether you like it or not. The Rise of Skywalker simple doesn't. It has around three scenes you remember faintly when you return home.

I wouldn't want to say the movie is thoroughly bad, but it's just a pointless mess. Not only it fails to end the story in satisfying way, it doesn't offer any interesting plot patterns at any scale. The movie does however have some neat visuals, and after all, it finally ends the saga. It's watchable piece of popular culture. No more, no less. Gladly I'm not a fanboy, because then I might be mad.

title: Don't get the critics hate on this movie
review: If you want to see a finale to a saga, go see this movie, it's action packed from start to finish, easily the best movie out of the sequel trilogy. Would see this again in the theater if given the opportunity. Already preordered it on ITunes.

title: I do not understand the negative reviews, this was excellent.
review: I saw Rise of Skywalker yesterday going in disgruntled by the early reviews. Upon further review, The critics negative input on the film, was incredibly wrong. I haven't been this drawn into a Star Wars movie since I was a kid watching the original saga for the first time. There literally wasn't a dull moment throughout this whole movie. A visually pleasing work of art that is filled with action, emotion, nostalgia, and so much more. This was about 90% of what I wanted out of this movie, as they executed the finale very well. I was no fan of the Last Jedi and feared that this movie would be even worse. Though, this was far from the case as REAL Star Wars fan will appreciate this film for what it is. Without saying too much, I see a lot of Return of the Jedi in this film, (one of my favorite Star Wars films) which is probably why I loved it so much. Please go into this with a positive mindset because it really makes you feel like a kid again, start to end. Thank You JJ Abrams for executing this successfully!

title: Visually great, plot lacking
review: Poor ending to a saga, the last 40 minutes had me asking "what am I doing here??".

title: Has almost nothing to offer.
review:
It's a movie that feels like a retcon of previous entry of the franchise, written by someone desperately trying to please the fans with nostalgia, quick story fixes and forcing emotional resonance that wasn't earned and appeared out of thin air. As a result it's an incoherent mess that deliveres only on humour in early stage of the movie - after a while even humour becomes forced to the point the whole project seems like a failed attempt at parody - and starts to be funny in a whole different over-the-top ridiculous way.
Movie juggles with characters forced backstories and motivations, seemingly more out of obligation than a real need to tell a story.
Plot seems to be a monstrous mix of double-what-The-Force-Awakens mainly consisted of - double the coincidence, double the in-your-face exposition and double the bland-interactions-between-the-characters-that-mostly-consists-of-shouting, dialogue that makes the prequels seem like they were written by Shakespeare.
It treats audience members as idiots or people that have severe lack of ability to focus or process information - thus need to be told IN A VERY DIRECT AND LOUD WAY through both visual and sound what is going on, and why characters behave the way they do.
It's similar to Game of Thrones Season 8 finale - it takes a deep drop to the ground level in terms of quality and characters' motivation and coherence, but when in case of Game of Thrones it's 10-storey building jump that has a serious impact, here it's like stepping off the curb - previous entries of the Trilogy has not much to offer either.

title: Satisfying conclusion to the saga
review: Managed to regain the fans' trust and love. JJ was able to provide the fans an entertaining movie, mixing it with an emotional finale

title: Saves the Franchise
review: I was hating the Last Jedi, but JJ Abrams saved the franchise. Sure, it's somewhat a corny, predictable, eye-rolling landing at times, but a landing it is, after The Last Jedi. Piecing things together in a way that even at times seems out of the blue, but they are pieced together in an interesting fashion and it's understandable why those choices were made and they were made well.

title: Spoilers Alert - Perfect film
review:
As you can see by my review rating and title I really enjoyed this film.

The film had so many references to the old films from the battle of Endor to the battle of Mustafar, I loved the new species and systems they brought into this film.

Rey's character journey is now complete with the big reveal of who her parents are and why she is important and so strong in the past it is so cool to see her abilities grow and I think it's incredible that she can heal such a cool power to see along with other abilities too!

Kyle's character transformation was excellent too going from badass to extreme badass was awesome!

I liked the way they handled Leia's death as I was worried they were going to shrug it off or do something lame with it but they didn't.

The final battle was superb the thrill I got from all those civilian ships arriving to help out and also seeing Lando again was great!

And well of course cant forget Palpertine's return this was done incredibly well and the connection he mentioned between Rey and Kylo was cool too.

Overall I loved every moment of this film and don't understand how anyone could dislike it.

title: Why Why Why Why Why.
review: Would like to just say thank you for wasting my valuable oxygen by producing this trilogy, I have no words for the disappointment I have. Would also like to apologise to Adam Driver for having to carry the entire god damn FRANCHISE on his back. Will not say anything specific as to prevent from spoilers but the idea of the force and the capabilities of an individual from the first 6 films are just completely thrown out the window and converted into blasphemy. The series has become too involved in trying to shape opinion in real life and has lost not only its individuality but its identity as a whole. Anybody who says that this any of these films are better than a single movie from the first 6 should never watch another film.

title: Unrealistic, unrealistic, unrealistic.
review: Also hectic camera, bad and boring story. Much boom boom action movie flair and humor every 2 minutes for 8 year old children. Many unneccessary characters, CGI everywhere. Worst Star Wars ever.

title: They ruined Star Wars forever....
review: Somehow palpatine is not dead.... and anakin/darth Vader did not fulfill the prophecy of the chosen one that brings balance to the force.... and Rey is a god alone with no training needed to know how to fly around and uses the shwartz... fact - there is only six Star Wars movies in the saga... the last three are stand alone films

title: Unintentionally hilarious
review:
Terrible contrived plot, wooden acting, but has great (unintentional) comedic value. So ridiculous in places that I laughed out loud more than watching any previous Star Wars film.

Yes, this is one of those films that is so bad you just have to laugh at it.

title: Wrong on so many levels
review: This film is just horrible. There is no way to enjoy it and honestly it is as bad as the last jedi.

title: Unfortunately since the project was rushed, it suffered the consequences.
review:
...The Problem is The Writing. Finn and Poe together would have been so Damn Amazing...

The Characters and The Audience should not be experiencing a lack of understanding the plot.

Digressing with Random happenstance, the universe is still beautiful than ever. The whole narrative throughout the sequel-trilogy feels same in pace as "The Phantom Menace". Rey needed more information on why she is the lead. She is a blank slate and could play off that. Why did she want to become a Jedi? Why is she just looking for her parents?! There also was No real introduction of obi-wan either who is the lead in TPM. I think the narrative of TPM really did work for that movie tho, it was a new direction with an original aesthetic feel that was consistent, and it was gooood.

I am a passionate fan of the series but the characters were just short or bringing in the action from years past. I wish there were more saber battles...

I rate the sequel trilogy a 6/10

I rate the original trilogy a 10/10 I rate the prequels a 7/10 I gave it a 1/10 on IMDb because I hear it might help bring it down to the 6.

Can we get a redo? Please? Make an alternate universe or directors cut? Continue the star wars universe with the Jedi and the their adventures.

title: Dont know what to say.... Its not crap but its not good either.
review:
To be honest, the movie is kinda into a fire, going out, then going into a new fire. DOnt like that They does so much call back to original movies, and not Prequel but sure there was some Prequel stuff in voice acting. Again Rey goes against Kylo, and of course, she defeats him... Dont think he never ever took her down. And we Saw Rey kicking Lukes ass in TLJ and this time Luke gets ass kicked by his own sister Leia during training montage. What is it about all these weak men?

And why is the movie called Rise of Skywalker, when the last Skywalker gets killed in the end, after giving life to our favorite heorine (not) Rey that kinda gets killed. Why doest she stay dead, the ultimate sacriface. That would have done so much to her arch. And Kylo should have been the last Skywalker. Noh.... sorry Disney. If you just dead whats needed. 3 new movies WITH the original characters, and then in the ninth leave it to the new cast, and then make three new movies with Rey, Poe and so on. Instead of this.... I am sorry. I wanted to like it, and there was stuff I did like. Sure.

One thing though. Remember those rumours that told that Luke was going to do this grand force thing in the TLJ? It was said he was to pull down a star destroyer. But as we all know, that didnt happen. He got to be the coward that was hidden. Sure, they did try to change Rey to a more insecure heroin this time. But it was a little to much a little to late. She just ran away when she wasnt sure about where her loyalies was. But that was just for a short second. She did though do this pulling down a starship with the force thing close to the Luke Rumour.

And why remove Rose that much. sure she wasnt annoying this time around, but she was one of the head characters and didnt get anything in sense to do this time around. If they wrote her like this in TLJ, she would have been much more liked. But in stead she got this cringe character in TLJ. Here she was much cooler, and should definately had more screen play this time around.

But cant forgive Disney for killing off Luke like they did. And all these small pointing that Luke wasnt really that powerful, he will always loose to a woman, in sense.

So, yes its better than TLJ, but its still isnt good. ALl this so called Trilogy from Disney, seems like they jumped so much history before TLJ and Rise of Skywalker, kinda like 2 movies are missing.

title: How is this rated so high on imdb?
review: There is no way this movie deserves close to a 7/10. Just looking at the user reviews confirms this. I took the chance and watched it last night anyways, its a bad movie. Story makes no sense, just jumps allover the place. Why is it so hard for Disney to make a good Star Wars film?

Light speed skipping is flawed. Performed manually, a nano micro millisecond longer and you are colliding with another object. Think about it, 983,600,000 feet per second. Obviously one has to perform a light speed skip at the exact angle escape and the exact duration to still be behind them at the exact spot. Yet numerous chasers keep up the chase. A fascinating power, I'll call "ForceTime", allows 2 force users to swap objects across the galaxy. Rey is on a planet, Kylo is on a ship across the galaxy, and he grabs a necklace off her and when the ForceTime call is ended, hands it to an aide to determine her location. Awesome new skill...to solve a much needed plot device.

Thanks to The Last Jedi, force ghosts can interact with the real world. This continues with force ghost Luke catching an object thrown at him. Why not have an army of force ghosts obliterate the enemy? There can be a scary Army of the Dead...if you are Darth King Aragorn.

Adding to the horror element, normal people can appear as ghosts! Maybe this is only to force sensitive users but who knows what's next in this degenerating series.

A coliseum of evil people watch a fight and no one intervenes when the bad guy is about to lose. Well, a few guards try against someone who can toss people around with a though. title: It's a great movie...
review:
If you are a casual fan and judge it as a standalone movie. The visuals are great, the soundtrack is on point, and the scene is more intimidating than the last two movies. However, if we were to judge it as a part of a larger story that the movie ties itself to, then it is perhaps the WORST Star Wars movies in terms of plot. This is not a hyperbole. The movie is filled with retcons and bad plot twists that don't make sense and just exist for the sake of introducing a twist. Let us explore some of the bigger ones (This is going to be long so strap on)

***Spoilers begin here, read at your own risk***

1. Palpatine is alive. How? The movie doesn't actually tell you. The characters actually throw this question in the movie itself and it is answered with a non-answer. Yep, no explanation how the Emperor survived the explosion of Death Star II. It is so clear that his return is unplanned that the writers don't bother to actually explain things and just expect the audience to go with it. The main problem with Palpatine surviving, however, is something else.

2. The Prophecy of the Chosen One. One of the more significant elements introduced in the prequels is the prophecy of a Chosen One, born of no father, who will bring balance to the Force by ending the Sith. Qui-Gon identifies Anakin is such and his status as the Chosen One is confirmed by the Father who is essentially a Force God in the Clone Wars series after Anakin brings balance to his world. See the problem with Palpatine being alive? It retcons an established plot point from the first six movies and the Clone Wars. Turns out Anakin is not the Chosen One as he failed to end the Sith. Rey did. However, Rey isn't the Chosen One either because she has a father--who is going to be the subject of our next point of contention. So, who is the real Chosen One?

3. Rey is Palpatine's granddaughter. Yes, you read that right. The Emperor did explore the moist caverns apparently. Rey is the daughter of Palpatine's son who ran away from his dad for, you guessed it, unexplained reasons. This revelation came out of NOWHERE and doesn't make sense. The best way to describe it would be a cheap plot twist created in order to create a parallel to Vader's revelation to Luke in Empire Strikes Back. This brings the question--why did Anakin's lightsaber call out to a Palpatine? Palpatine is directly behind the suffering and destruction of the entire Skywalker family. We'll never know.

4. Palpatine's great flip-flops. At first, Palpatine wants Kylo to kill Rey. Then he shifts to wanting Rey to kill him so that he can possess her. He finally decides to drain both Kylo and Rey's life force just a while later and kill both of them. Confused? You will be.

5. Snoke's Origins is retconned. According to novels considered canon under Disney and the Force Awakens Visual Dictionary itself, Snoke was a rather important figure who had witnessed the fall of the Republic and the rise and subsequent fall of the Empire. The movie just trashes all of that and makes Snoke a cloned puppet that the Emperor created while experimenting in the Unknown Regions during his exile. The movie not only retcons old material but the new ones as well. So much for consistency and coherence of Plot.

6. Rey "accidentally" casts Force Lightning. Yeah, you heard that right too. At this point it becomes obvious that JJ Abrams and Chris Terrio only watched the OT prior to making the script for inspiration and fanservice moments. The line of reasoning is that since Palpatine is the only one to actually use it in the original trilogy, it must somehow be a trait unique to his bloodline. Sadly, that's not quite the case as the Prequels and the wider established canon such as the Clone Wars shows us. Force Lightning is a difficult technique that requires great knowledge and mastery of the Dark Side. Merely accidentally tapping into the Dark Side is not enough. Otherwise, we would've seen characters such as Darth Maul or Kylo Ren himself who are very strong and fully immersed in the dark side cast Force Lightning willfully at the very least. Another retcon or mistake on the writers's part.

These are some of the major problems I had with the movie. There are some other things that bother me like the Force being on steroids and used as a plot device in the movie along with how Palpatine assembled his secret fleet. The movie also unnecessarily make quite a few aims at its predecessor.

This is not to say there aren't moments that are well done, however. I personally loved the Reverse Han-Kylo scene where he throws away his lightsaber and reclaims his identity as Ben Solo by embracing the Light Side, Luke acting like an actual Jedi master, Finn playing an actual role in the movie and being revealed as Force Sensitive (a plot twist that's actually done right). The movie has its moments.

Overall, it is a good movie as a standalone. However, as part of the Skywalker saga, the movie is hardly satisfying and breaks a lot of preexisting lore and established plot points. As a long time Star Wars fan, I care about the plot of a Star Wars movie the most and the movie's utter failure to have a consistent and meaningful one greatly affects my score of the movie.

title: Dissapointing ending of an epic and culturally important cinematic saga
review: It's time, the overarching storyline of "Star Wars" now known as the "Skywalker Saga", that started back in 1977, has come to an end almost 45 years later. It should go out with a bang, celebrating what has made "Star Wars" a staple in popular culture, and a pinnacle in the science fiction genre, but instead, it exits on a low note, more focused on satisfying needs of space ship battles and action scenes, rather than believing the loyal fans of the franchise could handle a compelling story. The upsides of Episode IX, "The Rise of Skywalker" are few; the Resistance has a final shot against the First Order, and Kylo Ren (Driver) who gets some help from Emperor Palpatine (Ian McDiarmid). Daisy Ridley returns as Rey, with John Boyega and Oscar Isaac's parts as Finn and Poe reduced to fun, supporting characters, although they never beat C-3PO and Chewbacca. What "Star Wars: Episode IX" does best is technical aspects, the CGI is sublime, so are prosthetics, costumes and other visual effects. As always in the space opera franchise, the setting and memorable aliens, are some of the most entertaining parts, but what the original trilogy - and the very first movie especially - did, which the sequel trilogy never does, is telling an emotional story of family, friends, loyalty, and good against evil. Mark Hamill and Carrie Fisher (who has scenes recorded for the film before her death), are, as always, nice to see, even their capacity is limited, and yes, the film is overall an entertaining experience, but once again, visually only. It had the opportunities to make some emotional impact on its audience through the scenes of Rey and Kylo, and Ridley and Driver has a good chemistry, but as with most other things in this movie, their scenes and plot line are rushed, feeling more like a tease of what the filmmakers could have explored in terms of family and relationships. With "The Rise of the Skywalker", the grand "Skywalker Saga" ends on a note indifferent to everything the marvelous space opera once meant to so many fans worldwide.

title: And the Fall of a Saga
review:
Thank GOD it's over, but mercifully, and the highest praise I can give this movie: the 141 minutes, unbelievably, flew by. Unlike the previous installment that was a tad longer, but felt twice as long.

I heard someone describe this movie as scene, then scene, then scene and then end. My Star Wars friend and I laughed as we pointed out that's how all movies are. Until...I saw this. And they were so incredibly right.

This film is just a checklist of things needed for a Star Wars movie with a few extra bonus scenes to conclude the 9-film franchise. It did NOT feel like a comprehensive story, it did NOT have any emotion to any character dying or almost dying and it did NOT feel like a continuation of the previous films - like, for the first time, you didn't actually have to see anything prior to understand this "plot" as a whole. (It would help, though, since there are about 50 little Easter Eggs for fans. Most pretty funny, and I did like.)

So, just like that checklist, they just went from scene to scene without much flow or great editing. It actually felt more like a chore to get to the end for the filmmakers and actors who ALL seemed to have checked out by now.

Let's see if I can sum up this movie in a non-spoilery synopsis, though, frankly, there's not much at all to spoil. If you can imagine what this movie is about, you're probably right. But, anyways, a dark figure emerges outta nowhere in the timeline and offers the series newest sorta bad guy, Kylo Ren, much more to defeat the good guys with since all they've ever proven over 9 movies is how inept the most powerful machines and forces are against a group made up of the tiniest of fractions of the Dark Side.

So, our good guys hear this and must go from Point A to B to C to...Z to try and work things out. Bring balance, whatever.

I certainly didn't hate this movie like I remember walking out of Episode VIII: The Last Jedi with such a broken heart. And previously I hated Episode VII: The Force Awakens since it was a 89% shot-by-shot remake of Episode IV: A New Hope. Since VII and VIII's releases and a few more re-watches, I'm warmed up to them a bit, though I still rank them low overall.

I don't know if the same can be said here. Like I said, I didn't hate this movie - the special effects were good and the humor, namely from C3P0 and Chewie, did make me laugh out loud more than a few times. But, I really didn't like it much. The story, if there was one, was so flat and so uninspiring. I really didn't care about any of the characters here. None of them. Well, again, I liked C3P0 and Chewie for the humor they brought me, but I didn't care if they lived or died. In fact, when some characters DID pass on, extremely little time was given to grieve and the setup to their demise was almost comical, almost a last-minute add-on...and followed by a quick MOVE-ON.

While it's watchable and has some great little homages to the series, it currently ranks as my all-time least favorite theatrical film in the entire series. Which is sad, because that was the exact same reaction I had when I saw both VIII and VII.

Recommended? Sure. Especially since there's nothing in here to really offend and it does conclude the saga, if you're a completist. I've seen a lot worst out there, so I guess I could recommend this faster paced finale.

***

Final thoughts: Here's my Best to Worst Theatrical Releases of This Saga:

1 Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back 2 Rogue One 3 Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope 4 Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi 5 Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith 6 Star Wars Episode VII: The Force Awakens 7 Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones 8 Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace 9 Solo 10 Star Wars Episode VIII: The Last Jedi 11 Star Wars Episode IX: The Rise of Skywalker

It's exactly as good as I expected. I'm not a huge star wars fan, but I appreciate the original trilogy a lot, and who doesn't love a good sci-fi/action flick. I feel bad for the die hard fans who keep getting let down film after film. There were a few people at my showing wearing Star Wars shirts, and the guy sitting next to me even brought a light saber, which is cool, I mean they're there to have a good time and watch a cool movie from their favourite film series. It's just brutal to see what Disney has done with this franchise and the complete disregard for these loyal fans. And is it just me, or does it feel like you're almost not allowed to say you don't like these movies? There are a lot of divisive topics these days; it feels like more than ever, and that people are angrier at each other more than I can ever remember. But movies? Can we not just say we either like a movie or we don't and get on with our lives?

PS: There is very little in this movie worth paying even a nominal amount of money to see, but the reason I gave it three stars instead of two or one is because the special effects were incredible, and the choreography was really, really good. Also, I laughed a couple times at C-3P0. All the main characters were cast really well, and at times I found myself almost liking some of them, but the fact that none of them are memorable is no fault of the actors. Many of the other characters/actors were very odd and felt extremely out of place. It was almost like the casting director just gave out all the minor rolls to friends and family. It was just a bizarre feeling. You'll know what I mean when you watch it. The whole movie just felt really strange and uncomfortable.

Star Wars Review Time! (No Spoilers)
Rise of Skywalker midnight screening complete. This film only demonstrates the disorganisation of Disney as they attempt to backpedal after The Last Jedi. Not only is the film unoriginal, but I'd go so far as to call it bland fan fiction. The plot holes are so obvious it literally hurts to watch. Star Wars is about the Skywalker bloodline, and more importantly the prophecy of Anakin Skywalker bringing balance to the force. The conclusion of the "Skywalker Saga" solidifies itself as anything but the story of the Skywalkers, but rather the story of a girl who got everything and didn't have to work for it. Poor writing, poor character development, and a story completely laden with "progressive politics" undeniably indicates that the core plot of Star Wars has been crushed under Disney. I forecast potential layoffs at Disney/Lucasfilm over this 3rd failed outing (The Last Jedi and Solo being 1 and 2 respectively). If you don't watch Star Wars for the story, then enjoy. But if you're a fan who's read into the lore, then I'm sorry, you won't be pleased. I suggest you save your money and make a statement to Disney that you won't accept this level of quality.

title: Well, they did their best at this point
review:
Ok, let me start by saying this movie is not terrible. That said, it is far from great.

TFA was not a bad start, but also nothing special. TLJ was an absolute disaster, leaving Abrams little ground to stand on

This film helped reconcile some of the issues from TLJ. However, everything was still extremely rushed. Palpatine is alive with absolutely no explanation other than a passing reference to the power he learned from Plagueis. This totally ruins the entire 6-film plot of Anakin being the chosen one. I do not hate having Palpatine back, but this tarnishes the legacy of Anakin/Vader.

Ben is redeemed and I really loved that, but it was extremely rushed and took a matter of seconds for him to go from totally evil to being good again.

Rey is Palpatine's granddaughter? Will someone please tell me who would get with Palpatine? Or why he would want to get with anyone? Also, this feels like a cheap rip-off of the big moment in Empire (although this entire trilogy is a cheap rip-off of the originals).

Rey claims to be a Skywalker? Sure it's a nice message that it's "not about your blood, but who you choose to be," but she simply is not the chosen one so it doesn't work.

Palpatine is suddenly MASSIVELY more powerful than ever before despite his extremely weak body. He could've used the abilities we see here in ROTJ and he would've won by a landslide. That said, it was fun to see the force used on a larger scale on the big screen.

Palpatine has the biggest fleet in history from...where exactly? Their planet-killing weaponry came from...where exactly? A few shots from a fighter destroys the cannon along with the entire ship?

Who does Rey love and who loves Rey? Ah, who cares?

On the positive side of things:

We finally see the true power of the sith on the big screen. We've seen it in games, books, etc., but never really in the movies. Palpatine finally feels like the most powerful sith ever, rather than lagging behind all the ones in games and books.

We finally get some development for Rey and Kylo beyond the surface level.

THERE'S FINALLY A DECENT LIGHTSABER DUEL

Overall, an entertaining movie that helps course-correct a bit after all the damage Rian Johnson did in TLJ. Still, at the end of the day, there wasn't much left to work with so we have a film where Abrams rushed to cover all his bases and control past damage (he denies it but we all know this film was damage control). The film is FULL of plot holes and problems, but it is still entertaining and has some enjoyable moments, which is much better than Johnson did.

title: the end of the saga
review:
Greetings again from the darkness. Ending the final trilogy of trilogies that covers 42 years of storytelling, was never going to be easy. And, given the rabid fan base's backlash from the penultimate episode, the ending was unlikely to appease all (or even most?). Keeping respectful of the sensitivity associated with this franchise, no spoilers are included here, certainly nothing that hasn't already been dissected and debated after the trailers were released.

As I approached the theatre, it was impossible not to chuckle at the irony of seeing the life-sized marketing prop for KNIVES OUT in the lobby. Of course, that current release is directed by Rian Johnson, who caused such an uproar with the aforementioned STAR WARS: THE LAST JEDI (Episode VIII), a franchise entry that happens to be one of my personal favorites. But we are here for Episode IX, the wrap-up of George Lucas' masterful vision. JJ Abrams (STAR WARS: EPISODE VII - THE FORCE AWAKENS) is back in the director's chair, and knowing what a fanboy he is, it's not surprising to see the familiarity and tributes to the franchise interjected throughout.

In fact, this finale leans heavily on nostalgia and humor, while tying up most loose ends - as well as some that weren't even all that loose. Writers Derek Connolly, Colin Trevorrow (originally slated to direct), Chris Terrio, and Abrams seemed intent on giving each beloved character their moment, as a sign of appreciation for their contributions to a legacy that covers a period longer than the lifespan of some of the biggest Star Wars fans. As one who stood in line in 1977, it's an approach that I respect and have no problems with - knowing full well that some will.

Any attempt to tie up previous threads must focus on the odd, mystical relationship between Kylo Ren (Adam Driver) and Rey (Daisy Ridley). Both are still conflicted and attempting to come to grips with who they are. Rey especially is struggling with her identity and roots. One of my favorite elements from The Last Jedi was inner-head conversations blended with cross-dimensional physical interactions between Kylo and Rey, and it's used beautifully here.

So, the biggest complaint from me is that despite its nearly two-and-a-half hour run time, there is simply too much crammed in. Too much story and too many characters and too many things that get a glimpse or mention, but no real development. This movie is jam-packed, and 'convoluted' would not be too strong of a word to describe. There are times we aren't sure where the characters are or what they are doing or why they are doing it. We do know that everything good is dependent on 'this mission', a mission that seems to change direction about every 12 minutes. In fact, the "new" players - Rey, Poe (Oscar Isaac) and Finn (John Boyega) - spend very little time together on screen. And really, Finn is given almost nothing to do except look worried most of the time. On the bright side for characters, Chewbacca (Joonas Suotamo) and C3PO both get their own sub-plots. Anthony Daniels (as C3PO) becomes the only actor to appear in all 9 episodes, although R2D2 joins C3PO as characters appearing in all.

There are many old familiar faces, both good and evil. Some of these play key roles, while others are brief cameos. Much has been speculated about how Carrie Fisher's role as Leia will be handled. Archival footage, combined with special effects and camera angles, allows her to be present throughout, and yes, she gets the send-off she deserves. There are even some new characters/creatures introduced, including a cute new droid (never underestimate or under-market a droid) that is already for sale in Disney stores.

No matter one's feelings or expectations, an area that surely will not disappoint is the visual effects. Somehow, this one is even more impressive and awe-inspiring than the others. In particular, a couple of scenes filmed in and around an angry sea left me dumbfounded, mouth-agape. However, what's most amazing is the consistency of the visuals throughout. It's just a stunning film to look at. Some of the story may be a bit confusing or cheesy, but some parts of the film are truly great. Cinematographer and Special Effects guru Dan Mindel deserves special mention, as do Production Designers Rick Carter and Kevin Jenkins. Of course the visual effects team is without peer - and take up about 5 minutes in the closing credits.

Lastly, composer John Williams gets to add his well-deserved personal stamp on this final chapter with new work added to the already iconic score. Very few moments compare to the opening notes blasting away on the theatre sound system as a Star Wars film begins. And as much as we'd like to treat this as the end, we all know Disney will find a way to keep us interested in a galaxy, far far away.

review:
As a life long fan, I was left cold by the Force Awakens. The movie felt almost like an insult to the intelligences of anyone who grew up with and loved the original trilogy: a half-baked copy of a New Hope with a severely under-developed and incoherent plot and a protagonist who seemed like there wasn't much more for her to learn.

Then the Last Jedi came out, and I was pleasantly surprised. I didn't love every creative choice made, but I loved that Rian Johnson and co. were brave enough to not care about what I or anyone like me thought. Unlike any Star Wars movie before, last Jedi encouraged its audience to really think about what they saw, and provided more nuanced character plot lines, giving its talented cast far more room to show what they could do.

Alas, between the massive basement-dwelling neard lashback and clear lack of planning or time to redirect, the Rise of Skywalker tries to do far too much with far too little run-time. The entire first act of the film has one of the worst pacings of any big budget picture of recent memory. The characters practically yell dialogue behind themselves as they sprint furiously past one another to the next set piece. There are maybe four references in total to anything that occurred in the Last Jedi, and some of them are non-verbal. Long-lasting series conventions are torn to shreds without any explanation, making it obvious to any non-child in the audience that rules are being broken for either coolness or convenience. This has been a major problem for the sequel trilogy in general- rather than creating stories that meld with the lush universe left behind by Lucas and hundreds of EU contributors, the Disney crew have opted to violently rend the Star Wars world whenever it serves the plots they have concocted.

By the second third, things calm down just a bit. Abrams deftly introduces an extremely lovable New Droid, and genuine, crowd-pleasing humor shines through. C-3PO gets his best turn of the sequel trilogy, a truly worthy and emotional, likely final performance for Anthony Daniels that any true fan will be unable to resist, other misgivings aside.

Perhaps the greatest tragedy of this final chapter is the (in my view) grotesque treatment of General Leia. Carrie Fisher's death broke our hearts, and created huge obstacles for this movie. It does not hurdle those obstacles. Abrams and Co. opted to force the plot around what remaining unused footage they had, and the result is some of the most awkward and incoherent sequences of dialogue ever put in a movie of this budget. I am unsure of what a better alternative would have been, but I am convinced one must have existed. It is ultimately an extremely disappointing send-off, one that constantly reminds the audience of Carrie Fisher's tragic death, rather than honoring her and the iconic character she gave life to.

The final act includes an incredibly bland and mostly silly CGI space battle. The final lightsaber fight between Kylo Ren and Rey on Death Star II wreckage is a highlight. It is choreographed with brutality and high-emotion, and is a worthy edition to StarWar's most memorable battles. The central conflict of this episode pretty much ignores or negates literally every Star Wars film that came before it, especially the Last Jedi. Palpatine, rather than being a welcome return, is made rather generic. Whereas prequel palpatine seemed cunning and diabolical, Rise of Skywalker palpatine seems to be mostly an obligatory shell of a villain.

The final 10-15 minutes of run time will be the most controversial, but especially the last 5. I found myself both happy and satisfied at some of the resolutions, and simultaneously disappointed and disgusted. By attempting to please everyone, I believe the rise of Skywalker will please very few people in reality. I do not regret the ticket price, but I just say that this is a disappointing and controversial end for a franchise that was such a huge part of my life. I'm frankly relieved it is over, but thankful for the flashes of old Star Wars magic that work in this film.

title: Hard to love. This shouldn't have been the final product. Why didn't they take more time to get it right?

The dynamic between Kylo and Rey has been one of the redeeming and most attractive character chemistry aspects in all of Star Wars for me; however they didn't stick the landing by the time they fought Palpatine. That whole action sequence was a letdown but the point being with how they had Kylo (now Ben by this time) force fade away after transferring life-force energy was unnecessary. They kiss for the first time and it works because the chemistry is just undeniably there. Although I could see it feeling off for some people just given that a lot of other things fell flat by the end of the movie. Anyway, Ben could have easily stayed alive and the romance/partnership of these two would have culminated into something grand. We waited to see how they'd transpire, and instead of a proper send off with Ben by her side in the end -- he just awkwardly lies down after resuscitating her via their somewhat innate ancient ability to use "life force" which was explained by one line from Palpatine. Maybe that particular shot of Ben passing just threw me but either way I hate their choice in having him die. Other notes: too much bickering between the squad, not really a joint feeling, Lando and many other moments came off as "member-berries". Kylo's helmet design looked like it was solely made for toy sales. Its ultra redness was distracting to look at. I enjoyed all of the lightsaber moments and duels aside from the dual lightsaber wielding face-off Rey had with Palpatine. Speaking of Palpatine, his entire plan was to have Rey succeed him by killing him? As I said before the whole final act could have been done far, far better. I was teetering around a 7/10 before the final act but it pretty much fell apart and genuine feelings were hard to come by given the looming, disjointed studio vibe throughout. So... 5/10 I liked half of it, but I'm letdown, so 5. Disney, word of advice from many fans: have a damn gameplan for a beloved franchise before crapping out a trilogy. The legacy of this trilogy will be muddled disjointed parts that could have been amazing if the proper time would have been put into it. Also, Kathleen Kennedy is the worst.

title: Bad ending to a bad trilogy.
review:
(Sigh), this film felt like a hasty attempt at compensating for TLJ, as well as explaining why Rey is so immensely powerful, and her origin story, oh and let's not forget the overload of fan service that they threw in as an attempt to win some nostalgia points.

First off, the conveniences were annoying and killed the tension that this could have had. For instance, Chewie is captured by The First Order and is about to be flown away in a transport ship, but then Rey and Kylo pull it with the force until it explodes. But later on we found out that Chewie was on a DIFFERENT transport ship, of course he was..... there's also a scene where C-3P0 has a Sith message in his memory but is forbidden to say it due to his programming (of course he is) and the only way they can get the message out of him is by finding a droidsmith that can encrypt it, and we learn that this will wipe his memory clean (of course it will). C-3P0 loses his memory, but then, wait for it.... R2 finds a way to get his memory back! (Of course he does). Also there just happen to be these "Sith wayfinders" that lead to a Sith planet!!! (Of course there are!) And Rey just happens to be Palpatine's granddaughter!!! Wait, what? Point is, I wouldn't mind seeing old characters disappear or be changed, because then it would show true sacrifice, stakes that would lead iconic characters to their end, and that would've made me feel tension, and it would've made me appreciate those characters even more for what they did to fight back against the dark side. Speaking of Rey....

Rey in this film is straight up ridiculous and over-the-top, to the point where she's like Starkiller from The Force Unleashed (a non canon SW game). There are some really silly scenes of her with Kylo on a desert planet near the start where she cuts off one of Kylo's TIE fighter's wings, sending the cockpit crashing down into the sand and exploding. Kylo surely died or was at least heavily injured, right? Nope, he just walks straight out and is in perfect condition, (sigh, of course he is), and then she starts pulling a transport ship out of the sky and Kylo battles her with the force, which I mentioned before and it was another awful scene. There's also this hilarious vision ahead has in the ruins of the Death Star where she fights an evil version of herself with a folding lightsaber and pointed teeth ðŸ˜‚, it just looked comical, and it could've been executed in a better way. Oh, and another thing, we could've seen Rey do some evil stuff, considering the fact that she had heritage from Palpatine (oh, here's another one: OF COURSE SHE DOES), I would've liked to see her join the Dark side and become Empress Palpatine, and then we'd get the true final conclusion in a sequel. I honestly feel like there was too much that needed to be covered in just one movie, TLJ is largely responsible. Disney could've done what they did with Avengers, and made it so that the enemy won and then we'd see the true final showdown between good and evil in the next film. But no, they had to rush an ending here....

I'll give the film credit where credit is due: the effects are spot on, as well as the music, the action seq- actually no, the action sequences sucked (especially the one where there were horse riders attacking a Star Destroyer, yes, I'm serious) and the performances from the actors were decent, they did their best with what they were given. Also some of the dialogue was great and genuinely made me chuckle. Other than that though, the film was quite a mess, and it failed to give us a satisfying conclusion. It also ended up wasting what could've been great new characters (e.g. Snoke and the Knights of Ren), since Snoke is revealed to be some product created by Palpatine, and the Knights of Ren barely do anything other than stand there and then get swiftly beaten by Kylo. All that teasing at the start of the trilogy for nothing.

But here's my final point: the ending. It sucked. Gigantic rebel fleet come out of nowhere to attack Palpatine's destroyers, Palpatine sucks the force power out of Rey and Kylo, Palpatine raises his old man hands and shoots force lightning at the rebel fleet, Kylo stands up but gets pushed away into a hole, Rey then stands up and Palpatine pauses his force lightning strike on the rebel ships and then they're back in power and start obliterating the star destroyers, Palpatine then shoots force lightning at Rey but Rey blocks it with her lightsaber, grabs another lightsaber and pushes the force lightning back, killing Palpatine in the process. Then the whole place starts crumbling and the star destroyers all get destroyed. But wait, there's more: Kylo climbs out of the hole to find Rey unconscious. Kylo mourns over Rey but then she wakes up, they kiss and then he dies. Amazing....

So there you have it, the Skywalker saga ends with a stinker, and I thought this film smelt bad on the outside (haha, get it?).

title: A Movie SCREAMING To Be Liked
review:
"Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker" knew what it was, a Star Wars movie and unlike "Star Wars: The Last Jedi", this movie has great fan service. It introduced interesting concepts into the franchise... a little to many. "Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker" was too caught up in trying to be liked that it forgot about more than half the ideas introduced. Paired with the feeling that there were several writers writing this movie and not communicating with each other at all, the dialogue was EXTREMELY cheesy. "My name is Rey... Rey Skywalker" "I am all the Sith! And I am all the JEDI" are just a couple examples of moments that tried too hard and in the end coming off as cheesy. There were moments of shock... but then shortly after it was all undone, for example Chewbacca and Kylo Ren's death.

The movie catches you right away by showing the iconic Emperor Palpatine and an action filled chase scene, tricking you into thinking you are about to watch an entertaining movie. The gang in the movie (Chewbacca, Rey, Finn, Poe Dameron and C3PO) go from location to location searching for a map to Exegol (the planet where Emperor Palpatine has been hiding out) seeming more like a video game plot rather than a movie. During the whole journey for the protagonists Finn said he had something to tell Rey, they bring up the fact he needs to tell her this thing several times throughout the movie, yet they never do, which is a little nitpick I have. Once everyone finally gets to Exegol Kylo Ren fights the Knights of Ren (which was one of the few good things about this movie) and Rey fights her grandfather... Emperor Palpatine. This fight had several cheesy moments and the same characters dying over and over again. It was chaotic and rediculous. During the climax of the movie I was feeling several parallels to "Avengers: Endgame" but unfortunately not played out as well (ex. all these people coming to help resistance similar to falcon saying "on you left" and the rest of the Avengers come and Emperor Palpatine saying "I am the Sith" and Rey saying "I am the Jedi" similar to Thanos and Iron Man's I am inevitable/I am Iron Man.

The movie was boring, cheesy with horrible writing. Worst of the new trilogy, although the special effects and fan service sere quite well done. You can tell they tried too hard to save Star Wars, it was basically screaming to be liked. But at least there is still "The Mandalorian".

title: There has never been a sequel that disrespects & retcons the previous movies at this level
review:
This is not a review but a sincere statement. If you really, REALLY don't care about logic & coherent storytelling, you may have fun with this movie. But before giving it a rating, think about these and realize we deserve a better film:

*How did Palpatine survive being thrown by Vader to a freaking abyss and subsequently the explosion of the death star ? Forget about that, how did the throne room even survive the fall from SPACE? Also, wasn't Anakin the chosen one who brought balance to the force at the end of ROTJ? I guess not.

*How did Poe perform the lightspeed trick at the beginning of the movie? Just like "Holdo's maneuver", it completely breaks canon and makes every escape scene from previous movies stupid for not attempting this.

*The sith dagger makes NO SENSE at all. Who built it? How did they know what was in those death star remains ? How does Rey know where to EXACTLY stand for it to function properly?

*After 3 movies, not only do we ignore how the First Order came to be, but all of the sudden you also must buy Palpatine's fleet of endless battleships and the Final Order? None of that with any proper explanation. It's just there because they need a threat.

*What the hell is FORCE HEALING? How come Rey & Kylo are suddenly able to perform such a miracle? Force Skyping wasn't enough to completely break suspension of disbelief ?

*Why would Palpatine keep going for force lighting when Rey started her counterattack?

This movie not only has awkward, frantic pacing and an incoherent story with increasingly unbelievable mcguffins & random uses of the force, it even retcons TLJ (as much as I'd like to see that as a good thing, it isn't):

*Old Leia is suddenly a Jedi. Her scenes are also hard to watch because you can tell they've been heavily retooled. *Force Ghost Luke suddenly does not want lightsabers being disrespected. He can also lift up his old X-Wing that somehow functions after decades of being sunk in the water. *Rose Tico is no longer a relevant character. Every development she had with Finn? Meaningless. *Rey's parents are the OPPOSITE of nobodies now. You also need to be a part of a legendary blood lineage to be a Jedi, so I guess broom kid at the end of TLJ is out of luck.

I could go on and on, but I suspect that you don't enjoy reading too much if you love this movie and no amount of reasonable questions is going to convince you of the contrary. Ep IX is a perfect closure for the Disney sequel trilogy...but not in the way they intended to.

This film, however, lets that all down.

The moaners and haters that have been absolutely infuriatingly relentless since the Last Jedi came out seem to have got their way with this film. There is absolutely lashings of 'fan' service throughout this film, lots of references, callbacks and, excuse the pun, forced nostalgia.

That, coupled with an incredibly rushed storyline that smacks off JJ Abrahams trying to tell some version of the story he wanted to tell. The story itself is weak, the first act in particular is an absolute mess, flashing through scenes at lightening pace all with really hokey dialogue (a tribute to George Lucas?) and humour that never once lands.

In terms of ranking, this film ranks firmly near the bottom for me, only being beaten in infuriating crapness by the trauma that was watching attack of the clones .

I guess what this film does prove is that if you stomp your feet loud enough, Disney will take notice. Naive though, as I'm sure they will now realise that the same group who were calling for a lot of this will end up hating this too.

title: Disjointed Skywalker never quite rises
review:
For those who didn't like Rian Johnson's deconstructionist's approach w/The Last Jedi, good news. Rise of Skywalker does not continue that tack. For those who were hoping that JJ Abrams would be able to take the disjointed and seemingly rudderless story so far and bring it all together, bad news. He doesn't. Not even close.

Rise of Skywalker had a rather impossible task, so it's hard to fault it for not sticking the landing on a story that never took flight in the first place. Instead I blame Disney, who failed to learn the lessons of its success w/its Marvel Cinematic Universe and plan and craft this saga in advance.

Abrams was blamed or credited, depending on who you listen to, for basically cutting and pasting from the original trilogy w/his Force Awakens, relying on nostalgia and fan service to smooth over the cracks. There's some of that here as well, and no surprise the very best moments of Rise of Skywalker involve callbacks, characters and cues from the first trilogy. As for the new stuff...

Little here makes any sense. It starts off w/all the focus of a fly at a picnic and its attempts to take the elements and loose ends its given and tie them up are less than satisfying. It does feature some striking visuals, but set pieces mean little if you're not given a reason to care about the outcome, and here I just didn't.

It does get better in its third act, but it's far too little and far too late to save the film or the trilogy as a whole.

title: Lackluster Ending Relying Too Much On Nostaglia
review:
Star Wars is a franchise that has fallen from greatness once Disney bought the rights to it. From releasing one film every year, resulting in people getting what is called Star Wars fatigue, to making decisions that have caused a lot of diehard Star War fans to rage on the internet, it seemed Star Wars will never be good again, especially after The Last Jedi proved to be a bad film. With The Rise Of Skywalker, this would not only end what is known as the sequel trilogy, but also the Skywalker Saga as well. And sadly, it fails to be anything exciting.

Basically, The Rise Of Skywalker is basically full of plot twists and relies way too much on nostalgia. One of those plot twists: Emperor Palpatine (a.k.a. Darth Sidious) is alive, having survived his death in the second Death Star by "unnatural" means granted by the dark side. Yeah, typical Disney changing the rules of how the Force works (with Darth Vader, Revenge Of The Sith explained he had cybernetic enhancements put in him along with the armor, which was his life support, to keep him alive after the fight with Obi-Wan put him near death, hence why Return of The Jedi had the Jedi Master call him "more machine than man", but Palpatine? No, all we get is a lecture on the many powers the dark side has to offer to justify how he survived being thrown into the reactor of the second Death Star, which, along with the space station's destruction, would surely kill him off).

The film's story is good, but sadly, plot twists weigh it down a lot (including the infamous one with Rey I won't mention). Also, the film relies way too much on nostalgia to try and make up for The Last Jedi (like bringing back past actors who played jedi in the films before this, and even bring James Earl Jones back to voice Darth Vader in one scene). However, it has some great action scenes, and the ending is a nice way to end the Skywalker saga. I hope it also ends Star Wars, as any more movies may not be great.

Ok so being thrown in the reactor of the death star and with the death star explosion was not enough to kill Palpatine for good, but his own lightning was? This is laughable. Now I can say that with all the flaws in the EU, it was a lot better than the stupid trilogy we've got.
