title: Well, what did you expect?
review:
If you like space mumbo jumbo and lasers and spaceships, this movie is excellent. If you think Star Wars was a mythology of quality and a story far more than just "space magic", then this whole trilogy raises the middle finger to your face.

And seriously, this movie is fine, compared to the beginning of the senseless downfall of Star Wars, that was "The Force Awakens". I never understood the people that loved TFA and hated "The Last Jedi". TFA is a complete trash, storywise, with great visuals. NO character in that movie made any sense. And that movie was the foundation for the rest. The Last Jedi was a nice space movie, that you may think that has destroyed the character of Luke Skywalker. No, the character of Luke Skywalker was destroyed when he was lost on an island and that was mentioned on the starting titles of TFA. TLJ had to provide an explanation to this complete nonsense and it did... Everything that Star Wars was, is destroyed in TFA. If you are fine with that, then all of these three sequels are fine.

Now on point: The return of Palpatine was known from the trailer. Unless this movie refers to 6-year old kids only, there couldn't be any good reason behind his survival. So the concept sucked anyway and you should be prepared. However, the movie manages to raise the middle finger to our face by providing no story at all behind his survival. No, there is an explanation: He used the Force. The Dark Side mainly. Suck it!

So, he survived. And then hides for 30 years on life support, in the unknown regions (that are apparently 30' drive from everywhere using hyperdrives...), where he created Snoke and he also created the final order and a whole new fleet with millions of people and millions of CGI hooligans that yelled in an arena. How? He used the Force. Why? Because he is evil. With what resources? He used the Force.

Then he sends a twit to the galaxy that he is alive. So Kylo Ren wants to kill him so that he will be the undeniable Supreme Leader (of what?) and he gets there and Palpatine tells him to kill Rey and he will give him a fleet that rises at that very moment from the ice (via the use of the Force of course).

Then the rebels or resistance or whatever find out that Palpatine is alive and they are scared (all 50 of them). Rey remembers that Luke was searching for something similar before he went on retirement, checks the notes a little bit and our heroes go for an Indiana Jones style adventure, which is not bad, but is pointless. However, it's fun and has a lot of action.

At some point Ray uses the Force casually, to stop a flying ship and Kylo Ren appears on a walking distance to Rey (after a TIE fighter crash that he survives using the Force) to stop that ship on the opposite direction, then Rey gets nervous and uses force lightning, but she uses the one that makes ships explode instantly. So the ship explodes, then Rey and the guys are in another ship in space and they are fine. At this point obviously Kylo Ren was not in the mood of using the force to stop the ship the guys where escaping with....

Then they are on another planet to continue the adventure of searching the way finder to Palpatine's secret Sith Planet. At this point Rey and Kylo have a lightsaber fight through the Force network that they share and Kylo reveals to Rey that she is the granddaughter of Palpatine. OK, this is not a bad explanation to this stupidly overpowered character that Rey is.

Then they move to the Death Star wreckages. Apparently, there is an "ancient" dagger that points to a location that occurred 30 years ago by random wreckages of the fully exploded death star... which landed intact in a nearby planet (with atmosphere obviously) with automatic doors working fine etc... And the nonsense goes on and on but, whatever, the Force was used. Rey sails, easily. through tidal waves to get to the Death Star wreckages. She is probably using the Force. I do not understand why she doesn't just fly to it... She fights with Dark Rey for 10 seconds, with no emotional impact and then she finds the way finder easily. Kylo Ren appears too and they have lightsaber fight again, where Leia intervenes Kylo gets emotional drops his lightsaber and Rey kills him in cold blood. But it's OK because she uses Force heal and Kylo is back without a scratch. And he is a good guy now. Actually, this scene is nice. The death of Leia serves her son and they handled the unfortunate death of the late Carrie Fisher well. Also Kylo Ren is the only character that makes sense and Adam Driver is a great actor. The memory appearance of Han Solo and Ford's performance works also very well. This is scene is nice from every aspect. As are other scenes as well, but they are not enough to save the general mess...

Oh yes, the new Star Destroyers have Death Star canons on them so they can now destroy planets. Because they use the Force. So, one of these Star Destroyers destroys a planet and two or three people care about it on screen for a few seconds...

Rey is disappointed and she would like to retire just like her former master Luke, who appears as a force ghost gives her a small pep talk and the lightsaber of Leia (for some reason...) and then he lifts his X-Wing from the sea, where it was sunk for several years. Of course the ship is working just fine because it uses the Force...

And then the chaos starts... the rebels fly to the Secret Sith planet (Rey shares the location). Lando and Chewie take the Falcon and fly through other systems to gather more people for help. These guys are good, because in 30 minutes they fly through several planets and they appear at the last moment with thousands of ships out of nowhere. And here is one of the moments Disney or JJ or whoever made this decision should be ashamed of. They ripped off the ending of the most successful movie of the same year!!!! e.g. Avengers: Endgame. As Captain America looses hope and Falcon speaks on the Radio and everybody appears through Dr. Strange's magic bubbles, Poe Dameron looses hope and Lando speaks on the Radio and thousands of ships appear to save the day (no magic bubbles in that case).....

At parallel Rey gets to Palpatine. Palpatine says that he wants her to kill him so that his soul will be transferred to her or something... Kylo appears as well, he kills the Knights of Ren (yeah they are in this movie doing nothing again...) and they are both in front of Palpatine, who decides to suck their life and kill them both instead. It seems that he was planning everything very carefully for the last 30 years..... While sucking their life he understands that they are a force dyad, which is a good thing for some reason.... So he continues sucking their lifes, but with more confidence this time and he gets younger and healthy and with a new outfit???? And he is now good old Emperor who enjoys dropping Lightning and punchlines. Kylo is almost alive so he drops him violently through a random hole that is there, which of course is not a problem if you use the Force. Then he shoots lightning for some minutes to every ship of the rebellion. This time the lightning doesn't destroy the ships, it just affects the electronics a little bit.... Then Rey wakes up, he shoots lightning at her, stops it with a lightsaber, but wait... she has two lightsabers. So blocking lightning with two lightsabers is much better because the Emperor dies in a few seconds and he does not possess the body of Rey because the CGI crowd of the arena didn't say the magic words apparently??? Here is also the second and even most shameful moment of "I am all the Sith" as we say "I am inevitable" and "and I am all the Jedi" as we say "and I am IronMan" and with the same spelling....

In short Palpatine is a mummy for 30 years so that he can be revived and die again in a period of 5 minutes. Then Rey is exhausted and dies, Kylo Ren comes out of the pit (of course) uses force heal to heal her, they make out and he dies. Ok that's normal. And this is probably what the title Rise of Skywalker refers to, because you cannot find any meaning to it anywhere else in the movie.

Then Rey goes to Luke's house at Tatooine, buries the lightsabers of Luke and Leia, like there is any meaning to it and then ignites her own lightsaber, so that we can see it...... Then an old lady drops by and she asks her who she is and she answers Rey Skywalker and for some reason this is OK.

I understand this text was too long. I find it hard to read myself. I'm sorry about that but it is my first review. In conclusion:
  • There is almost no meaning to these characters, their actions and everything that is taking place in these movies
  • Everything Star Wars was about is cancelled by the "events" of these movies
  • The glorious feeling of the Force is reduced to magic tricks that anyone can perform with no effort.
  • Science fiction is just fiction in space. Don't get me wrong in that, of course you will see unrealistic stuff in a sci-fi movie. However, the things that we already know from science cannot be altered for the sake of sci-fi. So a planet cannot suck nearby sons and move in space, without gravity and natural phenomena on the planet alternating crazily killing all life on it. Unless, you provide a reasonable explanation for that. A guy that exploded inside a reactor after falling for 100eds of meters and then the whole station that contained this reactor exploded as well cannot survive.
If you are fine with the arguments above then this movie is fine. All of these three movies are fine. You could not get anything better on the foundations set by TFA. The action is good, the visual effects, CGI or not are awesome, space magic and laser swords and huge spaceships are there. So everything is perfect. But if you belong to the people inspired by the Star Wars mythos you can disregard the new trilogy completely. It offers nothing than insult to the characters created by George Lucas and new characters that do not make sense at all.

title: Time To Correct All With The Negative Opinions
review:
First off, I need to say I was there from the beginning. I watched the original Star Wars before it was Episode IV, A New Hope. As with all episodes I was able to watch them on opening night. This one however, I watched a couple of weeks after the release.

Being curious, I read many reviews which trashed this movie. I don't know what problem people have with this movie. The things they are saying are just not true. I saw a review which stated they yawned their way through the movie. The only way I can see someone yawning through this movie is if they are tired. In that case why are they going out watching a 2.5 hour long movie in a darkened theater.

This movie is visually stunning, it has phenomenal light saber fights, it has quite a few twists and turns, and the story closes off the epic Star Wars story very appropriately. I asked my Son (11 years old) after viewing it with him, which was his favorite Star Wars movie. He could not pick a favorite but could only state what he thought were the best parts. He has always been partial to Ep 3 since he was most affected by Anakin turning, but he also likes other parts just as much to include those viewed in this movie. It is his age group which viewed the prequel trio first.

With a good marketing scheme any product can be hyped up. This is done by someone putting money into an ad campaign which supports a product. This is often dome just to make a profit on a particular product (pet rock, mood ring, etc). When these products die out no one remembers them. I feel the negative response to this episode is creating a marketing cloud around this movie. It is either done because some people want their name known or they are not treating the episodes as chapters in a book.

The Skywalker saga of Star Wars is a story. Just like ;picking up a book it is normal to not like a chapter, or not like parts in the story, because the hero is killed, or a lovable character is killed off. These types of story turns affect our emotions. We have negative or positive emotions. So, each viewing of this movie has various emotional responses.

I for one, had many emotional ups and downs during this movie. I care for the characters, whether created by George Lucas himself or the Disney owned George Lucas LTD.

Those who say this story makes no sense, or who say it's terrible are are either making things up for whatever devious purpose or they are failing to take into consideration, this chapter is a chapter from a much larger story. I also believe just like an marketing scheme people's expectations are unjust for this chapter. You have to watch it as part of the full story with no expectations. Just know it is sci-fi and is created to take you on a journey. For the Skywalker saga this is the end of the journey.

The cast, crew, writers, and Disney imaginers, deserve much better credit than they are currently getting. Go see it and judge it for yourself.

title: The future of Star Wars is on TV
review:
I have been reading the user reviews for the past week. I do not have much additional to say that has not already been said but felt compelled to create a imdb account and write my comments as a life long fan that grew up with the original movies. I have to say that I have been disappointed with the direction that Disney has taken the Episode VII, VIII and IX. Overall, Episode IX had rushed storytelling and had scenes written in to appease the fans. It was filled with plotholes, which I would like to predict that Disney will fill in with novels, comics and other media. I am sure that this was done to earn more revenue. I encourage others to only see this movie once in the theater and not let them get your repeat ticket business.

Episode IX is definitely the biggest disappointment with the writing on the wall with bad direction since VII with J.J. as director. All of George Lucas movies are better than these last 3 Episodes. I really wanted to see a good reunion between Luke, Leia, Han, Chewy, Lando, and it has been all spoiled by J.J and Disney. I feel that it was stolen from me. I find the latest episodes almost repetitive of storytelling and rehashing of scenes from the original series. I am not very excited on seeing the next set of movies that will come out next.

With this said, I am more excited by Disney in creating a pipeline of "made-for-TV" (streaming) movies and series. Of course, I will see all they publish on TV and in the movies but would like to see Disney use similar formats as what was done with Star Trek (all shows), The Expanse, Babylon 5, ("Enter your favorite Sci Fi TV show here!!") and expand on the Star Wars universe in TV episode/series format. I predict that this will be the start of the golden time of Sci-Fi TV in the next 5 - 10 years.

title: Weak entry, but not the worst.
review: This movie contains many cliche and unoriginal elements that feel exhausting along with somehow allowing the movie to feel silly and cartoony even for a fantasy movie. The chemistry between Daisy Ridley and Adam Driver carries the movie and is by far the high point. The finale doesn't seem as climactic as it seems rushed.

title: All the Plot Holes, Narrative Gaps, McGuffins, and Moments in ROS!
review:
The Knights of Ren didn't matter. They were on vacation in TLJ.

Rey's vision when she touched the lightsaber in TFA didn't matter.

Palpatine being thrown down a shaft inside the Death Star didn't matter.

Rose's character didn't matter at all. Jar Jar was more important than Rose.

Snoke didn't matter. No, Palpatine was not part of the plan for this trilogy.

Why would Palpatine reveal himself across the whole universe in the opening crawl? This is supposed to be one of the most intelligent Sith lords of all time.

There being a map to Luke Skywalker didn't matter because he wanted to be left alone. He told Rey in TLJ that he came to the island to die.

If Luke trained Leia long ago, what was the point of finding Luke in TFA? It doesn't work. Episode VII should have started off at Luke Skywalker's Jedi academy, training Ben Solo. We all could have gotten to see Luke's character regression in present time by the time the film ended. Then, dark side insurrections could appear in Episode VIII.

Why would R2-D2 wake up for Rey in TFA if she's a Palpatine? It makes no sense.

Lucasfilm confirmed a few days ago that Anakin was not created by Palpatine.

The Empire being defeated in the original trilogy didn't matter.

Rey finding out that her parents were nobodies in TLJ didn't matter.

Every single flirtatious line Finn used towards Rey in TFA didn't matter.

What Finn needed to tell Rey in ROS didn't matter. Why edit it out?

Finn's character arc in this entire trilogy was apparently completed in TFA...

Why can't the super star destroyers activate their shields in-atmosphere?

And, why can't they manage to raise themselves into the air? Riding horses was dumb.

Captain Phasma didn't matter. Both Jango Fett and Boba Fett were far more important to the Clone Wars era, subplots of Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi, and the Star Wars saga in general.

The Lando-Jannah scene at the end of the film didn't matter. It looked like a deleted scene.

Using hyperspace as a weapon didn't matter anymore. Low chance of it working again? BS!

One thousand Death Stars via super star destroyers sounds like awful fan fiction.

Viewers should have known in past movies that Rey is the granddaughter of Palpatine.

Is Rey really the biological granddaughter of Palpatine? Were those her foster parents?

Luke and Leia knowing about Rey's lineage the whole time was stupid. Luke didn't know anything about Rey when he first met her.

In The Last Jedi's artwork, it is explained that Luke destroyed his X-Wing after landing. Luke had no plans of ever leaving Ahch-To, so that's why. How was it operational? Disney's Lucasfilm's own lore contradicts itself.

Where did the huge Rebel fleet come from? It looks dumb after watching TLJ. The Resistance sent out distress calls to everyone. Why couldn't Lando help them? Did he just abandon his friends in the first two films? This is not good.

Anakin's redemption in Return of the Jedi is now undermined and anti-climactic.

The Jedi dying in the prequels is undermined because of the concept of force healing. Yoda and Mace Windu could have healed Jedi during the arena battle in Attack of the Clones. Obi-Wan could have healed Qui-Gon after Darth Maul beat him in The Phantom Menace.

Force healing was decanonized because it was part of Legends, which is not canon. It's quite desperate to take something from non-canon in order to explain away the events from TLJ.

Luke died a soulless, angry coward. They can clone Palpatine and Snoke, but not Luke or Darth Plagueis? Snoke being a reincarnation of Darth Plagueis would have been a more creative film.

Leia flying through space looks even worse. Why didn't we see her powers in TFA or TLJ? Except for Master Plo Koon, who wears a mask, Jedi can't survive the vacuum of space. General Grievous is also clearly not a human.

Why couldn't Leia fight in the battle at Starkiller Base if she was already force trained?

TIE fighters can't use light-speed because they have no hyperdrives. This is lore breaking.

How did Ben Solo get off the planet after Rey stole his TIE Whisper?

The ex-stormtroopers had vehicles of their own already occupied on that planet. Force ghosts can't physically touch animate or inanimate objects, such as lightsabers.

Force ghosts can't magically cast down lightning from the sky. Trust me, if it was that simple, why didn't Yoda cast down lightning on the Emperor's shuttle in the original trilogy? Why didn't all the Jedi force ghosts get together and bring down Palpatine during the Clone Wars? They shouldn't be able to impede like this in the real world. They have knowledge of the force, but they are still dead...

Han Solo can't be a force ghost; he's not force sensitive. This is basic Star Wars lore. He has a blue outline just like Luke Skywalker. He can't just be a memory. Different websites confirm that he is supposed to be a force ghost.

Viewers never received a logical explanation for how Maz acquired Luke's lightsaber.

The main characters not knowing about stormtroopers using jetpacks was stupid.

Using Jedi mind-tricks is so inconsistent. Why didn't Rey and Ben use it in TLJ?

Rey's survival at the end was not earned or warranted. She never suffered or lost a fight in this trilogy. Rey performed a Jedi mind-trick in the same day she found out the force was real, and she resisted mind infiltration from a trained force user at Starkiller Base in TFA.

What happened to the First Order? They defeated the Final Order, but not the First. The First Order controlled planets all throughout the galaxy. The chases make it worse. This is why Return of the Jedi gets a pass.

Why did multiple characters need to know Rey's last name in this film? It's not genuine. All we needed was a ten second scene of her writing her name on a ticket prior to boarding a transport to Naboo at the end of ROS. Perhaps, she wanted to learn more about Luke's heritage? That would have been less cringe.

If Jedi can use the force as a travel map, why couldn't Rey find the Death Star wreckage without the dagger?

Who made the Death Star finder Sith Sword? Why would that come into existence? It obviously didn't exist prior to the second Death Star getting destroyed.

Ben Solo was more relatable and likable than Rey in this entire trilogy, and he's a mass murderer. It's awful!

How would the rebels know about there being a spy in the First Order?

General Hux was a wasted character. There was no point of him being in this film. General Hux watched billions of people die on three different planets in TFA. This was a dumb move. If the motive is unbelievable, it makes it look inauthentic.

If Palpatine controlled Snoke, why would he try to kill his own daughter in TLJ?

How did Babu Frik and Zorii Bliss survive after Kijimi was destroyed? How did they get past the First Order to escape the planet? Nothing was shown. All they needed was a two-minute scene of escaping the planet before its destruction.

If Palpatine was hurting himself with his force lightning, why wouldn't he just stop? That seems so out of character for a Sith lord as intelligent as Palpatine. He didn't stop using his force lightning in Revenge of the Sith because he wanted to make it look like the Jedi Council was betraying him, in the presence of Anakin Skywalker.

If Kylo died from force healing Rey, why didn't Rey die when she force healed Kylo? How could they have learned this power? The events of TLJ takes place a few days after TFA. There is no timeline available to show how many years passed between TLJ and Rise of Skywalker, but it can't be anymore than two years.

This is what's aggravating the most: why did this sequel trilogy have to be Empire vs. Rebels 2.0 with Death Star III and Death Star MCX? Can they come up with anything besides lasers blowing up planets? This is why I will always cherish the prequel films by George Lucas. I am so tired of seeing planet destroyers in SW. The Star Wars universe has shrunk because of these sequel films. Episodes VII through IX could get retconned, and it wouldn't change a thing.

In conclusion, "I am all the Sith" and "I am all the Jedi" was obviously a copy and paste of Endgame. This trilogy is filled with bathos. It might work in Marvel movies, such as funny moments with Thor, Hulk, and Captain America, but it doesn't work in Star Wars movies, especially "your mama" dialogue. Marvel spent years planning ahead for their grand finale Avengers, Avengers: Age of Ultron, Avengers: Infinity War, and Avengers: Endgame films. All Disney's directors had to do was read more of the Star Wars books and play some of the video games. Jokes can write themselves when the writers are not always trying to be funny. Tone is important. How do these writers want their viewers to feel in a specific scene?

Re-watch the first Ghostbusters film. Sometimes, more intelligent jokes age better than more childish ones. Anakin accidentally breaking his lightsaber in Attack of the Clones at the droid factory on Geonosis was funny. Yoda using force push on Palpatine, causing him to get launched back into his chair in Revenge of the Sith, was a comical moment. R2-D2 burning the battle droids was a funny scene, even if it wasn't needed. Han Solo saying, "Who's scruffy looking" in Empire Strikes Back was good. C-3PO saying, "Sir, the possibility of successfully navigating an asteroid field is approximately 3,720 to 1" and Solo replying "Never tell me the odds" works in this saga. It's not as cringeworthy. Twenty years from now, these moments from the prequels and original films will still be funny. J.J. Abrams and Rian Johnson have no business directing Star Wars movies. I can't say they understand the basic fundamentals of the lore, either. The sequel trilogy has added nothing new and memorable to the Skywalker saga. Let's put the main titles to bed.

title: Uninspired end to a great movie saga
review:
A lot of people will see this movie. Some people will really enjoy it, when there's big explosions and characters running from scene to scene, from world to world, with barely a chance to catch breath. There are many jokes that somewhat lighten the mood. There's lightsaber battles. And who doesn't love seeing the old favourites back on the screen?

To an extent Star Wars is about action and effects, big space battles and lightsaber fights. But it is also about characters, about tension, about exploring an exotic, but believable universe shrouded in ancient mythology, of character development and redemption. Cutting edge effects are a given for any new Star Wars movie. What makes a great movie is everything else.

I feel somewhat for the producers who had a very difficult task, to come up with something fresh that continues and concludes the most famous story arc in cinema history. Undoubtedly some people were going to be disappointed whatever they did. However, I feel they copped out by basically recycling the characters and story from the original, and to add "a twist" just killed off a character (or not...they're still alive!), or just upping the stakes (let's just keep miniaturizing the death star and make more of them!) Easy way to solve the problem, but also lazy. The acting and pacing in this movie is better than the prequels, which were much maligned. However, despite the flaws they felt like works of imagination, of a story that needs to be told. I can't say the same of the new trilogy. Pretty much everything in this new movie is forgettable or unbelievable. The droid designs are the only cool thing. Even the special effects aren't all that great. There are few nostalgic, tear jerking moments, but these are almost inevitable given the stakes.

On the issue of diversity, I think they did the right thing by having a female lead and having a cast of different backgrounds. It is the future after all. But the cast lacks chemistry and due to the non-stop action we never get a chance to see them develop. Finn is relegated to bit part player and seems criminally underused, as is the other engineer, Chewbacca grunts a bit, and Rey wins of course. The jokes are jarring at first and rapidly become annoying - an easy way to get a laugh at the expense of tension.

In any case, Disney are on to a winner. They know people will see it just to have an opinion on it, because its Star Wars, and to pay homage to the cast of old while they are still around. But make no mistake, this is dangerously formulaic and uninspired, and eventually the whole franchise risks becoming obsolete as die hard fans find no substance between the set pieces and rehashed story lines.

As movies go this is okay, but doesn't feel inspired or magical, and that seems a shame given what it might have been. By playing it safe under the guise of "introducing a new audience", whilst diminishing much of the significance of the original trilogy, they have left many fans feeling dissatisfied and concerned about the direction of the franchise, of whether to keep investing in new movies, and whether they really care anymore. And I can honestly say I'm not sure.

title: This movie doesn't make any sense
review:
Ok look, I love Star Wars. I've loved Star Wars since my parents showed me the first one when I was 3. But what was this movie in all honesty?

I'm 16. So no I'm not old. I enjoyed the first 2 new movies, characters, ect. even with all the plot holes and things that didn't make sense. But I can't look past this movie.

Today is my birthday and I really wanted to see this movie, so my and I family went and saw it. And I can't tell you how disappointed I am.

What is this movie? Really? Like really? Yes I'll give Disney and the Star Wars crew credit. They've got some amazing actors, some great special effects, and some awesome music. But what was this?

NOTHING MADE SENSE!

Their are so many loose strings and plot holes and things that could have been easily fixed or things that were so ridicules you think they would have been taken out. It was almost like the Disney team decided, "let's just add this and this and this into the last movie."

Their was way to much going on in this movie. While I will give props to the Disney team, their were to many special effects and different plot lines going on at a time. It was to much for me to comprehend and I just couldn't understand and focus on 1 different thing.

The plot with palpatine is so STUPID. WHAT? While yes I didn't except Rey to be his granddaughter it was like the Disney team ran out of ideas. "Oh let's bring back a loved villain for no other reason than to screw with the plot and add an awful and terrible plot twist!" It didn't make sense.

It was like the whole saga didn't exist anymore because of this twist and I found myself rolling my eyes and laughing at the utter stupidity of Rey's heritage.

I also thought it was so stupid that she was palpatines grandaughter. We have no idea who her parents are (but I'm sure Disney will make another damn spin off) and leading up to this movie I was anticipating Rey being Skywalker blood. But this didn't make sense to me. We didn't get to learn about her parents and we really still don't know much about Rey's heritage. The plot twist just wasn't good and the fact that palpatine is back was so confusing.

The movie was also way to predictable. I felt like I knew what was going to happen every second of the movie (except for the utter most stupid plot twist we got) and it didn't feel very fun to know what was going to happen every second of this movie.

And the fact that Rey and Ben kissed just set me off. They have hated each other (wanted to; and almost killed each other) for the past 2 and 3/4 movies. Sure, Rey healed Ben (which I'll talk about in a second) and Ben stepped down from the First Order + they helped each other with palpatine, But wtf? Their wasn't any relationship building and definitely not enough for them to kiss.

This movie also just threw in a bunch of different, random characters and added many plot lines to characters that were irrelevant to the story and things to characters that didn't make sense. I thought Poe worked for the Rebel side and now your telling me he was working at one point for the dark side. Ok whatever you say. It felt irrelevant. Why did they add this in?

It felt to much like a fantasy movie. Not like a sci-fi, and definitely not like Star Wars. Their were to many spirts and things going on.

AND, APPARENTLY JEDI CAN NOW JUST HEAL PEOPLE AND CONTROL LIGHTNING TO ENHANCE AND MOVE THE PLOT OF THE STORY? Wtf? Why? This was never mentioned before but suddenly now they can do this? IT DOESN'T MAKE SENSE!

+ Rey and Finn don't end up together which we were anticipating FOR 3 MOVIES AND 5 YEARS.

The movie title doesn't make any sense! 'Rise of Skywalker' ok sure, at the end of the movie Rey calls herself Rey Skywalker. But why 'Rise of Skywalker'? It really has nothing to do with the movie or the loose ended plot.

This movie also TRIED to be dark, but added forced humor in, and it DIDN'T WORK! I didn't feel scared or like anything was at stake. I just felt like I wanted to know what the hell was going on, and why the movie was still running.

In conclusion, this movie felt so rushed yet it dragged on for SOOOO long. 2 and a half hours of my life I won't get back. We sit through a bunch of bull on a quest with Rey and her 'trusty sidekicks', watch expectedly as Ben turns good, see Rey fight between good and evil (likes she's done for the past 3 MOVIES), listen to nonsense, and watch as our 'favorite villain' palpatine comes back for no reason other than to make the plot seem good.

Their are to many plot holes and loose ends and IT DOESN'T MAKE SENSE.

I've waited years, IM TELLING YOU, YEARS, for this conclusion...and we get THIS. Wow ok.

title: If Endgame is a fine paella, this is a mediocre rice porridge
review:
If Endgame is a fine paella, with all fascinating ingredients cooked to storytelling perfection, delicately mixed into one grand, emotional one-last-ride narrative, and even decorated with some absolutely mesmerizing moments that would let all of us beg for more...
Then this, the Rise of Skywalker, is a (very) mediocre rice porridge, where all the ingredients are incomplete and half-cooked. The entire story telling is muddied up in the endless nostalgic showing-off and ended up disconnected and incoherent. Watching this film reminds me of an over-zealous novice chef serving a set menu that he was deeply proud of: he would always send an too ambitious dish out and stand right next to me; before I could finish one plate, he would toss me another dish and rush me to go through the entire night, even, at the end of the night, blindly adding some unpleasant and unbalanced extra spices that he considered as surprises.
"No, chef, they really weren't pleasant surprises." Same words to J. J. Abrams.
I did cry. I cried hard. But I cried for my memories of Star Wars as an important part of my life now officially ended, not for this film itself.
This film also proved to us as another example, following GoT, how unimaginably difficult to craft an end chapter for a massive storytelling universe and franchise.

Rise of Skywalker was excellent. Don't let the critics and fans that refuse to let go of the past and embrace the future fool you. The movie was full of tear-jerking nostalgic moments, it broke new ground in the powers of the Force, and was entertaining from start to finish. Yes, it had mistakes and yes it operates outside the rules of the original trilogy, but I don't really know what else people would expect? I think the biggest problem is that so many people were kids when they saw the originals (and for some the prequels) and since then they have lost that kid-like energy within that allowed them to enjoy Star Wars on a different level. Can you imagine how difficult it was to bring in a new generation and introduce new characters into the most successful and beloved movie franchise ever? At the end of the day that's what this trilogy was. It was a trilogy for a new generation of younglings, while still mixing in everything the original fans loved when we were kids and I don't know how much better it could've possibly been.
The sun has set on the Skywalker saga, it's a hard thing to accept, but it was beautiful to watch.

title: The Skywalker saga ends with a fizzle instead of a bang.
review: I'm going to preset this by saying that at least in most capacity, I have enjoyed this new trilogy quite a bit. I wasn't born for the original saga, and was barely old enough to comprehend the prequels before their end. So for all intensive purposes, this is the story and the characters I grew up. So for it to feel and end up like Last-Jedi cruise control sprinkled with a ton of nostalgia for two and a half hours is disheartening to say the least. Palpatine's alive and has been manipulating everything from the start, Snoke's one of his (many ?) clones. Do they explain how he's managed to survive this long? Nope. Luke's all of a sudden just hanging out like his sacrifice meant nothing and calling himself a fool for his TLJ actions. Nice jab at Rian there, JJ. Quite mature. Remember how scary Hux was in The Force Awakens? His epic speech before he unleashed the terror of the Starkiller base? Well, turns out he was a spy. He was just pretending to be an extremely pompous evil space general. Ray's parents were nobodies? Ha, you wish. Everything needs to be connected, she's Palpatine's granddaughter! Every single decision made in this movie, is to either backpedal on everything done in TLJ, or to jerk off the old trilogy fans who stuck around this long only to witness their original trio get dragged to hell and back in the name of character development. Meanwhile we also introduce a multitude of new characters into the fray, and still try to juggle the new-ish and old all at once. Sheesh! Shoutout John Williams and the performers trying to keep this sinking ship together, Adam baby, I'm so sorry. Imagine having one of the best arcs in the entire three trilogies just to die a virgin. Goddamn shame.

title: A great way to end this story. Fixed many issues with TLJ
review:
This was an excellent conclusion to the Skywalker saga. It fixed many issues from the last jedi, such as clarifying who rey's parents were, and how rey was so skilled (she trained hard, it turns out. Which should have been what everyone thought to begin with). I don't have much to add that you can't find from other positive reviews on here, so instead I'll respond to a few of the more insane ones: "Its made to pander to as many demographics as possible. Characters must be 25% white/25% asian/25% black, 50% women, all whites must be evil, etc." Um, I guess if all you were doing was tallying up what race/gender every character was, you probably didn't enjoy it. Since, you know, you weren't paying attention to the story. I have no idea how accurate his count is, because I was busy actually following the characters and the story, but since it doesn't really matter to anyone but angry racists /misogynists, it's pointless to speculate. "Pulled Palpatine out of thin air after he died" Um, he was tossed into a shaft. Sith and jedi have easily survived worse. And what other force user had the power to do the things snoke supposedly did? Many people speculated that snoke *was* Palpatine for that reason. "rey has abilities no one else has ever had! Cheap" Numerous jedi were capable of force healing. Using the force to sheath a lightsaber or halting the beam was something Palpatine had done before. "Rey shouldn't be as good as kylo, he studied longer" Rey has been wielding melee weapons for at least as long as kylo, and was already quite physically fit and fully grown. That drastically reduces the training time needed compared to a little youngling who'd never fought anyone before.

"ren was stronger than rey he should have beaten her easily" Again with that casual sexism. I think we can all agree that a young human woman is naturally stronger than an arthritic old man, and being such didn't stop Palpatine or yoda from using the force to compensate for their physical infirmities.

People may have genuine greivences that lead them to give this movie a 7, 8, or 9, but any rating below that is almost guaranteed to be for some ridiculous reason.

title: One Big Mess
review:
The Rise of Skywalker begins by invalidating the first 6 movies. In the opening crawl the emperor is said to be alive without any explanation as to how he survived episode 6. This completely negates the entire point of Anakin being the chosen one and the sacrifice he made to save his son and bring "balance" to the force. The beginning of the movie was very poorly paced as it hops quickly from planet to planet without allowing the viewer to even enjoy the planet while also trying to set up some semblance of a coherent plot for the rest of the movie. Overall, the whole movie felt very rushed. The plot was very bland and unoriginal as half of it was, "hey we need to find this object, to lead us to this other object ,to find this place". Most of the characters introduced were throwaway characters who were extremely forgettable and were only there as plot devices to move the protagonists to the next point in the movie. The knights of Ren were laughable as all they did was walk around looking cool before getting absolutely demolished.
The humor in the movie was very hit and miss and seemed very forced for the most part.
The visuals were stunning as they have been for all of sequel trilogy movies but the lack of any good story really took away from the awe and wonder of it all. It felt like talking to a pretty girl (or guy) with no personality. Eye candy, but that's it.
The Force in The Rise of Skywalker has become insanely overpowered in comparison with other movies without much explaining except a short training montage from Rey. The movie continually introduces new force powers without much explanation that conveniently allow the heroes to succeed in whatever they are doing.
The worst part of the whole movie for me was that none of the characters actions really had any consequences. Whenever they were in a tough situation or something bad happened the movie reversed the consequences. Any sacrifice or failure a character made had no weight to it as it would be undone 5 minutes later.
The only redeeming quality was the actors performances, Adam Driver does an amazing job as Kylo Ren yet again and Daisy Ridley did a fantastic job of portraying her struggle of finding her identity.
Overall the movie was a jumbled, hurried mess. It was glaringly obvious that there was no overall plan for this trilogy which resulted in this disaster of a story. If you turn off your brain and don't think about logic or good storytelling you might be able to at least enjoy the visuals and the fact that it is a Star Wars movie.

title: Rushed edit/directing, lazy writing
review:
Let me state firstly that I would not call myself a Star Wars fanatic. I purely watch the franchise just to be entertained by the movie as it has been generally since they restarted the franchise with Episode VII and multiple spin offs. Especially after seeing the Mandalorians. I was also one of the rare one who enjoyed The Last Jedi. I honestly didn't give a lot of thoughts about how the story should be written, as long as the story is told well and clever enough to keep me entertained. But despite my low fanaticism towards the franchise, The Rise of Skywalker manage to still fail in so many levels...

As someone pointed out here, the first 5-10 minutes of the movie I was immediately getting a really bad vibe. Its like watching a trailer of another movie where Palpatine is alive and there an odd pyramid looking artifact. Huh?! I stuck it out hoping the rushed feeling of the movie will finally subside after this, but alas it was maintained throughout. There were many scenes where it felt rushed and it jumped around; the scenes & dialogues felt rushed to fit the cut, as if the director doesn't care how to tell it well as long the viewer gets the story. Some of these scenes made me feel like I'm watching the movie at 2x the speed...

Then the amount of plotholes in the movie that just made you do a facepalm after faceplam. I don't mind one or two.. but this many?? Conveniently getting suck by a quicksand that leads to the clue, Rey controlling a starship but not a sand bike, Rey jumping like Neo but struggle to climb some structures, conveniently standing on a spot where the dagger shape fit the landscape, apparently an X wing submerged for years can still fly, easily going through the rough seas they initially suggest to be too dangerous, a Final Order starships capable of each destroying a planet but park themselves somewhere all these years and apparently can be easily shot down by a small fighters... sigh, I could go on and on

Also they decided to throw multiple new characters, who probably don't add much values..... a new useless droid, another ex-stormtrooper, another masked character. None of them play a crucial role enough and hardly any character build being thought of. They just throw them in there.. just because. They carelessly ditched some characters importance completely (Rose, Maz). Plus watching Lando in the movie feels much like having your grandpa sitting in the car with you & your friends, getting excited just because he get to hang out with the younger kids. LOL and yikes.

And what's with the last scene of Rey Skywalker? The orange lightsaber? What did Finn wanted to say to Rey? Kylo and Rey had a thing for each other? Didn't Snoke arranged Kylo & Rey crossovers in The Last Jedi, why is it still happening now? And you can pass things around using Force now? What? How? Why?! WTF!

Anyway, what a way to destroy the final trilogy...... GG

title: So finale for an avid stars fan and I just feel... empty
review:
So Star wars? the film series that got me into films all together. This series is one of my all time favourites and made me the film fanatic I am today. I am the person that will defend this series as much as i can, always a negative comment with a "But it means this which is good", SO how do I feel about the final film of the most iconic film series of my child hood.... well... empty

And that pretty much sums up this film in pure simplicity, empty - no soul with no bravery to show darker decisions and more fascinating conclusions. I could start off here with all the minor mistakes of the film - why did the green lightsaber turn to blue - why did palpatine insist that rey killing him would turn her dark so she ends up killing him anyway in the name of good - why were there so many character introduced in the last film of the saga - why dont the ships of the sith fleet just move to an angle so they can shoot up at the rebels - where did palpatine get all the men to fly these ships - How did Po's ex girlfriend get off the planet before it blew up after she gave Po the captains coin - Why did Po's ex risk so much in the first place - Why didnt Leia finish her jedi training and help Luke stop ben's turn to the dark side - Did lando and the stormtrooper chick just start a weird relationship out of know where - AND WHAT DID FINN WANT TO TELL REY. But if i did that I would be here all night nitpicking and going after every little poor detail of the film.

So lets just go with the major parts - first of all the gutlessness of the film. The film has so many beloved characters that could of had such iconic and meaningful endings. Chewie being killed by rey's darkside which has been hinted at throughout the films. C3PO making the ultimate sacrifice of his memory, which is basically his life to help the ones he loves. So many sincere moments... and how were they treated? They were rushed and overlooked so quickly because literally 3 minutes later "Oh they are alive and well dont worry". This film just showed literally no guts to kill off a major character in the final film of the series to show this amazing emotional scene because (and i can only guess) that it wanted to pander to the audience?

So there is the gutless part spoken about, now, what about the emptiness I feel? I mean you look at the end of this series and what do you see. Po - still afraid to lead, still finds it hard to trust. Kylo ren - still a brat who did a turn to the light side, which was the single most obvious thing that was going to happen since episode 7. Finn - still a ... kind of.. meh nothing character. Rey - still a loner. Where is the progression of the story. Why were the production team so afraid to create a true bromance between Finn and Po. Rather than have rose crash into finn in episode 8 because "she loved him" why couldnt Finn crash into Po, because He loves him, he respects him as this leader, and Po finally sees how people look up to him. And then in this film, it could just add and add to it, where Po trusts him with his life and would do anything for him.. instead they just add romance partners for both of them cos... what. Guys gotta get with girls I guess? And seriously what did rose do in this film....... Then we get to Rey... and I loved this character in 7, I loved 7, it set up such an amazing premise. and even in 8, the star wars saga was setting up for this amazing finale where maybe they will BALANCE the force, like in the prophecy. That yeah Rey is part sith, but her heart is part jedi too, and the combining of the 2 of them allows her to control her emotion and create a new order for balance and peace, not war. This would of created an amazing conflicting and more important thought provoking ending. And then rather than her own who she is, she hides herself and becomes a skywalker thus reinforcing the classic and to be frankly honest boring "Good beats evil" trope.

Then kylo Ren.... we all knew he was gonna turn good at some point, and he became good to.... get his butt thrown in a hole? Like what was the point of this character, just so he could have a creepy romance and then sacrifice himself for Rey so Rey can go be a recluse on tatooine? What was the point of this character this film... he just got in the way for a hour, then got trapped, found this ex machina tie fighter and flew over to get his butt kicked and then die.... I felt no emotion watching him die whatsoever....

So I could go on and on and on about this, but I would bore you, so how about I explain why I gave it 3 star and not the 1 I am hinting at... well first of all the film is beautiful, the scenes so such beauty and throughout the chaos, there are some beautiful scenes, like where rey hands ren the lightsaber (even though we all saw it coming). The entire galaxy showing up to help the rebels was a truly uplifting scene. - Lando felt nice in the film - they didnt disrespect carrie. The film had some nice and beautiful scenes, which were fun to watch.. but overall.. just a rushed movie with no guts and most importantly... no heart.

title: May the profit be with you
review:
I saw the original Star Wars back then in the cinema. I was 10 years old, sat on a wooden chair and was mesmerized. It was a great story about a young man and his friends who battle an evil Empire. A simple plot, but wonderfully made, likeable characters, great performances. Sir Alec Guiness, oh, he was truly great as mentor and father figure for Luke.

And now, more than 40 years later, with a budget to create 4 or 5 Star Wars movies from 1977, the creativity, the magic is gone. Nothing to see, nothing to feel. It's sad, that a young audience has to go through this kind of mess. The new trilogy has nothing special to offer. TFA was a modern "A New Hope", not bad, not good. We all waited for the next episodes to see all the questions answered. But Rian Johnson's TLJ subverted all our expectations. It peed on the legacy of the great character Luke Skywalker, it crapped on the Star Wars lore and I am not sure, but it seems as if Rian Johnson tried to make fun of Star Wars, a "Space Balls" in disguise.

Fast forward two years later and JJ Abrams tried everything in his book to erase TLJ. Really? Is there a fight going on within the Lucas-Disney-Branch? How was this even possible? Maybe Rian Johnson had a darker vision for Star Wars (see the first Trailer, there are no jokes, no humor in it and visually really stunning!) but the Execs got cold feet and inserted all that nonsense and forced humor and merchandising figures.

For me, this question (What was going on behind closed door?) is more interesting than the final showdown of Rey and Palpatine in this fan-fiction appeasement movie "The Rise of Skywalker". Overall, the film is shallow and at best mediocre. For me it was a big disappointment and I wonder how Disney will handle that failure.

title: Went in and expected to hate it and was still SHOCKED
review:
The movie premiered in Sweden wednesday the 18:th. Me and my two friends watched in a VIP theatre where being QUIET is usually the way to go because you payed extra money for a nice experience. PEOPLE LAUGHED AT THE MOVIE, not with it. AT IT.

But let's start with the good stuff. I loved the arguments and banter between Rey, Poe and Finn, they had good chemestry. I liked some of the humor even tho it felt really tacked on at moments. Chewie had som great moments and ONE moment made me gasp (even tho the movie fooled me into emotion) Eh... Some of the action was fun, I liked the first space chase it was really fun... The Sith temple of Palpatine and his followers was done really well, it had a creepy time and was something new for Star Wars.

That's about it, there are alot of smallet moments that I liked but it's hard to remember after just one viewing. But the BAD is just too much. This movie is a MESS, it's obvious that J.J had to continue his ideas from TFA and try to retcon The last Jedi at the same time. FROM THE FIRST SCENE we are introduced to a slew of clunky exposotion, "my boy, I made Snoke!" like okey? How? Why? I trust the movie to give answers once again but no. "You are Rey Palpatine!" Like... It's so bad. My biggest problem is however the constant *WE HAVE A PROBLEM, WE NEED TO FIND A THING, BUT TO FIND THE THING WE NEED ANOTHER THING, AND TO FIND AND USE THAT THING WE NEED TO DE PROGRAM C3-PO SO HE CAN DO A THING, BUT THAT WILL ERASE IS MEMORY,ALRIGHT LETS DO IT, OH NO HE LOST HIS MENORY, BUT OH HERE COMES R2 AND GIVES IT BACK*

There are many such moment where an unnecesary threat comes upp and they introduce a new power or tool to handle it in the same scene.

Also the ending... It's beyond stupid. I wont say too much but Palpatine is BAD in this, like poorly written and poorly used. They made him SUPER powerful to the point of feeling like a fan film, The effects weren't even good which was kinda shocking. And then Rey does the most stupid thing to overcome him and you go "Oh so there was no point of making him powerful" BUT then something happened that actually was pretty good and I was pretty satisfied. And then it was ruined a couple of minutes later (if not seconds)

This is probably one of the bottom Star Wars movies to date. For different reasons than say Phantom Menace. This makes The Last Jedi look good and I'd rather watch that one again. Sorry Star Wars

title: Ruins George lucas Star wars
review:
First of all ive loved star wars since i was 10. Grew up on the original trilogy about the time the special editions were coming out. I really did like the prequels, with "revenge of the sith" possibly being my favorite star wars film overall. One thing in the George Lucas era of star wars was that each film built on what came before it. The prequels expanded the galaxy with new worlds and creatures and environments and gave a great backstory to how the galaxy came to be under the empire in the original trilogy. When disney announced a new trilogy i was hopeful but from the first moment knew they were heading down a dark road. Before i get to the new movie first of all they destroyed everything the rebellion achieved in the originals, along with all the old characters before killing them off one by one in favor off poorly developed new characters. What they done to Luke was unforgivable. However i was going to go see this first chance i got simply because it was star wars and somehow the greatest villian palpatine was making a return.

The film started of good. Great opening scenes, and wasted no time getting into it. Effects were great overall, but why wouldn't they be. There were some complaints about the pacing, but i thought it was fine as there was a lot to cover. The new characters in this trilogy are still totally underdeveloped, but we stick with them. Although it was about half way through you notice more and more its just expensive fan fiction rather then the star wars we all know and love. The emperor was just thrown in there and the story of him been Rey's grandfather was just terrible. Its not once explained how he came back or even hinted at. Worst of all it 100% destroys everything Lucas had in his 6 films. "the chosen one" prophecy ment nothing overall. Anakin's sacrifice now means nothing. Darth sidious the master manipulator doesn't really seem to have any sort of plan. It looked to be thrown together at the last minute as expensive fan service hoping nobody would notice how empty it is. This new trilogy undone everything George Lucas wrote and everything all the other chacacters achieves for a quick cash grab that wasn't thought out at all. It gets a few stars from me cos some scenes were entertaining and can't fault the effects. This is apparently canon now, but for me and i'm sure many fans out there when it comes to the story there is only really 6 star wars movies and some expensive fan fiction. The end of the skywalker saga ended in ep6 return of the jedi.

title: Enjoy this sci-fi popcorn ride (not as a Star Wars main entry)
review:
I like Rise of the Skywalker not as an entry in the trilogy but a popcorn sci-fi film. Yes, it is entertaining. There is so much fan service, so much corny dialogue, but if you could overlook that alongside its contingency errors and rushed pacing, you could actually enjoy this film as a pure Star Wars nerd; I just think people can be too obsessed sometimes and forget how to have fun.

People are taking the chance to lash at Disney for their mismanagement of the franchise (how could you start a trilogy without a roadmap??). I agree, but honestly the disconnect between ep.8 & ep.9 is not the fault of the talented JJ Abrams and Rian Johnson, both of whom were very adept at achieving their singular visions. The films as a stand alone are at the very least good films, and to me it applies to both ep.8 & ep.9 (ep.7 retread is fantastic).

At the end of the day, I feel entertained. I probably like it more than Chris Stuckmann and Jeremy Jahns combined, and trust me, I mean it when I say I am a pretty cynical filmgoer (I stick with the yms rating system). Star Wars are nerdy movies that shouldn't be taken as seriously as a Scorsese picture. ep.4-ep.6 are terrible if we delve into their technical aspects, but since they are fun, they become classics. Double standards do not apply here and I am giving ep.9 a pass because of that.

title: Underwhelming and hectic
review:
I guess this is exactly what you get when you go to see the end of a trilogy that's driven by feminism/diversity agenda instead of you know..an actual story.

Of course there were epic fight sequences and some good jokes, but overall the movie just tries too hard to please everyone. Too much course correction, too much fan service, too much bang but no actual storytelling. Or soul. Originality what?.. Last Jedi was flawed but it had some great fresh ideas - about the force abilities not being tied to a certain family name, about the need to balance the light and the dark within; this just erases it all and essentially ends up retelling the ending of the Return of the Jedi. There's no balance. No real closure. It's just so painfully obvious that there never was a clear plan for this trilogy.

Obviously this movie doesn't deserve the angry 1* ratings that you will see here. The visual effects are stunning. And some of the cast are absolutely fantastic trying to work with what little they are given. It's just that it feels more like a quest-filled video game with too many wookiepedia facts crammed in rather than a worthy ending to this epic saga. The ending just leaves you with a tired "That's it..?"..

[Spoiler-ish?]

This movie figuratively and literally kills the only interesting character of the new trilogy. Repeatedly. For what? Some cheap tear-jerking attempt at the end. Let this sink in Disney - literally everyone at the premiere was laughing at what was supposed to be THE dramatic self-sacrifice moment of the movie.. none of the actual jokes got such a reaction. Just Meh.

title: What did I just watch?
review:
Firstly, all the reviews over 5 are clearly fake (or written by ultra-Star Wars fan people who feel anything attached to the Star Wars franchise must be good). Secondly, most people giving it a 1 are a tiny bit too triggered to be taken seriously - okay, the movie isn't great, but it's not a "Weekend At Bernie's 3" bad. Thirdly, here's my view abbreviated:
  • the script is atrocious. Repetitive, dull, unimaginative. "Whoa, yeah!" was probably said about 400 times.
  • Adam Driver was miscast. Sure, he's a decent actor. But throughout the trilogy he looks like he's constantly about to cry, and that's in between him actually crying (which he does a lot). An emo pretending to be an all-powerful Force wielder.
  • Rey is... Utterly uninteresting. Her character development was atrocious, and this movie doesn't help her cause with the audience. By the end I was hoping she'd be killed off.
  • Too many side characters. I mean, there are hundreds of 'cameos', none of which add value to the story.
  • Lots and lots of big time action sequences - almost none of which made sense. (As an example, a universe filled with Dreadnaughts fall to a few rust buckets - what?)
JJ ruined the Star Trek movie franchise, and now he's done the same to Star Wars. Great work, mate.

I recommend watching this if you need closure. But if you've seen Return of the Jedi, and you're not fully invested in this current trilogy, best take your kids to see Frozen 2.

title: Limping to an irrelevent conclusion
review:
This is one of the worst films of 2019, not in regards to Production (which is as you imagine at a high level) but in regards to the expectation placed against it. A 200 million dollar budget, 40+ years of lore, a talented director and capable studio behind it - and yet this is an utter mess.

It seems a good sign when the best scenes of a film are the first scenes and the last scenes, but these are just bookmarks for a non-sensical film built around another long and unnecessary "chase the MacGuffin" that derails the film for Acts 1 and 2. There is pointless world hopping that removals all character building. The filmmakers settle for the fact that we finally have a number of the original trilogy and new trilogy characters together.

For all the hate The Last Jedi gets - at least it was brave and more importantly, general functional. That film attempts some brave things but throws substance and logic out of the window in a desperate attempt to achieve. This script, desperate to retcon TLJ, is messy and worst of all lazy. The amount of conveniences in this film can easily be counted on 2 hands. It's frequent enough that it seems to be occurring if every scene. When you can't finish a scene without a point of convenience, there is a problem. A final 3rd act tries to turn the wheels around, but it's too little too late. Despite some big action scenes, the stakes are non-existent.

A lot of the praise seems to be the film's satisfying conclusion. I disagree. This film, and more so the trilogy as a whole, adds nothing that that original 6 films didn't already wrap up. Nothing feels expanded on, nor anything feels added. It just exists.

Star Wars has limped to it's conclusion. The Mandalorian and future Star Wars TV and games will keep my general interest but after this, I more than okay with never seeing another Star Wars film again.

title: A sad explotation of what used to be great
review:
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker. A review (I wrote this on my FB page and posted it here likewise.)

No spoilers.

When you read a comic book, there are certain ACCEPTED limitations on the medium. You only have panels to work with, every panel must advance the story, and thus going from panel A to Panel B doesn't necessarily have to make sense in the FLOW OF ACTION as it does in the flow of storytelling.

When you read a book, the author winds you on a tale of details, most of which matter. BUT... some of them don't. That's generally called "Character developement". As in reading Harry Potter and finding out that he likes tuna sandwiches. It has nothing to do with the story --- it has EVERYTHING to do with creating a character.

When you watch a movie --- a GOOD MOVIE --- the action has flow and continuity. A great example of this is the car chase scene in Matrix: Reloaded (Matrix 2). In that incredible 14 minute scene, every detail is in place. You follow the flow of the action and you know where every player is. Everything actually makes sense (in the Matrix world) and there is no part of the scene which requires you to say "How'd they get there? How'd they do that?" There is complete flow and continuity to the scene, and it propels the story forward.

I read a review by Roger Ebert once which praised "Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back" for a single 3 second scene. Ebert said (I miss him, by the way... he was always the sensible reviewer in my opinion) that it was this MINUTE attention to detail which made George Lucas a genius director / story-teller / producer.

Luke drops into the Rancor pit and has to fight for his life with whatever is there. It's a tense fight, as the Rancor is not a beast to take lightly. In the end, Luke defeats the monster and walks away. HERE IS THE SCENE.... you'll miss it if you don't watch closely. The Rancor lays dead under the door, it's head crushed. Up runs the Rancor's keeper ..... crying... because he's obviously grown attached to the beast.

Does it help the story? Does it give "Character developement"? Does it ever come back to play in any future Star Wars movie? The answer is no. George Lucas simply threw it in because it's a TRUE TO LIFE detail. We all love our pets. Lucas did that more than once in his movies, and these little scenes actually serve to make for a great movie experience. They made his movies "REAL". (A kiss for luck...)

Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker has none of that. it's more like a comic book where the action squences make no sense. Where the story is more important than the visuals and you can skip a page or two and not miss anything crucial.

seriously. I honestly fell asleep last night at one point.... and when I woke back up I felt like I missed NOTHING important for the story.

New characters get thrown in.... with no relevance or developement. OLD CHARACTERS come back and feel so tiring and over-worked that you really wonder why they're there (except maybe to elicite that fanboy cheer... which has nothing to do with good story telling). Sadly.... entire new worlds are introduced.... as if they existed in a vacuum and now we're just supposed to accept that 600,000,000 ships can appear overnight.

In the end... you walk away feeling like Disney has stolen a major part of your childhood... took a dump on it... and served it as "Star Wars: New Brown Hotdogs". The movie, in my opinion, was really that awful.

title: A fantastic final chapter to this new trilogy
review: I have seen online this film has been gaining mixed reviews across the board by fans and critics alike but I have seen this film twice now and I have to admit as a huge star wars can this was a fantastic experience to watch in the cinema and a worthy addition to the Star Wars franchise. The premise of the film sees Rey, Finn & Poe on the hunt to track down an ancient evil to save the galaxy while kylo ren does his best to find them and achieve his grand plan. Daisy Ridley was really made by the force awakens and her character of Rey has really evolved from that time, she has a really interesting story here which is continued from the previous two films and Ridley does an excellent job in making you care about her character and the situation she is in. John boyega as Finn and Oscar Isaac as Poe are given more to do in this film then they did in the Last Jedi and they do really good jobs in this film, their chemistry together is fantastic and you really are both of them step up into big roles in the film and it really works. Adam driver has been fantastic as kylo ren in these films and he possibly has the best story in this film, there are huge layers to his performamce and his dynamic with Rey is really interesting in the film and really drives it. Also a special shoutout due to the circumstances they do a really good job with the late Carrie Fishers role as Leia as she plays a really important role in this film. The story of the film is very fast moving and exciting, they answer the majority of questions that needed to be answered in a fulfilling way. However, my biggest criticism of this movie is that it does play it a bit safe with is story telling and sometimes the stakes don't feel as large as they should do for a final film in a trilogy. The script is great, there is an appropriate use of humour and some really good drama that makes the characters feel more interesting and human. The style of the film is enthralling, the combat is exciting and the action scenes will keep you on the edge of your seat and as mentioned before the pacing is fast and will keep you engaged. Overall this is a fantastic addition to the Star Wars legacy and an experience you need to have on the big screen.

title: Tried to get the series back on track in predictable ways
review:
I'm going to start by saying that the best of the recent starwars movies were the "anthology" ones. I think that Solo and especially Rogue One were better than episodes 7, 8 and 9. Ep7 was too much rehashing of the original trilogy and Ep8 - well allowing a director to completely disregard story elements that the previous director was clearly building up to was a huge mistake.

Now episode 9 is here. After watching all 3 movies it felt like we've been watching an argument between J J Abrams and Rian Johnson.

"This is important" "No it's not" "YES IT IS!"

Such a massive mistake not having someone directing the story across episodes. So what we got in Episode 9 was largely Abrams trying to yank the story back on to the track he originally intended. It had its good moments (threepio got all the best lines). But it was for the most part pretty predictable other than a couple of cameos I didn't expect (I cheered to see Dennis Lawson, however briefly).

Including Leia was always going to be difficult with the passing of Carrie Fisher. Her scenes were cobbled together using unused footage from Episode 7. I suppose it was done about as well as they could have done but much of her dialogue seemed general and vague in the context of the scenes she was in. Clearly the other dialogue was built around using as much as they could. It came off as being a lot like one of the Weird Al Yankovic mock interviews where he takes a celebrity's answers to interview questions and then changes the questions to alter the context.

When I first watched the Last Jedi I really enjoyed it and for the most part defended it against its critics. Over time I began to agree more and more with those critics. At the moment I'm a bit torn over whether I liked this one or not. Time will tell what my final verdict will be.

title: Oh how the mighty have fallen - the Rise of Tedium
review:
In my previous review of the Force Awakens for IMDB, I stated that I'd likely watch the latter films on TV, rather than the cinema, such was misfire of that film.

I actually broke this in going to see the Last Jedi - maybe the good reviews were right this time? No - just the reviewers again refused to see the wretchedness at the heart of that film as well. After seeing that, there was no way I was going to the theater for the last one.

So this review is from seeing it on TV. Decision rewarded. I hoped beyond hope that somehow, Jar Jar would somehow pull something new out the hat. No.

What an appalling film, and conclusion to the new Trilogy - from somebody who loved the originals, and to some degree, liked even the Prequels.

So many have listed this film's flaws individually here already - I won't do a forensic on it. Summary - it just jumps from one tiresome, bloated, unoriginal battle set piece or Macguffin to another. Just like its immediate predecessors did. No notable writing, or character development beyond cardboard cut out archetypes. Scarcely a scene anywhere to fill one with wonder. Plot holes and recycling of previous films again aplenty.

A film like ROS is an embarrassment to the original Trilogy - in fact, it makes even the Phantom Menace look admirable, and Revenge of the Sith a masterpiece in comparison. That should tell you something.

I'm done then, as far as Star Wars and films go. We have to hope somebody can pull this trainwreck of a franchise in a more modest and thoughtful direction. TV series such as the Mandolorian I hope can help to erase in time the memories of this stinking third Trilogy.

Advice - try and forget that the third Trilogy existed, and go to a fan film like Darth Maul: Apprentice on the Internet. Better story, pacing and tension in less than 20 minutes with amateurs producing, than this film or its predecessors managed with multimillions.

Why did I give three stars, you wonder? Cinematography and music mixing and score are fine. Make up and CGI/special effects functional. Everything else - forget it.

title: Absolute shameless hackery. But at least it's not Cats.
review:
It's hard to write a single review on Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker because so much happens of so little consequence that it's almost impossible to pinpoint what to talk about and what to completely ignore.
It was pretty well known that Kathleen Kennedy and JJ Abrams royally screwed up when they didn't bother planning a three-movie franchise from the beginning of the first film's pre-production, even when George Lucas himself handed them a book full of ideas and a cohesive trilogy outline (they just threw that in the garbage). This screw up solidified with The Last Jedi, in which Kennedy just told Rian Johnson to just do whatever, nobody cares they'll buy it anyway. And they did buy it, since they didn't know what kind of disaster Rian had barfed into existence.
With Last Jedi, those former fans know better, and considering what I'd seen, I'm glad, because even in trying to undo TLJ, it manages to be just as awful in its own special panicked neurotic way. I've never seen JJ Abrams trip on himself this clumsily since reluctantly directing Star Trek Into Darkness, and Into Darkness looks downright magnificent by comparison to this trash.
I'll just skip to near the end when the truly heinous crap goes down.
After a bunch of nonsensical romping through several equally forgettable planets and a handful of beloved character death fakeouts and one actual character death that should've happened in TLJ when Carrie Fisher actually passed away, Rey Skywalker Palpatine Solo finds out that Emperor Sheev Palpatine came back from the dead, cloned himself (which ended up being Snoke because of course it did), and had a kid who ended up giving birth to Rey. Kylo "Ben Solo" Ren Skywalker is still evil but also still in love (wait, JJ later confirmed that he was still in "friendship") with Rey. They end up fighting each other, who cares, blah blah blah, and then Kylo fights Sheev, who throws him down a cliff or something. Then Rey uses two lightsabers to knock Sheev's lightning back at him until he doesn't exist anymore and then dies.
Then Kylo comes back and uses force healing to bring her back, and then he dies.
Then Rey decides her name is Skywalker.
The End.
Pad that with a bunch of useless spectacle nonsense and you have the epic conclusion to the Skywalker saga: a movie that managed to be worse than Phantom Menace. Well done.
