title: Never Did I Think I Wouldn't Be Excited for Star Wars
review:
I don't even know where to begin here. This movie is just a mess. I've loved every single film, yes even The Last Jedi... but this just wasn't it. Most of my issues come from Disney more than the film itself, they made Abrams cut 20 mins out of the movie and they cut another 20 behind his back and filmed a different ending without his knowing as well. Had it not been missing an entire hour almost I'm sure it would've been fine but we'll have to hope they release the Abrams Cut. But now on to the review itself.

No backstory with what happened between episodes VIII and IX. We aren't shown how Palpentine broadcasted himself to the Galaxy, or how the First Order found out before the Resistance when it was all broadcasted on the same coms channel (revealed in the opening crawl).

Rey was too powerful for how little time she trained. Somehow she is able to Force Lightning and blow up a ship, Force Freeze Kylo Ren in place AND she knows how to heal someone through the Force. Leia couldn't have taught her that because according to the movie, Leia cut herself off from the force and never finished her Jedi training.

Reylo was forced, or wasn't given enough time to grow properly (at least in the cut we were presented with, in the 3 hour version that was supposed to be released it may have been explored more). The Knights of Ren weren't even used except for Ben Solo to absolutely slaughter them.

Rey being a Palpetine may be a nice "twist" and a decent answer to why she is so powerful but there is no way that in one year those powers would all just come at once as she starts her proper training. Rey defeating Palpetine the same way Windu got his scarred face (Lightning to the face) feels like a cop out and makes it seem like he was dumb for not stopping an attack he should've known would've happened.

Ben shouldn't have been able to fade into the Force when he died. He was way too young to have been taught how to do that. The same sex kiss at the end had no merit to the story at all except to please SJWs. I'm not homophobic or anything but it just felt misplaced, had that relationship been built upon a little bit I wouldn't have minded so much.

And finally... Rey identifying herself as a Skywalker. I can even say my disappointment in that. She wasn't close enough with either Luke or Leia to adopt that family name. Their relationships weren't built on at all, so it felt she had very little right to claim the name. And what's the point of burying Leia's and Luke's lightsabers but building her own when Luke's was technically her property. She could've just kept that one. And if there's no more evil, why even make a new one in the first place?

This movie suffers from pacing issues, points that don't correlate to the story where it should, hardly any proper answers to questions The Force Awakens asked. If the Abrams Cut is released and the other questions are answered and it doesn't feel as rushed, I will happily take some of my statements back. But as it is, this is probably the worst Star Wars movie I've seen, and it's sad too because I really wanted to like it, but the further it went on, the more I knew it wasn't going to get any better.

title: Anticlimactic final word in the story of Skywalker...
review:
The disenchantment of this trilogy really destroys my ability to sit down and enjoy an original (well made) Star Wars film as it can't seem to find it's potential. Shot down in flames by hi7;s apparent 'cinematic failure' of a film The Last Jedi, The Rise of Skywalker focuses more on the mess that Rian had left from the other film more than its own story by which it's really trying to tell. I felt there was supposed to be something huge in this film but it was like it couldn't reach that potential of a larger scale because of its inability to forget and move on. This film tried its hardest to subtly retcon everything The Last Jedi did meanwhile trying to balance it out with decent storytelling, but if you don't plan out a trilogy with a basic idea of where you want it to go by the last movie, maybe you shouldn't of made the film or at least given the trilogy more thought? Sounds like common sense to me.

If there is some resemblance of hope in this film storytelling wise, no. But entertainment wise, yes. This film features characters old and new for one last 'hoorah' in the Skywalker saga. Another nice thing about this film is it's use of vibrancy in colour, this film looks really good, but so did The Last Jedi. The special effects were spot on, so was John Williams's final score ever. The cast were great with what they were given with, even if the source material was something a 7 year old could of probably written in a week. But if you like fun Star Wars entertainment and aren't bothered by the trash storytelling side of thing then this is definitely a watch. But don't expect anything masterful.

title: Tries to fix what the last movie broke
review: SUPER loved this movie. I was 13 years old, voted in Tiger Beat's contest (should Princess Leia end up with Luke or Han), and loved Luke. I saw this movie 13 times - which is a lot for 1978. Luke has always been my favorite character. I've watched the original trilogy more times than imaginable. My own children grew up with the prequels and the animated series, so I know Star Wars. I'm not a 'fly by' fan. The Force Awakes - wow! The gasp of the murder of Han Solo in the theater was like a scream when so many did it at once. I was SO happy to see The Last Jedi, hoping to have answers to so many questions from the first...who was Rey? What happened to Phasma? What was Luke going to do? I waited through the WHOLE first movie to see Luke for two seconds so I was thrilled to learn what had happened. BUT - OMG - The Last Jedi didn't answer anything like I suspected. Evil Snoke was gone in a flash. Phasma, who? Rey is no one. Let alone the idea of poor Princess Leia turning into Mary Poppins...especially since she passed away! WHY didn't he change that scene??? Who would do that??!! SO - I was hoping Finn would wake from a 'dream' of the horror of the last film, when The Rise of Skywalker opens. I hated the second film in this trilogy so much that I don't own it. I own every bit of movie/animated series out there. I happen to really like Solo. I think it suffered coming out so near that horrible film. I loved how the leads had Han and Lando's mannerisms ... how we had a back story on favorite characters. SO - fingers crossed - we went to see The Rise of Skywalker at 6pm on Thursday - the night of opening. YES! It tried so hard to wrap up all of those mistakes from the last film. Rey, Poe, and Finn - along with the droids and Chewy - THAT's what was missing from the second movie! I loved the 'feel' of the film. It was so Star Wars! It dealt with the death of Carrie Fisher in a respectable way. It brought up a kite fair celebration that happens only every 42 years - I counted in my head - YES!! That's the original Star Wars date!! YAY!! There are so many WOW moments in this film. So many times to break out in claps. I SUPER loved this movie!

title: Star Wars Rise of Disappointment
review:
The Stream: The uninspired storytelling fell flat and leaves you wanting more.

The Big screen: The action sequences are still priceless.

The Final Bill: The story ends, whether you like it or not, but you'll be entertained.

-S2S

Stream to Big Screen, welcome back you are. This week we are reviewing the long awaited third film of the newest trilogy from the Star Wars franchise, Star Wars: Rise of Skywalker. This movie reprises the roles of many of the cult classic's favorites dating back to the 70's. But let's get to the review.

Honestly, this movie is a letdown for the Disney/Lucasfilm's brand. In a way this felt like the producers just going through the motions to end this never ending story. My sentiment is definitely heighten coming off of Disney's other colossal film product, Avengers: Endgame, from this summer. You can't "end" one properly and just let the other suffer. I'm not sure who dropped the ball on this but we had a movie where all of the stakes were on the line and it felt completely lifeless. We went from planet to planet, searching for their Maltese falcon that will save us... just to realize we have to find something else insignificant to eat up 20 minutes of theater time. We get your formula Star Wars... particularly in this trilogy. But for 2 hours plus, we end up at the obvious ending and they still expect us to be wowed. I think the die hard fan base, which I am not even though I've seen all of the movies except Solo, deserves much more than what they got from this film. Even in the scenery, nothing new was even explored in this film. Same old desert, rain forest etc. One thing I did enjoy about the last Star Wars film Last Jedi was the scenery they gave us. That red salt scene at the end... hot fire. This movie not so much. And don't even get me started on the lame acting in this movie.

Now don't get me wrong, the story of Star Wars in this recent trilogy is annoying at best but it's still a wonder to see visually on the big screen. This movie does have some really good, yet unoriginal action scenes, throughout. Who doesn't love racing around spaceships, light saber duels, endless inaccurate blaster shots by the bad guys. No seriously, even though I was bored with the movie, I was enthralled by the constant barrage of action and entertainment.

Long story short, nothing I could say would stop a Star Wars fan from seeing this movie. So let them enjoy their big popcorn. Everyone else, you have to have seen all of the other movies to understand whats going on. So it's not worth wasting the theater monies on this film. Check it out on Disney+, if you ever catch up on the other installments of Star Wars.

May the force be with you.

review:

I found Reys journey did relate to the characters progression in TLJ and did see somewhat of a link to the dark side but found Finn, Poe and the rest of the rebels to fizzle out a bit. title: I wanted so much more!
review:
Let me start by saying that, overall, I liked this movie. The visuals were absolutely amazing, there were a ton of Easter eggs, and the cameos and throwbacks were a nice touch. Seeing Lando again was pretty cool, and the cgi with Leia was pretty seamless. It was nostalgic seeing the death star again too.
With that being said, as an old star wars fan I'm left wanting more. I have more questions and disappointment than I do joy and closure.
The writing on this was just lazy. Pretty much copy and paste from rotj with little originality.
The whole palpatine plot actually angers me off because not only does it negate the whole story line of the first 6 movies, but it was a plot that just came out of nowhere, with no explanation of how he was resurrected. Anakin was the chosen one. He brought balance to the force by redeeming himself and killing the emperor. The fact that the emperor wasn't dead this whole time just means that Anakin's whole story was a sham?! Plus when the heck did palpatine have a chance to conceive a child?! I feel like it was all quickly put together just to be able to advertise that the emperor is back.
The last Jedi last showed rose and Finn kissing, and they just abandoned that arc in this movie.
The massive fleet was built on a planet that seems to have 0 resources and each ship is pretty much a death star?
Rey is barely trained, and yet she is able to do things no other Jedi has ever been able to do. So I have to buy the fact that she is the most powerful Jedi to ever exist?! Nope. I love her character, but no.
There was no character development, or any awe moments that made me relate to the characters.
This whole trilogy lacked a good love story.
And arguably the best thing about star wars is the lightsabers, particularly the battles. The lightsaber battles in this movie were absolutely horrible! Neither kylo nor Rey could use one for their life and they are supposed to be at the top of their game?! C'mon man!
I could go on, but I think you get my point. This movie just left so much to be desired. Did I have fun watching it? Sure. I'll probably even watch it a few more times. Did I get that same gut wrenching feeling mixed with tears and excitement like I did watching Avengers endgmame? Absolutely not.
I really wish they would have planned this trilogy better and kept the same director for all 3. Overall, Disney dropped the ball on this whole trilogy, leaving us all wanting so much more.

title: This trilogy never needed to exist
review:
Not only did this trilogy not need to exist, but this film was the worst of the new trilogy. Because, while last Jedi was too ambitious, it hit simultaneously hit the highest of the highs and the lowest of the lows. It sucked, but at least it had some originality (looking at you Force Awakens).

Then you cut to Rise of Skywalker which tries oh so desperately hard to recover the crap story we've been handed on a silver Disney platter that says "buy my merch", but I ain't havin it. This whole trilogy ruins Star Wars. It shows us that the galaxy would have been better off without the Skywalker family. We start off with a kid who's prophesied to bring balance, and he does, just in a bad way. Then his son helps the galaxy to rebel against oppression, and his father redeems himself by actually bringing balance. Space station explodes. Oppression over. The end. Great story right? Well no it's not good enough for Disney because apparently Luke and Anakin were utterly useless at bringing down the oppression because this "First Order" comes outta nowhere like the empire didn't literally just collapse. And remember that prophecy anakin fulfilled? Well forget about that, because Palpatine is still alive for marketing purposes so anakin no longer has a fulfilling character arc. Also that Luke guy you once liked is now a coward and he hates the force. Then the new Skywalker boy turns mega evil and oppresses the galaxy while killing tons of people. And his entire existence is supposedly justified just because he stopped the very thing he started. That's like someone pushing me into the street in front of a car and then pulling me right back before it hits me and saying, "well you better be grateful because now I'm a good guy." And how does Palpatine just create these super powerful Snokes that are naturally strong in the force? Where did all the Star destroyers come from? In the end of this film nothing has changed for the better, so how is this a good end to the saga? Now Palpatine is dead and the oppression is brought down (again) only its 3 movies later and with a bunch of unresolved characters. Not a single character from this new trilogy is redeeming except for Kylo Ren and even his character arc blows. Thanks for giving us this entirely new and original story Disney. You guys really knocked it out of the park on this one👍🏻

title: What a steaming pile of Palpatine!
review: This film felt like really bad fan fiction right from the opening text crawl. It starts at break neck speed and doesn't slow down, it leaves you no time to breath or reflect on big events. Absolutely no dynamics or nuance. There so many plot holes and moments that leave you laughing out loud at what is the hell is happening. For me this is the worst Star Wars film so far, it ties up nothing at the end except for the very strange plot points that felt forced and panic written for this film. When the end finally came I was just left with the feeling of disappointment and a realisation that this was the most pointless trilogy they could have made.

title: It's okay.
review:
I went into the theater with high hope that this would be the Star Wars movie to make the sequel trilogy make sense and bring balance to the Force. It was not as much of a disappointment as I thought it would be is all I can really say about it. The whole plot of the movie just doesn't make sense and it doesn't add anything new to the series. Nothing new at all. I so wish that they would have had a long sit down and actually come up with something new for the series instead of give the director creative liberties and make this mess. This movie is so upsetting that I actually made this IMDb account so I could write a review about this so called movie.
Watch it if you must but you are better off staying home and re-watching Episodes 1-3 because they make way more sense than this hot mess.

title: Slightly below 21st century action flicks' average
review:
Episodes VII - IX were very, very poorly written. What they offered in terms in visuals, they lacked in terms of storyline, depth, character development and consistency with the previous SW movies - even with Episodes I - III, which were definitely better in comparison.

What really makes no sense to me is people saying that Episode IX was better than VIII. How? Why? Both were equally awful. Episode IX could have simply followed VII, as VIII didn't prepare viewers for anything that would happen in IX, other than seeing pretty much the same faces. To me, that is the definition of awful story-telling.

There are many, many things to criticize about Episode IX, such as how easy and non-sensical it became for characters to turn from bad to good (although Ren's story is so irrelevant that it only disappoints by comparing it to Anakin's, which is so much richer, sensible and natural, sand or no sand). But the saddest thing, by far, was the way in which the Emperor died - shamefully and gratuitously. (Almost) the same thing can be said about including him in this movie, for no other reason than to give a few minutes of screen time to pretty much all of the major characters from the original trilogy, in a sad nostalgia act meant to sell tickets. By bringing the Emperor back from certain death (with absolutely no logical explanation, by the way), Disney not only turned Anakin / Vader's entire existence obsolete, but it also killed arguably the baddest villain in the SW universe in a timespan of 5 seconds, at the hands of an untrained brat.

I seriously expect Disney to bring back Vader in the next trilogy, 4-6 years from now. He will have turned bad again because hey, why not? Let's give someone the chance to kill him *again*, too. That's what the masses seem to want.

Finally, a short message to those of you who say that this was a good movie / trilogy: you are the reason why movie studios can put out crap like this without getting ran into the ground.

title: Just felt a bit bored tbh
review:
As a heads up, I'm a strictly neutral. I haven't watched any star wars films since phantom menace. But I could see this film was laden with Easter eggs. It's a film for the fans with throwbacks to give you a feel good feeling like seeing Lando again. It's a big sci fi costume melodrama and oh boy, the costumes had a lot of thought going into it.

I tell a lie actually. I did watch a star wars "film" recently. And that was the story of Cal Kestis in Fallen Order. And that is something internally I would compare with. Because there was a point in that where I felt I need to stop everything and focus because I want to know what's going to happen. There was no pull.

I've given this film a low rating because I just didn't feel much invested in any of the character with the exception of Poe Cameron and Finn. I just felt the film was flawed because so many things were left unexplained and characters underdeveloped.

Where the story telling was going on eg the urge of the dark side on Rey, there was just a point where it stopped making sense. There was only point where I thought she'd submit to save her friends. But compare this to Fallen Order and the blind rage of Cere Junda, and there just wasn't the same emotional depth.

There were lots of action scenes and an epic lightsabre duel which features in the trailer. So lots of special effects. But it was the charge of the light brigade towards the end which was actually pretty cool. The Jedi training scenes were also good.

But I'm wondering why so much was just left unexplained. The story kept jumping. The only coherence was the narrative flashback to Rey's family and its significance in explaining the ritual. But then what was the purpose of Kylo Ren in the end. I'm sure he was told to kill Rey. The problem was it just never added up. And there are countless examples of this.

This review will be contrary to prevailing ones because people just want a film that makes them feel good and touches on nostalgia. But I'm pretty sure the studio just inherited a convoluted mess and rewrote the story in order to just get something out. There were lots of cameos based upon memories and I think that was at the expense of writing a formidable plot.

I liked all the British accents in the film. I remember at one point Christopher Lee was in it and it gave the drama a theatrical gravitas. This time that role was played really really well by Richard E Grant. I felt he stole every scene he was in

title: Solid 5.. I suppose I enjoyed it, but it left me feeling empty.
review:
Dramatic headline I know, but it is the best way I can sum it up! I'll keep it somewhat simplified..

You can tell Disney is tweaking the blueprint for these movies (and this genre) moving forward - one thing I noticed in particular that stood out was instead of speeders just blowing up (for the most part) and the assumption that the pilot is dead, Disney made it VERY clear that the pilot bails just before impact thereby potentially surviving.. strange thing to focus on. I can't help but think of the resources that were diverted from the source material to make this a 'thing'.

For the main review of the movie itself honestly overall it was a decent film. The special effects are obviously amazing, albeit there is a bit of special affect fatigue that I found growing over the course of the ~2.5 hours. The story is very clearly meant to wrap things up in a neat bow and provide a bit of closure for the fans.. this of course was never going to end up being perfect.

As absolutely ridiculous as it is to even say this probably the biggest issue I had was plausability.. (spoilers ahead). I know, I know - plausability in a star wars film. So the 'big reveal' is that Emporer Palpatine has been in hiding all these years building a gigantic 'secret fleet' of Star Destroyers that he calls the 'Final Order'. Each of these star destroyers is equipped with retrofit death star technology so each ship can destroy a planet. This to me is a constant game of 'one-up' the previous threat. At this point it is just a tired mechanism.. a fleet of thousands of super death star destroyers rising out of the ice just seemed like it came from the mind of a 10 year old. "Not just ONE evil space ship, but a bajillion!!" Here is the plausability issue.. lets say 5,000 ships, each with 5,000 trooops/technicians/officers/etc. - that is 25 million people apparently just hanging out under the ice essentially until they get 'activated'? What did they do with their time? How were they fed? How did so many people get to this seemingly impossible to find planet? Brings me to another point.. apparently only 3 Sith Wayfinders exist (lol @ "Wayfinder" and "Light Speed Skipping") so did ALL of those people use one? Just seems to contradict its own storyline..

Now lets talk resources. I get Palpatine is the super uber bad due to the force - how does he organize all these resources and credits that would be required to create this SUPER fleet? Just think of the sheer volume of raw materials.. does the planet have massive shipping ports? Industrial construction facilities? Unlikely.. how is he paying for all of this?

I think my main issue with Palpatine is he was just recycled on his own. The other sith and guards were all nameless/faceless so it gives the impression that Palpatine is a one-man show, which is frankly just ridiculous. In the original trilogy you got the feeling that a huge network of people were working towards a goal with boards, committees, generals, sith lords, etc. and Palpatine was the essential CEO - this is plausable! A decrepit corpse strong in the force living off a robotic arm under the ice managing to coordinate probably the single largest logistical gathering and organization of resources in the known universe is just... annoying and lazy writing.

The last thing I'll touch on is the odd use of force powers. We have been taught for literally decades what it is and how it works, and how some can use it better than others. In these latest movies it seems to be all about convenience or inconvenience.. one scene you'll have Kylo and Rey stopping light sabers with their hands and doing crazy sky jumps, the next they are struggling with regular 'troopers' or unable to do very standard manuevers. Its almost like they forgot they could just use the force instead.. I can understand restraint, but Kylo doesn't have that, and in one scene he throws a general-guy up against the ceiling with an instant choke. So he HAS the power... yet he struggles with normal folks.. could he not just flick his fingers for the majority of them??

The rest of the review I'll just list out in bullet points.

Pros:
  • Great lightsaber battles
  • Lots of good dogfighting and general space shenanigans
  • Mix of practical and CGI was pretty seamless
  • Sound mixing excellent
  • Lando was GREAT
  • Kylo clearly had Rey beat until his mom distracted him causing him to get stabbed.. cheap move
  • Nice to see some different uses of force powers


Cons:
  • Lazy writing and wrap-up
  • Palpatine seemed more of a one-note villain here, why was his mission to have Rey just kill him... then what? Yes yes I know the rule of two, but it just seemed forced and with no real purpose.
  • Felt like it was more of a story about the 'Legend of Palpatine' whereas the original trilogy appeared to be the 'Legend of Skywalker'
  • Lightsabers seemed to be tossed and traded around like trinkets, takes out the reverence for the items
  • Not a single resistance person got even remotely scratched from what I can recall. I find this takes away the feeling of any danger.
  • Rose... just felt FORCED in
  • Why is Ben Solo wearing an outfit from the galactic Value Village at the end? Such a lame 'final' outfit for his redemption
  • 'Force healing' seemed way too simple and convenient
  • See ya Hux? Again, felt just forced and shoehorned in
  • Too many McGuffins and red herrings 'get the thing, go to place!'
  • Whole C3PO memory wipe was a complete waste of time and pointless? R2 just booped him back up to speed...
  • Han Solo cameo, again FORCED, but more effective


All I can think of for now!

title: Credibility lost
review: After seeing this last film of the final trilogy, which is supposed to complete what we all have been waiting for for forty years, I could say plenty of things about how spectacular it was, how the duality was interesting, how Ben giving his life to Rey was touching, how through all the disappointments it really seemed like an ending. Or how bad it was, how inconsistent, how simple, how fake. But I don't even want to talk about that. I just want to talk about how after some days, I realized that the good thing Star Wars was, the good thing the real Star Wars people learned to rely on and live with throughout these 40 years, no longer was good. In vain my spirit kept calling upon this thing, but where in the past there was quick satisfaction and solution, there was now nothing. What about us now? What about the Star Wars people? Disney has spoiled and corrupted the good name Star Wars was, meddling with a Force of which they had and have absolutely no understanding, and turned it into something bad and useless, leaving us with nothing. That good name was more important than finishing the three trilogies, and now I'd rather have that they had kept things the way the were, even after the prequels. We Star Wars people are left with no other choice then to buy into something else now, because what was worth about Star Wars, is now worthless. So sad.

title: After TLJ killed Star Wars, TROS had NO HOPE.
review:
That being said what we end up with is a vast improvement when compared to TLJ but that isn't hard. Even the old Ewok films are preferable to TLJ and that's saying something lol.

title: TFA is the only good movie of the new trilogy
review:
I know I already added a warning, but spoiler alert anyways.

I love Star Wars, and I don't regret saying this. Watching SW always brought a dreamy smile to my face and lifted my spirits like nothing else. I was, admittedly, obsessed when I was a kid, but now the obsession has waned into a soft, nostalgic corner of my heart.

When I saw The Force Awakens, I was happy! I saw it more than once, and I still love it. It has flaws, of course... But it made me feel happy, and nostalgic. And it left me giddy with anticipation for how the following movies would go! I was psyched. And then Rian Johnson happened... And with him, The Last Jedi. I mean... What the hell happened? He had a good formula, a million ways to expand on the characters from TFA.... So he chooses... To sideline Finn... Make Poe look like an idiot... And try to make us sympathize with Kylo Ren?!? I mean... What. The. Hell. This brings me to episode IX.

They brought back JJ, and despite having hated episode VIII, I was foolishly hopeful. But the joke was on me yet again, as I was forced to watch Kylo Ren - a MURDERER, A MASS. MURDERER - not only be redeemed (having done NOTHING to deserve it, might I add), but also kiss Rey???? The woman he tortured, back in TFA?? Which, if I'm not mistaken, was only a month or so back? (if I am wrong, sorry. I really don't care though).

Sorry, I won't and will NEVER sympathize with Kylo Ren. He's an undeserving little who killed his own father with no remorse, killed who knows how many people, and tortured/maimed countless others. He's an annoying brat of over 30 years old.

I am only giving this movie 3 stars due to 3 factors: Kylo died; I got to see Finn, Poe, and Rey on the big screen; and despite it all, Star Wars still holds a place in my heart.

title: Never even tried to go for the stars
review:
The only ambitious aspect about this movie is how much stuff they try to fit into it without prolonging the run time. This movie feels bloated as hell and this is probably because of: A. Disney not sticking to one overall vision for the entire trilogy and B, JJ trying to steer it back from where Rian Johnson took it in episode VIII.

The main pull for Star Wars fans was the heart with which the universe was crafted. This feels like it was put together by a committee, which it most definitely was, but the interest behind it was money and not the love for the source material and genuine interest in making a good movie. This feels more like a generic Sci-Fi movie that happens to use laser swords and telekinetic powers than actual Star Wars.

Spoilers below: If anyone, at any time, can explain to me why Disney keeps faking deaths in movies, I'm willing to listen. There are four fakeout deaths in this movie:
  • the ship Chewie is on gets blown up by Rey, only to reveal 5 minutes later that he was on another ship (undercutting an interesting arc where Rey would have had some actual struggle)
  • C3PO gets his entire memory erased. This was a good idea as well, since he could be the fish-out-of-water for comedic effect for the rest of the movie. No worries, R2 has a backup by the end of the movie, so he's as good as new.
  • Kylo is mortally injured, so Rey heals him immediately
  • Rey is mortally injured, so Kylo heals her immediately.
This is the emotional equivalent of the boy who cried wolf. By the time Ben Solo actually died, I was somewhere in between not caring and being annoyed at the only character who actually had an arc this movie. There are other smaller things that get on my nerves as a Star Wars fan (Force Ghosts interacting with real life objects being one, for example)

In retrospect, this movie had some really good ideas story-wise, but, for me at least, it took wrong turns at every single one of them.

title: Disney and J.J. go into full-on Schlock Mode!
review:
The two words that came to me watching this enjoyable mess were "desperate" and "cowardly".

Desperate because the film tried so hard to please everyone by working in so many characters and references that it completely lost focus. With BB-8, R2D2, and C3PO, we just have too many damn robots. So what do they do? They add in yet another one! We lost our big and bad female stormtrooper Phasma but replaced her with two new pointless female characters (a bounty huntress and a former storm trooper) who both only seem to exist to give Poe and Finn someone to have chemistry with aside from each other. Rey is still doing her own thing, so overpowered and invulnerable that the film creaks along with a total absence of tension...

...which leads me to the Cowardly aspect. The film pulls absolutely every punch from the start. Remember when Finn almost killed himself in The Last Jedi, only to get rescued from it at the very last second? Well here we get at least 3 instances where a character makes a brave sacrifice only for their "death" to be undone in the very next scene! It's as though Disney just can't kill off any of the main characters no matter what happens. The emperor shows up again, because "duh, what else were they gonna do?" However the moral conundrum he puts before Rey gets solved in the blandest way possible, which would never have even been a problem for him had he not just announced his plan to her seconds earlier just like a Bond Villain.

I really cracked up at his new ability to summon star destroyers at will, complete with loyal crews on several vessels. There's a ton of throwaway, possibly ADR'ed afterthought-lines thrown in here and there by offscreen characters such as "it's time to recruit more children on planets to serve in my fleet" but later a character says "they're going to deploy their fleet in 17 hours!". Well hell, those child-slave star destroyer crewmen grow up quick! I guess a lot can be accomplished when you go at light speed while Relativity makes time freeze for everyone else (when it serves the plot). However the rules of light speed, warp speed, hyperspace, etc. come to make absolutely no sense in context to the plot and what happens during the last act of the movie. Apparently it's just as easy for the heroes to summon a good guy fleet into existence in mere hours when all they need is "hope"! Luckily, for all the star destroyers the First Order had when the movie started, they couldn't spare any to defend their new fleet at its most vulnerable moment? Or spare a few extra control towers in case one gets destroyed?

These plot holes and contrivances come on fast and furious like every other plot element in the film. It would get annoying if it wasn't so quick that one literally has no time to think about it... just like an Umberto Lenzi crimer like THE TOUGH ONES or one of Kinji Fukasaku's Yakuza movies. It's not helped here that there's already too many characters but the film finds time to dump in plenty of new ones (in addition to the ones already mentioned) as well as so many ghost cameos of the old gang that it actually becomes funny after a while.

What a mess. It's disappointing that we never got to see the gang all back together as we had hoped before this new series came to theaters. Instead, we get all these bland new characters who never go on any arc and don't have any flaws or motivations at all. Adam Driver stands as the bright spot here but even his character suffers from Rian Johnson and J.J. Abrams pulling a tug-o-war on him over three movies. In the end, this franchise will make its money, but at the cost of having me, or any of the other fans of the original films, ever take the Star Wars brand seriously again. Worth watching for mindless fun, some laughs, and ultimately to join in on the conversation of why these movies didn't work.

review:

I do have a lot of issues with the plot, but these come across as the worst examples:

Rey starts movie showing her poor handling of the lightsaber once again, only to overpower everyone by the end of it. Must have trained for that off-screen... oh wait they put a timer on, a clock on the things they were supposed to do or the bad guys would win, so there goes the off screen training. So couldn't they just change the control from ship to ship until they could take the good guys out? Or even better, change it back to the original control tower since it was not destroyed. Finn and his crew pretty much went all in on that one, so....

But well Chewbacca finally got his medal.

title: Just Meh.
review:
JJ: "wanna see me save Star Wars?" "Wanna see me do it again?"

The most compelling part of TLJ was the idea of anyone using the force, of children out there needing guidance, of a new story that could stand on its own. Sure, they screwed Luke with that "gotta kill Ben even though I saved my dad," bit, but I was really looking forward to a nobody, standing strong on her own, like Anakin was from the start. But nope, just capitalize on past characters but making weak connections that are never fleshed out completely.

Embrace who you are Rey, but tell strangers you're a Skywalker so they like you. Take back your name and give it a new meaning girl, what are you doing.

They didn't have to kiss, why can't they be connected without it being romantic, they couldn't just be tied up in their destiny to kill palpatine, they had to shoe horn in some romance just to kill it immediately.

There were moments that made me smile, and moments that were touching. Lando and chewie saving the day, chewie's heartbreak over Leia, some cute new droids and side characters. But overall, Disney just wanted this over with, they asked JJ to wrap it up in a pretty bow to hide the flaws, and the performances were mostly phoned in.

I love you Mark Hamill, you deserved better than being forced to crap all over Luke, then getting one line, a shrug and a "I was wrong," to make us forgive you. As Weird Al wrote, "But I know that I'll be coming back some day I'll be playing this part 'till I'm old and grey The long-term contract that I had to sign Says I'll be making these movies till the end of time, with my Yoda, yo yo yo yo yoda."

title: Disney finally killed George Lucas

title: No Rules.
review:
I won't go into detail why its only 4 Stars for this one, so here is what bugged me most.

There are no rules anymore! I had a problem with Episodes 7 and 8 as well in this respect, but here it's the worst. So what do I mean by that?

Obviously, some of it is connected to what a force wielder can do. For instance, we all know that a light saber can block blaster shots. If it's too many shots at once (Order 66), its too much, the Jedi (or Sith) dies. And here with Episode 9, there are absolutely no rules anymore. It's like watching Superman. The Jedi and Sith can do almost anything now. At least when it is convenient. I could not establish a (personal) ruleset throughout the movie, and that bugged me a lot. Don't get me wrong, they tried to explain even that, I think. But in my opinion, not believable.

Secondly: technology. Again, no rules! Here it's hard to argue without spoilers but I'll try. So in Episode 4-6 it's all about the death star and how hard it was to get plans for it, there even is a spin-off for that whole topic. Yeah, thats nice, it is really hard espionage work and a lot of people died for information. Not in Episode 9. Things just... are there. And don't get me started on battle tactics.

Third: Love. Friendship. Emotional ties. They don't just rain from the sky. They need to be earned. Again, Episodes 1-6: Fine! 7:ok, 8: meh. 9: WT!

Conclusion: I read some bad reviews before seeing the movie. That kinda saved me from disappointment. It made me buckle up and switch off my brain when the movie started. Furthermore, I'm not what you would call a hardline Star Wars Fan, but I really like the Universe (seen all movies, read Thrawn, Boba Fett and Han Solo Books among other). So with my brain shut down, the movie was a solid 4/10. It's below average because it made me cringe at about 4-5 scences throughout the movies. I had to ask my theater-mates 3 times why something in the movie happened because I did not get the reason at first. And there was a reason every time, even though that made some scenes even worse.

Fun fact. I watched the movie with two friends and their girlfriends. They (the women) have seen, like 2 of the Star Wars movies, so they were untainted. And in their opinion, it was a mediocre movie. Not epic but not all bad for sure. They also thought some scences extremely silly, but others they just took as they came. Thats what you expect of a Superhero Movie (their words).

So go, see the movie, switch off your brain an probably be fine. Cinematics are great. Nice effects, beautiful places, but thats it.

if you have just read a Brandon Sanderson Book, I suggest you don't do that because the movie will not make a lot of sense to you.

PS: I just came from Frozen 2, and boy this was way better. Proves to me that Disney CAN write a story if need be. So long and thanks for the fish... (Celebration every 42 years my a..)

title: Whatever
review:
TROS is basically exactly what I foresaw happening ever since I realized the destruction TLJ caused to the saga. One could argue that said failure was set in motion since TFA, but I think it was TLJ that sealed it in stone. TLJ enforced the irrevocable destiny of TROS to be a pointless mediocrity, a pretentious sleeve of nostalgia to mask the desperation and despair that dominated the minds of its creators and investors.

It was a sadistic pleasure to observe the verification that TLJ did, indeed, ruin the "Skywalker saga", and no--that's no longer some bitter complaint from a disenfranchised minority of toxic fans. Behold TROS as it flails its feeble plotlines at the confines of the abyss it had awakened in, anxious to merely survive two and a half hours as a credible conclusion to the Star Wars films. It utters Star Wars-esque phrases and displays Star Wars-looking things--but what is, "Star Wars"? Who cares? Nothing matters anymore--nothing, but survival. Like a starved prisoner in a forced labor camp, soul long lost and forgotten, it sloppily spills its time and precious assets about as it scrambles to meet its minimum quotas at the threat of financial catastrophe's gunpoint.

You know you have failed when you make the movie that singlehandedly dragged the Star Wars franchise into the underworld look good. At least TLJ had themes and interesting ideas, and awareness of its own complexity. The mind of an edgy teenager still writes a more meaningful story than that of an oblivious prepubescent child. At least the edgy teenager enjoys some faint awareness of the intricacies of the human condition, even if he may completely fail to understand it. What depths has TROS explored? Trick question-S-tar Wars was just a kids movie about lasers and space wizards all along. Only maladjusted nerds would seek depth in this franchise.

Oh well, whatever. At least TROS isn't trying to insult me for liking traditional Star Wars with some lofty meta-narrative. It is a relief to not cringe every time the rug gets pulled from beneath me, and then ponder that it's being done in order to incite astonishment at the creators' profound contrarianism. No awkward progressive agenda and simultaneous mockery of general conservative values--(what even was that, anyways? Oh right--I, a depraved alt-right Star Wars nerd, must have my political views promptly corrected now, while I am distracted watching Star Wars.) But oh no, no more layers of edginess and unwarranted political polarization? What are we going to rage about now?

Now TROS is just boring and pointless.

TROS is now in the league of the late Michael Bay Transformer movies. It's a cinematographic portfolio with actors and cool designs and stuff. There's tears and pauses and important music to indicate important scenes. There is a big climax to all 9 movies. You can tell it's the biggest climax of all, because there are so many Star Destroyers and Rebel spaceships, and Palpatine uses the biggest force lightning ever seen. And the fate of the galaxy hangs in the balance. Only our valiant protagonist, Rey, can save the galaxy from the evil, evil big bad.

+1 for trying

+1 for amazing visuals and good acting

+1 for not trying to lecture/insult portions of the audience like the last movie

0 for childish story

0 for being creatively bankrupted into resurrecting Palpatine

0 for emotional intangibility

0 for cultural insignificance / pointless movie

0 for failure to abide by the preestablished lore and very basic logic

0 for failure to take the opportunity to explore and expand upon the human condition

0 for failure to realize Star Wars' full potential

title: Really Bad
review:
I never thought a Star Wars movie would make me miss the Phantom Menace but this one just did some how. This is one of the worst movies that I've ever paid to go watch. I'm a lifelong Star Wars fan and while I didn't think the new trilogy held up to the original one I certainly enjoyed the first two films and was looking forward to this one as well.

This movie is a complete mess. There are so many ridiculous things that this film does that just walks all over canon from the past films, including the last one, that it's disappointing events in this scrap pile will become Star Wars canon. The prequel's took some liberties with Jedi abilities but I didn't think it went too far at all. This movie just makes the Jedi seem like a whole other type of character than what Luke Skywalker and Darth Vader were. Suddenly those that are force sensitive can know heal each other, meet and fight through some type of force portal and transfer force power.

The ending had zero climax to it. Just because the riders decided to add 1 million star destroyers and 1 million alliance ships doesn't make the scene any more exciting than the one in Return of the Jedi. It just look like a giant video game. a star destroyer was actually a really cool thing in the original Star Wars and now there's so many of them that there's nothing special anymore. The problem is they didn't come up with anything cooler than a star destroyer so we're still stuck with those but now they're a dime a dozen like a track home. Also the new emperor's throne looks like a rip off of the iron throne in that little known HBO series that just finished....

Killing off Chewbacca and bring him back two seconds later and having an emotional goodbye with C-3PO all the while he comes back to his regular self 10 minutes later it's not a way to get the audience on edge. The movie relies on nostaliga and cheap tricks to get people involved but those are fleeting moments that don't work.

This movie is a total cash grab and opportunity to sell more toys. There were so many cool things that could've done with the new trilogy and they didn't do so bad in the first two but this is just the complete opposite of sticking a landing.

Can we start a gofundme to buy back the Star Wars franchise from Disney?

title: Fanboys have ruined Star Wars
review:
Catering to fans is a dangerous way to go.While it may seem to make sense to want to pleas your target audience, in the end though all it does is muddle creative intent, and that's exactly what happened here.

This movie seemed entirely created as a safe space to those fanboys who hated Last Jedi. I'm not talking about those who had legitimate complaints about the movie, I mean those 30+ year olds who were upset because all their fan theories got thrown out and Luke wasn't some big bad ass that they wanted him to be.

For some reason, there's a new narrative that honoring the original trilogy means milking it to no end, and if all you want from a Star Wars film is that then congratulations, you got it. This movie makes all of the nostalgia and fan-service moments of TFA seem tame, to the point where you just are cringing in your seats at the movie theater. Literally every 5 minutes I could count a reference or an over the top throwback, I get this is "the last of the saga" but this is supposed to be its own movie and instead all we get is some fan fiction rewrite of Episode 6 with a new coat of paint... again.

Even as its own movie it has a lot of problems. The plot makes no sense and is entirely thrown out through exposition, and it moves so fast that you can't absorb what happened as characters are racing from one awfully contrived magguffin to another. Characters are reduced to tropes rather than actual people like Rian Johnson tried to do in TLJ. The dialogue is so forced and corny it makes George Lucas's writings in the prequels look shakespearean. Palpatine coming back makes no sense and completely invalidates the efforts of the previous 8 movies combined to the point where you might as well not bother watching them. How did he build a fleet so massive, who was manning it? New characters are introduced but aren't really explored and old characters, such as Rose, get unfairly pushed to the sideline. Rey being a palpatine comes out of no where and clearly an attempt to cater to those hurt about not getting some family theory right about Rey. Finn does absolutely jack squatt, speaking of that what did he want to say to Rey? Oh, and he somehow has the force now, even though Star Wars is now back to saying that the force is bloodline based, lol.

Things happen in this movie so fast and for no reason. Someone died? Just kidding. We're going to this planet now so you don't have to think! Let's chase this MacGuffin! More nonsensical force powers are introduced with no explanation or without reasonable cause for the users to have known them. Leia, though they try their best with her, is at her worst, and Lando shouldn't be in the film. They turned him into a meme.

In fact, this entire movie is a meme, just an attempt to remind the older generation that they're still the best. All of the callbacks were just annoying, yet people still cackled and clapped in the theater as if this was oscar worthy. Instead of creating a movie to move Star Wars into the future, this literally takes Star Wars 3 steps back to the point where the only way it's enjoyable is if all you're looking for is a reminder of the original trilogy, and sadly that will be enough.

I understood some issues with the Last Jedi, but it was a solid film that actually innovated the franchise, but apparently fans don't want innovation, they want their safe spaces and want to be coddled with what's familiar. This movie is an insult to fans who actually think, and leaves Star Wars on such a sour note that I can't bother watching this trilogy anymore.

I give this movie 3 stars for the visuals, the acting (Adam killed it despite being given such a mortally awful script), and for 3p0 as he was the only well writted part of this. Other than that, this movie was just atrocious, and it seems fanboys are ok with it. They can say Last Jedi ruined Star wars all they want, but in truth this is the nail in the coffin because Disney caved to their needs. Fanboys have turned Star Wars away from being a possibly innovative franchise for the future to just be that safe space for them with eye candy. Remember, these are supposed to be for kids, and yet now Star Wars is being adapted for a generation that is far too old to be the target audience and just can't let go of their Luke Skywalker PJs.

title: An entertaining and thrilling but messy piece of melted cheese that somehow has a lot of holes in it.
review: The film has a lot of charm and definitely delivers that popcorn cinema feeling. It is a spectacle and you enjoy it while you watch it, but if you are a lifelong Star Wars fan, who has read a ton of books, comics and played the video games, you will not be able to take this seriously. The film is a rehash of Return of the Jedi, with sprinkles of Empire Strikes Back and it feels like two movies crammed into one. The non-stop roller coaster ride is there to stop you from thinking about whether or not any of this makes sense and unfortunately in the grand scheme of the saga, it doesn't. Not only was there no plan for this trilogy, but it was only made to end what George Lucas created and bury it, so that Disney can start fresh with new characters, locations and stories, unburdened by the past. Whether the film makers realise it or not, this film's plot actively destroys the main plot for both the Original and Prequel trilogies.

title: Great beginning, bad middle, DREADFUL ending
review:
I honestly left feeling ANGRY about this movie. Nothing felt connected in this last film. It felt like a disjointed mess that never knew what it actually wanted to accomplish. This was terrible

The dialogue is predictable, abysmal and cheesy as it can be, in my theater almost NO ONE laughed at any of the intended humor, they kept feeding you everything, everytime something important a character said "happens" the character in the scene HAD to tell you the same line of dialogue, just in case you are too dumb to figure it out in yourself. There's a couple of character motivations that are either too short, uninteresting or just never concluded.

SPOILER ALERT.

What was the spy's end goal? Why did he want Kylo Ren to lose specifically? And wtf did Finn want to say to Rey? Also that final kiss... not earned, established or emotional. What was the emperor's final plan? He wanted Rey to kill him to take over him, but he told Kylo he wanted him to kill her, but then he just drains the energy out of both of them making him whole again so... was he making it up as it came along? It felt that way. For such a master manipulator he sure didn't seem to know what he was doing or at the very least, HOW he was going to do it

The two new female characters are just... there. We are supposed to relate to the other desserted Stormtrooper because her story is very similar to Finn and that chick with the Power Ranger Helmet... she loves Poe. Also how TF did she get out of that blowing planet without that coin First order thing?

But I think the biggest sin is... Darth Vader was practically rendered USELESS thanks to this movie. Anakin was the chosen one, even after he fell into the dark side, because HE delivers the finishing blow to Palpatine. He brings balance to the force after SO much time of him being corrupted, but now, Mary Rey Sue is the one that does him in; in the most godlike way possible. It's almost a slap to the face to George Lucas and all the fans that have been inspired by Star Wars. If this was REALLY the route that they were going for, why wasn't Kylo involved in Palpatine's death? He kept saying in the first movie: "I will finish what you started" to Vader's destroyed helmet. This movie not only broke the canon of the first movies, it broke it's own canon. It's almost like they ACTUALLY had no plan since the beginning

This movie was DREADFUL. The only good things I can say it was Kylo Ren (The only saving grace of these movies), the beginning and Chewie finally gets his medal, FFS

Also, at the risk of sounding like , Poe and Finn should've ended up together. Even in this black hole of a script they still showed more chemsitry than any other in this up and down of a trilogy.

title: Similar faces...similar mess.
review:
The 'last' (and I emphasise last as there is likely to be another 27) instalment in the Star Wars saga was meant to have it all but instead had all the ingredients of a narrative failure. The obvious, rushed attempt of trying to have it all only highlighted the true essence of the narrative mess.

So many unanswered questions, so many overly-clichÃ© lines (even for Star Wars) and so many near deaths. I must start with the very beginning as the Emperor reveals he never died and has been all the voices Kylo Ren has heard throughout his reign. Snoke was a creation of his amongst 'many others' and he was under his control the whole time. Whilst I can partly come to terms with this lazy explanation, there is little to none explanation of how the emperor is alive and why he is alive. Apparently you can survive a huge fall into a pit and now he's keen to build a ton of a star destroyers that don't move and will eventually blow up planets?

I get that he wanted Rey to carry this on after killing him. Although as soon as she refuses to do this he kills her and Kylo Ren anyway showing that Plan B may have been favourable after all. This consistent theme of rushed narrative choices with little development went on throughout the whole film. A big example of this being Fin saying to Rey as they were sinking to expected deaths 'There's something I need to tell you' or 'something I've always wanted to tell you.' This does not get mentioned again when he tells her to worry about it later. Something I missed or just lazy scriptwriting?

Action scenes are well done in the film's defence. Lightsaber duels are well choreographed and some of the ship fights at the beginning are very cool. But, as a friend had pointed out to me, the film felt like a Star Wars video game. The dialogue felt quick and rushed with not massive character development whilst the action was well sought out and in-depth. Mind you, not a video game I would have finished.

I appreciate that Fisher's sad passing surely had an effect on production but her conclusion, such as the rest of the film, just felt sudden and rash. I'm not gonna get into the boundaries of the force because I'll be writing the whole night. The only thing I will say is that Leia passing simply from uttering a word through the force but flying through space only creating a bed-ridden princess is an interesting comparison of power. But hey, the force has no boundaries so doesn't really matter.

Character motivations are just all over the place to be honest. Poe and Rae have an intriguing character divide at the beginning of the film with no follow up. Fin's obviously romantic feelings for Rae never get mentioned. Kylo and Rae kiss for no reason what so ever other than a quick thank you for resurrection I suppose. Emperor's plan seems scattered and frankly stupid - Rae's ridiculously op presence in this film epitomised by her destruction of the emperor. If the emperor really knew how powerful she was then how did he let her destroy him so easily? Could he really not be more powerful than two lightsabers?!!

I don't know, maybe I'm just a keen Star Wars fan who just had too big expectations. To me thought, it seems as if JJ Abrams tried to repair a very broken product. The complete change of narrative direction in TLJ emphasises the need for a trilogy plan; not just a franchise that wants to sell all its new toys before Christmas. The decline of quality since TFA is staggering. It's just shocking how a whole team looked at this before it's release without questions themselves.

title: I didn't believe the haters... Now I do.
review:
I really, REALLY enjoyed both The Force Awakens and The Last Jedi. Their different tones and visions had more positive aspects than negative ones, for me.

But I don't have the faintest clue how filmmaker J.J. Abrams and Oscar winning screenwriter Chris Terrio were capable of writing this sh**. Maybe they were under the influence of narcotics, who knows. That's the simplest explanation I can come up with. I still genuinely can't believe how this was even green lit. It seems like it's the first draft of a bad video-game script. Again, I didn't believe it when I first read the reviews, but it's truth, all of it.

After many people on this site discrediting the haters, plus the high audience score on Rotten Tomatoes, I went to the screening open minded, saying to myself that even if it's bad, it would get at least a 7,5 out of 10. After all it was the gran finale and it was J.J. Abrams. It couldn't be that bad anyway. Oh boy, I was wrong.

I didn't believe the haters when they complained about the plot's convenience. But, literally, LITERALLY the characters get things FROM UP THEIR ASS. They literally fall into the right places when needed and are introduced to new force powers only to get the script flowing. Powers which make aspects of the original trilogy pointless.

One might even say that they simply copied and pasted story beats and dialogue from Avengers: Endgame. All to create a crowd pleasing epicness they thought would work. It's cringy actually.

I see people who liked the movie trying to explain the great, HUGE amount of plot holes by assuming things and creating excuses for them. If a movie ever needs that, it is a bad movie.

Also, there are no consequences whatsoever. Here we have some of the greatest one-movie set-ups of the entire trilogy - but there is no payoff. When you think something serious or relevant has happened, the writers rush to undo it before you even feel anything.

After all, I feel obligated to talk about the good too. There are a couple of emotional scenes that actually land, but they make about 10% of the whole movie. Some of them fall into that category of set-ups which lead nowhere, but they were nice moments anyway. That's the reason I'm giving this movie a 5.

The ending is the worse. It seems like a IT chapter 2 kind of ending. Not a satisfactory ending at all.

I feel so bad for it - I really wish I enjoyed this movie. I'll watch it again, now knowing what to expect, and maybe it will be better.

title: Not the real Star Wars...
review:
It started so well with the force awakens but as I soon realised it was the same plot from A New Hope it gave a negative feel, but the movie was still fairly good.

The Last Jedi, possibly the most boring and disappointing film which attempted to be funny but was just a failure made me come to a conclusion Disney have ruined it.

As a true fan I obviously went to the Rise Of Skywalker with an open mind and I couldn't be anymore disappointed. The film had some amazing fight scenes with good CGI and sound effects. On the other hand, too much cramming in was the real downfall and excess of nostalgic moments such as Lando and the X wing. Even moments such as Princess Leia who somehow has a lightsaber but we only found out so many movies later.

So after the end of this saga (until Disney want more money) I only remember Star Wars as the original three, the most classic and entertaining films of all time.

title: I felt nothing
review:
There are a thousand things wrong with this movie. From bad pacing, choppy editing, the story can't pick a lane, etc. There are some good concepts, but I'm not sure it gets too much credit because it didn't really execute them well. It's clearly at odds with the other movies in this Trilogy, and the Saga as a whole.
But at the end of the movie, I realized the worst thing about it was that I felt nothing.
I was never exited, I was never upset. I'm not angry that this movie was a disappointment to me. I doubt I'll even remember my movie going experience. I saw a Star Wars mainline movie in theaters and it was one of the least memorable movie going experiences I've had.
Just a few weeks ago I was rewatching the Original Trilogy and even after all these year and multiple viewings I still got chills. That's almost embarrassing to say about cheesy sci-fi movies "made for kids." Even the Star Wars movies I don't like make me feel something. Anger for feeling like it ruined something thst came before. Regret and the failed potential of characters and story. They could make me laugh by being so bad.
But it's clear this movie was dead before it ever breathed. The "creative" "team" was uninspired and at odds with each other. There were boxes and limits put on them from past movies. But obstacles in the creative process can make a product greater than it would have been without them. But instead this movie decided to ignore these limitations and in doing so it all feels hollow.
I don't think I'll ever watch this movie again. I don't even recommend other people to watch it. I don't think it's worth someone's time. This movie was just cranked out to finish the Disney Trilogy on time. There's no heart, there's no emotion. There's nothing.

title: Damage control with a hint of jam
review:
JJ might be a good director, but as an ending this movie breaks a lot of things within the universe. I walked in with little expectations and laughed at the really canned dialogue and breaking of logic that flows throughout the movie, but as a star wars movie, this very much is not worth your time.

First, pacing issues run rampant throughout the movie, the first hour is litered with many many camera cuts, visiting various planets from various character perspectives, until we have enough background knowledge to really start the film proper.

Some scenes felt a little handfisted just to try and flesh out Po's history. If you watched, you know what I'm talking about. While it's not minded, it felt very forced. Most of the macguffins felt forced to push the plot in specific areas. Eg. We HAVE to do X, there's no other way, so let's go to planet Z.

My last big complaint is C3PO, who in this movie is without R2D2 to respect the actor of R2. However, all C3's jokes don't land, they come off really annoying and honestly could have been written out easy.

I like the few callbacks to RotS, but it's more just a shoehorn for a cool backdrop rather than necessary to the plot.

If you're a star wars fan, watch, but watch with low expectations. If you're just a fan of action blockbusters, think without logic. The movie likes to just throw things at you and hopes you don't hold it to the logic of the universe.

Good luck, and may the force be with this franchise after this movie 🙏

title: Just pretty pictures...
review:
I've always been careful comparing the old Star wars movies with the new instalments. Time and memory tend to make the stories we've heard and seen in our childhood more magical then those in our adult life.

But in this case I have to admit it: Disney didn't end the Saga, it killed in. It's not just the enormous plot holes, clunky dialogues or stale jokes. What it truly lacks is 'gravitas': solid storylines, characters you can relate to, and dramatic events.

This was more like watching a videogame, where everybody is running around, going from place to place, finding clues and as a conclusion fighting the end boss. What a waste of this wonderful story and great actors like Adam Driver and Daisy Ridly. And also a slap in the face of everybody who love this story; Disney totally missed the point.

title: The rating wars have begun
review:
First off, to get this out of the way: The movie is nonsense, the characters almost all fall flat, and the story is just one stupid MacGuffin + fan service after another. It's clear to anyone going in somewhat objectively that there was no real plan or vision for this trilogy, and that it was a great disservice to the Star Wars franchise as a whole.

But of course we see the typical review wars now, as a reflection of our polarized society. If you hate this movie you're a manbaby or a nazi, if you love this movie you're a shill. And to be honest, all those 1s and 10s fall exactly in this category. For some weird reason we feel like we have to choose a camp, and then support it at all costs, even if it means we have to smear and belittle our opposition.

I couldn't care less about Star Wars anymore, it's just not for me anymore, and that was that. But the way we attack each other for seeing things differently makes me way more sad than a freaking movie ever could.

title: A confidence trick of a movie
review:
JJ Abrams is now confirmed as - albeit one with good intentions I would say. But, he doesn't have an original creative bone in his body. This film is an absolute mess - though for some the emotionally manipulative script and overblown CGI spectacle will leave them feeling like they enjoyed this, when really it just kept their attention.

And to do the latter, JJ makes the most caffeinated, ridiculously fast paced Star Wars film of all time. He speeds though, hoping you won't stop to consider how ridiculous a lot of what is unfolding really is - not least that SOMEHOW the damn Emperor survived the ROTJ (electrocuted, thrown down a vast hole, then blown up minutes later in the Death Star's destruction). This last plot point should be enough to make any die hard Star Wars fan suspicious...but apparently as mentioned if you tug their heartstrings cynically, assault them with nostalgia, and keep the pace at monster energy level they will forgive this. Which, to me, speaks of the lowered standards of modern day cinema goers. And maybe that video game plotting has become acceptable in films. The exposition in this is, frankly, laughable.

But the thing that irks me the most is the aforementioned lack of creativity. This really is just a bunch of macguffin, video game fetch quests until you can see that it really is just ROTJ 2.0. Even the Emperor snarls "Strike me down". I couldn't frickin' believe my ears. The way Abrams spams you with CGI spectacle is, again, so unoriginal and badly done that you just become numb. There are some beautiful sights in the film...but the space stuff is terrible. And, in Star Wars, that's just not acceptable. Like it or lump it, a good portion of what made the originals great was the use of models to make some of the best space action ever put to film. And I would say the end space battle in Return of the Jedi is STILL the gold standard for exciting space battles committed to film. I have no idea what was going on in most of the space scenes - JJ thinks throwing the camera upside down, or throwing the angle around makes these scenes work, but really once again he's just 'doing stuff' because he doesn't have any vision or eye for framing at all. He shoots stuff like a university film student would. On too much caffeine.

Overall, this film will likely keep your attention, but your ability to like it will be down to how much you can keep an open mind, let it off its various inadequacies, and unoriginality, and your appreciation of nostalgia. I enjoyed some scenes. Adam Driver was awesome as usual. The other actors did pretty good with what they had.

But, disappointment on a grand scale is the feeling I was left with, even despite very low expectations going in.

review:
40 years worth of the story OF Anakin Slywalker ...all for nothing. He ends up having no effect on anything. For those of you who are into star wars only in the last 10 or so years...it's ANAKINS story. "Return of the Jedi" is actually ANAKIN returning to being a Jedi again, it's not about Luke, mind blower to many people to learn. And what's it lead to? title: Expert reviewers should get their heads examined
review:
Have been a SW fans ever since the big spaceship crowded the screen in 1970s. Having watched a number of the intervening sequels on DVD, decided to venture into the theatre for this run, based off all the "expert" reviews in the newspapers.

This was an unmitigated disaster, from the opening sequence with Kylo Ren to all the scenes of people running around and the numerous sub-plots with new characters.

I could see JJ Abrams trying to string together elements of the original Episode IV with the "Cantina" scene replicated, and also the Death Star run at the end, but they all seem to be thrown in just for reminiscence rather than any logic.

title: Scripting under the influence
review: Clearly the makers of the film were high and never bothered reanalyzing the plot. Highly predictable moments & some crap that isn't explained or makes no sense.... Still fun in a way

title: How did it come to this?
review:
If you like the new trilogy so far then this is for you. But for a lot of older fans like me, Disney's handing of Star Wars has been a disaster that risks destroying the franchise altogether. Now JJ's bookend failure is complete. This latest effort does not move away from a rinse and repeat formula like that used for Force Awakens. Not does it rectify the total mess of Last Jedi. Rise of Skywalker boasts non-stop loud and shiny effects wrapped around a paper thin, stupid plot which desperately calls on a "fan service" lifeline. But what true fans would want something this silly and insulting?
With all the millions of dollars available at their disposal plus the "talent" on board you have to ask yourself... is this really the best they can come up with? Fortunately the last 3 attempts to continue the saga have been so poor it makes it easy to forget they happened and go back to Return of the Jedi as a fitting end to a proper story.

title: The past if officially dead....Disney killed it.
review: There movie was mediocre at best. Another example of how George Lucas just got lucky with the original and how Disney does what Disney does. Takes a classic, tries to fix what was broken, and ends up breaking it more. There is nothing about this movie that makes sense. The timelines are all screwed up, and characters made famous in the originals are completely negated with one character reveal today. WTF Disney. We understand you are trying to fix the atrocities the are the prequel movies, but this is your solution? At least make your story make sense. Better yet, you should have left well enough alone. If you want to make more Star Wars movies then do it like Rogue one. That was incredibly well done in my opinion and actually made you hate the empire and brought a true understanding of why Darth Vader was feared. Rogue one proved you don't need Luke Skywalker to make a good Star Wars movie.

title: The reviews/ratings are inflated
review:
This is literally my first review, only now have I ever felt so compelled to write one. RT has joined the dark side considering its audience review score has been fixed to 86% despite an influx of 7,000 new ratings. Lol.

I want to lead with 2 apologies, one for those of you who actually spent money on this and the second one is because this may come off as a rant/conplaint. That is not my intention, I actually do love Star Wars. Luckily, I had a gift card from last christmas which has been one of very few saving graces for this experience.

CGI: 9/10 SFX: 9/10 Score: 1/10 (Not Star Wars imo) Writing: 2/10 Acting: 7/10 Originality: 2/10

TLDR: Jumps from scene to scene. Plot is contrived. Retcons parts of TLJ. MASSIVE amount of exposition. Recycled plot points. Action throughout, decent saber battles. Plethora of force used but then not used when the plot asked for it(Fly to the top of Death Star or scale it by hand?) The dialogue is cheesy, whenever Lando spoke, my stomach churned. Deus Ex Machina in everyother scene (idk how many times somebody can get saved by a ship, just in time) The music did not fit at all. I'm not sure why this movie is the way it is, it gives me Game Of Thrones Season 8 vibes, so maybe it was rushed? I think a trilogy needs to be written from beginning to end with a full idea in mind and to me this movie seems half-baked at best. The actors involved tried but it simply fell flat for me.
