This film has to find the finish a saga when all of the story arcs set up by Abrams in TFA had been destroyed in the TLJ. Meaning that that the third movie was always going to be hard no matter what. JJ coming in late in the day for this film didn't help but it would have been a better movie if he was at the helm for the 3 of them.

I think that this film is fine and could have been better and thats fine. This is not only a better film than TLJ, the middle movie should always carry the story and when it failed to do this they had a lot to fit in to 2 hours and 40 mins.

Of course I would have liked more but all the questions I had were answered and even if is was obvious what they outcome would have been. But the action piece are great and the stuff between Rey and Ren is Strong. So i can live with this but I wish they had less CGI Leia in this and more time was spent of the dialog.

Still this is not the worse star wars movie and it is not the best. It is fine and I will gladly watch this again.

review:

People complaining that the story told in this new trilogy was not of epic proportions, was due to the fact that ep VIII ruined that possibility. Lucky for us, JJ found a way to stop the bleeding and give us a very entertaining ep IX with very nice surprises, great tributes to the whole saga, great chemistry among the whole cast and a very suitable conclusion for many characters and for the whole story that began with The Phantom Menace.
The most important ingredient for any movie is its story. Is this story what JJ Abrams thought when he wrote ep VII? Possibly, yes. And if they had developed that story throughout ep VIII and IX, then a much more compelling saga we would have had.
I believe that this episode rivals in entertainment with ep IV and V. So IMHO, you are in for a treat,

title: Old fans just cant let go of the past.
review:
If you are old enough to remember going to see one of the original trilogy movies after waiting in what seemed like lines that spanned for miles, you're probably old enough now that you have children of your own that are about the same age as you when you first experienced Star Wars on the big screen. I took my daughter to see this movie as her first big screen Star Wars experience. When I saw the look of amazement and wonder on her face that reminded me of mine, I knew Star Wars franchise gained a new fan. The conservative viewers will never be satisfied because nothing will compare to their childhood experience. The more open minded viewer will see this movie for what it is. Entertainment. Action sequences were great, special effects were great, costumes were great. The story was about the ending of the original Skywalker Saga and beginning a new one.
Of course there will never be as epic a reveal as the "I am your father" in any movie ever. To measure any recent or future reveals or surprises to the Vader-Luke surprise is by default, a set up to dissapointment.
As my daughter walked out of the theater asking when we can see it again, I saw that the director and producers accomplished what they set out to do. Make a new fan, and make this old fan a happy and proud father.

title: Critics are WAY too critical, AMAZING ending for an AMAZING series!
review:
As a HUGE fan of the Star Wars Universe ever since I was a child, these movies have a sweet spot in my heart.

I think The Rise Of Skywalker is an AMAZING ending to an AMAZING series. I found my self jaw dropped, emotional, excited, laughing, crying, on the edge of my seat, I loved the fight against good and evil, the secret relatives, the rise of the hero and I'm going to say it, the NOSTALGIA. It brought a stronger and deeper connected between the old movies and the new series that was so beautiful. Like how the fight scene between Anakin and Obi-Wan in Revenge of The Sith paralleled between the fight scene between Rey and Kylo Ren. Where the lava represented death and the water represented life and in Revenge of The Sith, Anakin is finally turned to the dark side, but whereas in Rise, Kylo Ren is finally turned to the good side. I could name 20 more beautiful parallels and nostalgic scenes, but you get the point! Just think, what would Star Wars be without those attributes? That is what makes Star Wars, Star Wars. So for critics to say there is too much nostalgia, or too much resemblance between the older movies is like saying there is too much Star Wars in the STAR WARS movie!!

Not only was the movie emotional In so many levels, it was cinematically stunning!! When you look at a movie from a filmmaking perspective, the amount of people and work it took to create something as beautiful as that deserves a 5 star review ALONE! And no highly judgmental critic can fight against that.

The redemption of Kylo Ren was by far the most powerful part of the whole movie and frankly, the whole series. Throughout the movies, Ben is just a young boy, fighting the demons inside his head. The amount of pain and suffering that you see Ben go through then to FINALLY see him free of it and turn into a loving and self sacrificing man deserves another 5 stars ALONE! His story is inspiring, moving and so FREAKING EMOTIONAL! It shows you that it's never too late and we all have the strength to fight against the evil inside of us.

Sure, I do have a couple complaints against the movie, but they are only complaints because I wished for them to happen, like how I wish we saw a scene of Lando Calrision seeing Lea before she died. I feel like that scene was very much needed. But it does look like Lando was able to see her, because he was already there when Po came back to the planet and talked to Lando. So inside, I like to believe he did, but still, I wish that scene was in the movie. Maybe its in the deleted scenes, who knows..

AND I wish in the last scene, when Rey sees Lea and Luke as ghosts, I truly wish she saw all of the past Jedi's or at least the main ones, like Yoda, Obi-Wan, Anakin and Ben as well. I feel like that would have been the perfect ending, since she is connected to them all. But these are just things I wish that were in the film, and like Abrams said, you cant please everyone, especially in a finale and you shouldn't even try when making a film. And for that, I understand and respect Abrams and Rian for taking the journey to even give us this new series. We should accept what was given, not just so we can be at peace, but so we can truly admire and love the story for what it is and not what it isn't.

ALSO!!! I would like to point out how I think that the movie is called "Rise Of Skywalker" not only talking about the rise of Rey Skywalker but also talking about the rise of Ben Skywalker!! Yes, Ben's last name is Solo but his mother, Lea is Skywalker, so in my opinion, Ben is the true Rise of Skywalker since he rises to the good side and is finally free of evil in the end!!!

And its the huge connections and deep meanings like this that make this movie get 5 stars. The beauty, power, emotion and hope of this movie outweighs all of the stupid critics who are just too judgmental.

For me this hugely underplayed the return of such a big and intriguing character.

Next, the sentence 'I made Snoke' ruined all of the time people such as myself had spent thinking about where the mysterious sith lord from The Last Jedi had come from and why he was for the most part very powerful with the dark side of the force. If the emperor knew of this force sensitive grandchild of his it seems very odd that a man of his intelligence, power and resources couldn't get his hands on Rey sooner. To think he had the time to accomplish everything that he did but not contain that situation seems highly odd to me.

Along with the quick throw in of the fact that Leia has a ligtsaber and is a very capable force user was a wasted opportunity, the waves and scenery being the most exciting thing about Rey and Kylo Rens duel (far better duels in the prequel trilogy) and the life swapping moment between Rey and Ben at the end I think on the whole this was a disappointing end to the story.

title: It had heavy lifting to do and it held up
review:
I would honestly give this movie around an 8/10 but because of all the unfair low ratings I rated it higher. First thing to understand is that this movie has a lot of pressure and heavy lifting to do, including concluding the new trilogy, concluding the Skywalker saga as a whole, and bringing the momentum of the story back after "The Last Jedi" slowed it down significantly. I will say though, the overall problem with the trilogy is that the story, I have to assume, was not clearly written from the beginning, hence why the change of directors had an awkward shift and we were got to see two different versions of a story at the same time, which was not pleasant. However, here are the positives and negatives of this movie, "The Rise of Skywalker."

Positives 1. Rey's story arch is developed very well, and we get to see the conflict of the dark and light in her and they tie this in well with being Darth Sidious' granddaughter. Her scenes with Kylo Ren are the best scenes in the movie, because we get to see their relationship develop more and the connection they have through the force. Their duel is the peek of the trilogy and, in my opinion, in the top duels in Star Wars, because we finally get to see how powerful both Rey and Ren are in the force

2. Kylo Ren finally finds redemption. We see this over arching story throughout the trilogy of him dealing with the guilt of killing his father. He comes to terms with his guilt after his mother touches him through the force and then he confronts his father through a memory and gathers the strength to do what he wanted to do since the beginning.

3. Finding out that Palpatine is all the Sith is an awesome conclusion to the saga and the "rule of two" which states there can only be two Sith Lords fits in to this conclusion. ( the disappointing part of this is that Palpatine never fully explains it)

4. The Visuals are amazing. The lightsaber fights are epic. The unexplored parts of the galaxy are visualized well. C3PO and Chewy are still enjoyable. The planets look better than ever. The starship battles are pretty cool to say the least.

Negatives

1. I'm okay with not explaining some things that are not essential to the story and later explaining them in books, comics, etc. But it's not okay when it's essential to the story. How is Rey Palpatine's granddaughter? This is the main question, but there are manymore, especially about Palpatine that probably should have been explained so that we're not scratching our heads till it's explained in issue 13 of "Palpatine."

2. Finn's character has no development besides the fact that he thinks he's force sensitive. Since the moment he took off his helmet in "The Force Awakens," his character has been flat and not interesting, especially for being a stormtrooper.

3. Leia's death is forced. I don't know if it was because they didn't want to mess with her scenes or add CGI to her but I don't really care what it was because it felt like they just threw that part in the scene because they needed to get rid of the character. There are many other routes they could have taken but this was route was not a good one.

4. The final battle was a bitter sweet moment. It was going sweet till a little before the final confrontation between Rey and Palpatine. It was anti-climactic. We see that Palpatine has reached is full power and Rey, with the Jedi within her, reaches her full power. And then... SURPRISE Palpatine is defeated by his own electric. Seriously? No final duel? No epic music? Think about it this way, a big bad guy is built up for 8 movies and when he finally reaches his power he is defeated by his granddaughter blocking his electric Meanwhile, the battle above reaches its anti-climatic ending as well.

Overall, I enjoyed the the movie, and there will always be things we think they could've done better on.

title: Rise of Skywalker not as Bad a The Last Jedi, Not in the League of Empire Strikes Back
review:
The Good: The Last Jedi was a chaotic mess and off Yoda-brand. Rise of Skywalker is not that nearly that bad.

The Bad: This movie is forgettable, because it did not have a discrete and memorable villain. Yes, there was good and bad, but not focused. I was not fully engaged, but I did not want to walk out either (like in ). It filled some time.

A great movie has the viewer loving and hating, agreeing and disagreeing, predicting, fearing and hoping. That is, engaged.

Compare. Remember Yoda, Luke and Darth Vader? Clear good guys, clear bad guys. Focused. Unforgettable characteristics: Yoda's philosophy, Darth Vader's ominous breathing. The movie characters resonated. They were and remain unforgettable, in fact, they are legend. Moreover, they taught us something. "I don't believe it," said Luke, "And, that is why you fail," retorted Yoda. Classic movies; more than movies, works of true art, with blended core philosophy. The corrupting "Dark Side," like Tolkien's One Ring, feels good, while it corrupts.

But, Disney's caught up in the present social message that is adopted by its new leadership. In The Lion King non-animated, Disney even removed the plot-critical Rafiki stick strike, "Yes, the past can hurt, but you can either run from it or learn from it" plot shift statement. (The animated scene is too plot-important to be an oversight. Noting the entire me-too is past-based, not ungrounded, just past-based.) Then Rise of Skywalker slides in a same-sex kiss at the end, which was no less gratuitous than an unnecessary nude scene. (Giving an intended audience a little something not required for a substantive purpose...)

Then there's the little issues. The comic relief did not work in two ways: first, not enough pressure built up to require it (see "engagement" above), then the comic statements themselves didn't work on their own merit. Compare Harrison Ford's banter with Princess Leia over kissing a rogue, or the Wookie insults. Moreover, Rise of Skywalker failed clearly to tie the loose ends regarding the characters and chaotic mess of The Last Jedi.

Another missed opportunity. The problem with Disney is the same issue that plagues successful musicians who can release a bad album only because they can do it. No one else can do it without critical mass momentum. Any new artist would fail. But, momentum has its advantages. Earned momentum certainly, but that does not excuse the work itself.

There can be value in seeing the production on the big screen, but, from a plot perspective, waiting for television is fine. Ultimately, this movie is forgettable.

title: Everything comes full circle
review:
Star Wars has always been a ride worth enjoying. It's full of hope, redemption, family, embracing who you are and not letting your past dictate your future, what can occur when you allow the darkness in you to be control you and what happens when you embrace the light. There is just so much in Star Wars it's hard to put into words everything involved. Do all the episodes always measure up to their predecessors? Absolutely not. While I enjoy to an extent the prequels even I admit they are flawed bogged down with bad writing and too much cgi. But I still like to watch them because they are Star Wars and I was there for the ride.

Coming to this present movie The Rise of Skywalker let me first start out in saying I absolutely did not like The Last Jedi. This did not come right away I watched it once but I felt so off about it I didn't feel satisfied. Things implied in The Force Awakens never occurred and it was riddled in plot holes. I watched it a second time and realized it was copy of ESB and ROtJ. A really bad one at that which ignored the fundamentals of Star Wars and it's past movies. It wasn't at all original except for some stuff here and there. I was about to leave the Star Wars franchise for good.

And then this movie happened...

This movie took a jump in a new direction and headed back to the original course of The Force Awakens. It established a new and original story amongst the sequel trilogy. It takes you to the edge of your seat throughout a thrilling adventure filled with many surprises and exciting moments. It manages to also respect it's past and treat those from the original and even prequels with respect. This is definitely the story Abrams was trying to tell through The Force Awakens. Foreshadowing from that movie play into this one give a flowing narrative. It might be argued that it is to quick and has inconsistent but honestly it tells a more cohesive story than The Last Jedi did.

It takes the viewers an epic adventure and explores various places and new situations. While paying attention to it's roots and racing forwards towards the future.

This movie at heart contains a lot of self sacrifice, send offs and an implication of the new future. Who are you going to be? What is your legacy will you let your past heritage dictate who you will be? While this is a send off to the original crew and the end of Skywalker story it doesn't just spit in the face of that legacy but rather let's that legacy build the foundation of the future. Which is why Rey's last words in the movie honor the past in so many ways.

A lot of the movie focuses on the Resistance picking up the pieces of their remaining crew and continuing the fight against the first order and Rey struggling with her identity.

Rey isn't satisfied with Kylo Ren's words that she's a nobody and nothing special. It's almost like she shouldn't exist at all. And while people say it dismisses expectations and gives it's own roots. It's nice and all but we need to pay attention to the mythos of Star Wars. Rey is strong in the force and no one questions from that why? She had no training in the beginning and yet she could hold her own against a trained force user. It was impractical since Jedi and Sith alike are trained from a young age to use their abilities. The only way she could be this way is if she was connected to some one from the cannon who has strong force abilities. The fact remains that the foreshadowing is in The Force Awakens that implies more to her. I think Rey's reveal for a heritage makes sense. Let's be honest she was so powerful in the force and Kylo was so focused on her that there was definitely something happening there. Throwing that all away just takes away from the story as a whole. If you are telling a story you shouldn't ignore foreshadowing if it was implied.

The fact remains that despite her heritage she needed to move past it and make her own destiny. For me this was the overarching storyline of this movie. Recognizing where you came from and establishing who you choose to be in the end.

This movie is chockfull of emotional moments, heartfelt send offs and returns it was just a thrill to watch it felt like a Star Wars story and it played out beautifully. It felt like a Star Wars story it took the current sequel story and brought it full circle while honoring and respecting the past it came from. It had the adventure, the lightsaber duels, the struggled between the jedi and the sith, and a fight for the future of galaxy. It felt right and a great ride the entire way through.

At the theater every one in the audience cheered at the beginning and the ending of the film. It was packed theater and every one had their various moments to cheer and gasp at the scenes.

It was definitely everything you could want and nothing you'd expect.

Will I say it's perfect no it's not perfect and it's not the best Star Wars movie I've ever seen. However putting it against The Force Awakens and The Last Jedi it was the best of the group for me. It feels original in so many ways and that in itself is remarkable after Force Awakens makes me wonder if this was Abrams plan all along what he'd been leading too. It tells a story that moves away from the Skywalker legacy while at the same time establishing a new connection that honors it's past.

I realize some will say it pandered to Star Wars fans but I disagree. The story was always for it's viewers. It has a legacy that has been around for 42 years and to ignore that and end in a direction that merely is played out to divert expectations doesn't work.

Also Chewie getting the medal was never to me a fixed point. It's Han's medal which Leia had been holding onto. Now that both of them are gone it's the thing gives Chewie a memorial of sorts to their legacy specifically Han Solo his best friend and partner. It wasn't about Chewie getting a medal he deserves it was about getting something that will remind him always of his best friend.

I now look back on this initial review and I'll say I've changed my mind about The Last Jedi sure there were things I didn't like but it actually helped make this movie and built on its predecessor if you pay attention to the ending. I will never like where Luke was taken because there is no solid reason for his actions in there. But I did appreciate what they were trying to do between Rey and Kylo. And Poe did need to grow through the movie to be who he is now. So I'm okay with The Last Jedi now thanks to this movie.

Every one is entitled to their own opinion but for me I'm satisfied with the outcome.

Thank you J.J. Abrams for honoring Star Wars and keeping the legacy alive for this last movie.

title: How did we get to this???????
review:
What on earth did I just watch???? There is so much to process I know I'm gonna miss things out.............there is a LOT going on in this film, whether that be bad or good!!!

Quick set up.........I grew up on the prequels they have a special place in my heart but they aren't that great and I can live with that........The original trilogy is the gold standard for trilogies in my opinion!!! I thought that TFA was good but just A New Hope remade slightly differently............However I really really liked TLJ, yes I know I'm in the minority............loved its brave and bold choices even if I didn't like all of them.

Now we have The Rise of Skywalker...........I still think its a terrible title now like I did when it was announced. Lets start with the positives there are some really really good parts in this mess of a film.

Daisy Ridley and Adam Driver..........whenever either of them or both of them are on screen.......the film is great !!! The story of Kylo Ren and Rey has been the best part of the sequel trilogy in all of the films............and Episode 9 doesn't disappoint!! Their chemistry is really good and there is real character arc/ development..............loved both of their performances !!!

The force connection between them is emotional and the heart beat of the film. It is best shown when they are fighting...........sort of what Rian Johnson started to play with in Episode 8.........for me its fresh , new and exciting...........although it stretches the boundaries of Star Wars lore. I think the endings to both characters was fitting...........Rey, revealed as a Palpatine and killing the Emperor......winning essentially............but the revival of Ben Solo and the death of Kylo Ren was the best part of the film for me. I had no idea Harrison Ford was in the film...........extremely good part.

Thats pretty much it for the things I liked..........

Now the things I didn't like..............this film has way way too much going on and it doesn't really deliver on any of them fully. It is trying to be a sequel to TFA whilst ignoring TLJ..........but also trying to connect to the original and prequel trilogies. This film is trying to be Episodes 8 and 9 at the say time..................who is to blame for this J.J Abrams......no........Rian Johnson.....no..................Kathleen Kennedy 100% yes. This film demonstrates that there was never a plan for this trilogy from the outset............HOW is that aloud to happen?????

The story is weak and thin...............and all over the place. There is no stakes or tension in the film because whenever any is presented it is instantly taken away because the film is moving so fast and needs it to be resolved........and well characters flip and change their minds or are in the right place at the right time. Keri Russell's character, one second wants to kill Poe.............then the next is helping the group and giving up her one way ticket to freedom?!?!?!?

There is a lot in the film that doesn't add up, characters just appear from know where really quickly or find out what there meant to do instantaneously. I understand the Kylo and Rey stuff cause well I can buy thats the force doing that............but everyone else no just no...........also Palpatine back no explanation, he just didn't die?!?!? How does this connect to the Skywalker saga really, and the story of Anakin Skywalker the chosen one???!?! Does Rey's power undermine Anakin/Vader??? The Final Order......how so many ships, how did all the people live on that planet?!? Planet killing star destroyers really!?!??!

Finally there was a huge huge miss opportunity...........we heard their voices but I desperately wanted to see them. I am pretty confident I heard, Ewan McGregor, Hayden Christensen, Liam Neeson, Frank Oz and Samuel L Jackson's voices telling Rey to rise up..........I so desperately wanted force ghosts, It would have connected all the films together better...........a small couple of minutes not much!!! I'm so bummed

Overall I'm trying to be kind to this film 65% out of 100 its ok/average and that is me being kind...............there are few things I liked about the film but those things I really really liked. However the majority was boring and forgettable, the re-watchability of this film is probably gonna be the lowest of the sequel trilogy for me. Episode 9 is the worst out of 7,8,9..........I'm sorry. Does this now mean that the prequels will be looked back in a better light?!?!? I'd take Revenge of the Sith over any of these any day!?!? What a sad end ?!?!

title: Solid though familiar end to the series
review:
It seems that with every sequel to a film, the odds of infuriating series fans grows exponentially. Episode VII was lambasted for being a retread, Episode VIII was slammed for going too far astray from Star Wars' mythology, and IX has been eviscerated for going back to the VII retread approach. So you could say Star Wars sequels are a lose-lose proposition if not that they all make tons of money and are thus, ultimately, a win-win.

IX continues on with the story of conflicted chosen one Rey and conflicted evil one Kylo Ren against the backdrop of the approach of a final, obliterating Sith attack. The characters wander here and there seeking this and that and fighting this one and that one until they reach the big finish. Which is pretty much the description for every Star Wars movie.

The path of the conflicted duo is interesting, as are their long-distance battles. There are some nifty action scenes and the last half hour is big and exciting and dramatic.

On the downside, the movie's determination to include all the iconic characters from the original trilogy is nothing but strained and awkward fan service. And using cast-off footage of Leia to shoehorn her into the film doesn't work that well, since her responses are controlled not by the logic of the story or the character but by what footage they had on hand.

While I would have preferred the fresher approach of VIII, I understand the appeal of ending the series as mindlessly as it started, and of erring on the side of sentimentality; this series has been a big part of a lot of people's lives, after all.

While there were weak moments, overall I enjoyed this movie, and thought it was a solid ending for a series that has gone on forever. And with that story finally done, offshoots like The Mandalorian TV series can take the Star Wars world in all sorts of interesting directions.

title: I guess people are entitled to their opinions...
review:
I'll preface this by saying I've been a big Star Wars fan since the original release in 1978. I've seen all the movies multiple times, read some of the fiction and watched the Clone Wars, Rebels and Mandalorian through and through. My son and I saw it today with no expectations but with a keen awareness of all the hate this is getting. We walked out after it was over and could not understand for a minute what all the bad reviews were about. It was a very good movie.

The pacing was quick for a Star Wars movie in the beginning, at least for the movies along the main trilogy line. A friend said the pacing toward the start was similar to Solo. I agree with that, but thought it was even faster. Not a big deal for me as I had no problem following everything from start to finish, and it found a rhythm fairly quickly.

I have a hard time contextualizing it within the structure of the first 8 movies. It feels like it's own trilogy, and I don't even think I could rank it along side the other films. It's that big in scope. It stands on it's own as an epic, but you need the rest of the anthology as primer. There are some absolutely jaw dropping moments, as well as some very emotional scenes. I had a tear in my eye at least 3 times.

Long story short, don't believe the low reviews. There's plenty of character development, especially around the origins of Rey and her connection to Ben, as well as with Leah and the deeper underlying influence of Palpatine across the entire story arch for the series. I don't by into the argument that The Last Jedi was retconned for a second. If anything, it was fully realized. I also took no issue that some characters were passed over. They had more screen time than they needed and fell outside of the core story arch anyway.

It isn't perfect, but with the exception of ESB, none of the Star Wars movies were. ESB set a very high bar. With RoS, there was a moment or two where I questioned some of the action (I need to see it again as I may have missed something), and a few of the digital facial reconstructions fell deep down the uncanny valley, albeit fleetingly (hello young Leah with a light saber).

Anyone saying they walked out of this is either a troll or needs to have their head examined. Anyone else rating this lower than a 7 needs to get a grip and learn how to pay attention.

title: Finally it's over....

And the fans are right to be upset...100% right! But the blame does not fall on Disney. Disney does what any mega conglomerate does: it values money above any and all things. And JJ does what any average director does: he makes his bosses happy so that he may continue to work in the future. For me, its plain to see that the demise of this franchise falls squarely on one man... For you see....a long time ago in a galaxy far, far away....one man grew his vision into the most imaginative and appealing franchises in movie making history. And then for reasons we will never know, he turned his back on that beloved creation and auctioned it off to the highest bidder After that, Star Wars existed no more. The franchise ended unfinished, with only 6 movies instead of the 9 that he promised.

Star Wars The Rise of Skywalker is the culmination of one man selling off his dream....

Stay away from this one folks....'cuz if George Lucas can walk away from his dream than so can you....

Go in with a blank slate and try to enjoy the movie. As a huge Star Wars Fan, I am more than pleased and will definitely go see it again. title: Reviews lost in politics
review:
In a time where we will judge a movie and start slating purely based on a trailer that we saw 6 months ago it is hard to get a genuine reaction to a film.

Take "The rise of skywalker" for instance. Two years ago we were treated to the marmite that was "The last jedi", critic adored it and fans hated it in equal measure, unfortunately I came in the latter although I found more to like on a 2nd viewing. Trolls rose out of the shadows and grownups overreacted, threw temper tantrums and declared their childhood destroyed. Two years on here we are with "the rise of skywalker" and once again we are in the marmite phase only this time its the critics who are getting angry.

Is the film perfect? Not by a long shot. The first 30 minutes feels rushed as we race fro maguffin to maguffin but there is a point where the film levels out and I finally found myself unclenching and enjoying the film.

I really enjoyed "the force awakens" and hoped for a similar feel. Unfortunately it felt like JJ had a lot of boxes to tick however with the detour and scrapping of future plot point courtesy of Rian Johnson, and the tragic passing of Carrie Fisher, JJ has been handed ball of wool that he needs to untangle and all things considered he does a pretty good job.

I would have loved it had he been a bit braver in relation to certain characters surviving/dying. Some of the new characters are instantly forgettable but that's more of an issue with them being underwritten and I feel like a few missteps were taken with "the force" but I guess they can do what they like, they're writing it, it's up to me to get on board.

Is this a 1/10 defiantly not, those who rank it so are your trolls, is it a 10/10, no it is not. I'm just glad I saw it and made my own opinions and I hope you all do the same.

title: A lot happens but overall very good
review:
I thought this film was very good. It answered all the questions set up in The Force Awakens, the acting was good, there was a lot references to the past films, the music was brilliant, Palpatine was menacing, the main characters had good chemistry, Rey and Kylo Renn's story has a good conclusion, there's were a few twists, the lightsaber fights weren't over the top like Episode 3 and it looked brilliant.

To me it seems that Disney realised that while some people like The Last Jedi, the majority of the audience and fans really hated it (probably when Solo did a lot worse financially than they expected). As a result, they basically told JJ Abrams to fix it and make a film full of fan service that pretty much deals with all of The Last Jedi criticisms and answers every lingering question. The best description I have seen is that The Rise Of Skywalker feels like a 4 hour movie squeezed in to 2 hours. In hindsight, Disney should have given JJ Abrams the whole trilogy so he would have been able to tell a consistent story. Some story arcs felt underdeveloped, such as stormtroopers turning good, and other parts felt shoehorned in to try and explain everything. Snoke is a good example. Originally it felt like he was going to be an original character with an interesting back story but now it's revealed that it was Palpatine all along. This only happened as Rian Johnson killed him off. He really should have been the main villain throughout as bringing back Palpatine lessens the impact of Vader sacrificing himself to kill Palpatine and save Luke. With Marvel, Disney plan quite far in advance but with Star Wars it felt like they made it up as they went along.

Overall, I think if they had split this film in to two films and got rid of The Last Jedi then the sequel trilogy could have been much better. The last scene is a very nice way to end the Skywalker saga though.

title: Fun, visually pretty popcorn movie
review:
I don't know what movies most reviewers are basing their expectations on, but if you go into the cinema expecting a visually polished, nicely paced, entertaining fantasy-in-space action flick, that's exactly what you're going to get. Is it the best or most original in its genre? No. Is it easy to sit through the 2,5 hours this thing is long? Yes. Does it suck you into that very typical Star Wars universe of the first movies through visuals, music and humour? Absolutely.

Verdict: the plot won't stand up to close scrutiny, but if you turn off the over-analyzing part of your brain and accept that plot-holes and goofs actually add to the charm of the thing, you're in for a very enjoyable night out.

title: The best of the new trilogy for me
review: I'm disheartened to see all the negative reviews on here as I had a really good time with Rise of Skywalker. My expectations were low after The Last Jedi and some of the negative hype but the film was a success for me and made me feel like Star Wars had been redeemed by the end of it. title: Plays it safe and is consequently very forgettable
review:
I feel like if a film is 140 minutes long then it needs to have a lot of depth and layers to it. 'The Dark Knight' for example had about 5 or 6 story lines that all could have justified their own movie. 'Star Wars: Episode IX - The Rise of Skywalker' felt like it had one story line that it just expanded out and bloated to the run time it got. I expect more from a 'Star Wars' movie. I feel like I should almost be overwhelmed by the end and need to see it again (and possibly again) to fully appreciate it. That was not the case here.

The films looks great. There is one location that features at the beginning and end of the movie that really looked especially terrific and perfectly sets the mood for the scenes that take place there. There are also some decent action sequences sprinkled in here and there, but they do feel too few and far between. The humour in the film rarely lands. It always feels very forced and just isn't particularly funny.

My biggest gripe with the film though would be how safe it decides to play it. I understand this is a Disney film and so it has be pretty formulaic, but come on at least through us a bone or two. There is no element of this story that I will remember a week from now. Nothing that blew me away or made me give it a second thought. I got chills when 'Star Wars' flashed up on the screen at the beginning of the movie and that was literally the highlight of my entire viewing experience. This isn't a bad film, it's just an extremely bland and uninspired one.

title: Incredible final chapter
review: Star Wars: Episode IX - The Rise of Skywalker is an action packed, consistently very funny and extremely emotionally satisfying conclusion to the Skywalker saga. Daisy Ridley, John Boyega and Oscar Isaac all give incredible performances once again and have excellent chemistry. Adam Driver is also incredible as usual. Newcomers Keri Russell, Naomi Ackie and Richard E. Grant are really good. Billy Dee Williams is excellent in another effortlessly charismatic performance and Ian McDirmid is great. Carrie Fisher's scenes are used effectively and Anthony Daniels is fantastic with much more screen time than the previous two installments. It's fast paced and consistently thrilling throughout the entirety of it's run time. John Williams' music is perfect as usual and J. J. Abrams' direction is incredible and the film is visually stunning with consistently excellent CG. It's got plenty of fan service that works, provides some much needed answers and comes to an extremely emotional and satisfying conclusion.

title: Best Of A Bad Bunch. Regurgitated Storylines.
review:
The original Star Wars trilogy is swashbuckling, boy meets girl, good versus bad, sexy heroes and heroines fun. It was full of imagination/creativity and verve.

The latest Star Wars trilogy has taken a rather large damp cloth to the essence of the original. Why? Okay:

This film is the best of the latest trilogy & that's not saying much. It chops and flips, flashes & flops.

title: JJ, you hack
review:
Wow, what a mess... but a fitting ending to this botched trilogy. Well done, JJ and Rian Johnson, you made the prequel trilogy look masterpieces compared to this garbage. These guys... While Rian has vision, it's not true to Star Wars, and JJ is just a hack without any vision whatsoever so he just copies and pastes everything from earlier movies. I'm so tired of seeing the same ideas, visuals and scenes over and over again. Oh, and Disney, how on Earth is it possible that there wasn't a definitive arc for the trilogy? I'm just baffled by this level of incompetence.

Plenty of reviewers pointed out all the inconsistencies before me. It's perfectly clear that the filmmakers have no idea or don't care about Star Wars, it seems as if they haven't even watched the previous movies. But as filmmakers they could have at least made a movie that followed the rules of filmmaking. Let the scenes breathe a little bit for Christ's sake, add some conversations or something! It's like watching a music video that was cut together randomly. You blink for a millisecond and the cast is in a totally different location without any transition. I bet Disney was scrambling like crazy to finish this thing in time.

They are going to teach this trilogy in film school, and not for the reasons Disney would hope.

Kathleen Kennedy is out, but unfortunately it's too late to undo what happened to the most beloved movie franchise. It's ruined forever.

title: Tie Fight: SWe9 vs The Room #Cerb
review:
Disclosure: this is not a bot-post (hence my nickname tagged in the title). I watched the film in its entirety last night, focused, and without interruptions. Also, I've been a fan of the franchise since 1990. This review is by 'Cerberus' (AKA Cerb). All information is my complete honest opinion. That said.....

I have to start by explaining that this film is so bad, it revealed how review systems - have issues with false reviews, & the likelihood of bot accounts being used to boost scores for sequels of popular franchises such as this and the Birds of Prey film (as the most recent examples). Hence the disclosure. Also, I guess somebody needs to remind everyone: films (entertainment) are and always have been ART; acting, effects, story, script - it is ALL supposed to be ART. That being said, Rise of Skywalker has NONE of the artistic concepts mentioned. Not ONE.

Effects: Honestly this is the least relevant concept to me when scoring films because well, these days even Indi films have bare minimum capabilities to include digital effects and thus also made body costumes (like a puppet or seseme street character) obsolete. However I have to say I am shocked and frankly appalled to notice this film had one particular scene where Rey encounters a monstrous alien snake, which HAS TO BE either pupet or costume, unless they were using the cheapest software they could find and get away with using. The fight scenes were ridiculous and illogical more than ever. I thought episode 8s bomber scene was unbelievably moronic but 9s is just.... So so so bad. To give them some sort of credit though at least the extras weren't swinging and falling at/over nothing because of bad choreography; instead in 9,they don't have extra enemies. For example, our heroes infiltrate Kylo Rens ship, landing nice n soft (unchallenged) in one of many many conveniently open parking spots in the hanger, only to be casually checked by 2 troopers (motivation literally casual) then I guess 2 additional troopers who were killed immediately after but never seen so maybe there weren't ANY there and they were shooting at a wall for all we know... I mean WOW.

Story: Palpatine should not be relevant anymore after episode 6 (I don't think I need to elaborate since there are countless reviews saying the same thing basically). The bulk of the movie is about Rey getting an object called the Wayfinder (which there are 2; Kylo found the first one in the first scene of the movie (more on that in a moment). These Wayfinders and a dagger which Rey STUMBLES UPON UNINTENTIONALLY & UNEXPECTEDLY after she and her friends literally just finish a speeder chase (the jet pack scene in the trailer) and crash in ck?]sand.... annnnnd drop into a CAVE where said dagger is found among the remains of its previous holder whom seemed to have a small backstory to him but felt like it was cut and forgotten (I can only assume). This dagger has sith writing on it which NOBODY KNOWS except 3pO and it just so happens there was a law passed at some point apparently that outlawed translation of siad language, so the new objective instantly becomes to erase/reset his mind so that law doesn't exist (basically). Finally I have to elaborate on the concluding line "Rey Skywalker". This line spits on the pre-disney trilogies. Rey is in NO WAY a Skywalker. Not by relation nor metaphorical or anything other. They could have AT LEAST (AAAATTTTT LEEEAST) have her say Rey PALPATINE considering he wanted her to win (kill him) because apparently by doing so, he would possess HER youthful body instead of his century spanning decaying self (he needed an upgrade in other words so who else better to ENTER than his granddaughter, right? (Whoever added that was definitely passing around some awesome drugs that day of filming. Wow). But yeah at least changing it to REY PALPATINE would have gave a couple points for a better ending (though still light-years from even being DECENT).

Script/Acting: Lines seemed so very basic. By that I mean in my opinion every actor EVERY ONE OF THEM did their BARE MINIMUM to get paid. They didn't show half as much emotion as they could have.

I want to go on but I think my point has been expressed well enough. There is truly nothing I can even blindly say is a positive for the franchise.

How else can I put it... If this film were a cake on the shelf of a bakery, it would not only get the business shut down permanently but probably have its creators sued. On the shelf, it looks fine. Smooth white frosting covering it.... - covering the mold underneath from its expired as well as incorrect ingredients. This cake would hospitalize the consumer.

The movie does do a good a job at making you nostalgic for the original trilogy and there are super really cool and exciting lightsaber fights.
Cons: Palpatine's return was not needed, the movie retcons too much stuff that happens in the other movies, Finn should have been given more character development, the new characters were unnecessary and for the most part had no development , and the reveal of Rey's parents was fine but the reveal kind came out of nowhere. Also some of the humor just fell flat and felt out of place.The movie has a lot have things going on at times and this can drag the movie on and make it feel rushed. Rise of Skywalker is a decent finale to the saga but has many flaws and it does its best to clean up the mistakes of The Last Jedi.

title: Does a good job on its own, but differs a bit from the trilogy
review:
I think a lot of the critique is somewhat unjustified. I really dislike episode 8 and that's maybe why I can see past this movies flaws. They kind of introduce a new take with new ideas, while trying to tie up loose ends.

Therefore the story is very fast paced and feels a little rushed and messy. Fortunately the story is pretty focused without a lot of side-stories, but overall falls a little flat, since it introduces new stuff instead of really following up on the previous movies.

They added some much needed depth to Rey, which could've been even greater if introduced in one of the previous movies. Also Ben/Kylo is portrayed more like Darth Vaders "heir", whereas he's been a little underwhelming in episode 7 and 8. This movie does a fine job developing these two characters, given what little time there was. Wish they had more screen time to add even more depth.

The ending is fine, could've been more, but does a decent job on tying everything together.

All in all there's some great new storytelling, but parts of it could've been divided througout the whole trilogy and elaborated, instead of being cramped up in a single movie. Good on its own, but a little lackluster ending to such an epic saga.

title: Wrapping up a long roller coaster ride....
review:
I am certain this film will not make sense to you if you have never seen any of the Star Wars movies or read the books. The 9th film in a series it is a bit of a mad sprint to the finish line and assumes some understanding of the past.

There are times the story will ramble in a direction that leads no where but in typical Star Wars fashion it meant to go there, often as a reference to bring the past to the present. If you were a true fan of the series it was a nod to those who took the ride along the way.

A great popcorn movie, I never wanted to get up and always felt the story was set at a pace that allowed the action to sink in and the story to unfold and allow the audience to be a part of it. It is a find way to end the story as well.

We all knew from the earliest of films how the story was going to end. The guys in white always seem to overcome the guys dressed in black. Been that way since the first cowboy film was ever produced.

Episode IX is a film I will see again before it leaves the theater and I hope others will enjoy it as much as I did. You MUST go to see this in the theater not only for the big screen appreciation but the audience. I know my family absolutely loved the 2 guys that came in with their own light sabers carrying a 3 foot tall R2D2 filled with popcorn and soda. Hysterical!

title: An improvement for sure.
review:
I actually quite enjoyed the movie but being honest, whilst it is a massive improvement over tlj it still can't hold a candle to the prequels or the original trilogy. This is my opinion not fact but just how I saw it.

I loved Palpatine, was definitely a bit of fan service bringing him back but he just didn't get enough screen time for me and it was all over rather quickly. Id have rather had a story with him creating Rey rather than being her grandfather, could have been an awesome sith power and tied the story in around the "he could create life" line from ep 3.

I like the Kylo story of redemption but again it all happened rather quickly and felt rushed. The death was quick and that was the story done. Definitely should have spent more time around this storyline and built it up more. With the Rise of Skywalker title, for me it would have made much more sense for Kylo to be the last man standing.

The main grievance for me was the total lack of Anakin/Vader full stop. After all Star Wars is the story of the Skywalker's/ Anakin. His mask is shown quickly in TFA as if to signify this will be a big part of the new trilogy and he is nowhere to be seen, if you are going to base the movie on fan service at least give us some of the main character.

The end scene on Tatooine completely confused me, we have force ghost Luke and Leia but nothing of Kylo or Anakin, who are both Skywalker's.

Basically I enjoyed watching the film and it is a massive step up from TLJ but I'm not happy with the end result and clear omission of some big character's, especially Anakin. For me, delete TLJ from existence, split Rise of Skywalker over 2 movies and expand more on Palpatine/ Kylo's redemption and we have a much better trilogy.

title: Anakin WAS the chosen one!
review:
After watching Rise of Skywalker, I went to sleep with the movie tumbling around my mind... how did all the pieces fit? I woke up from the middle of sleep with an epiphany! Anakin WAS the chosen one!

Why was that Sith navigation thing on board the Deathstar? Clearly, it was the rebuilt Deathstar from Return of the Jedi ... AND It was also plugged in when Rey finds it.

Is it possible that Vader was going to use the Deathstar to destroy the secret Sith world?! Revenge for his wife/kids? Vader's suit wasn't a mercy, it was a prison ... a cage. Anakin's hatred for Palpatine must have been enormous. Anakin also knows that Palps can beat death, and could only truly be stopped by the destruction of the Sith temple.

Ben knows this ... the helmet is the symbol of that imprisonment. That's why Palps forces Kylo to wear the reforged helmet, and why Ben obsesses over Vader's twisted helmet. Ben knows what he must do ... complete his grandfather's mission.

In A New Hope, the rebels ruined their own best chance at piece by taking down the Deathstar. In Empire, Vader wasn't trying to turn Luke ... he was trying anything to stop him.

Thoughts?

title: no soul
review:
Every movie fanatic should see this movie... to get a clear look into how average dialog, below average directing, and poor story progression can not be disguised by technical excellence.

Star Wars: Rise of Skywalker feels like a project that wants to do everything: do right by every character, fix what people didn't like about the first two films, complete the story, and be fun, grand, spiritual and great entertainment at the same time. But in this quest - the film becomes a chase after one McGuffin after another, with zero foreshadowing, and what feels like very loose plot structure trying to tie everything together. A lot of the content feels unloaded, instead of woven into the story structure. New characters are introduced, but none are well developed within the film, and few even change very much. I was never engaged in the story, nor interested in the characters, and felt almost no SW magic. The Rise of Skywalker is, to my eye, less than the sum of its parts.

There are some nuanced moments that hit a particular chord: emotional, subtle detail, character revelations - but these moments hit like temporary nostalgia and are not sustained.

The villain is not interesting, which is an absolute crime by SW standards. There are no anti heroes or morally textured characters. There are good guys and there are targets, and the consequences of violence carry little weight - which might be ok if The Rise of Skywalker had a lighter, more entertainment based tone, but it doesn't - it is a very serious film, but one that does not build to meaningful emotional payoffs. Perhaps fitting that one of the more consistent characters in this trilogy is hidden behind a mask for most of the film, squandering his presence, and depending upon voice acting for impact. Yea, this worked with Vader wonderfully in the original trilogy... but that is how that character was entirely designed from the beginning! It is one of many poorly conceived elements placed into this film with good intentions, but with no finesse or artistic skill.

The serious tone is visually supported by a lot of grey tones and darkly lit scenes - but visually, I really feel The Rise of Skywalker is at its best with bright colors, and crisp detail - which is there at (fleeting) times. But mostly? It is like a lot of the effects were intentionally blurred and greyed out to create a gritty realistic look. I didn't really like this aesthetic choice, that is consistent throughout the film.

SW is known for its saber duals and space combat - and it astonishes me how much more effective a movie like Return of the Jedi is than The Rise of Skywalker. True, the lightsaber effects, lighting, and sound have improved, but there just is no emotional weight to the saber fights. The mix of music, effects, setting and performance just never add up - and the same can be said of the space combat. Nothing is ever clear. Sure the viewer knows about mission objective in a generic way, but one never feels a part of the combat, or engaged in any meaningful strategy. Again, the cockpit lighting in the Hoth combat scenes in Empire Strikes Back are far superior to what is on display in this 2019 film. I never felt like I was in the cockpit of a spacecraft in the midst of a big battle - the presentation of these scenes is often more just documenting the event than any attempt to make the viewer part of the experience, and the attempt to make things more epic? Just add more! More ships! More targets! More friendlies! But how about a little immersion please! That is just bad directing, or a poor vision going in, but that would also be the directors fault. If I give the film an overall C+, I'd have to give JJ a D - which is tragic. The Rise of Skywalker depends upon its technical merit to prop up the entire experience, which I recognize, but hard work doesn't make a good movie - it takes vision, leadership and (hands off) producers who trust the artistic vision of writers and directors. I bet this film was not a fun one to make, in any phase of production - it just kinda feels that way coming through the screen.

To this point, the only Disney renditions of SW with any merit would be Rogue One and the Mandalorian - and in my opinion, these projects are the bare minimum of what a fan should expect delivered. With the writing and directing talent out there, and the continued fanaticism of SW, the failure of this film to be little more than average? pretty disappointing!

title: Honest Fan Review: Rise of Skywalker and Trilogy
review:
First let's give credit to J.J. Abrams. ( Next paragraph is the movie review)

Looking back on The Rise of Skywalker I believe JJ did the best he could considering what he was left with. He started with a strong start with The Force Awakens. Granted, The Force awakens was safe, floored, and was similar to A New Hope. However, it's characters were developed very well for the first movie and the enemy was revealed well. The story felt almost like Star Wars and did a good job of setting up a trilogy which had countless directions anyone could take it after the first movie. I feel JJ wanted to create a story/trilogy in which foreshadowed similarities to the originals as it still followed the Skywalkers and the constant battle with the dark side. This accompanied with Rey a new force strong Jedi to create a fresh journey. I also believe JJ always wanted to finish the Skywalker family story within this trilogy and if had done the second instalment he would have explained everything that got rushed within The Rise of Skywalker in more depth. The last Jedi back peddled a lot of the directions that The Force Awakens had opened and it has hardly any main plot other than the fact that Ray would overcome the temptations of the dark side advancements being pushed by Kylo.

The Rise of Skywalker:

There's no denying this movie is a mess. It's pacing begins way too fast, and later slows down to speed up again later. The story is a miss match of things and it starts with back pedalling a bit of what happened in The Last Jedi by not acknowledging any of the events or discontinuing stories and relationship builds. This is fine as The Last Jedi did not contribute to much of the story, it was like a side Star Wars story for the the trilogy, and you could get away with watching 7 then 9 without feeling like your missing much...I digress. TRS Was fun it concluded reasonably well, it's enjoyable and told a story about togetherness. It was very floored in lots of ways but the story was there. It's not the greatest story and it felt like it was on steroids for half the time, including the powers and attributes of the characters, but it was there and the story's within the film were fun. It cinematically looked beautiful and it didn't seem like it was overwhelmed by cgi with most alien extras wearing costumes. It's filled with cliches and is a bit over the top sometimes and I disagree with lots of parts of the film but I enjoyed it even though it wasn't hitting close to any of the original trilogy films. I'm not telling you to like this film I'm telling you that it's better than The Last Jedi in terms of the content that it adds and the story. (Sorry for all The Last Jedi hate. I don't hate the movie, it just didn't do anything for me or for the trilogy)

Conclusion:

This trilogy was never gonna be as good as the originals, and it never has felt exactly like it was Star Wars and the stories weren't deep enough. I still enjoyed many aspects but that's the truth. Maybe if JJ had done the second we could have had a deeper picture of the vision of the trilogy and have something that came close to the originals and accept that. It's also hard for the directors as there's not much time for them and the writers to produce a decent enough film and script for the demand that Disney pushes so hard to deliver on.

It didn't give me that feeling of the originals and I still hope that we will be brought something new and as refreshing as The Mandalorian or Rogue One but in a trilogy.

title: They did well with what they had
review:
I really enjoyed Rise of Skywalker and I was prepared to be disappointed.

I can, however, see why others are disappointed and frustrated. This movie packs so much into it that the story doesn't really flow as well as it could have.

The plot twist and big reveals are very much shoehorned in to make the ending worthwhile, but it does feel forced and unnatural even though the reveals are quite interesting.

I do feel this movie does cop some unfair treatment though, as the pacing, reveals, and quick character development have to happen because literally nothing happened in The Last Jedi. The Last Jedi should have been the movie where Rey developed a lot (she doesn't) and the plot twists should have occurred (Similar to how Empire revealed Luke's heritage). But none of this happens making the first half of Rise of Skywalker a retcon catch up.

Rey does have some decent character development in this movie, but she was so under developed in the previous films (Again, Last Jedi -.-) that it feels incredibly forced.

The people have a problem with Palpatine coming back and being the big bad is fair to an extent as it does kind of take away from Luke and Vader's victory (not entirely though as they clearly stopped the destruction of the galaxy and forced palps into hiding for 30+ years). I feel he too should have a least been hinted at in the previous film. However, it is also hinted that this Palpatine could be a clone, or at least created with Dark Side energy. THIS did happen in legends so it isn't too far fetched.

Overall, an incredibly busy film with some excellent ideas. It is a great shame that The Last Jedi forced a massive amount of catch up and retcon which took up too much of this movie. Seriously, it's good, if you can acknowledge the fact the The Last Jedi really didn't help set this movie up and also ruined the set up from Force Awakens.

title: Serviceable but sloppy end to the Skywalker Saga. The Internet gets what it deserves.
review:
J. J. Abrams concludes the Skywalker saga in suitably epic if uneven fashion. The duels are more elaborate, the Force powers are more bizarre, and the space battles are grander than previously seen. It looks expensive and epic, with some impressive visuals and action set pieces. However it's merely adequate.

That's almost entirely thanks to the cast. They're not slouching through it. Daisy Ridley and Adam Driver are the standouts as Rey and Kylo Ren. The returning characters like Finn (Boyega) and Poe (Isaac) are a welcome addition to the adventure. They rarely separate during the space battles and chases and their playing off each other elevates otherwise complicated plot turns and overwrought exposition.

Since he's on the poster and used in advertising, I think it's safe to say Palpatine is definitely back. It is jarring to see him again. Ian McDiarmid is having fun as the Emperor but I wish they used a different villain instead of him. It makes the comparisons to Return of the Jedi all the more reasonable because what else is there?

The crux of the plot is that both he and Kylo Ren is vying for supremacy over the tyrannical First Order. But the main 3 heroes journey from planet to planet in search of a means to thwart the villains. And yes, Rey's backstory is retconned as a slap to Rian Johnson to make her seem more important. Instead the plot seems smaller because everyone's related to someone that's famous.

It's been widely reported that the movie was made by Abrams in a way to retcon The Last Jedi due to fan backlash. Unfortunately it shows. Exposition and plot points emerge to serve as a quasi-apology for that film which is so unnecessary. I always felt The Last Jedi got too much hate. Rose Tico (Tran) is barely a character in the movie and there's a new female lead paired with Finn that participates in the action so much, it seems like it'd make better sense if Rose was combined with this character. Kylo Ren and Rey's love/hate relationship is compelling as ever but the conclusion would surely dissatisfy most viewers even if part of it does make sense in conjunction with The Force Awakens.

As a result the film does feel disjointed and messy in the first act. The second half is admittedly a much better paced story the climax is exciting if unoriginal. It's basically another fight between a giant fleet versus another giant fleet. The cast truly does elevate the film and their sense of camaraderie feels genuine. Daisy Ridley has some stand-out moments and Adam Driver successfully conveys Kylo Ren's inner turmoil. John Boyega is treated with more respect as a protagonist (unfortunately he doesn't get the girl despite so much teasing between him and 3 different female characters!). The surprise improvement is for Oscar Isaac as Poe Dameron, who's been otherwise wasted in these movies. He's charismatic, cocky, and funny in the tradition of Harrison Ford or contemporary action stars like Chris Pratt or Dwayne Johnson.

The ending for the trilogy makes it clear that it is wrapping things up but still it felt safe. There's nothing offensive or terrible about it necessarily but it feels like they didn't want to go further just to upset the already mercurial fanbase.

And I'm going to say this. Star Wars fans ruined Star Wars movies. They nitpick and complain about everything. With the new sequel trilogy they disparaged filmmakers and in some extreme cases, made threats against the actors involved including Kelly Marie Tran especially. That is unacceptable behavior. Disney blinked with this movie. It needs to be said. The movie feels like something made to cater to fans while still finishing an entire franchise's story. Abrams' direction is competent but it always seems like he's thinking of pleasing the internet instead of crafting an original conclusion that audiences truly deserve.

For a finale to a franchise like Star Wars, that's a shame. But considering the idiosyncratic nature of the sequel trilogy, coupled with the fans' obnoxious attitude, it's inevitable.

title: Production issues and years of difficulties don't always lead to a disaster.
review:
As a Star Wars fan since I was six years old, I've been anxiously anticipating the arrival of "Star Wars Episode 9: The Rise of Skywalker". While not as hotly anticipated by others as 2015's episode "The Force Awakens"; I was going to go in with an open mind, not ready to hate it like some others were (mentioning this is probably going to get me downvoted into oblivion).

This just turned out to be decent. The massive scope of filmmaking on display from "The Force Awakens" and "The Last Jedi" (both were films that I loved) is present here, along with some incredible and dark imagery.

The cast is fantastic as always, including a new supporting character played by Keri Russell. While Princess Leia's inclusion in this film was made difficult by Carrie Fisher's passing, she is done justice and is a solid supporting presence for protagonist Rey.

There are some satisfactory moments throughout the movie that help give closure to beloved characters like Rey, Finn, Poe Dameron, etc.

Like other reviewers have said; it suffers from some too much familiarity, namely the climax. Whereas "The Force Awakens" integrated classic Star Wars elements into a new and fresh start, there's some treading water here.

"The Rise of Skywalker" is a mostly serviceable conclusion, and if it doesn't do it for you then probably "The Mandalorian" or future projects on Disney+ might restore the hopes of certain fans.

* These are mainly my initial thoughts and feelings, but I'll be seeing it again soon to see how things change for me or not. *



Grade- B

title: My least favorite Star Wars movie
review:
Star Wars is my favorite movie series. Even though The Last Jedi wasn't that good, I was still curious to see how the Skywalker saga would end. Now that I finally saw The Rise of Skywalker, I'm sad to say it ended on a whimper. Before I continue, I'll briefly go over my thoughts on the Star Wars series.

1. A New Hope: Some aspects of the movie feel dated, but I still have a good time watching it. 8/10

2. The Empire Strikes Back: This is one of the few movies I would consider to be perfect. I can't think of a single issue with it. 10/10

3. Return of the Jedi: Out of the three OT movies, this is the most fun to watch. However, the 2nd act is a drag and I'm still not a fan of the Ewoks. 10/10

4. The Phantom Menace: The visuals, the action, and the music make up for the boring characters and story. 6/10

5. Attack of the Clones: While Anakin, Obi-Wan, and Padme are better here, I find the story to be more dull than Episode I. 6/10

6. Revenge of the Sith: Besides some bad dialogue and action scenes, I think this is a great send off for the original 6 movies. 10/10

7. The Force Awakens: Although it undoes ROTJ's ending, I still have fun watching the movie. I think this is a great introduction to the new characters. 8/10

8. Rogue One: The first two acts are dull, but the third makes up for it. I appreciate the movie for telling a different kind of Star Wars story. 8/10

9. The Last Jedi: Besides some great individual scenes and visuals, I think everything else isn't good. 5/10

10. Solo: The story and the action aren't anything special, but I still have a good time watching it. Just like Rogue One, I appreciate it for telling a different kind of Star Wars story. 6/10

Now that I got that out of the way, let me explain why The Rise of Skywalker is my least favorite Star Wars movie.

First off, nothing stood out here. At least The Last Jedi, which used to be dead last in my series ranking, had some great scenes.

I can't think of anything memorable in Episode IX. The new characters weren't that interesting, the new planets consist of environments we've seen before, and the action was pretty meh.

Another issue I had was that it felt really bloated. There were so many characters, locations, and McGuffins crammed in two hours. A rewrite or two could've made the script more focused.

Despite all of the criticisms I have, there were some things I liked. It was great to finally see Rey, Finn, and Poe Dameron together. I thought they had good chemistry with each other.

Overall, Episode IX is a disappointing finale to both the sequel trilogy and the Skywalker saga. I give this movie a 5/10 with no recommendation.

So it was a mixed feeling where the viewing experience is one of the best I've had, but so many annoying plots happening in the movie and way too much copy paste from the other movies, I'm glad the Skywalker saga is over and the last movie was way better than I expected.
