title: I liked it! Although I'm not sure I loved it
review:
The movie is a solid ending to the new trilogy. It was so many emotive, nostalgic moments that worked great on me and moved me. For example, seeing Luke and Leia in their prime, training, or Luke lifting his X-Wing out of the sea. The overall pace is perfect. Never slows down, never gets boring. Rey's internal struggle is equally solid and visual. Seeing Rey throwing lightnings out of her hands was impressive and shocking. And, although I didn't hate Last Jedi, JJ gets extra credits for fixing that little mess.
On the other hand, there a few things I felt were unnecessary. First off, obviously, that weeeeeird kiss. Not set-up, no reason for it. Second, some characters and the confusing romantic relationship between characters. It felt like at one point, Rey could end up with anyone in the cast. Then, Poe gets his girl, and nothing comes out of it. Then Finn, who kissed Rose in the last film, meets another character, also former stormtrooper, but nothing comes out of it either. Neither of those two characters felt special, and neither really adds anything. They're only there because the plot needs them.
I also feel that, even though I liked the climax, Palpatine never felt unbeatable. He was, in fact, just a little dull for me. I did like how Rey came from behind and beat Palpatine, and I liked how Kylo sacrificed for her. Also, Palpatine being Rey's grandfather was great for me.
Overall, it's a nice ending for the trilogy, and presumably the saga. I admit being on the verge of tears in a few occasions. I liked it! The denouement with Rey saying she's a Skywalker in Tatooine was beautiful.

title: Lifelong Star Wars fan here & I loved it!
review:
Just to preface this review: at the age of 9, I saw Star Wars in the theater 7 times (4 of the times by myself as I couldn't get anyone to go with me again. Keep in mind, that movies stayed at theaters for months at a time back then). I have also read 11 Star Wars books (none of them considered cannon as I read this 18-20 years ago).

My husband (also a lifelong SW movie and book fan, having read about 50 SW books) and I loved this movie. I haven't loved all of the movies. The prequels were disappointing due to some of the worst dialogue and child acting I have seen (Natalie Portman, Jake Lloyd and Hayden Christiansen). The Last Jedi was middle-of-the-road for me, though it does rate higher than Phantom Menace and Attack of the Clones. Thankfully this movie, like The Force Awakens, captured the feeling of the original trilogy and what I have always loved about the SW universe and stories. I teared up with emotion in the movie, and I walked out thoroughly satisfied.

Clearly, most of the fandom doesn't agree with me. I see people picking things apart left and right. But I don't really care about the inconsistencies that critics found and ripped apart. When you have a long-running franchise, it's okay IMO to change things up a bit to enhance your stories as you go on.

The one complaint I will share is that they included too much of Princess Leia. They didn't have enough unused footage and overall it was kind of distracting. I understand that Carrie Fisher's death left the storytellers in a quandary as to how to handle the character, but I think they should have used less of her. And oh, I guess another small complaint: the way that they completely dropped the Finn-Rose romance was a bit distracting as well, but I didn't love that romance in the first place anyway.

Overall: a Solid 9.5 stars for me.

JJ Abrams steered course to a much more satisfying movie than the last one. Unfortunately I can't get over the main issue that the latest trilogy just feels like it doesn't need to exist.

Not only that, it seems to undermine the original trilogy. The war you won? You didn't. The big bad you killed? You didn't. The redemption of Anakin meant something? No, it didn't matter.

This was an entertaining movie no doubt. And JJ had to do some deus ex machinas and some logic jumps to try and correct the damage of the last awful movie. I can forgive all that.

Although a house divided cannot stand, and the competent first movie of the trilogy and this will be forever undermined by the absolute stinker in the middle.

I enjoyed the generally upbeat tone of the movie - and the cast chemistry really was at its best as the trilogy came to an end.

But the resolution felt too easy and some tired old plot devices used again, this trilogy just felt unnecessary.

Move on to new Star Wars pastures please, Disney.

title: Let's stop taking this so seriously.
review:
Look, every Star Wars movie has problems. This one isn't an exception. The first act drags, some of the twists and retcons seem forced (get it?). Some of the dialogue is expository nonsense.

And yet...

It's hard to not be swept up in the fantasy. Star Wars (for how seriously some people take it) has always been about one thing: fun. It's a ridiculous space wizard saga with creatures, robots, superpowers, space battles and sword fights.

This movie is FUN. It brings back the best of the OT and blends it with the best of the sequels. It leans into the crazier corners of this sci fi universe and delivers payoff after glorious payoff. The characters have great interplay and the emotional beats hit hard, even when they're a tad nonsensical.

Star Wars has always aped the goofy Saturday morning serials of old and Rise of Skywalker acts as a love letter to them and the saga They inspired. It may not be the best Star Wars film, but it's certainly the MOST Star Wars-y flick ever made.

Just lean in and enjoy the ride.

title: Somewhat entertaining but deeply convoluted sequel
review:
I enjoyed both "The Force Awakens" and "The Last Jedi," love the original trilogy, and do not care for the prequels. I was excited to see how the Skywalker story would finally end in this finish to the "Star Wars" sequel trilogy. The film isn't bad, and is better than many critics are saying, but it's still far from great and does not fully satisfy as an end to the Star Wars films for now.

The main story for this installment deals with our heroes having to save the galaxy from an imminent invasion from Emperor Palpatine (from the original trilogy,) who has somehow come back to the galaxy. I have always felt that the sequel trilogy has not crafted engaging characters on the level of the primary characters in the original trilogy (Luke, Leia, Han and Vader.) While Rey is better this time around--both in terms of range and character development--than in episodes VII and VIII, the other characters are not especially handled well again. The film is engaging and often fun to watch, but its pacing is extraordinarily fast even by the standards of action-packed blockbusters. While, for example, "Avengers: Endgame" had tons going on during its three-hour runtime, it was able to balance exposition and character with action and plot to make a truly impactful--but never overwhelming--film. Here, the film's narrative is a gaudy mix of "too fast in terms of things going on" and "too little in terms of things of consequential substance until the third act."

The score and production values are good, and the film's writing is often solid. It manages to play some nice homages to elements about the original trilogy that we love as well. Yet by the time this conclusion ends, we don't feel completely satisfied for something hyped as the definitive (for now) end of a nine-film epic series. 6/10

Note: I saw the film in Dolby Cinema. The picture quality, sound quality, and rumble effect were all excellent.

title: A satisfying conclusion

An old villain resurfaces and Rey, who has been continuing Jedi training under Leia, following Luke's departure into The Force, finds herself facing an even greater threat than before.

I don't want to put overt spoilers in an IMDB post, so I'll remain vague in my synopsis. Suffice it to say that the ninth - and final? - episode of the Skywalker saga wraps up most loose ends tidily and satsfactorily.

It is clear in the storyline how much Carrie Fisher's unexpected death resulted in necessary retooling, but the plot still works well enough. It was good to have assorted cameos from old friends, even if many of them were blink-and-you'll-miss-'em voice cameos.

The visuals, to me, weren't as good as usual - there was a lot of excess darkness where it was difficult to make things out, and also shaky camera work, both of which have become fashionable - contrast the climax of ROTJ, also dark and full of action, but an object lesson in clarity.

Most of the criticisms I've read didn't matter too much to me. I did feel that The Force turned out to have areas which were somewhat unexpected (again!), and the sudden revelation of Force Dyads matched midichlorians as conveniently expedient plot devices. They weren't deal breakers for me, though.

I enjoyed it hugely, and it repaired a lot of the samage Episode VIII had caused for me.

title: An Epic Finish!
review:
I am absolutely in love with this film, it was the ending to a long running series that I needed, and what a way to finish. This one is right up there with SW: A New Hope (1977), SW: The Force Awakens (2015) and Rogue One (2016).

It picks up where that God awful film, SW: The Last Jedi (2017) ended and might as well have just carried on from The Force Awakens (I see no point to The Last Jedi at all). My only real criticism is that there is a lot in this film, which perhaps could have been spread out a bit more in its predecessor to make it more interesting, and give time for this one to flow a little easier, but I have to say they all did a brilliant job, especially as they had to fix what had happened before and deal with the death of the brilliant Carrie Fisher, I thought they were very clever with that and not over the top or gushy as they could have been. They tease you throughout that others may die and the trailer makes you think that Lando will play a bigger part, but I think they had a good balance of everyone. Bringing Palpatine back is not a cop out at all and the revelation of Rey's parentage helps to make more sense of all of the "Sequels".

I'm still not a fan of Adam Driver as Kylo Ren, feeling that he lacks the charisma and appeal necessary for the character, but I absolutely loved the others in this one, especially Oscar Isaacs who was hotter than ever, particularly in those trousers. The return of many characters, even if only by voice, was very clever to show that we are at the end and give some closure to our favourites, that we have lived with for so long.

This is what a Star Wars film is all about, a small band of rebels bringing hope and saving the galaxy, uniting the universe defeating the bad guys! So many things to list that made me happy, but I suggest you watch it yourself and find out what makes you happy instead. I'm sure you will have the warm fuzzy and joyous feeling that I had when the plan all comes together and success is achieved.

title: TOO EASY! (But I liked it)
review:
Make no mistake, boys and girls! This is a Disney movie. Maybe we wish it could be different, but ... the only thing left for us to do now is just enjoy it the best we can.

(Or, if you want, there's the other option. You can spend your time and money feeling mad/sad/whatever. I decided not to go that way.)

This movie has a scale that only a Star Wars finale could, with some serious eyebrow-raising moments. The "spaceship" battles are just gorgeous. The lightsaber duels channel a surprising amount of emotion. Palpatine is incredible.

And man, I love that Rey/Kylo dynamic. It's just so damn cool.

But ... despite some *truly impressive* fireworks on the part of the bad guys, at no point in this movie did I ever feel like the good guys could actually lose.

I mean, c'mon. Would they ACTUALLY end this saga with the bad guys winning? No, of course not.

I feel they could have taken a lot more risks here. They could have easily gotten away with making this a 3-hour movie, and adding some "sophisticated adult" content to make it more emotionally compelling. I DEFINITELY would have slowed down the first 10 minutes... holy moley, that was frantically-weird.

With all the above said, I certainly didn't end up feeling disappointed. Personally, I plan to see "Skywalker" in theaters at least one more time, and I'll definitely be buying the Blu-ray. (I'm hoping for a behind-the-scenes look at how they got Leia to look so amazing?! It can't all be reused footage...)

And hey! Threepio gets a little moment of actual character development here. That only took 9 movies. :)

I'll leave you now with a few quotes I agree with...

"The Rise of Skywalker provides about as competent an ending as one could hope for from such a sprawling, weird saga." - Nick Johnston, Vanyaland

"It should surprise no one that a mixed bag of a franchise ends with a mixed bag of a final chapter." - Rob Hunter, Film School Rejects

"Abrams and company get around the Last Jedi fanbase blowback the easy way ... essentially pretending there never was a Last Jedi." - Michael Phillips, Chicago Tribune

title: A Galaxy Saved and Salvaged by J.J Abrams
review:
Being a huge fan of the original trilogy and enjoying the lore of the prequel trilogy, I can respect and finally see where J.J Abrams was going with the Force Awakens and Rise of Skywalker. Turns out Rey is a Palpatine and wouldn't be revealed until episode IX, where Abrams wanted to clue us into new mysteries and to raise new questions in order to keep us on our toes. Examples of this is introducing a new villain like Supreme Leader Snoke, who really was a puppet and clone of Palpatine.

PROS: I can appreciate the story for what we were given by trying to repair the damage after Rian Johnson's terrible writing of The Last Jedi. The characters all had good stories, except Rose. I love the lore of how Palpatine survived and how he was behind the entire saga, which tied the events of all the movies together. I also loved when Rey called out to the force and seeing older characters return such as: Yoda, Ahsoka, Anakin, and Obi-Wan. The ending was well written mimicking the original movie of A New Hope of Luke Skywalker looking out into the sunset, but now it is Rey returning to the home world of Anakin and Luke. The cinematography was excellent! The CGI was great and we got Ewoks! Also we got porgs for merchandising just like Yogurt says in Spaceballs "Merchandising". The Emperor's story is the best part of the movie and makes it feel like a Star Wars movie and also it ties it in with lore from Revenge of the Sith essentially making Darth Plagueis true as that the Emperor claims that all the sith live within him. Essentially, the Emperor struck down his own master in order to obtain Plaguesis life force. This also explains the power that Anakin was so greatly after in order to save Padme from death, which is the power of healing that Rey has since she is a Palpatine. I like how the Knights of Ren were finally used as Palpatine's servants. It was also nice to see the visuals of him decaying as so much time has passed from the events of Episode XI to now, which means he would be over 100 years old. Now let's move to other characters. We got more C3PO this time around and Daniels did a great job for the final movie of this saga making him have a good purpose to the story. We got Lando back and it was fun to see him and Chewbacca in the Falcon for the final battle. Princess Leia was a gem in the movie and I appreciate what they were able to do with her since she passed before the making of this movie. Luke Skywalker as a force ghost was awesome, but I wish he was still alive to fight the Emperor along side Rey and Ben Solo. Ben Solo character came full circle and was enjoyable. Adam Driver did an excellent job with him! Han Solo came back as a vision to Ben and I loved how he got that time with his son through Leia's sacrifice. Fin and Poe were fun to see, but were more of a B plot to the movie, while Rey, the Emperor and Ben were the A plot. There was plenty of nostalgia and it was a good and fun movie to see on a Friday night!

CONS: The plot was good, but had a few holes that were unresolved from The Last Jedi that Abrams couldn't explore when seeding up for the next movie in the franchise from Force Awakens. Rian Johnson and Kathleen Kennedy ruined Luke Skywalker's arc and made him way to feminine out of his own character. Not to mention, the infamous throwing the lightsaber off the cliff part, which nearly happened again with Rey. I personally didn't care for that part. It seemed that the movie had a lot of different locations, but were too much for a single Star Wars movie for me. Another small issue was over usage of the light speed control on the Falcon that Poe used during the escape scene in the beginning part of the film. I was not also a big fan of the Chewbacca death cliffhanger only to find out he survived 10 minutes later. That part was a bit forced. I think some parts of the movie could be trimmed and were unnecessary. It did feel like the movie was based on entirely nostalgia and fan service for terrible efforts of The Last Jedi.

Overall, Rian Johnson should NOT write another Star Wars movie. The saga is done, so don't make episodes X, XI, and XII. The new trilogy by Disney is decent if you don't count The Last Jedi. The lore was fun to explore and the story was good and the movie was fun to watch, which made it not predictable unlike the Last Jedi. We got Ewoks! We saw old familiar locations, yes Cloud City I am talking about you! The fan service was not much, but we deserve it after The Last Jedi. I really enjoyed this movie and the best part is the tie to the rest of the saga, which is the Emperor's story! Nicely done, Jar Jar Abrams! The galaxy will finally sleep in peace after avenging the evil Rian Johnson and Kathleen Kennedy!

title: Say What You Want...
review: 1/3 of the way in, I caught myself several times contemplating on where this Episode stood on my list, as I was most certain it would be top 3 (behind, III & V). However, the drama never let up, the stakes remained high, and the action felt like a nuke had dropped on the entire theater. As to why critics, whether or not they're paid to post, regard this film as lackluster or simple fan-service, I don't understand. I chose to not watch a single teaser or trailer for the movie and by doing so, I was blown away and will always cherish this installment. I felt the humor was far more natural and less forced, contrary to VIII, the action surpassed any preconceived notions, and the ending was absolutely perfect. On my drive home, I debated where exactly this episode stood, and as I finally surrendered my outright love for Revenge of the Sith, I had no choice but to place The Rise of Skywalker on top. I was honestly skeptical how the finale would salvage what The Last Jedi had damaged, as far as the essence of Star Wars storyarch is concerned, but thankfully, I too can fade away, leaving behind nothing but the garbs of a man out of touch with style.

title: Rise of Skywalker Has Some Magic but a bit of the Lustre has Worn Off
review:
The Rise of Skywalker is essentially about the re-emergence of an old foe and their collective efforts to stop him. They've already spoiled who it is but I'll dance around it just in case. I originally thought that bringing this character back was a lazy choice, there are so many great unused characters in the Star Wars universe, why bring this character back? But they brought enough new angles with his return that I was willing to go along with it. The plot is hit or miss period, there were scenes that really grabbed me (I liked the land speeder chase on the desert planet, it had some nice moments) but there were others that fell really flat. But I had heard some pretty terrible things from critics going in and it still kept me interested for the most part.

The cast of these movies usually doesn't get the attention with all the nitpicking of the writing and the minute details of the franchise canon. Daisy Ridley has always been underrated, she's not Scarlett Johannson but she was a good choice as an unknown for Rey. There's a lot of emotion in her acting, she knows when to turn it on and when to tone it down. I hope she has a bright future ahead of her, this franchise tends to make or break careers. I would say John Boyega has been a victim of his character, I really liked him in the Force Awakens and I kept hoping that Finn was going to grow more and but they gave him very little new or exciting to do in this. The more established people in the cast (Mark Hamill, Ian McDiarmid, Carrie Fisher, Billy Dee Williams) all slip into their roles like fitting into an old pair of slippers. It was good that Oscar Isaac got more to do and I was happy Kylo Ren as a character seemed to grow into Adam Driver's strengths. It made his casting better. Driver was improved in this movie and he's a rising star for a reason.

One of the more intriguing aspects for me as this new trilogy has developed was the evolving relationship between Rey and Kylo. One of the more inventive parts of the story is how they choose to move forward with not only the changing of Rey's past (which is presented in a clunky was but I went along with it) but how their respective moral compasses' is still being shaped and changing with each passing event. The changing of Rey's lineage was a genuine surprise for me and I liked how they continued to intertwine Rey and Kylo despite them being on opposite sides of the chess board. This really becomes THEIR story, the rest of the characters take a back seat (we get a little more time with Po but Finn's job in this is to trade witty one liners with Po and Jannah and scream when Rey is in trouble) but it works for the movie and while not every choice is perfect, they did a good job continuing the development of these characters.

I largely enjoyed this movie but I do have some problems worth mentioning. The largest is the amount of exposition and sleight of hand they have to do when reconciling the separate continuity that Abrams and Johnson had planned. It was embarrassing in some scenes. There are huge exposition dumps. One of my friends was making excuses for there being too much material to fit into one movie so they needed to use that to catch the audience up. I still thought it was distracting and sloppy. They also bring up so many minor issues that feel like they're going to play a part in the story later but they just snap their fingers and they've been handled. Some of them are also just dropped, why bring them up if that's the case? I also thought the comedy was very hit or miss. Some of it worked but other parts seemed recycled (I'm not going to blame Anthony Daniels but giving so much to C-3PO might have been a mistake, its just the same kind of joke over and over). That's not unusual for this genre thought so its not a huge problem.

Rise of Skywalker features some good action, some interesting choices with the Star Wars mythology and gets the job done developing Rey, Kylo and the main cast. But after all the drama around The Last Jedi (which I really enjoyed but it has admittedly aged poorly), I can't watch these movies anymore without over-analyzing it. There's way too much expository dialogue, the continuity from the previous entries is just tossed aside and the comedic bits are hit and miss at best. Its pretty obvious that the Disney executives and J.J.'s team fell all over themselves trying to pacify the fans (whether that was deserved or not) and it works sometimes and other times it doesn't. I enjoyed myself in the theatre but I'm actually glad this is wrapping up. The constant hate spewing from everyone (on both sides) ruined this property for me and while I'm happy to keep my mind open to future movies, lets all collectively move on. I'm recommending this to Star Wars fans, specifically to the Last Jedi haters because there is a major course correction. I think for the more casual fan, this will still be enjoyable. My actual rating is somewhere between an 8/10 and a 9/10.

title: Best Star Wars movie since Empire!
review:
Spoilers ahead - Let's start at the end. How do you put a final bookend on a IX volume series written over the course of 40 plus years? You have to end where you started, in this case, Tatooine. We met Luke and Anakin on Tattooine and this is where we say goodbye to Rey, but also Luke, Leia, and all of our old friends as the the book closes at the end of the final chapter of the most epic saga ever told on the big screen. I couldn't have loved this ending any more. It just felt right. The other 140 or so mintues of the film did their best to give callbacks to characters and lines that we had to experience one more time. If you felt it was patronizing, you missed the point. We also saw new force abilities revealed, just like we first saw lightning from the fingers of the Emperor in VI. The healing from Rey was new as her power grew and in the end, it brought balance to the Force. The prophecy from Episode I was finally fulfilled. Interestingly, the 9 Episode story arc is really now the story of Palpatine and the Sith's long game to rule the galaxy. He along with Chewbaccca, R2 and C-3PO are the constants that anchor the story as we move from Anakin's story, to Luke's and finally to Rey's tale. The pacing of XI was great and seemed shorter than it was. The best thing about this movie was the score. John Williams bought back every feeling and emotion from A New Hope and hit the magical melodic lines at exactly the right moments. We got the full Jedi fanfare just when it was needed. Were there some silly creatures and bad jokes? Yes, exactly the right amount to be in line with Episodes IV-VI. Vader dropped some pretty corny dad oneliners in his day. This film was Star Wars through and through and Abrams delivered where Johnson came up short in Episode VIII. Fans, if it is closure you're looking for, then you will be satisfied.

Thank you to Lucas for sharing his Galaxy far, far away with us.

The movie is quick paced as JJ tries to fit two movies into one but it never left me confused. Not everything is explained but it doesn't need to be, why anyone needs ever to make perfect sense in a fictional universe is beyond me. The Emperor is back, ok, it's not explained how, ok, is Ian McDairmid still awesome, yes. Easy as that. The Rey/Kylo stuff that was the best of The Last Jedi is taken up a notch here and you can see where JJ wanted this story to go all along and he gets there with some big fights, and even bigger emotional payoffs. It worked for me. Just be entertained, if you're not, then don't go see it because it wasn't made for you. If you need to be overly analytical then just go back to whichever Star Wars movie you prefer and continue to pretend they are perfect. This was made by people that are clearly Star Wars fans and this is the last hoorah for those that have stuck with it with for all these years.

title: This movie pulled so many threads together in a very satisfying way.
review: This movie was far better than I expected, especially after reading initial critic reviews. The movie isn't perfect but Star Wars has never been about sublime narrative or great acting. It's been about fun plots, homage to the past movies of the series Andy the genre that inspired them, the relationships among the characters, and a present day morality tale. This movie tied up the numerous threads hanging after the eighth movie and it created, to me, a very satisfying ending to the nine movie arc that started when I was 10 years old. I'll miss the sequencing of the next chapters to my life but liked very much the way this movie created seen ending.

title: A clever, clever movie, if a bit rushed.
review:
Warning: This is a real review and does NOT contain any spoilers. Unlike the multiple, identically worded (and identically mis-spelled) reviews here, I hope it will come across as honest and let YOU decide whether to go and see it.

This is undoubtedly the best film of the current trilogy. Is it Star Wars? Yes. Is it perfect? - No, which means it IS Star Wars. As a 6-year- old kid I loved the original movie. I was happy to ignore the stormtropper who hit his head rushing through the door in the Death Star. I was happy to believe that you could HEAR SOUNDS IN SPACE and I was happy to be sitting next to my Dad in the cinema - an experience that to me is priceless now he's gone. I'm passing the torch to my daughter, seeing the movies at Midnight the day they are released, suspending disbelief in the laws of physics and cherishing a shared experience with a loved one. Did I get upset with Episode I? - Yes. Was that a realistic, mature, reasoned reaction? - No. Life moves on, films move on and anyone who judges this movie against a low-budget 1977 movie is saying more about their inability to grow than they are about the film's quality. If you want pure escapism, go and see this movie. If you love space opera, go and see this movie. If you claim to love Star Wars and are filled with hatred and negative criticism towards any and all sequels, then I politely suggest that you've missed the point of movies in general, let alone the message of Star Wars which has always been about family, whether that be through blood or circumstance.

title: Amazing ending of the saga!
review:
Right now the movie has a 58% for the critics evaluation on RT. And this is coming from the same critics who gave a 91% to the train wreck that was The Last Jedi. Don't believe them, the movie is awesome! It's Star Wars in its truest essence.
People forget that Star Wars has always been a light, somewhat predictable, good vs bad dilema kind of story. Remember: this is not Game of Thrones, where the evil guys sometimes win and it's based on what would happen on the "real life". This is Star Wars! The force is strong in the good side! :) Critics and boomer fans praise so much episodes 4, 5 and 6, but everything bad they're saying about episode 9, could be said about 4, 5 and 6 as well.
Not only that, Rise of Skywalker spent around 30/40 minutes correcting the story of The Last Jedi. Only then, they start to tell the Rise of Skywalker story... Because of that, I felt that only 2h and 20 min was too short of a time to tell such a great story. I feel that a length of a little over 3 hours would be ideal. That's my only complaint: I WANTED MORE!! lol
Bottom line: it's amazing, full of nostalgia, epic battles, good vs evil dilema and emotional... A true amazing ending for the Star Wars saga. And the most amazing thing: they did that after The Last Jedi, and even corrected the bad parts of that movie.
Congrats on everyone who was a part of the movie, the fans appreciate the hard work and the great ending of the saga!!

I don't know about the rest of the star wars fandom, but I want Star Wars to succeed. Because what do any of us get out of wishing for it's failure? Sure you can gloat and say you told us so, but how does that benefit anyone in the long run? It doesn't! The fans dug their own grave once again! They dug it with the prequels which caused Lucas to give up and sell it to Disney! And then they complained that The Force Awakens was too similar to a New Hope and so they tried something different with The Last Jedi which ticked everyone off, so they played it safe with Rise of Skywalker. Congratulations fans, you killed Star Wars!

And for the critics to complained about it being a crammed and unoriginal piece of fan-service. Learn to evaluate a film for what it is, because anyone with a brain would know that critics have never been Star Wars target audience. When you enrage your target audience like Disney did with The Last Jedi, you are left in a vulnerable position. And based on the less than desirable circumstances, I think it turned out fairly well.

review: I was aware of the mixed reactions this film was getting, not none of the complaints I'd heard rang true AT ALL. The story flowed logically with good narrative drive. I loved it. I found it to be a really satisfying ending to the whole Star Wars saga.

review: Movie was fantastic! Only gripe I had was the level of exposition and quick explanations in the film for issues that should have been covered in previous films. These moments did not take away from the quality of the movie. You just notice these things as a fan of the franchise. Great story, great actors, great performances and satisfying ending. title: The Rise of the Trolls!
review:
Most of the early reviews which are 5/10 or less are from people that wanted to hate this film before it even came out. This is why they were all here on the first day with the genuine reviews coming later.

It's very sad that Star Wars now has a community of trolls who rise up every time a new film comes out.

Getting on to the film - I loved it! Now while it's not perfect as I do have a few moans and gripes as a 40+ older fan I am very happy with this film.

My friends who are all in this same age category are all of the same opinion and loved the film as well.

Notice to all older fans - you may get emotional several times in this film.

For anyone still going to watch - it gets really good from the trailer teased second Death Star sequence onwards but the opening acts are all still fine.

I am also noticing a trend aside from the new film hating trolls, where a lot of fans who loved The Last Jedi have taken a real dislike to this film.

Im guessing that this is because JJ Abraham's corrects a lot of the mistakes made in the The Last Jedi, as The Rise of Skywalker is like two films in one. You could almost disregard The Last Jedi from the timeline if you choose to do so.

My gripes...

In terms of my gripes with this film... well it does appear to suffer from a hangover from The Last Jedi in the early stages (This was to be expected), and this does mean that there is just too much going on in those early acts. This does however settle down.

There is also a bad Leia CGI moment which is a shame.

There are a few small plot holes which I might be wrong about anyway, and it would have been nice to have had a bit more space dog fighting just like we had in the Return of the Jedi.

Gripe list over.

Please just go and watch this with an open mind and no preconceived notions. It's a real roller coaster ride with some truly amazing visuals and a fantastic story.

title: It's not a bad movie. People just don't get Star Wars.
review:
New trilogy, new story. One that had minor to none influence of George Lucas but one that respected and reminded us of his great creation. The SW Universe.
Yes, disney got their hands on it, Star Wars is everywhere, not all of it is good, some is actually really bad, but lets talk about the Rise of Skywalker.
The story may not have been the one we wanted, palpatine returns?? What about ROTJ? Anakins legacy that relies on killing the emperor, all for nothing ? Yes, i agree, they could have done it differently.
Given the story and plot they chose to present to us.. This movie is a MASTERPIECE. It's not a kids movie where lightsaber fights are cool. Its not a spectacular CGI demonstration. It's the score we love, the environment we love, the characters we love, and, most importantly, each character has so much complexity, for them to still understand, for us to understand and for us to identify ourselves in.
It's the universe we love, in a story about friendship, love, about what's right and wrong. Not only this movie is amazing, it's the only Star Wars that genuinely explores feelings and characters in such a deep way.
Star wars was never about lightsabers and stardestroyers, that made it better, for sure, but not what it was all about.
This movie is STAR WARS. Maybe not the best, but could easily be.
If you didn't like this movie, i feel sorry for you because you were a fan... One who never understood what Star Wars was all about...

title: Satisfying closure (Spoilers)
review:
That movie is far from being a 10, but even further from a 1. Guys, there are 10 possible ratings for a reason, stop this hatred. I am absolutely positive that Return of the Jedi would be hated by those "Star Wars fans" if it came out today. It is simply impossible to satisfy this toxic fandom.

The movie has a very extensive story, that does often surprise the viewer (e.g. Rey's parentage). Yet however, the story is not incredible - I mean we accepted that Darth Vader was Luke's father and Leia his sister. Back in the 80s, this wasn't less surprising as today is Rey's origin. All in all the movie serves its purpose with a story that concludes all nine episodes very well. If you understand the movie, you enjoy it. Some elements follow a deeper meaning, a mythological sort of destiny and symbolism (e.g. Ben's final deed) - which I found great. But quite many fans expect Star Wars movies to be like the Prequels, where every little bit of story ans character development is explained so extensively you just can't not understand it. You have to think about IX, then it does all make sense in a very beautiful interconnected way.

What I liked especially was the humor. Whereas TLJ had a lot of slapstick-comedy (Canto Bight, ugh...), ROS uses humor rather punctual to bring certain scenes even closer to the audience. This was especially true for the droids. Another very good element was the appearance of the elder generation: Luke was very similar to Ben Kenobi in Episode VI, yet with more humor (also very nice callback to his training with Yoda there). Han's short scene with Ben was one of the best moments in the entire trilogy, perfecting Ben's character development and giving a last goodbye to Solo. Leia was really great. At some points you might see that the dialogue of Carrie Fisher was not written for this movie, but you can still love her role. Her force capabilities are also nicely attached to the original trilogy. Also, Chewbacca's reaction to her death has to bring every decent fan to tears.

One other thing that was very good was the dark side around Palpatine. For the very first time we see the Sith from the prequels with their fantasy-religious style connected with the cold and technologically superior Empire. This is finally a movie that proves Star Wars is more fantasy than science-fiction and always has been. The dark side finally gets its own traditional setting as they Jedi already had before. Palpatine as the ultimate villain just makes sense, as he always has been for all episodes. The dark side of the force was seen as equally powerful to the light side, especially regarding Rey's struggle (to all Mary Sue haters: She is no Mary Sue! How could a Mary Sue make this kind of character development?).

What I disliked was the pacing of the plot. The first third of the movie feels simply overpacked with stuff, too many scenes and developments lacking sufficient "picture" to catch the audience. I would maybe appreciate an Extended Cut which does not alter the story but gives it more time to develop. At some points, the movie just went a little over the top. I didn't really need the lightning attack of Palpatine (although it was one hell of a show), for instance. Some things were just explored to intense and others not enough, more runtime would have benefitted this movie.

Yet all in all, the movie fulfills and sometimes exceeds all expectations one could raise after TLJ. I found the character development of Finn, Rey, Poe and Ben quite deep and realistic, for the first time without stereotypical roles. It is not perfect and it could have been better, yet I really liked it. Other opinions of course are welcome, but those 1/10-reviews are only unjustified hate. Thank you JJ Abrams for two fine additions to the saga.

title: Don't believe everything that a critic tells you
review:
Alright here we go. I went in with low expectations after the disappointment that was The Last Jedi (if you like that movie, good on you, I'm glad someone did, just wasn't for me)

The Rise of Skywalker is an enjoyable movie, it has everything a true fan of the franchise could ask for in its conclusion. This doesn't mean it's a perfect movie without any flaws but not every movie can be Schindlers list. Is there a little too much fan service? Yes. Is the dialogue a bit clunky? Yes. Is it a perfect movie? No. Does it warrant a 1/10 rating? Hell no.

Critics have had a field day ripping this movie a new one. The same critics that consider the Last Jedi a timeless classic. Gimme a break.

The biggest issue with this film is that J.J tries a little to hard to please everyone and clean up the mess that Rian Johnson made with the last film. The plot is a little confusing at times and the film suffers from the "Disney Effect" of taking away from dramatic elements with the use of cheap gags.

Now let's talk about what was good. Adam Driver is the best part of the new trilogy and that doesn't change here. Kylo is such a good character. Oscar Isaac is again phenomenal as Poe Dameron. Some of the acting is a bit average at times, but that's nothing new with Star Wars films.

The movie actually made me root for Rey. I wasn't sold on her the past 2 films but she was a believable hero with flaws this time round. Better late than never.

John Williams's score is, quite obviously, phenomenal and brings in elements from all 8 movie in the saga. The visuals are stunning and the movie just feels fun, something that The Last Jedi lacked.

No Star Wars movies come close to the original trilogy, but this was on par with Revenge of the Sith and better than the other films in the saga outside the OT. Give it a chance and you may be surprised.

title: Any other reviews between 1 and 10?
review:
The reviews are a bigger mess than the movie ever could be. I keep scrolling but all I see are 1s and 10s.

Did I enjoy the movie? Pretty much. Did I like the storyline? No, not really. Did I think the big plot twists were "good"? Nope, really disliked those. Did I think the acting and action were good? Yes, absolutely. Will I watch this movie again? Probably not. Do I think the 3 sequels successfully completed the Star Wars saga? No.

In fact, at this point I'm ready to sell my whole collection of movies and memorabilia.

There were some issues with the prequels, but I still enjoyed the story they told (it felt like one cohesive story).

There are bigger issues with these three sequels. And I really didn't enjoy the various stories that were told. (Rival storymakers, trying to "one up" each other and the fans, cannot write a good story.)

I won't make everything I liked or disliked because I don't like to include spoilers in my reviews.

I will say that I thought Solo and Rogue One were much better than I expected. Maybe I'll keep the original trilogy and those two.

George Lucas.... could you please pair up with another really great story teller, someone like, oh ... Ron Howard ... and write 3 complete screenplays for sequels that would pick up from "Return of the Jedi"? If Disney will just set aside Kathleen Kennedy, and get, oh ... Ron Howard... to direct, I promise I will go watch them all ... unless they have someone coming back from the dead.

title: occasionally, very occasionally, reminds us of proper star wars
review:
As an ending to what could have been the greatest science fiction franchise ever, this is a major disappointment. I hated the first half, but was pulled in somewhat in the second part, mainly because Adam Driver's Kylo Ren is kind of intriguing, at least compared to the rest of the cast. When he's around, the film almost seems like it might become proper star wars, and that despite the fact that for part of it he ponces around in the silliest Sith suit you could imagine. Whoever thought that red streaked helmet looked cool should be summarily fired from their job.

Kylo Ren inherit's the film's tradition of quasi-oedipal conflict. Motivation wise, it's not quite clear what's going on, but we know his past, who he's killed (actually I needed a reminder) and his precarious relationship with both the dark & light sides of the force & it's representative in this incarnation of the star wars universe. If only because of Driver the dreadful first half gives way to a second half that at times actually feels like proper star wars.

Unfortunately it never quite pulls it off. The story bitty & far from compelling. Rey seems like a nice girl but she's just too bland to really care. It's not Daisy Ridley's fault. She's not at all objectionable, but there is simply nothing remotely exceptional about her. As a Skywalker, she should have been a re-tread or reworking of the Luke story, the wonder of which was a bored teenager trodden down by his workaday life who suddenly finds himself swept into a galaxy spanning story of epic proportions as the key player. Technically Rei was designed along the same lines, except there was never even a remote sense of her really being swept up from the mundane in in the same way as with Luke. This is entirely the fault of the writers & a perfect example of why progressive writers with agendas really do their pet projects absolutely no favours: by making her far too powerful almost from the get-go in the very first film, they simply broke the character & plot development that was essential for her to become the pivotal character she is supposed to be.

We are never remotely worried she will fail. At anything. Because she's far, far too powerful. There is a scene at the very end where - not to give too much away - she appears out-matched albeit very briefly - but it is so out of sorts for her character it seems really odd? There's someone more powerful than Rei? That can't be.

There is some attempt at character development on the part of Rey, insofar there is the ever so slightest suggestion that she might be toying with the dark side, but we never really believe it & after three whole films it's clear that as the central character of this final trilogy she never quite makes it as a character we believe in. This is compounded by the fact that all of those with Jedi powers in this film, i.e. both jedi & Sith are suddenly imbued with vastly amplified powers, something which just makes all the rest of the action, not really seem to matter that much. Jedis are supposed to represent the power of the force, sure, but they are not supposed to be virtual Gods.

As for the rest of the cast, they are not really alive in the same way as the original characters, or even those of the prequels. John Boyega is ok, but after 3 movies I still care nothing about the guy flying the Millenium Falcon, not even to look up his name, and when - spoiler - he suddenly ascends to a top rebel commander rank, it just seems odd & jarring.

There are few good set pieces, the best of which features the broken form of the fallen death star from the very first film (or possibly the third, I'm not sure), now but a wreck in a very tempestuous sea. This is probably the point where the film feels most like Star Wars, and it's not coincidental that this is where we encounter the film's central (& arguably most climactic) conflict, where both Kylo Ren & Rey get to work on their inner demons, such as they are.

At this point it looks like the film, after a dire first half, could really redeem itself and provide a real conclusion. Unfortunately, it's unable to sustain the improvement. We are soon presented with the final conflict, unsurprisingly the final conflict between the evolved first order, now re-made as the Final Order & the still ramshackle rebel alliance. It's a shame but it isn't well done. We encounter the Emperor Palpatine once more, but now he seems increasingly like a pantomime character & the final conflict that occurs both above & below, above in the form of the clash of the imperial fleet versus the ragtag rebels & below between the adults - the jedi & the sith - working out their differences - never seems properly balanced in the way it once would have been. If you think back to the original star wars film, & the tension, the sheer impossible odds involved in the a no-hoper farm boy from Alderaan firing the killer shot that destroys the entire death star, and compare that to the pedestrian, go through the motions foxy boxing that we get here (I'm exaggerating a bit, some of it's ok I suppose), it's hard not to rue what a wasted opportunity this was.

title: As a single movie maybe a 4-5, but of no value at all for the franchise or the sequel trilogy.
review:
The movie is not actually terrible in some places. It's a fantasy adventure action movie with albeit featureless characters and unmotivated actions though, but not much in the way of a Star Wars movie. It's just incredibly generic and bland, you could probably have put the same story into the Xena franchise and made a more interesting movie from that, as it's gotten less of a space fantasy movie and more of a high fantasy narrative. The narrative connections between TRoS and the other two sequels are... pretty much nonexistent except from an interpretational point of view. You could very well have forgone with the other two movies - or with this one, as it's the least structured or well told of them all. Some MacGuffins could be taken directly from a badly written text adventure.

The actorial chemistry between Daisy Ridley and Adam Driver works very well though, while the other characters don't really show any life of their own, being the punchline of one or two or nostalgia jokes aside.

The connection to the franchise as a whole is... to say it mildly... stupid and infantile. The premise, which ties it into the saga, is off from the get-go, starting with the rolling title. After that, one logical and dramaturgical inconsistency ties itself to the last. With these inconsistencies comes a strong notion of weightlessness to every action or character in the movie. What was a dire danger or loss in one moment, was completely restored or resolved in the next.

So all in all: No recommendation from me - and a sense of bewilderment about the rating of 6.8 on here.

title: Rey and Kylo's Third Act Lacks That Special Something
review:
Evidently upset by Rian Johnson's contribution to the series in The Last Jedi, JJ Abrams has returned to the Star Wars universe to set the record straight, often directly contradicting the plot points and character arcs set in motion by the preceding film. That makes for an awkward sort of arm wrestling competition, as Johnson himself often seemed intent upon bucking the conventions established by earlier chapters in the franchise. In other words, "you undid my work, now I'm going to undo yours."

The result, in this case, is an overstuffed mammoth of a film that tries to do too much while also, somehow, accomplishing very little. Not the first time a Skywalker film has been messy, but the lack of enthusiasm and excitement is certainly new. Even in the much-maligned prequels, there was something unique and special about seeing a Star Wars movie. This time, despite the enormous budget, eight films' worth of lead-in, tons of new environments and alien races, plus constant callbacks to please the die-hards, the final product is rather bland and pedestrian. And that's probably the most damning thing I could say about it. This isn't the grand conclusion to a generations-long space epic, it's just a nondescript, run-of-the-mill science fiction shelf-filler with a billion-dollar sheen. It's a mass of writer's room concepts, tossed into a tumbler and belched out onto the screen without much connective tissue.

Episode IX does have successful moments. The law of averages says, given enough options, something's bound to stick. Yet, even when they hit upon a winner, Abrams and company's lack of conviction, their reluctance to take a risk and get firmly behind any one direction, lessens the meaning of the whole. How disappointing that it's come to this.

title: I'll forget it like I forgot Episode VIII
review:
I got part-way through Episode IX and realised I couldn't remember Episode VIII at all. I do remember Episode VII. That sums up this trilogy pretty well. The Force Awakens was good. It felt like a new Star Wars Movie and it felt like it belonged in the series. I hardly remember a scene or a line from The Last Jedi.

In The Rise of Skywalker - inappropriately named - there are enough familiar elements and characters to feel like another Star Wars Movie. However, this whole trilogy has mostly been ripping off the original trilogy. Blowing up another Death Star (again) in VII, for example. Rather than new ideas and plots, they brought the Emperor back to life, revisited the scene in which he electrocuted Luke with lightning by having him do the same to Ben and Rey.

They also mess with the canon. There are rules for sequels and prequels, including that you have to be consistent with the original plot, characters, abilities and so on. In The Rise of Skywalker, as others have pointed out, people use the Force without training, Jedi can now heal people (that would have been handy in previous movies, but clearly that ability was invented for this movie), the dead spoke to people in previous movies, but they didn't move spaceships with the Force. The Empire's ships had star destroyers on them, undermining the reason Death Stars had to be so big only 40 years ago, in real time and in the timeline of the movie.

Rather than be fresh or new, this new trilogy, especially The Rise of Skywalker, just rips off familiar plots. It doesn't do anything new or interesting. There are no great twists like there are in the original trilogy. The way it breaks from canon ruin it. We can't expect a movie made now to be like one made 40 years ago. However, with Star Trek, Spider-man, Batman and so many other movies based on old movies, TV series and comics, there is always some consistency with the original text. In some ways, Episode IX feels a bit like a parody of the original trilogy, making a bit of a joke of the ending of the series. Another reviewer said Spaceballs showed more respect for Star Wars than The Rise of Skywalker. Not a bad point at all.

I'm glad I saw this. It's watchable and it's cool to watch another Star Wars movie, but it's not at all mind-blowing, like the original trilogy was. Episode IX is just derivative. Others have said that maybe if George Lucas had made this third trilogy it would have been better and felt more like part of the Star Wars story, universe and canon. Probably true.

title: Both a very good movie and fitting conclusion to the Trilogy and Saga...
review:
I saw this movie on the very first day of the new decade, the final chapter of the Saga which has spanned forty odd years of my life. Overall, I was pleasantly surprised how it was able to bring a fitting conclusion to most of the core elements of the Trilogy, and serve as the final word on some classic core Star Wars plot-lines. Is this movie outstanding and in the realm of the classics? Absolutely not. However, Abrams and the rest of the screenwriting crew in my opinion did a fine job restoring the narrative from the odd and questionable turns taken in Episode VIII... Visually, the movie is stunning. Obviously there's a ton of CGI throughout, yet I found it hard to recognise the blending, as compared to say the Prequel Trilogy. There is so much action and story packed into the movie - too much in fact. The overall pacing is more what you'd expect from a superhero movie. The twists and turns in the story are enjoyable though. The cameos are well pulled off; they are natural and genuine, not forced or schmaltzy... Many general observers of film have recognised and acknowledged that Abrams would be panned regardless of the movie he turned out here. In some respects that can be expected, saying goodbye to characters that have transcended even the film genre in popular culture. We remember the original movies romantically, and can't fathom a physical ending. Just as in life itself - a reverence for birth and youth, with a fear and denial of death. On the other hand, modern Star Wars fandom does have a unique vitriol underpinning the passion.

I will conclude my thoughts with a piece of advice for both Star Wars fans, and others still deciding whether to see this movie. Completely ignore any review you read around here that is four stars or below - it's likely to be either from merely a silly troll, or review bomber.

title: Star wars the rise of skywalker
review:
Star wars the rise of skywalker

2019 12A director: J J abrams starring: Daisy Ridley,Oscar Isaac,John Boyega,Adam Driver,Carrie Fisher,Mark Hamill,Anthony Daniels,Richard E Grant,domnhall Gleeson,Ian Mcdiamid,Billy Dee Williams etc

overall rating 61/100

Star wars the rise of skywalker brings the new trilogy to an end. Where Ray is finishing her jedi training. But as her bond with Kylo Ren grows stronger she must find out what kind of person he really is. With many unanswered questions about her family tree. Rey is about to make a discovery that will change her forever. The rise of skywalker was ok and entertaining for some parts. But for me extremely disappointing and the worst film in the new saga. Lets talk about why this is.

First of all the films visuals and action sequences were great to see. First of all the film looked fantastic. With breathtaking set locations and a wide variation of aliens and creature designs. It was a visual delight. And the action sequences were great. With the perfect blend of traditional fight scenes used in previous star wars movies and new and creative action sequences as well.

However for me the film had both pacing and tonal issues and inconsistencies. This film had a mixture of slow pacing that dragged and really rushed pacing because they crammed to much in. Having one of these issues is bad enough but to have an uneven blend of slow and fast pacing really makes for a poorly pit together and clunky movie. And the film had several tonal issues as well. It had scenes that weren't supposed to be funny but were and then when they were trying to be funny it didn't land for a large majority of the time.

Next the film had good uses of nostalgia and well executed plot twists. The film did have a lot of good fan service and uses of nostalgia to please all fans of the franchise both old and new. Having the return of characters like Lando and palpatine were admittedly fun to watch. And they had some great moments within the film especially Palpatine who was one of the few fantastic characters within the rise of skywalker. And next the film had surprisingly well executed plot twists that i didn't see happening. Having Palpatine be Reys grandfather was an interesting and well executed twist. And bought a very interesting conflict with Reys characters about what side she was really on which i thought was great.

My next two negatives would be the bland characters in the movie and the Carrie Fisher moments. For me sadly despite the nice intentions none of the Carrie Fisher moments worked for me. In order for her to be in the film they had to find previously unused footage and piece it all together and it was really obvious and clear that she was not actually on the screen the whole time. She almost looked like a hologram and she looked different in most of her scenes. So this for me made any scene with her in disjointed and made the narrative clunky whenever it was her character on screen. And for me aside from the characters of Rey,Kylo Ren and Palpatine all the characters in the film were bland and there charecter arcs were not bought to a satisfying ending and not even really an ending for them either. C3PO and R2D2 were there for pure nostalgia and a silly plot point about C3PO's memory being wiped. Poe and Finn were aweful in the film. They spent so much time focusing on,lets face it the only really entertaining characters the film had to offer. That they pretty much forgot about everyone else. And they just gave the characters no personality and there character arcs were practically non existent for the last film in the sage.

My next two positives would the films good use of character arcs for the main two characters and the performance of Daisy Ridley. Reys charecter arc throughout the rise of skywalker was great as time and attention was put into her character. To see her battle with herself about whether she is good or bad and choose to keep the legacy of the jedi going was a very satisfying development throughout the film. And for Adam Drivers charecter to make the slow transformation into an ally was very well executed as he realised his true potential. And i have to give credit here Daisy Ridley did an amazing performance in the film. Taking it very seriously and delivering well in her serious,funny and action scenes leading her to be a fun and likeable character that is easy to get behind. And i do also have to mention Adam drivers performance and the chemistry between Rey and Kylo ren/Ben solo was one of my key highlights. There connection made the film the most entertaining. Seeing there bond growing throughout the film was very interesting, and the fact that Rey was the cause of Ben going to the light was fantastic.

my next two negatives would be the new characters and the nights of Ren and the storm troopers. I honestly thought the new characters were chucked in the film for the sake of it.They had no real purpose,no back story,no arcs or development, they were just simply pointless to the movie. And contributed nothing towards the film. And the nights of Ren showed up like they were important characters, which had the opposite effect of me as they were pretty much not used before. So they lacked any form of threat or urgency. And they just went a step to far with how ridiculously easy it was to beat the storm troopers. They literally stood there and practically fell for the characters they were that useless. They did add a nice arc for the storm troopers adding that the people under the helmets were forced to do the bidding of the bad guys which was nice, but it still didn't take away from the fact that there action sequences were poor.

My final positive for me would be the entertaining final act.This saved the film for me. Reys and kylo Ren's arcs came full circle, the nostalgia was heavily and effectively used, and the action sequences were at there best. This improved my opinion on the film a fair amount as if the final battle underwhelmed then my score would be much lower. Its a shame they waited until the final act to pull out all the stops effectively but i still appreciated the effort.

However sadly my final two negatives are there poor execution of deaths, and the fact that they just crammed to much plot in to little screen time. The films deaths,especially with princess Leai were disappointing and rushed. They Wasted her character and the way she died was ridiculous. And they mourned for about 5 minutes and then moved on,taking away the emotional impact that these scenes should of had. And they just left themselves with to much to do for the final film. They had to much plot to cover, to many character arcs to finish which they only managed with two characters and this just led to the film feeling rushed and messy.

Overall despite its performances,good character arc for there main character and a fantastic final act. The rise of skywalker is the worst film in the new saga and sadly ends it on a very disappointing and messy conclusion.

review: First of all, this movie is very predictable. I can't fully explain this but I made a joke yesterday about how this movie was going to end and I was completely right. The pacing in this movie is so bad because as much as this pains me to say this but this movie is kind of boring to sit through. The movie never really picks up the pace and everything just feels like they had to drag it out in order to get the longer run time. As much as I think J.J. Abrams is a good director this movie wasn't his strongest and I feel like it's because he has to try and explain everything that happened in, "The Last Jedi" in this movie which caused this movie to be slightly boring. Even the action scenes weren't the greatest. I really wanted to get into the finale action scene but honestly, I just couldn't. It was such a great experience getting to see it all happen but nothing really happened to bring me into the action and put me on the edge of my seat. I will give them credit for trying but then it immediately gets resolved which is another thing that bugged me was things getting resolved so quickly. Things got resolved so quickly that there were no threats for the audience to be like how are they going to get out of this one because something would happen and resolve it. I do have to say that I love what they did with Leia in this movie due to the passing of Carrie Fisher in 2017. All of the actors in this movie did the best they could with what they were given but it wasn't everybody's best work. Really the only good things about this movie is the nostalgia and John Williams score. In the end, The Rise of Skywalker could have been better if J.J. Abrams didn't have to do damage control. I definitely will rewatch this movie for a spoiler review and to cement my feelings on it.

review: I love some of Abrams' credits - especially as producer for "WestWorld". Contrary to some earlier iterations in the Star Wars series, this one needs story help. It's full of illogical jumps and plot holes. In my estimation, storytelling - ultimately - falls on the director's shoulders. Given the resources put into the film, going weak on story seems to be sad mistake. Movie goers should expect better.

title: A fitting ending to an inter-generational legend.
review:
Finishing off this nine movie phenomenon was never going to be easy. Like Game of Thrones recently found out (and to an extent the previous movie, The Last Jedi), it is anextraordinarily difficult line to tread between fan service and trying something a bit different. It is left to one of the few genuine storytellers to try to pull this off, and I am delighted to say that he has done so. It is by no means a perfect movie but it is difficult to see how it could have been given what was riding on it.

TLJ was too devisive to call a genuine success so some recalibration was needed. To that end, we get the return of Palpatine and Lando who ably justify their inclusion. It is also noticeable that previously sidelined stalwarts of the series get more chance to shine here, righting some of the perceived wrongs of previous entries to the series. The script is forced at times but, on the whole, rattles along at a good pace. The standout performance is Daisy Ridley, who has the screen presence to hold the story on course. She is the glue to which everything sticks. There are surprises, twists and laughs but they do not become distracting. They are also genuine moments which will bring a tear to the eye of those of us that have been there since the beginning. All in all, it has it all. I did say it was not perfect but I can't explain these without huge spoilers so you will have to judge these yourselves.

This is not The Empire Strikes Back, but neither is it Attack of the Clones! It is about as good an ending as we could hope for and therefore worthy of your hard earned currency.

title: Star Wars: I Gotta A Ménage à Trois Feeling About This
review:
Star Wars: I Gotta A Ménage à Trois Feeling About This

Star Wars: The Rise Of Skywalker or SW:TROS or just TROS - is not a bad film. Not as good nor will any be as good as the first three Star Wars films released beginning in 1977 and certainly nowhere near as bad as the media is making it out to be.(sidenote) About 95% of folk who claim to be 'film critics' in the 21st century suffer from an affliction known as 'heaDUPtheIRAss', which I think is a Dutch term that means they have no idea what they are talking about. Anyway, with Star Wars: The Rise Of Skywalker you still experience the 'roll your eyes' moments, the story suffers from 'convenience' and the logistics of the characters never make sense - this transcends every one of the trilogies and is almost expected from any Star Wars film. The VFX in Rise was meh....other Star Wars productions have produced better. I was hugely disappointed in Oscar Isaac, an Oscar caliber performer who pretty much dialed in his delivery. The one whose star shone bright, who after The Force Awakens stated she was not a Star Wars fan, Daisy Ridley blew the doors off everyone - this version of the Rey character is what Star Wars films should have contained from the beginning. It was sad to see the Kylo Ren character be transformed into what Rise delivered, which is no fault to Adam Driver, because..... J.J. Abrams should have never been given the the latest Star Wars trilogy mantle in the first place. J.J. Abrams has a bit of originality, but there is way too much of his mentor's vision in the majority of his work. Of course, Rian Johnson took a HUGE dump on The Last Jedi, so bringing Abrams back for the save on Rise was a worthy attempt, nut in no way could make up for the damage done by Johnson. Also, J.J. loves introducing new audiences to existing sagas by taking old storylines and elements and reconditioning them as new - these are as obvious as a $3.00 bill and... Just Stop It, J.J.. Star Wars: The Rise Of Skywalker was an OK film of a troubled trilogy that should never have begun without a team of writers, producers and directors who bled Star Wars from their veins and had the complete vision of the complete Star Wars saga documented and storyboarded before casting.

title: Redeeming and perfect finish to a franchise that deserves it
review:
I grew up watching the films in chronological order and loved the universe in general including the KOTR games and comics.

So when I watched The Last Jedi I was devastated by the bad direction when it came to Rey and the force and I believed there was no fixing the damage done in that film. However I was proved wrong!

This film answers all the questions of the whole franchise. It finally humanises the previously unreal strength of Rey and answers the question as to why she is so strong. Closes the story of Finn, Poe, Rey, Kylo and gives so many dramatic moments. Develops Rey and Kylo's relationship beautifully. Does not put any plot points to waste. Fixes the Snoke and Skywalker plot problems of the last film in a genius manner. This film manages to fit in everything the other films failed to do.

A truly spectacular end to a saga. I understand the frustrations many older fans had with the film however for the position the team were in they managed to pull an impossible fix to the franchise since Disneys take over of Lucasfilms. I understand there were mistakes made in the previous Films and I admit the trilogy was not perfect and that brings many valid reasons that would challenge my rating but personally the directing of this film was the best it could be with the narrative resources it had from the franchise hence why I give this Film as a finishing piece itself a 10/10. This film saved the trilogy. If you have not watched this film you would find this film narratively satisfying as a feel good action adventure family friendly franchise.

title: A MASTERPIECE OF A MOVIE
review:
To begin with, The Rise Of Skywalker is an excellent movie. Regular movie-goers should be able to see that. Brilliant cinematography, acting, scoring, directing in general. JJ Abrams knows how to make a good movie. Star Wars fans now should be more than happy. Not only is it an improvement from The Last Jedi (which was also a good movie objectively speaking) but it also gave tha saga a more than satisfying ending. The non-stop action, excellent dialogues, incredible storytelling and writing, tear-jerking scenes, etc were more than enough reason for this movie to deserve an objective 10/10 rating. This movie easily stands next to Empire Strikes Back as the best star wars movie.
I wouldn't really listen to critics, biased fanboys or people who think are real star wars fans just because they were in a movie theatre in 1977. I've personally seen every movie, animated and live-action show, read many many comics and novels, all of which is more than those fans I mentioned earlier have done. Meaning that I can review this movie knowing more about the sw universe than people who give TROS low ratings just because "it's not the ending that they wanted".
Go watch this movie without listening to anyone and make up your own mind. Everyone who worked on it poured their heart into this film. It deserves our love.

For me, it's all a cool story but it just doesn't have the substance to be as impactful as any movie from the original trilogy.

title: Loved it
review:
Yes I know I was not around when the original films came out and since I am not the ORIGINAL fan I don't know any better and have no right to have an opinion, but I loved this film.

First I take into account the fact that its impossible to come up with something as original as the original films, however unlike popular opinion I do not think they should stop making films in this universe because of it.

Agreed several terrible choices in the film: 1. Palpatine is alive - it diminished Anakin's sacrifice 2. Rey is Palpatine's grand daughter - just absurd 3. Rey's and Ben's healing powers - not really in line with how the force works

But the first one sort of could make sense since it has been outlined in the prequels that Sith have such powers, the third one's thought process could have been that Rey and Ben both have a touch of dark side so...

Now what I loved ... all these maybe because I have never had any expectation for these movies to have the originality and depth of the original trilogy, but still: 1. Fight scenes - the whole film is set almost entirely of the fight scenes of some kind which was really cool 2. Parallels to the other films - several times in these film we have seen some kind of scene that has reminded me of the old films 3. The final battle - this film has outlined very strongly that the Sith are over, the balance has been brought, so it was a nice ending to what has started in the original films.

In this sense, for me this trilogy and the last film itself was kind of a small shot of Star Wars to make me remember that adrenaline once more. Not an in depth Star Wars movie but still great to watch.

I had fun, I enjoyed and that's all I had expected so I am satisfied. Surely this will not remain a classic as the original films did and the attempt to create new Leia, Luke and Han in Rey, Fin and Poe will not work, but enjoyed this and will watch if they make another one as long there are light-sabers and that soundtrack.

Oh, and one last thing I was worried about since it had to be done for obvious reasons I think it was a perfect way for Leia's ending to happen for connecting to her son and saving a new hope of the galaxy.

title: The exact reason I love movies and hate 'fans'
review:
Firstly, and to be plain: there is no such thing as a perfect film. This is because the whole point of art is that it's subjective.

Now that we've cleared that up, I want to say, as someone who grew up watching these films, and whose parents grew up watching these films, I am absolutely thrilled at how this ending turned out and think it was a beautiful tribute to all the previous episodes and characters. The story was strong, it had the same sense of self-deprecating humour, cheesy moments, gorgeous cinematography, brilliant fight sequences and, of course, some incredibly moving moments. I thought the loss of Carrie was handled respectfully and woven into Leia's story really well.

It just felt like the right way for it all to end.

And, to briefly reference my review title, reading so many of these reviews reminds me why I view self-named SW fans with contempt. They have this incredibly specific vision for how they want the films to turn out and, when they don't get their own way, they have a tantrum. I cannot imagine how much work and love has gone into this film and it must be really annoying for everyone involved to see spoilt non-fans try to tear it down. I honestly don't understand what there could be not to like about this film.

Personally, I got everything I needed and wanted out of the film. Of course there were some minor things I might do differently had I been making it, but, because I'm genuinely enjoy films and am an actual movie fan and not just a frustrated critic looking to be upset, I can appreciate another person's vision and still enjoyed the film as a whole immensely.

Well done to absolutely everyone involved on such a gorgeous and emotional film. I cried, partly from nostalgia and partly because it is, at its core, a film about hope.
