title: Pulp (Science-Fantasy) Fiction
review:
There's a popular term in internet circles for THE RISE OF SKYWALKER, calling it "fan service" i.e. providing fans what they'd want or expect from a STAR WARS movie. Imagine if The World Series was lambasted for the players using wooden bats to hit a white ball around a grassy field...

So compared to Rian Johnson's understandably maligned THE LAST JEDI, director J.J. Abrams hits it out of his own safe ballpark in a hybrid/rehash of RETURN OF THE JEDI with similarities to another Lucasfilm classic, RAIDERS OF THE LOST ARK...

In particular, a Staff of Ra type device that, maneuvered strategically against an adjoined-perspective-backdrop, can pinpoint another, more important device (i.e. McGuffin) that will locate a lost Sith planet, where a resurrected Emperor Palpatine has poised more Star Destroyers than we've seen in all three trilogies combined (hardly a spoiler since it happens within the first minute)...

Surprisingly, with loads of gun fights, lightsaber duels and race-against-time corners to get out of, there's not very much tension or suspense in SKYWALKER, more about the fully-collected ragtag group planet-hopping in a basic, frolicking fashion like ROGUE ONE (that borrowed from GUARDIANS OF THE GALAXY) instead of the awkward and disjointed LAST JEDI... which isn't entirely neglected...

A mentally-linked Rey and Kylo again keep winding up together despite being in different places, where the most important action/fight sequences occur. It's creative enough but can get confusing, turning an otherwise breezy and pulpy adventure into that Rian Johnson mindtrip kinda thing that simply doesn't flow very well...

Meanwhile, the cocky Poe Dameron, while no longer under the henpecking thumb of Laura Dern's interstellar Hillary Clinton, seems almost equally burdened, somehow...

In fact, throughout the entire "new trilogy" he never really cuts loose like he seems created to do (intentionally mirroring the original endearing rascal, Han Solo, who makes a brief memory-cameo; Carrie Fisher is neatly patchworked through archive footage; and Luke's the inevitable advice-giving Force Ghost)...

The faithful Finn is more of a tagalong with Chewbacca, the sidekick of a tagalong, plus a returning (finally accessible) C3PO and an underused Lando Calrissian, who could have easily been another newly-introduced good guy helping our heroes plunge from Point A to Point B...

Or rather, D to E or wherever they wind up in this scavenger hunt maze that, during a non-draggy two-and-a-half hours, doesn't provide very much depth for the audience. But perhaps that's the point...

Like Abram's THE FORCE AWAKENS, now confirmed as the best of Disney's STAR WARS Trilogy, THE RISE OF SKYWALKER is old school energetic escapism, and really doesn't try to be anything else...

As for being the end of the Skywalker saga: it actually seems more like the beginning of The Adventures of Rey since the original heroes weren't used all that much, and were basically her own personal catapults throughout.

title: VIEWS ON FILM review of Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker
review:
It was the fall of 1977. I was only three when my dad took me to see the original Star Wars (A New Hope). I may have fell asleep during the opening crawl but it still remains my earliest childhood memory. Now forty-two years later, J. J. Abrams has come to wrap up the Star Wars saga via Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker. The Jedi are still battling the Sith, Rey and Kylo Ren are still confronting each other with badass lightsabers, and Poe and Finn are still on rescue mission mode.

Reflecting on the first three Star Wars films (episodes IV, V, and VI), "Rise" resembles them somewhat even if it lacks their fabled, magical dust. Abrams returning to direct the final installment, doesn't get all artsy and cerebral like Rian Johnson did in The Last Jedi. He fashions "Rise" as rather a fast-clipped, popcorn pic. At 142 minutes, it's long but far from being boring.

There are critics who say that Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker is confusing, poorly edited, and lacking in continuity. This critic followed the flick just fine. Abrams packs every frame with action to the gills, some friendly Resistance ribbing, and some whizzing set pieces. His CGI is effective without being overdone yet his tying up of all things "galaxy far, far away" is a little brusque. Oh well. It's not easy trying to finalize nine movies over the past four decades.

Let me put it this way: J. J. Abrams improves greatly on his foray into Star Wars lore sans the meat and potatoes vehicle, The Force Awakens. He keeps it old school in the heirloom-ed, space opera universe. Look for a Harrison Ford-Han Solo cameo, the return of Emperor Palpatine, and the return of good old Lando Calrissian. Bottom line: Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker rarely feels retreaded or riskless nor does it bring back any annoying characters (I'm glad I didn't have to see Jar Jar Binks). It's exciting, knife-edge, and aerodynamic in its approach. Rating: 3 stars.

title: Not perfect, but a very enjoyable movie!
review:
The first part of the movie felt a bit rushed in my opinion. There was a lot of spaceship action going on and it was quite hard to follow at times. This was actually a bit of an issue all throughout the movie. There were a lot of things going on all over the place. This is not necessarily a bad thing as it can add value when you rewatch the film, however, if you get distracted for only a little bit, you can miss some things. These little things often don't really matter in the bigger picture though. halfway through the movie(till the end) I really started to enjoy the movie. the plot was very interesting, and even surprised me a bit. I like how it diverts from more classic narrative structures which makes watching this movie a more adventure like experience in which you don't really know what's going to happen next. I also like the themes in this movie. The battle between Rey, Ben and Palpatine was for a large part psychological. The resulting self doubt and even fear added an extra dimension of complexity and danger.

Overall I really enjoyed Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker

Pros:
  • Interesting characters
  • Both visually and mentally a spectacle
  • Themes like fear and hope impemented in interesting ways
  • Some references to original Star Wars movies( like how the ghost of Luke lifted his spaceship out of the water, just like he tried to do when he began training with Yoda )


Cons:
  • Very long
  • Some scenes and sudden turns of events felt unnessecary
  • All the baddies died and pretty much all the good guys lived in the end.

title: It delivers exactly what it says on the tin....
review:
Ok, so.... Star Wars - The Rise of Skywalker.

I liked it!! In fact, I'd go as far as to say I really liked it!

Yes, its Cheesy. But news flash all ye film critic wannabes.... so was Star Wars - A New Hope. So was Star Wars - The Empire Strikes back. And so was Star Wars - Return of The Jedi. They were all cheesy. They were meant to be! They are classic Heroes vs Villains tales set in space!! What did you honestly expect - Shawshank Redemption??

Heroes always win! Thats the moral of the tale, after all.

But if you can let go of all the "Urgh, Disney ruins everything" hangups that folks seem so dead set upon, what you are left with is a visually stunning, action packed, nostalgia fuelled, honest to god "Space Pirates" sci-fi film that delivers exactly what it says on the tin.

Star.... Wars!

Kudos to JJ Abrams for taking on George Lucas's legacy, and making an epic adventure film full of galactic explosions, stunning light sabre duels, and every boys (and tom-boy girls') laser gun stand off fantasys', despite the impossible expectations of "fans" and film "critics" alike.

I, sir, applaud you.

(And Daisy, I applaud Daisy Ridley too.... I mean, you guys have seen her right?!? 😍 Ahem!)

title: You've seen it before, only then it was better.
review:
I'm a Star Wars fan, simple. The magic of the original trilogy thrilled me as a child in the eighties. Every iconic scene and character will stay with me forever. New Jedi, seeing more of their powers in action, even jar jar was a digital experiment that, while not great, worked at the time. Attack of the clones and revenge of the sixth completed a good story arc, again filled with memorable set pieces and scenes, good actors. These last three films, and rise in particular have had almost nothing of what made Star Wars great. No originality. Rise for example has a scene so like pod racing from phantom menace it was embarrassing. We have seen these planets before, yeah give a little fan service nod to other places and character, but keep it subtle. The ending of this film includes a massive battle to end all space battles, thousands of ships both good and bad - it should have been incredible, should being the key word. It flopped, it was boring! How the people that made this film have managed to make a thousand space ship battle boring is honestly quite impressive!
To say I'm disappointed is an understatement, to have this as the final film is heartbreaking. No care for the characters, no care for a coherent story, respectful of what has come before, no originality, no drama, passion or love. Throw in some old characters, planets and scenes we have had before, send it to the cinemas and make a billion. A win for Disney, a loss for fans.

title: Silly and mostly bad
review:
I always kind of wondered if JJ Abrams was a hack. I enjoyed his film Cloverfield and a few others, but ever since Star Trek Into Darkness, where he retconned the Star Trek 2 plot and basically just redid it with different actors, I began to wonder, "Is this guy a "good" director, as I originally thought, or a talentless hack?" After Star Wars 9, I'm thinking more the latter.
For all the praise he gets, many of his films now consist of taking the storyline of other, better films, and jury rigging them into slightly different plot lines. Look no further than his much more lauded feature in the Star Wars myth, episode 7. It's Star Wars, A New Hope, with different people and a different setting. It even has a new Death Star, just planet-based.
Ultimately though, my biggest issue isn't the sameness of the story, compared to other outings, it's the absurd length JJ goes to erase episode 8, and the culmination of the film. I won't go into too much detail, as others have done well with that. I'll just point out that when we first see the stupidly sized "dark Star Destroyer" fleet (how did more ships than existed in the entire Empire get built secretly without anyone noticing?), the equally-stupidly sized Rebel fleet, and the Emperor "force-lightning's" the entire rebel armada, I was noticeably rolling my eyes in the theater, was I watching a Monty Python sketch?
Bottom line, it's just a dumb movie with a terrible plot that feels like it was written by an army of 13 year olds who saw the original trilogy exactly one time. Maybe that sums up JJ's level of writing.

title: This really was the last hope, and it failed
review:
What was it about the original trilogy that made it so magical ?

I remember going to Leicester Odeon in London in 1979 as a 10 year old boy, and being blown away, nothing was ever the same again.

Sure thats alot harder to do in this day and age, but its like they didnt even try.

Episodes 1-3 are best forgotten, though #3 is likeley better than #8, but that is not saying alot.

I liked #7 more because it went back in the direction of Star Wars compared to #1-3 than it being itself a great movie, it was kinda above average repeat of #4, but it gave us hope for the future.

#8 was an absolute joke of a movie, insulting our intelligence, and 40% of the movies being totally unnecessary.

But #9 was our last hope, JJ was back to build on his safe version of the Star Wars Universe kickoff, but its fell hugely flat.

There were some very good fresh ideas that were started in #7 that were crushed in #8 and could have worked better in #9 but did not.

As multiple reviewers have said before, its like they had no outline of the basic plot for #7 thru 9. They just made it up with each movie.

JJ said he laughed when he saw that Snokes had been killed off in #8, i think that is code for he was really "pissed off", so its almost like he used #9 as revenge for killing off snokes.

How can Rian murder a star wars movie, then go and make something as intricate as Knives out ?

Its scary they have given Rian the rights to direct the new star wars trilogy.

title: Bringing balance... to all these negative reviews
review:
(my first review! it felt a bit necessary) I don't entirely understand why people are so insistent on annihilating Disney's Star Wars trilogy. Is it trendy? Is it upset 40+ year olds missing the way it used to be? I wasn't alive when the originals were released, I grew up on the prequels (which people trashed when they came out(!!)) so I reckon I can be a bit more objective about these things.

Anyway... was it perfect? Not really. It was a bit predictable, it probably could have has 20 minutes cut out to speed things up a bit.

Is it a 1/10? Abso-bloody-lutely not. It was a fitting ending to a decent trilogy - Ben was reunited with his parents, Rey discovered her heritage and came into her power and the gang finally saved the day. It made me laugh, it had my heart in my throat a few times, and it made me cry. And I think that's the point - it's not an Oscar-winning masterpiece, but I went into the cinema expecting a Star Wars film and that's exactly what I got, with all the trimmings. The acting, the effects and the suspense were great, the action was fun, the stakes were high and the climax was powerful (aided by John Williams and his incredible score, as usual. He's really good at hitting us right in the feels, y'know?) The cameos were an exciting throwback, it made me feel nostalgic for a time I never lived in.

So maybe it's just me being "the youth", but I thoroughly enjoyed it. Maybe more "fans" should let go of their preconcieved Star Wars notions - the originals aren't all you idolise them to be, that's just childhood wistfulness and misplaced nostalgia talking. They were good, sure, but so is this. So please (for once) stop complaining, and enjoy what is, objectively, an exciting film.

title: A Forceful last hope of the Empire's Solo Rouge Return
review:
A Long time ago in a galaxy, far, far, far away George Lucas watched a bunch of Japans films and thought to himself... let's do it in space! Billions of dollars later, 11 films and 2 decades we come to it, the end of all things. Star Wars: The Rise Of Skywalker. So the reel question is, can this work? Can J.J.Abram's pick up the pieces left off the floor that Rian Johnson blew up or is it too much to ask for even the man who made Mission Impossible awesome?

Rise Of The Skywalker is like a psychological test. Do I forget the logic that I carry and enjoy the film for what it's worth or criticize it for plot holes and inconsistency with the rest of the franchise? This is how a lot of Star Wars cult fans must see the movie. I enjoyed it for its successful large scale set pieces; I forgave it for its surreal plot moves and irrelevant characters.

That seemed to be one of the issues The Last Jedi faced, it always had too many plates spinning for Ryan Johnson to handle. He couldn't keep up with his multiple plot threats which both somehow separated everyone and brought them all back together simultaneously in a seemingly organic way. He failed, miserably. Thankfully J.J. Abram's destroys The Last Jedi in the opening moments by (, SPOILER!) revealing that Snook was nothing more than a clone created to lure the real prize to the ultimate villain of the piece... The Emperor.

This sets us up perfectly for the nostalgic ride that The Force Awakens gave us... Kylo teaming with Emperor Palpatine? Why? Because the fans demand it! That possibly could be the answer to many of the questions that Rise Of The Skywalker hands us... Because the fans demand it! I don't mind that the film is ultimately just fan fiction made flesh just as long as it embraces it too. In justice to the movie, I believe it does. There is just too much fan services for J.J. to not be conscious of what he is doing.

This is undeniably the most Star Wars film since Star Wars. Everything you could want from the film and more is broken down into little chunks and spoon-fed to us. Each beat is neatly signposted so we can't get confused or be surprised. That's the challenge of the new franchise, merging the nostalgic while keeping it fresh. Princess Leia Poppins is the ultimate example of this, we know Jedi and Sith can lead great distances, we don't want them to fly that's just silly.

Rise Of The Skywalker is not the greatest Star Wars film ever made, that is still Rogue One, but it is far from the worst. J.J. succeeds in tying up his part in the franchise whilst serving both old and new one's enjoyment. Rise Of The Skywalker is a fitting conclusion to the reboot of Star Wars.

title: Slimy, Yet Satisfying
review:
*Slow clap* Put simply, I enjoyed it. The music... Oh the music. The story was original enough to be interesting, with some rhymes to other genres. The acting was great. The visuals were nothing short of brilliant. The fan service was pleasing. Did it all make perfect sense? Of course not, but then again neither did episode IV. It can't, otherwise it would be bland.

This was an EPIC story of two young, powerful, and influential people rejecting the concept that things must be a certain way as commanded by a narrow-minded old person who thinks they have it all figured out and young people must ultimately want what he wants. Could the underlying idea be more relevant but also timeless? Rey is a Skywalker because she relates to their struggles more than Palpatine. She builds off the lessons of Anakin, Luke, Leia, and Ben thus putting the story to rest while honoring their sacrifices. How is that not a plot line or story worth telling?

To address the elephant in the room... haters gonna hate. Please see the movie as a positive fan like you were when you were young and saw episode IV - VI. Many of the reviews here are laced with such negativity that I almost feel sorry for them. Story telling is challenging, and SHOULD evolve in lots of different ways. As an avid Star Wars fan, I can say it held true to lots of canon and legends material, and I wish I could address all the comments I've seen incorrectly shouting down concepts that indeed exist in the Star Wars universe, but there isn't time. If you Chase a feeling, you will never be content. If you've ever had a perfect vacation, then gone back and tried to re-create it years later you know the disappointment this can cause. Make new adventures. Let it go and remember the good. Enjoy the new with the old. You will be happier and more appreciative.

The movie isn't perfect, but it is certainly worth the price of admission. I'm excited for more Disney Star Wars, because the alternative is no Star Wars. You'll get some duds (Jar Jar... I'm looking at you buddy... and you aren't even Disney), but you'll also get some gems (Mandolorian). Keep em coming.

Yet I always feel like a child sitting in the movie theater with at least one of my parents next to me. Star Wars makes me feel young and it is sad to see this is the real end. I was overall pleased and this sequel trilogy finally redeemed itself after a shaky start. I complained about The Force Awakens, then I saw improvement in The Last Jedi and finally The Rise of Skywalker makes it feel like the old Star Wars with old characters returning for nostalgia.

One thing is that having J.J. Abrams returning to write and direct had me worried. He went back to the winning formula of Return of the Jedi which is a big part of the reason why Episode IX works. It was nice to see recycled and unused footage of Carrie Fisher to complete the trilogy. Some of the mystery plot points in this saga are solved and it opens up other questions.

The Rise of Skywalker does this trilogy justice. Go see it with your family and a new generation.

TRoS answered (although not always greatly), many of the questions I had from TFA and TLJ.

Was the movie perfect? No, it had its flaws. But it was absolutely enjoyable and provided a satisfying conclusion to the new trilogy.

If you go into this movie with the mindset of nitpicking it the whole time, you will not enjoy it. Nor would you enjoy ANY movie if your goal was to nitpick it the entire time. If you go in with an open mind, you will find yourself engaged with the story and enjoying every second.

title: Unimaginative and simplistic, yet entertaining enough.
review:
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker concluded the Star Wars saga with an uplifting spirit of togetherness. While it lacked originality and imagination, as did the other two films in the sequel trilogy, it provided the audience with a simple-yet-heartwarming closure to a decades-long galactic adventure.

The main problem with the sequel trilogy rooted from the creative differences during the production, especially in the screenplay department. For instance, the original trilogy was primarily written by George Lucas with the help of two other writers. The latest trilogy was written by several different writers, with Star Wars: The Last Jedi written and directed by a single person, who was then not involved in the making of the final episode. This resulted in unfocused plots that failed to tell a single coherent story. Moreover, the trilogy also suffered from the absence of a main villain - each episode had its own antagonistic characters, but not a single strong character to faithfully lead the dark side of the force. It seemed that Rian Johnson's decision to kill off a potentially major supervillain in the Star Wars: The Last Jedi was a blunder that the filmmakers simply could not bounce back from. This had set a mountain too high to climb for the writers and director of the final episode, and they could only do as much.

Nevertheless, one could still enjoy watching their favourite characters back in action after more than a decade of absence. Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker was also full of reminiscences of the past events in the saga that took the audience on a pleasant final trip down memory lane. This showed a commendable devotion of the filmmakers to the fans and an understanding that a Star Wars film need not be complex to be successful - it needs only to entertain and this film did just that. Overall, Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker was entertaining and evocative, although its unimaginative plot story and reliance on the appearances of characters from the original trilogy would draw criticisms from both critics and the general audience alike.

title: Star Wars: Episode IX the Rise of Mediocrity. The Skywalker Saga has fallen so low.
review: It's clear now that this film franchise was doom from the start when Disney buy out Lucasfilm. Nobody had a clue how to further tell the story. So, director JJ Abrams and producer Kathleen Kennedy closely just rehash the same formulaic tropes of the original trilogy again with a few lazy reconstructing twists. They didn't even bother using with any of the establishing lore from books that could had made the films seen somewhat unique and new. Look, as much as people hate the prequels. At least, they gave us somewhat of a beginning tale that somewhat fit into the continuous story of the originals. As for these sequel series, they really do hurt most of the canon lore. This movie being the worst. It ruined the whole Skywalker redemption arch by having Darth Sidious (Ian McDiarmid) return with yet again with the over clichÃ©s easy to pick off out of nowhere planet killing ships rather than going all in with more complex well-acted Kylo Ren (Adam Driver). It also gave the whole Chosen One prophecy to somebody else. Perhaps the biggest let down in the movie was finding out that semi alright Rey (Daisy Ridley) does indeed have a grand gifted lineage rather than the idea that great power within the Force can manifest in anyone. Don't get me wrong, having Rey be related to the real villain is not a bad idea. It just shouldn't be biological parental because it's a bit off putting that somebody pork her grandfather. Instead she should be one of the many female Sith cultist clones that was model after Sidious including trailer fodder Darth Rey. Emperor Palpatine that died previous should be the male clone also separate from Sidious. It would better explain why the ancient dark lord look like in bad shape as he made copies upon copies of himself over time and why he can heal himself back once a clone like Rey dies. As for the old Supreme Leader. I would love to think that the reason why he looks rough was because he was one of the very few copies of the demise Darth Plagueis. It can explain why Sidious was able to gain control of him so easily. All this would make more sense than what the film gave us. Another thing that was disappointing is having Ren work with Sidious and Rey trying to burn the lightsaber. It dropped the ball with Rey's beliefs of preserving the past to gain knowledge and strength was counterpart to Kylo's wants to destroy it as he felt that it binds people to weakness and ignorance. The film also ignored their dyadic idealistic understanding that future peace can only be made with the meager of the cookie cutter light and the dark side of the force into the grey area way. It sucks. Also having Rey fall in love with the man that killed all her mentors is an unhealthy forced romantic relationship. Such a turn off more than the last movie. That was one thing that should had been retcon! At least Abrams keep the good thing about their communicate. The idea that they can move items through their mental and physical force powers despite not being in the same location was cool to witness even if it never established or used in the original or prequel series. Yet the used age of the new half-baked force healing was not well done. It makes demise seem like a game of hot potato. Likewise, if the force can straight up heal people and even bring them back from near death. Why would Jedis forbid the practice? It sounds like they could had saved the universe all this problem if they taught a certain Skywalker how to do it many moons ago. To add onto that the idea that most of the dead Jedis would be alright in helping Rey rather than any of the previous heroes like Luke (Mark Hamill) is such a cop out. She is more prone to use her anger and fear. Also, the idea that Sidious is able to use all the powers of all the Sith to knock out all the whole fleet through force lightning is over the top silly more than the Holdo maneuver, not only because every dark lord in the past has betrayed each other but as well their long history belief to limited their numbers to a very few. It makes no sense. Along with that, the whole 16 hours ancient Sith dagger wayfinder fetch quest really felt like wasted nonsense filler. The idea that the blade edge lines up perfectly with still surprising mostly intact wreckage of the Death Star was outrageous dumb luck seeing how the explosion burn it up nor the tough waters eroded the metal over time. The story pacing is kinda hard to believe like Rey fixing Luke's old ship in a few hours after years being underwater. It kinda like how they never explain how Maz Kanata voiced by Lupita Nyong'o got a hold with Luke's old lightsaber or what Finn (John Boyega) had to say to Rey. It's really bad editing. While the performers are great, their characters are wasted along with less annoying Rose (Kelly Marie Tran) and Poe Dameron (Oscar Isaac). Also, the death of Carrie Fisher in late 2016 caused major problems in production as well. The repurpose unused footage of Leia was kinda jarring. The visual/special effects from ILM were still impressive along with the sets & costume but some of the action scenes does cause dangerous photosensitive epilepsy. Not good. At least the film score by John Williams was still amazing. Overall: This movie is a mess from start to the cheesy name changing finish. I can't act like the previous two were perfect, but this seems especially maclunkey. I didn't like it. At least 'the Mandalorian' TV show is giving new hope for Star Wars because this movie certainly tries to kill it.

title: Let this be the end
review:
The final chapter in the Skywalker saga and the final piece of the new trilogy. The Rise Of Skywalker has a mammoth task on its hands, trying to wrap up everything built up in The Force Awakens and the plot points that were either ignored or pushed aside in The Last Jedi all of this whilst being its own film and a satisfying conclusion for our characters and what has been built up to since 1977.

The film sees the surviving Resistance face the threat of a still alive Palpatine (Ian McDiarmid) and Kylo Ren's (Adam Driver) First Order as Rey (Daisy Ridley), Finn (John Boyega) & Po (Oscar Isaac) use the power and knowledge they have learnt from the generations behind them as the final battle commences.

Lets start off with the positives. Visually this film is jaw-dropping, the cinematography features several memorable shots that really give a sense of scale and epic-ness, Palpatine's lair is a horror inflicted nightmare zone filled with distorting strobe lights and giant statues and huge corridors, the colour filled upbeat celebration on the desert planet Passanna, the dark and snowy zone of Kijimi, the desolate and broken crashed Death Star surrounded by a thunderous storm and crashing waves and a spectacle filled finale battle. The sound design of the film is also excellent, the effects of the vehicles, explosions, creatures and sabers are brilliant and the John Williams score is solid and the nostalgic themes do still land.

The action scenes are solid, as I mentioned the final battle is a visual spectacle with the 'War' part of Star Wars really showing itself here, it brings in many aspects to the battle to make it memorable, even including horse creatures riding across enemy aircrafts. The chase sequence on Passanna is a fast paced riot, the shootout on the Star Destroyer is a literal and figurative blast and Rey & Kylo Ren have two memorable light saber duels which are well choreographed and visceral.

The acting is good here. Daisy Ridley conveys Rey's anger and confusion at her situation very well and she delivers in the action sequences especially the finale where she really shows her action hero chops. Adam Driver helps Kylo Ren's arc become the most interesting of the film, sure he is still mostly mopey and stoic, yet he has some great line delivery and the sound design of his voice in the helmet is still cool. He also features in possibly the best dialogue scene in the film with (remember, spoiler review) Harrison Ford returning as Han Solo in Kylo's head and he's not phoning it in, delivering a genuinely emotional speech. John Boyega & Oscar Isaac give enthusiastic performances, C-3PO has some of his best comic relief moments, we have a fitting send off for Carrie Fisher/Leia and Ian McDiarmid is once again chewing all the scenery as a Frankenstein Monster influenced looking Palpatine. Mark Hamill (like Ford) also isn't phoning it in with his cameo return delivering motivation for Rey.

However what really is the film's weakest aspect is it's plot. It's instantly apparent that Palpatine was never the real end plan for the series. The reason he is here is barely explained, it's just a rushed statement within the opening title crawl which expects the audience to just agree and accept it and move on. He does nothing until the final section, his motivations aren't clear at all and just comes off as generic and lazy. The only reason he is there is because it turns out Rey is his Granddaughter. This feels completely out of the blue (because it is) there is no build up no reference to it in the previous films, its supposed to be shocking but it doesn't feel it at all because it doesn't fee earned. Which is the case with a lot of story moments here. Rey and Kylo kiss and have apparently been in love this whole trilogy, which I really haven't felt whatsoever considering their conflicts. On the opposite end of this what does feel like a genuinely impactful and risky moment is when we think Rey has accidentally killed Chewbacca, she's finally lost control of her power and murdered her friend and an icon of the franchise, there is stakes and a feeling of 'did that just happen?' but no, he's fine because apparently there was another ship which we didn't see (which there definitely wasn't), this is the same where Rey temporarily kills Kylo and vice-a-versa, there's just no stakes or consequences here at all for a finale.

The plot structure is repetitive, as it is essentially go to one place find an item to help go to the next place, all the while with Kylo Ren force projecting to Rey so he can find them (with his completely underused Knights of Ren) and they can then escape and the cycle repeats. It does feel very much like a video game plot at times. The scene transitions and pacing is jarring, the first act especially is extremely rushed and fast paced with no development or focus at all. It completely ignores events from the previous film and goes for more of a direct sequel to The Force Awakens which just doesn't work considering the amount The Last Jedi added to the story. We meet Lando quickly then he goes onto add nothing until the finale which is just for fan service, General Hux who has been a staple of this trilogy as Ren's second in command turns out to be a mole for the Resistance, because...? He doesn't care but he can't let Kylo Ren win for some reason which is never explained. He is then replaced by a new boring commander character who I honestly can't remember the name of, this goes the same with Po's friend Zorii Bliss, she seems interesting and has a cool design but we get no time with her whatsoever and lastly Finn tries the majority of the film to tell Rey something important (I'm assuming "I love you." ) which he immediately forgets about even when standing face to face with her after the battle.

I don't hate this film, in fact there's some scenes I really love and it is never boring at all. The technical aspects are phenomenal, the cast give good performances but there is no denying that it is the product of a disjointed not fully planned trilogy with unearned and seemingly rushed plot points and character motivations. The Rise Of Skywalker is fine but it should have been so much more.

title: Lame story, lack of appetite
review:
I am a big time Star Wars fan, and to make it clear, I love all the other 8 saga films, some more and some less.

This is the only saga film that I am not intending to watch again. It's unintriguing, dull, inconsistent, scattered and rushed. This is the only saga film that I would label as a bad movie.

The story goes nuts at a certain point, to a point of no return, completely killing any remaining hint of curiosity and tension regarding what will happen - because nothing makes sense anymore.

There is a point where everything becomes overly metaphysical, ghosts manipulate matter, everyone suddenly has new ultimate powers (here The Force is basically "god mode"), and good characters can't die.

The whole Emperor Palpatine thing was completely unnecessary, and a sad excuse for not coming up with a real backing story.

The newly discovered family trees hint at a script writer just trying too hard to impress, and show up as pathetic. They could as well make Han Solo the son of Donald Trump and Chewbacca the grandson of Ned Stark, wouldn't look that different.

The ending kiss scene (no spoilers here) - it screams "disney" so loud, is so out of place and idiotic, it's almost like they HAD to include that because their Disney movie formulas state you must include a kiss scene at the end. Instead of being excited, I wanted to vomit when seeing this, and felt embarrassed for seeing this movie.

Don't expect the battles to thrill you. They don't. As said above, once you realize that the good characters have "god mode" activated, and even killing them is not really killing them, then that's it, the movie loses its appetite. No edgy, thrilling action like in previous films. It's more like Teletubbies.

There is nothing during the movie that will shock you, or stir you up. Disney avoided that at all cost. They were afraid of "hurting" their fans. They were trying to take the "safest" storytelling route that will not anger anybody - which ironically, is exactly what kills this movie and makes it lame.

To the positive - great effects, nice humourous parts, inventive new worlds and aliens, good acting.

title: Best Star Wars film ever and one of the greatest films ever made period!

title: Spoilers - Ignore one star reviews
review:
I didn't want to read any reviews before seeing the movie in case there were spoilers, but now that I'm reading them a lot of the one star reviews are bigoted pointing to including "too much diversity" (black, white, Asian, hispanic, male, female, etc) in cast members as a bad thing. That was their complaint about Disney as a corporation ruining the franchise. Note: Lucas Film is a corporation. Also, diversity is always a part of futuristic sci fi. So disregard one star reviews.

I loved it! I felt a lot of emotions. I thought the fan service was good, not overbearing. I liked the way they wrapped up the struggle between the last of the jedi and sith. Amazing writing, amazing acting, amazing battles, but pretty good story. One review said it played like a 2 hour trailer for the last STAR WARS movie which I agree with. I loved the resolution between Ben and Rey.

*SPOILERS*

Leia had a lot of screen time, and it didn't feel like they changed her story. It was wonderful to see her legacy carry on 3 years after Carrie Fisher passed away. It felt real when her daughter, Billie Lourd, was by Leia's deathbed. I'm glad Han Solo came back like superman's dad and finally turned Ben back to the light side. I cried. I loved that him and Rey were overpowered with their force connection because that was the rumor I heard for the plot of the sequel trilogy in 1996. I didn't mind it being choppy because they packed so much into the final movie, and it was a rush the whole time. I'm SO GLAD Wedge Antilles came back in an X Wing with white hair. Lando was dope, but I wish he had more screen time. NOT ENOUGH R2D2. Every real fan knows R2D2 is the real hero of the first two trilogies.

My one problem was Palplatine. How did he come back to life? Why? Who saved him? Most importantly why tf did they invent his children in the last hour of the skywalker saga. I knew they were always going to go somewhere with Rey's parents, and that they were saving the reveal for the last movie, but that was a real bonehead move. It was like the ending of episode. 3 "It's over. I have the high ground" "You're (padme) with THEM" " From MY perspective, the jedi are evil" Wtf Disney?

title: Good but not great
review: It was very enjoyable. The production value was good as always. title: Swing and a Miss
review: Episode IX felt like a rushed chaotic patchwork of sorts. A course-correction made out of a desperate attempt to appease the critics and save the franchise. Unfortunately, I don't think it worked. The entire trilogy is a mess at this point, and it's been massively mishandled. There are (of course) many aesthetically pleasing things to enjoy about this movie, and the performances are fun and quite entertaining. And as always, the score is tremendous. But as a satisfying conclusion to the saga this falls very short. It never had a chance to truly reach it's potential after the crippling effect of TLJ and Rian Johnson's shenanigans. I don't envy the overwhelming task that JJ had on his hands. Star Wars is a machine like no other. But there was simply too much to resolve in a way that felt natural. It's a very commendable attempt, but TROS was always doomed with the disjointed and shambolic creative team behind this franchise. At best, it's a visually pleasing fun watch with a good score. And Palpatine rocks.

title: Flat ending to the Skywalker Saga
review:
I will start off first with saying, YES I do like The Last Jedi. I really enjoyed Rian Johnson's fresh take on the universe. The Force Awakens was an alright and fun movie. I forgave the plot point comparisons to A New Hope as it was a solid start to the series. TLJ was really fun and I liked where they took the characters. The casino part could have been trimmed up a bit and made it a better movie overall, but I truly enjoyed Johnson's mark he left on the series.

When Colin Trevorrow was announced as IX's director I was skeptical. His directorial debut, Safety Not Guaranteed, was really great. The giant pile of dino doo-doo named Jurassic World came out and soured my interest in anything he had to do. From interviews he seemed like his head was in the right place and he wanted to emulate Lucas' early years as a filmmaker. But he then left and JJ Abrams was his replacement. I figured it would be TFA again, safe, but still fun.

It sure as hell was a safe ending, but just not a great or fun one at all...

Bringing back the emperor is probably the biggest reason this movie fails. Why not have just Kylo be the villain??? Why did Palpatine have to be back and be revealed to be the catalyst for luring Kylo to the Dark Side? His inclusion just soured the whole movie.

Even without Palpatine, this movie is just all over the place. Rey and the gang are on a relic hunt for a map to lead them to the secret Sith planet and Palpatine. This is the whole plot of the first 3/4ths of the movie. They just go from planet to planet and really have nothing interesting happening. Sure, even the simplest plots like that can work. Raiders of the Lost Arc is like that, but the stuff happening, road blocks, and character interactions are what made it such a damn fun movie. This is just really uninteresting.

Also holy crap is there so much fan service and callbacks to the original trilogy out the wazoo! It annoyed me in Solo when it happened, but this is 100x worse than solo. Whether it's repeated lines from the original movies being said in a new situation, or really poorly place musical cues, this movie really wants to mooch off your nostalgia to make you happy.

TFA worked, despite being safe and trying to please your nostalgia zone, this just really wanted to please all the online crybabies who disliked TLJ.

None of the resolution is satisfying for the ending of a SAGA. Kylo's redemption is quick and really doesn't have any emotional depth. Rey being the granddaughter of Palatine is stupid. The Knights of Ren are no more than glorified stormtroopers and barely utilized. Finn has no character arc at all. Poe's past is hinted at, but no depth is shown. They did the best they could with the Leia stuff, but knowing what they did to recreate her in this, it was really obvious they had to create other character's dialogue around hers from TFA deleted scenes. Lando was brought back just because Williams is still alive, his addition makes no sense. Rose, who I really loved from TLJ, is thrown to the background and barely a tertiary character. JJ really gave in to all the gross people who hated Rose, disgusting move on their part to make her appear in maybe 30 seconds total.

This trilogy needed one core storyboard writer to keep the whole thing consistent. As much as I like TLJ and TFA, they too feel like three separate movies and not ones that fit together as a trilogy. Directors can change, just like the original trilogy, but the core writers needed to stay the same throughout the series. Sure, the director has some leeway to tweak parts of the scripts, but the roadmap needed to be established as it's clear they had no idea what they wanted to do from the beginning. Palpatine was never a thought on JJ's mind when doing TFA, but since he was recalled after tons of fans were butthurt about TLJ, he had to do the best he could and his easy fix was "Hey, Palpatine is still alive and the catalyst for everything happening!!"

This is just extremely disappointing. It as so many great small parts, but they're surrounded by such a middling movie. Babu Frikk is wasted in such a mess of a movie, C3PO's reprogramming was sort of fun, and that's all I can think of that I really found memorable or enjoyable.

I will still enjoy the first two new trilogy movies on their own, but it will be in the back of my mind that they didn't even come close to properly ending the saga. If anything, this makes me excited for any non-Skywalker movies as we don't have any preconceived notions on old characters and we can start anew in the universe. That's part of what makes the Mandalorian so great, though despite it's fan service and call backs too.

Fingers crossed Rian Johnson gets his own separate SW projects, but seeing as Disney wants to appease the "die hard" fans, I doubt those will happen. I'm fine with him making original wonders like Knives Out.

title: Saga of Balance and How it Ended
review:
If Episode I II III consist a nostalgic European story of love and lust, and Episode IV V VI presents a classic American tale of courage and redemption, then Episode VII VIII and IX is a saga of balance, the saga of this generation, a saga that this century deserves.

Many Criticize that Rian Johnson brought a lot of new elements in the Last Jedi and J.J. ignored them and tried desperately to "correct" them, ending up in a hot mess. I disagree. In my opinion, the message of this saga is loud and clear: it is a saga about balance. You can't have balance without diversity- J.J. opened up the story with much tranquility, Rian brought many elements in and thus intensified and broadened the diversity, then J.J. wrapped up the story with a clear and powerful note of balance. Perfect.

Did the Rise of Skywalker have the perfect storytelling? No- I agree that some things could be done more smoothly in this 2.5-hour ride. Was the Rise of Skywalker a satisfying ending of the saga? Yes. If you simply look at the protagonist Rey, who I vehemently adore, she is the very embodiment of balance. At the first scene that the character appeared in the galaxy, with that flowy figure of her with her staff and that translucent character music, I couldn't help but be reminded of another hero in the East, Son Goku. There you have it- the balance of western and eastern cultures and spirits in a single character, Rey. To put it in a shallow way, she is the combination of Western love and Eastern warriorhood.

This balance becomes so much more over time, especially in the Rise of Skywalker. Rey has a powerful bloodline but also a humble family. She has hatred but also an equal amount of love. She is a Sith but also a Jedi. She harms but heals. She is Rey but also Ben (who gave his life).She is a Papaltine but also a Skywalker. Anakin and Luke are fantastic and beloved characters but neither of them was balanced- Anakin had too much to hate and Luke was just a tad too courageous (hot-headed?). However, Rey is perfectly balanced and that's so powerful and impactful at the same time.

There are other elements beside Rey that shows the balance- the balance of society, the balance of race (a bit more), the balance of sexuality etc. these values, after all, are in some way, representative of what our generation and our century are about.

So they finally showed us what the force is- Rey Skywalker is the force. She is the balance. She is the imperfect satisfaction that we love.

title: Tragically, a Masterpiece
review:
Don't misunderstand the 10 I've given this film.

Often reviewers rate highly to compensate for low ratings, or vice versa. As much as I'd like to improve the image of this behemoth of a film, I rate it 10/10 because it is, for all intents and purposes, perfect.

I've followed Star Wars all my life. Despite the common consensus that Originals = Good and Prequels = Bad, I've always held every film in high regard. When The Force Awakens was released, I found that although it held tight to the formula of A New Hope and didn't meet every daydreaming fan's obsessive speculations and expectations, it was an entertaining and intriguing start to a trilogy that offered mystery and character.

This mystery and character was snuffed out in one fell swoop with The Last Jedi. I enjoyed it enough on release but hated it in retrospect, along with the global criticism bandwagon. It was a mess that can only be hoped against when wild ambition takes the reins. Despite this, it was a fun mess. A well made cinematographic achievement, a kind of beautiful disaster.

After this troubling start, I was worried about the final Star Wars film. I couldn't see how they would come back after two films that raised so many questions and left so many paths untrodden. What would come out of Disney's doors at the end of a beloved 40-year saga would likely be underwhelming at best. Defying that, though, my hopes were high, and I'd like to emphasise this:

My hopes could not have been high enough.

The Rise of Skywalker does not answer every question. It hasn't pleased a great amount of reviewers. These are minor offences. Let me tell you why.

Start to finish, it is awesomely tense and thrilling. The plot twists and turns, but it is never hard to follow, and never is there 'too much going on'. We are led through the film by series-defining arcs that are necessary and indeed essential. It is paced exquisitely, covering everything that needed to be covered without dragging any of it out or cutting it short. You are taken on a climactic journey that is surprisingly dark, insightful and truly groundbreaking.

Characters that were beginning to feel misrepresented and underdone are hugely developed and are all at their best. The cast are consistent and thorough with their performances, and at last, this new group of strangers feels like a family. The antagonists are more menacing and unsettling than ever, instilling the same sense of isolation and hopelessness that the Original trilogy pulled off so well. The greatest parts of each character, good or evil, are expanded and showcased for pure enjoyment and to strengthen the narrative.

The score is, of course, delivered to the experience expertly. John Williams brings us climbing crescendos, crashing climaxes and quiet lows, a reminder that the grand scale and distant setting of these films is representative of a story that is much closer to home; you and me, us and them, hatred and love, anger and peace, despair and hope. The dark and the light.

These themes are carried beautifully across a finale with a deep gravity that so far has, tragically, failed to move many of the series' fans. For this film to be executed so perfectly and still be attacked relentlessly and overwhelmingly is truly a tragedy. However, I hope the majority will be like me and stand up for the film that saved a trilogy, and even the saga. There's still hope that the fair and considered opinions will overpower the harsh and cynical responses that dominate the scene at the moment. After all, there's always hope. After all....

"Hope is like the sun. If you only believe in it when you can see it, you'll never make it through the night."

title: Could have been better, and here's how...
review:
This was a rare swing and a miss for JJ Abrams, though one cannot place all the blame on him. The main reason that this movie was such a mess was this: too many characters.
Not only did ALL of the main characters from the original three movies get brought back during episodes 7-9, you had the introduction of at least six new main characters, and over ten minor ones. JJ appears to have tried to give all of them screen time, with limited success. Another huge problem was that half of the new main characters were utterly forgettable. I'll be honest, if Poe and Finn had been killed off in the first movie, no one would have cared; or at the very least they should have been relegated to background roles. BB-8 was an absurd concept, and what the hell was Keri Russell's character and the scene with the horses even doing there?
Kylo and Rey were both done very well in all three films, and a few of the new characters like Rose Tico were done well, but there were so many characters in 7-9, and especially 9, that focus on the real story (the Kylo-Rey conflict) almost got lost.
The end result was a major mess, punctuated by short periods of great film making.
The final scene for Carrie Fisher was good, though a little forced, the final scene for Harrison Ford was well done, the final battle and conclusion of the Kylo-Rey conflict was poignant and fitting, and the last scene for Rey was emotional. Abrams should have expanded on those parts of the story and eliminated the entire Poe and Finn parts. In fact, you could expand that statement to all three of the last films.

I hope they won't waste that potential.

title: An unsatisfying end to this unsatisfying trilogy.
review:
Three movies in and we get this? Really Disney, come on...

You would think a trilogy of the greatest science fiction franchise of all time would have a plan, as it's a trilogy, well according to these movies, that's not the case, thank Kathleen Kennedy, she's the one who's shat all over your beloved Star Wars.

As JJ has returned to finish what he started, let's take a look back at the previous 2 movies in this trilogy.

First what kickstarted it all off, The force awakens, sure this movie is a complete New hope rip off, sure it's slightly uninspired but we got a fun movie, and most importantly, a fun star wars movie, introducing us to new characters, rebooting the franchise as well as clearing up some things from the originals and setting up a concept of where this new era of Star Wars could go.

Fast forward 2 years and the reigns of director is handed over to the infamously divisive Rian Johnson, letting him have his take on where he thinks the future of Star Wars should go, Rian seems to think it should go in the complete opposite direction to where JJ was planning on taking it, making the hype and questions raised from The force awakens completely irrelevant, and outright stupid, the last jedi had balls, and it's balls where far to big for it's boxers, it throws cheap twists and turns that are uninspired, it tries it's best to be smart but completely fails as a good star wars movie.

2 years later...

After a firing of director, countless reshoots and script leaks, the rise of Skywalker finally hit theaters, it was safe to say it couldn't be worse than the last jedi, and it, well it wasnt, it's actually quite fun.

Now I respect JJ Abrams for doing his absaloute best in the time given, as well as being dictated by Kathleen Kennedy, he's done a good job for what was thrown at him, all these reviews slandering JJ, that's out of order as the poor guy has tried hard here and it really shows. That might be where the film fails, JJ has tried too hard, too hard to please the massive fandom, dumping fan service here and there, but this is too where I enjoyed the movie, yes it is crammed in, with little space to dwell or think about moments that should have impact, the return of Palpatine was, alright, a bit stupid, but alright, and the questions raised in previous movies are still just kind of left, unanswered or just glanced over. It is clear to see beyond all of its convolution however, lies once again, a fun star wars movie with some of the most interesting things that we've ever seen from a star wars movie. It certainly isn't the best, but it's certainly not the worst, it's just a very cheap way to finish a messy trilogy, and in doing so, trying to fix the whole trilogy.

The rise of Skywalker deserves a fair 6.5/10. The sequel trilogy as a whole deserves a 6/10.

title: A worthy ending to the saga
review:
First of all I have to respect JJ Abrams for at least trying to conclude the whole sage using the mess of a universe Rian Johnson left him with after episode 8. For a star wars fan, the movie is great because one thing it does and does well is fan-service. But there are flaws in this movie. Some bigger, some less important, but all of them are worth talking about.

!SPOILERS AHEAD!







If you haven´t seen any trailer to this movie, you might be a bit shocked at the beginning. Because the title scroll tells you that Palpatine(Ian McDiarmid) is alive and that he has told the galaxy he´s seeking revenge, even though he fell down a reactor shaft and exploded during episode 6. The time span between the original trilogy is estimated to be around 30 years. Palpatine is revealed to have always pulled the strings from the back as he used to in hte original trilogy. He founded the first order, he created Snoke(Andy Serkis) in an attempt of cloning himself, he has been building a ginormous fleet of star destroyers, each of them with the power to destroy whole planets. It´s always been him. Exagol, Palpatine´s base of operations was one of my personal favorite locations in the entire movie. The grim music combined with the lightning and the horrorish atmosphere inside the emperror´s new home were just great! And how could you introduce Palpatine better than with his arguably most famous quote? :"the dark side of the force is a pathway to many abilities some consider to be unnatural." When the emperor lifts up his new fleet, the last order, a more threatening, epic version of imperial march(by John Williams) can be heard to make the viewer aware of the fact, that this is the biggest menace ever seen in the whole saga.

Might I also add that the imperial march, one of my most favourite theme in the whole universe of movies and by far my favourite star wars one was used excellent in this movie and I really enjoyed every time it appeared. One scene which is one good example of this is when Rey(Daisy Ridley) ascends the second death star, we see Palpatine´s old throne and a silent version of it can be heard in the background to remind the audience of the original trilogy and curent location of the story. Another great thing which caught my attention was the dynamic between Rey, Finn(John Boyega), Chewie(joonas Suotamo) and Poe(Oscar Isaac). Finally they go on a mission alltogether and we don´t have several side stories like in The Last Jedi.

In episode 7 the force connected Rey and Kylo Ren(Adam Driver) or at least we thougt so. Because in episode it was established, that supreme leader Snoke had connected them using the force, and not the force on its own. This concept known as Force-Skype is a strange one to me. In The Rise of Skywalker it seems to be a merging of two dimensions with effect on the reality that can only be seen by Kylo and Rey. Talking about the force, it seems to be as powerful, as the screenplay wants it to. There can be things done with the force, that have never been established before. The most discussed is of course the power of transmitting force power from being to another to easily overcome lethal injuries and even cheat death! With this now being cannon, nearly every death of a main character could have been prevented.

One thing which confused me a bit was the situation with the sith-wayfinders. It says there are only two in existence but if you count them throughout the movie, three can be seen. The first one in the beginning aqquired by Kylo Ren, the second one located on the second death star and the third one in the posession of Luke Skywalker(Mark Hamill).

After Kylo had found Exagol with his sith-wayfinder, it must have remained inside his ship which is the same one, Rey flew to Luke´s island with. And now I´m asking myself the question: Why the heck did she not use the wayfinder inside Kylos ship and instead burned the whole thing? Back to Luke Skywalker: In episode 8 it was established that Luke came to the island to die and suddenly in episode 9 it was his goal all along to find Exagol and confront Palpatine one last time. That´s a prime example for episode 9 telling excuses for the movie that came before it.

One thing which has now been used more than enough times before in the Franchise is the short death of main characters. A voice in one trailer can even be heard saying:"No one´s ever really gone." We had an emotional death of our beloved C3PO(Anthony Daniels) in this movie which was of course teased at in the last trailer. But once 3PO meets R2D2(Jimmy Vee) again, R2 revives him using a backup. When Kylo Ren pushed Rey to her limits on desert planet Pasaana, which was also a clear hint at her parantage, she seemed to just have killed Chewbacca in his transporter. But just a few minutes later, she feels his presence and everything´s fine again.

One character who died, but just one half of him was Adam Driver´s Ben Solo. After Rey just took his personal the "TIE Whisper" as it´s called and left him Han Solo(Harrison Ford) appeared in front of him. And after a short but heartwarning chat with his father he killed, he threw the weapon he commited the murder with in the ocean and concludes Kylo Ren´s story arch. "Let the past die, kill it if you have to, that´s the only way to become what you´re meant to be" like Kylo said himself in Episode 8.

At the end of the second act, I had great hopes for the final battle and I was not disappointed at all with what I received. I most enjoyed the scenes which Rey and Palpatine, or should I say Rey Palpatine and Sheev Palpatine shared. My most favourite however was the final battle between them. There was a particular moment which was just a few seconds short, but remained the best scene of episode 9 for me. After Palpatine sucked out Rey´s and Kylo´s force essence and transmitted it over to himself, he was fully restored and more powerful than ever, which of course he had to proof to the audience by presumably killing the last Skywalker and thowing him into a bottomless pit. Than Rey somehow stands up again and the final showdown begins. At the beginning we can hear Palpatine´s theme "the emperor arrives" to synergize who´s having the upper hand right now and after he says:"You are nothing! A scavenger girl is no match for the power in me. I am all the sith!" the positive part of Rey´s theme, that resembles hope starts playing and Rey answers with:"And I... I am all the Jedi" then she overpowers Palpatine by using two lightsabers and the power of all the Jedi past her and finishes the emperor off for good.

While I was watching this spectacular moment in cinema, it reminded me of something I saw only a few months ago: Avengers Endgame. If you watch Star wars Episode IX:The Rise of Skywalker the next time, think of Iron man and Thanos´s showdown during the final conversation of Palpatine and his grand-daughter. the energy and sheer power must´ve been too much for a human´s body. Because even Rey, arguably the most powerful Jedi or the Jedi with the highest potential didn´t survive the final showdown. Well she was dead for a few moments. Suddenly a hand can be seen gripping onto the edge of the hole Ben was thrown down. Then Kylo Ren´s theme plays and more than half dead Ben Solo is crawling his way to Rey to revive her with the last bit of force he´s got left in him. After this they share an emotional moment which also was one of the most discussed considering this movie:they kiss. I personally think that it was not a necessary but well executed conclusion of their story.

At the very end Rey returns to Tatooine to bury Luke and Leias lightsabers and call her self a Skywalker. That´s just ridicoulus. The whole movie was about her accepting she´s a Palpatine and at in final scene she suddenly is a Skywalker?

In conclusion I would say that Star Wars Episode IX is a good movie with great ambience, a lot of fan-service but also a few flaws which cannot be overlooked.

title: Return of the Form
review:
After the disappointment of the last Star Wars outing, here we see something of massive improvement. It's exciting from start to finish with some excellent action scenes, special effects and emotional moments. It crams a lot in but this movie can be watched again multiple times.
At the end of the day, what does a Star Wars movie have to do? Be fun, exciting, full of action with characters you care about. This has all that. The negative reviews are often adults in their late 40s / early 50s who watched Star Wars as a child and now want the same feeling. Truth is, you can't because you are watching it from an adult perspective, you are analysing every scene, and coming out with comments such as, that's impossible, daft, the physics is wrong, the force can't do that, that character wouldn't do that etc. You know what, when you were a child, you watched it, enjoyed it, then went to play with the action figures.
I'm in my mid 40s but watched it for what it was supposed to be, and I will in future watch it again.

title: Die hard fans, you will be disappointed.
review: J. J. Abrams takes George Lucas' concepts of the force and absoultely disrespects it. Somehow objects in this movie have the ability to teleport, using the force. Two characters can have a lightsaber duel while they are in different parts of the galaxy, using the force. The only believable thing about the force that J. J. Abrams introduces is the ability to heal others. As far as cinematography goes, the movie has goregeous visuals and backgrounds. The CGI in this movie was actually spot on and looked really good. What really killed this movie was the writing and plot. It is more than obvious that this movie is attempting to cover up the mistakes that the first two movies made. One thing that goes completely unexplained is how the emperor is alive, we get no backstory on how he survived at all. The sith wayfinders were completely pulled out of thin air and thrown into this movie, and they make absolutely no sense when it comes to how they work. The light saber fights in this movie were so bad and slow that they almost belong in the original trilogy. It is also revealed that Rey is related to Palpatine, which Disney pulled right out of in order to 'save' this movie. The movie just lacks a lot of character development, storytelling, and pacing. The entire movie feels so rushed from start to finish, it just does not have a good flow to it at all. Oh, and don't get me started on that kiss and subsequent death at the end. That had me and the rest of the audience wondering "what the hell was that?". All in all, if you are a die hard fan of the Star Wars franchise you will be disappointed and pretty upset by the conclusion of this film.

title: No franchise is ever really gone...
review:
The final chapter in the sequel trilogy of the Star Wars Saga has arrived. In this review for Star Wars Episode IX: The Rise of Skywalker. After witnessing a large decline in popularity since the divisive release of The Last Jedi. Is The Rise of Skywalker strong enough with the force to restore the last of this franchises reputation? Let us begin...

Plot After the cataclysmic events of The Last Jedi. The Resistance are on the run from the First Order, while also struggling with their own inner turmoil. Meanwhile, Kylo Ren and Rey discover that the Sith Emperor Darth Sidious has survived the destruction of the second Death Star who plans to exact his revenge upon the entire Galaxy. With time desperately running out for the forces of Good, only Rey and Kylo Ren are the galaxy's best hope for survival. All leading to the final showdown between the Jedi and the Sith.

Likes The Rise of Skywalker is a seismic, space faring sci-fi epic carrying plenty of suspenseful action, blissful effects and much needed character development. J.J Abrams returns since The Force Awakens from a leave of absence. I am personally glad he's back in the chair after Rian Johnson kind of disappointed us with The Last Jedi not delivering on its promises of story and revelations. But for Abrams he brings back some of the enjoyment of what made Star Wars such an amazing Sci-fi epic in terms of action and practical effects. And even does offer more insight to the plot points he established in The Force Awakens (Only by a small margin. More in the dislike section). Also by finally giving us an answer to Reys parentage and one I'm actually very surprised by. More below. The sets and practical and visual effects are immensely crafted and continue to be a highlight for this sequel trilogy. From the new aliens, to the set design, to the locations, to the ships. I just can't get enough of it! For the characters, let's start with Daisy Riddley as Rey. The infamous Mary-sue of this series who miraculously is good at every bloody thing without trying. But in this film, she does show she is capable of displaying flaws just like every other character in the series prior and actually feels like a better written character than how she was previously. And actually displays how she can in fact be tempted by the dark side of the force just like every other Jedi. SPOILER WARNING! Mainly because it's revealed she is the daughter of Darth Sidious/ Emperor Palpatine. Which was unexpected cause' I thought she would be a Skywalker or a Solo, Or even a Kenobi or a Jinn. But she did take on the name of Skywalker in the end so that's something at least. John Boyega returns as Finn and of course is also getting better writing in the film unlike how the The Last Jedi reduced him to a side-character who acts like an idiot and a coward. But unlike last time, he is actually more involved in the movie and gets some much needed development. Oscar Isaac as Poe Dameron is once again portrayed better than the "Other movie". Where instead of being a Rebellious Dick who doesn't follow orders. He goes back into being the likable, hot shot Rebel Pilot people know and love him for. And he is definitely more likable again to me than he was before. Also, LANDOS BACK! Finally! So many years of absence and he finally comes back to kick some Empire tail again! Billy Dee Williams continues to bring in the charismatic, lovable charm of the Bespin Card Player we remembered. The Classics of Leia, C3PO, R2D2 and Chewbacca come back into this movie and also get to have some more part in the story than how they were severely reduced to minor roles. My biggest highlight of the movie would be near the end where all the Jedi from all over the franchise return as voices helping to encourage Rey to keep fighting The Emperor. I ultimately geeked out because you got to hear classic characters like Luke, Yoda, Obi-Wan. And then to Qui-Gon Jinn, Mace Windu and even to Clone Wars character Ashoka Tano! Much appreciate the fan service there Abrams!

Dislikes Once again we must go through the dislikes of this sequel trilogy. And to be honest, you probably will already know them before you start reading. I don't really know whether this film has even bigger dislikes or the same amount as before. But I'm just gonna put down what I dislike about the movie. It's pretty much a soft-remake of Return of The Jedi. Rehashing another planet killing plot, confronting evil fathers, getting captured on a desert planet. That stuff you've already seen before. And to be fully honest. It's even less original than The Last Jedi which I can tell was trying to be different. Now it is less long than The Last Jedi. But it is still very long in terms of everything else bad I will be putting down. And by the time you get to the end of this you'll more likely feel relieved that this movie is over more than anything else you've seen. One thing I remember liking about The Last Jedi and The Force Awakens was the ever-evolving action sequences. But in this movie though... it doesn't seem to have improved much since last entry. In a way the action seems to face a large scale of problems and seems less innovative. Like it's as if Michael Bay was hired to direct the action sequences while J.J was on break time. But still, they seem less exciting. And Star Wars, even the prequels had enough original action you could sink your teeth into. Also there is a lot of incomprehensible logic as to how certain new abilities in the force occur. Like with how Rey and Kylo can still talk to each other without Snoke bridging them. How does that work? Yeah, still not buying it guys. And on that note. They still don't present the basis of the overall plot of the sequels. And not forgetting they still don't reveal much answers to revelations set up in previous entries. All the while adding more and more Questions in this film that still don't answer a damn thing: What the Hell happened to the Jedi? How did the Empire become the First Order and gain so much power again? What is this Awakening BS that Snoke was on about? How did the Emperor survive being blown up by the Death Star in ROTJ? How is Han Solo a force ghost even though he isn't a Jedi? What actually happened to Reys parents? What was Finn going to tell Rey before being sucked into quick sand? How does Rey and Kylo use the force to teleport and communicate between each other? How is a dagger able to help Rey navigate the ruins of the Death Star? How did Chewie escape death in a shuttle after Rey used force lightning? Where are those kids from that Casino Planet? Where's the Mandalorian and Baby Yoda? (Just kidding!) Ok, I know this is Star Wars tradition to expand the series to other forms of media. But you can't all expect everyone to watch and read everything else in the Expanded Universe to get all the answers when you could just straight up give them to us. Lucas did that before you in the past six films without expanding it all into other material and he made more sense of things. Lastly. They cut Rose Tico (Kelly Marie Tran) out of most of the movie. Why I'm mad about this you ask is that it appears that Lucasfilm and Disney were reading too many hateful posts labelled against the actress that they decided to go in favour of the Far-Right and straight up reduce her role. I don't like her character that much as with most of the other newbies to the sequels, but she did give her character a lukewarm performance worthy enough of acceptance. But in a world ruled by The Apprentice, suddenly an Asian character like her is attacked just for being cast in a Star Wars movie. And it feels shameful to see this as nothing but a petty excuse to incite propaganda. And if this is how Hollywood and Disney is going to combat prejudice. Then I want no part of this series anymore.

Verdict? The Star Wars franchise has come a long way since its Disney Ownership and to be honest. It has been painfully exhausting the way through. The Rise of Skywalker can prove it can still pack a punch with interstellar action and deliver the thrills and references fans love about the series. But it cannot reach its full potential with its lacking plot, unoriginal action sequences, confusing twists. Overreliance of nostalgia, pacing and repeating most of the same problems that Disney Star Wars films are infamous for these days. Some fans will find satisfactory, but not enough to appeal to all fans of the genre. I give Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker a score of 6/10.

title: "The Force Awakens" fans get their sequel, and If you liked Rian Johnson's "The Last Jedi," this film is not for you.
review:
Did J.J. Abrams mend the broken pieces from "The Last Jedi"? Well, he did have Kylo Ren reforge the mask he shattered in the previous movie. That was one of the many indicators of Abrams trying to rewrite the events from the "The Last Jedi."

Abrams "The Rise of Skywalker," erased the direction the previous film was going and went back to the nostalgia-driven style he used for "The Force Awakens." The film delivers when doing action scenes, and the performances from Rey (Daisy Ridley) and Kylo Ren (Adam Driver) were great. Daisy Ridley did the best in this film out of the trilogy for me, whereas I found her flat in "The Last Jedi." I imagine Abrams to be the reason behind the better acting in this film than the last. As a director, J.J. Abrams works well with young casts like these--- 2011's "Super 8" comes to mind.

There's undoubtedly a clunkiness to this film. A lot of world jumping and going from place to place, not sticking too much story in one location. "The Rise of Skywalker" brings us back to old locations and sets from the original trilogy. I could see many fans liking this to see familiar places and hear that familiar John Williams score.

For Composer John Williams, this marks his last 'Star Wars' film, where he will compose the score. As the final notes in "The Rise of Skywalker" played, I couldn't help but notice the music has been easily the best thing in the trilogy. As it was for the prequels, John Williams' work has always been top-notch.

Visually, I enjoyed the look of the film. The watery lightsaber battle fought on the remains of the death star in the ocean looked great. The large scale landscapes reminded me of what George Lucas would do in the prequel films. I never enjoyed the 'Star Wars' prequel films storytelling, but visually and technically, they did deliver. I never got the big-budget blockbuster feeling from "The Last Jedi," but I did from "The Rise of Skywalker."

If you're a die-hard 'Star War' fan, well of course, "The Rise of Skywalker" is a must-watch. But, if you like, "The Last Jedi" this film is may not be for you. Many of that film's characters and themes were all but completely removed or only subtly used in "The Rise of Skywalker." As for general moviegoers, I can't see them enjoying this film. It's the third of a series, and obviously, those usually require prerequisite films to understand everything that's happening.
