title: Clear attempt to fix TLJ issues
review:
When you look back on this trilogy, it is clear Disney made a clear error in not having JJ Abrams direct the whole trilogy. It is clear JJ is a true fan of Star Wars as both TFA and TRoS largely have the tone, look, and character approach of the original trilogy. It is also clear that he recognised TLJ was a misstep veering too far from the approach, mythology and tone of the original trilogy such that he scrambled to fix so many of those problems Rian Johnson crested. Hey, of course Rey is somebody - let's use Palpatine (even though there is nothing pointing to his return in the first two movies). Where were the Knights of Rdn in TLJ? Oh, here they are - they've been there all along of course! Rey didn't receive enough Jedi training to be so powerful in TLJ - hey, we'll add the training retrospectively in this movie ! Finn romance in the TLJ - of course that was unbelievable! So let's go back to him sort of liking Rey and hey here's another option with the other ex-stormtrooper! Luke the weak sourpuss in TLJ - of course he was wrong to be portrayed this way so we'll remake him to be the selfless, heroic and optimistic character he was in the whole original trilogy! No back story at all on Snope? No problem - it was Palpatine who created Snope (literally grew or bred/cloned him or many of him it looked like I believe?!)

If JJ had done all three he would have written a true trilogy story arc and not have to try and fix the huge diversions and holes TLJ made.

Put these crammed fixes aside, I actually enjoyed the movie. I'm a huge Star Wars fan, but let's be clear - none of the original movies were perfect. Some of the writing and acting was patchy and wooden. What elevated Star Wars (like the Matrix) was the original mythology, effects and originality of the universe it introduced us to. Plus interesting characters we grew to really care combined with exciting, ground breaking action. This movie harked back to that approach - heavy on the reverence to the Force/Sith mythology, honouring the skywalker family legacy, more fleshed out and fun characters (Po back story, good chemistry/humour between Po and Finn, etc), lots of general fandom. And there's nothing wrong with that - just that it wasn't consistent across the trilogy (TLJ again).

I know a lot of fans hate what Disney have done to the franchise with this trilogy, but actually if they had just taken the approach they did with the Marvel final Avenger movies they would have nailed it. There, they created great solo movies (introducing lots of new characters and sub stories) that still linked to the overall story arc culminating in a clear set of climatic movies. Those franchise phase ending movies rewarded all the hardcore fans by paying heaps of homage to the past movies and the origins of the characters while still being generally hugely entertaining for the casual fans. JJ could have done the same here by linking and paying homage to the original trilogy more naturally SPREAD over all three movies (excluding the additional Death Star!) for the long term fans but then creating additional new characters and stories to move the franchise to "phase 2" beyond episodes VII-IX.

So it's clearly a case of what could have been with one man controlling the vision and approach of the entire trilogy from start to finish (just like George Lucas did originally).

title: Emotional Rollercoaster - True Star Wars though a bit too fast-paced
review:
The movie manages to turn the crap that Star Wars 8 was into gold. *SW 8 was crap for a Star war's movie and did not convey any feeling associated with Star Wars.

The Rise of Skyealker is all around very enjoyable and includes a lot of story that makes sense. The movie is an emotional rollercoaster which is great and keeps you staring at the screen craving for MORE!

The downsides are: The movie feels a bit too fast paced (ESP. at the beginning) which stops the characters from showing emotions to the loss of loved ones and the likes which is a pity. A slower pace would have made this movie a masterpiece!

Overall despite what critics say the movie is very enjoyable, thrilling and very very Star-Wars-y in every good way and it feels like a dignified end to the Skywalker Saga. It answers a lot if not all questions left and is (imo) what the movie franchise needed.

Watch it, you won't regret it!

title: Film of the century
review: Simply fantastic. What a way to end the Saga. This film has everything you could want and does indeed tie together all of the Skywalker films as promised. I am a fan of 40 years and fully appreciate what a challenge such a new trilogy is. JJ pulled it off in a mega way. You could ask for nothing more (apart from a few more force ghosts). Simply stunning filmmaking and storytelling with treasures for die hard fans Luke myself. Seen twice in first 24 hours and will see many more times.

title: Disappointingly average
review:
You can tell J.J. Abrams had a specific direction for this trilogy and Rian went off the rails in regards to that direction. The third film tries to undo the doing of Rian Johnson's film which in a way makes the overall trilogy feel disjointed. I believe a fan-edit can help correct this mess in the future, combining scenes from VIII and IX to make a coherent story. Having Palpatine at the very beginning didn't feel organic, it felt as if he was supposed to be introduced in VIII and was not, so as a result, tacked on with a rushed first half. I hope that this specific film ends up having a couple hours of additional footage that can convert this disasterpiece into a miniseries that attempts to balance the storytelling - wishful thinking, however. Next time, keep the same filmmaker for the entire trilogy - it may had worked for the original trilogy but clearly does not work in today's reality where mostly everyone is completely divided in perspective.

title: Screw it, we are doing return of the jedi again.
review:
First of all, this movie was way better than The Last Jedi, but it had a lot of problems. Mainly the 5 hours worth of plot cramped into a 2 hour movie. If this movie would have been properly build up by The Last Jedi then it could have been really good.

title: Way too much action
review:
It was too packed with action. There was no breathing room and no time to enjoy the amazing scenery. There is nothing wrong with the action scene's in themselves but it's important to have balance. So there were too many unnecessary scenes that made no difference for the story. It would have been better to slow down the story and instead focus on character building and relationships. Make the viewer feel more connected to the characters.

I usually get more emotionally affected by movies, but this one didn't make me feel much except some wow moments and some amusement. This movie really had the potential to be a masterpiece, too bad.

There's were also too many references to the old movies that it kinda took the fun out of it.

title: Everything was good except the plot and dialogue
review:
Acting, direction, set design etc. etc. were all good. The movie had a disappointing plot but at least it had one as opposed to TLJ being waffle for 2 hours and a half.

Pretty disappointing that interesting ideas such as Finn's background are never used.

My main issue is that this movie contradicts the previous ones including episodes 7 and 8. A non-spoiler example would be that the movie starts off with everyone aware of Palpatine even mentioning it in the opening crawl when in TFA (written and directed by the same person) the Jedi, Sith and the Force was all considered a "myth".

This new trilogy should have focused on rebuilding the Republic with Leia as well as rebuilding the Jedi Order with Luke. The prequel trilogy with all its flaws at least served a purpose of showing a republic falling from within, this trilogy serves the same purpose of defeating and rebelling against the Empire that the original trilogy had except done worse with less interesting characters.

title: Empty
review: I think there were 4 or 5 scenes which were noteworthy... outnumbered by many cringeworthy scenes. Often, one gimmick followed another. And when the movie occasionally seemed to be finding its legs, in comes an embarrassingly overacted Finn or Poe, killing the legitimacy of what should have been an instant classic. Dialogue was reminiscent of what Lucas would give us. Battle scenes were boring. Seriously, if the movie could be trimmed down to just the scenes with Kylo and Rey (except that extremely awkward bit towards the end), it would have been much better. Fortunately, The Mandalorian will help wash the taste of disappointment from my mouth.

title: Keeps the foot on the pedal until they run out of hyperroad?
review:
The last installation of this new trilogy starts out feeling very messy. The movie picks up the pace straight away and for the first half of its duration it doesn't lift its foot from the pedal. The effect is that whereas good story telling would require buildup, suspense and surprises being satisfied with explanations, the movie opts for simply squeezing the plot into a time frame it can't possibly fit. Much of what happens we never see the characters truly react to, because there simply is no time for them to do so before jumping on to the next major event. For the same reason many of the characters are pushed entirely to the sidelines to make room for new (or old) ones, and the point of having them there in the first place is not obvious.

Half way into the movie the tempo changes somewhat. The main focus of the story becomes clearer and we get a return to the connection and inner conflict between Kylo Ren and Rey as their story unfolds. The story has us visit places that act as beutiful and eerie backgrounds to it playing out, and so the second part of the movie is rather more enjoyable than the first.

The lasting impression however is that nothing has been said or shown that was not apparent in the first trilogy. The liberal message about choosing who you will become is the exact same as in the first trilogy. So while the movie is somewhat enjoyable and entertaining it does not attempt to really send a new message or tell the audience member something really new, which makes it rather forgetable.

title: The Perfect Ending to the Trilogy
review: To be honest, this movie was kind of a hot mess, but it was the good kind of hot mess if you know what I mean. title: Where we at!

After all, he's got something to *impart* to us: It's about Nazi Germany, and how the Götterdämmerung needs to get turned on its head. How is a 1 or 2 possible as well? You are saying that at no point in 2hrs you enjoyed a moment of the film? How did you finish it if you hated it that bad? Nothing was redeeming? Ok. I though that having the origin of Rey being the opposite of what i would have suspected was a neat twist, then making her to be stronger than any Jedi i have ever seen was pretty rad.

There was quite a few moments in the film that i wish would have been cut down in length for one reason or another (boring, long winded, doesnt add to story, cheesy, etc) but that wasnt a whole lot of moments. It did bring back some characters from prior movies which was a near nod to those films, like the originals but it also felt like they were going for cheap nostalgia tricks at the same time.

The special effects throughout the film were pretty good but felt more video game-ish than movie, i dont know if thats bad or good. There was also some pretty horrific dialogue uttered once in a while. While much of this i didnt really notice at first; i was able to once i backed up the film or discussed with others later.

Overall, id say this film was a 7 or 8. Im not going to make comparisons of it to the originals because thats unfair to compare it to something so much pop culture, nostalgia, memories, etc are tied to, but i understand why its difficult for so many to distance the 2 because they are connected by a story line. It was a pretty good film, far from perfect but quite entertaining and I've really enjoyed watching what Rey and Finn have had to deal with in them.

title: The Star Wars Franchise Has Risen...
review:
Continuing on from Star Wars: The Last Jedi (2017), Rey continues her training in becoming a Jedi while living amongt the Resistance with friends Finn, Poe & General Leia. It is obvious that Rey is still coming to terms with not knowing everything about her past including who her mystery parents were. Soon the Resistance is shocked to discover an old enemy on the Dark Side of the Force is still alive- Emperor Palpatine. The most powerful enemy in this galaxy is still somehow alive... The team is sent to find a way to deal with the Emperor, accomplishing multiple objectives along the way and forcing Rey to deal with her own personal conflicts. Rey is also still in contact from time to time with Kylo Ren who continues to give her an invitation to join him. Kylo Ren also hints to Rey that only he knows the complete truth about her parents and her destiny.

Going into this film I was very opened minded. I personally felt for director J.J Abrams as he was tasked with following on from a movie full of really complex plot points. Not only that, actress Carrie Fisher had sadly passed away prior to the making of this film and her role was a critical element to making this film successful.

The opening of this film felt exciting but suddenly I thought to myself that I was watching multiple plots points. Main characters were tasked with one thing only to be tasked with another. Sometimes these tasks were interrupted only to load the characters up with more tasks and more plot points. Not only do some of the elements feel rushed, but some of these plot points weren't required by the core plot or main objective. It's not awful and it's still entertaining as a Star Wars film, it just felt... forgettable. On rethinking about the 1st half of this film again, if I had to explain each and every element to a friend I probably couldn't do it without a second watch.

Once the 1st act of the film passes the film gives a different vibe and feels more like a Star Wars film that fans would be familiar with. Satisfyingly, mysteries that Star Wars fans have been wondering about for years were finally answered. I was personally satisfied with all the plot twists in this instalment but I can also understand why some would be disappointed. In the end, I'm thankful the director has done the challenging task of answering the questions the previous films had lined up.

Key performances were generally what I would expect given the previous two instalments, but must say I'm once again impressed with Adam Driver (Kylo Ryn) as an actor. The director also has a better way of directing humour which I felt the last film really failed to do (just my opinion).

From an audio and visual stand point Star Wars: Rise Of The Skywalker looks and sounds rather incredible. Some CGI effects didn't always convince me but for most part it's enjoyable and it has my praise.

Overall, I found myself really enjoying this film despite the 1st half which does have forgettable moments and plot points. Despite my enjoyment, the first act really hurts my score and the entire film. The questions fans have been asking are finally answered, but granted, not everyone will be pleased with the answers. For me I found the film better than what I expected but I can't help think that some opportunities were missed, particularly during the setup/opening. Regardless, I feel Star Wars fans will find lots to enjoy as they go down memory lane with the greatest sci-fi franchise that ever lived.

7.3/10 Walkden Entertainment

So go see it for the graphics and to close out this faded saga so you can finally put a nail in the coffin and no longer have to hear any more about this long, long-ago, far, far-away...cash generator.

title: Rise of Skywalker: Review and Preferred Ending The Long Anticipated Conclusion
review:
The Rise of Skywalker. Episode IX. The Finale. The end of an era. The final film in the long anticipated series of Star Wars did perhaps bring the story full circle and to a close (which appears to be most temporary). But it did so in near the exact same fashion as the past.

And yes, it is good to end the story with a loop, and there were many great references to the originals that one is very much a fan of and which fit very well in their parts, but I feel they were not all they could be. You, of course, had classic lines, glimpses of familiar faces, reminders of past events, and I think, the best part of all, when Luke finally raises the old X-Wing out of the water just as Yoda did to Luke's disbelief before. All of this had me eagerly awaiting more. When Rey finally comes to the throne room of the old Death Star, why was she not bombarded with visions from the past? Why did we not see more attempts to connect to the force and be guided by past Jedi? How come we received no back story for all these sudden new fangled abilities? All of a sudden we can create wormholes to pass things, we can duel each other from different locations, and we can heal?!

I know there will be many people out there who will disagree with my opinion and many of the comments and ideas I state later in this text. Some will say I am a "fool" or "you know nothing about Star Wars." But I know, like many others deep down in the back of their minds', I was dreaming for a little more.

But the whole situation was a complete mirror of before. A team battling it out to save the galaxy from total annihilation, a Sith from the dark side (Darth Vader/Kylo Ren) in conflict with a Jedi from the light (Luke/Rey) while the exact same emperor is trying to influence the Jedi. Sound familiar? It goes on, you know the rest. Jedi turns Sith back to light, Emperor taken out, good guys succeed in blowing up bad guys, villain turned good dies in arms of hero, celebration throughout the galaxy!

I said it's good to have the story come full circle, but this is a complete clone. And this has been the case from the very beginning with this whole final trilogy. Same thing again and again. Evil people, people who rebel, giant weapon of mass destruction, crazy scheme to blow up weapon, over and over. Though everyone does seem to despise episodes I through III, you at least have to admit they had originality.

The thing that people always seem to say to me when it comes to Star Wars is: What is the lesson, where is the underlying message? Yes, it began with, say a revolution in film, a worldwide phenomenon that created the universe of Star Wars from a simple rounded trilogy of films. But then came the expectation for more. An expectation that has grown and been built upon for decades. Now it is here. But what did we take away from it? Where is the resolution?

This is my view. If you read further you can see my adaptation for the conclusion of the story of Star Wars. I do hope that George Lucas sees this so that he can tell me truly what I got wrong, and we can discuss his original intentions over coffee and how the final product turned out.

review: Rey (Daisy Ridley) is training on the secretive resistance safe haven planet with General Leia (Carrie Fisher) while Poe and Finn barely succeed in an operative. Meanwhile, Kylo Ren (Adam Driver) has felt a disturbance in the force and goes looking for a Sith finder to gain access to the hidden Dark Side planet. It is there that Kylo learns that the Emperor Palpatine has raised himself from the dead using the Dark Side and has been running the first order from afar since its inception. They discuss Rey and Kylo promises to turn her at last to the Sith side and present her to the Emperor. As such, Rey also senses the same disturbance and comes to the conclusion that she, too, must get her hands on a Sith finder (there are only two in existence) and find out what's what. As the gang of Rey, Chewy, Poe, and Finn go to strange new worlds, the First Order has a traitor in its midst, giving them important clues. Also, Threepio, along for the ride, has valuable info in his being but, because of his programming to never reveal Sith information, the only solution is to find someone to exrtract the hidden data illegally. There is also, very importantly, new information about Rey's parents and grandparents. When Kylo and Rey finally meet, what side will be victorious? This superlative film has it all; great cast, grand story line, sensational settings, amazing art direction, fantastic special effects and a solid direction. Special mention in the cast should go to the return of Billy Dee Williams as Lando and newcomer but polished actor Richard E. Grant as the new general of the First Order. Also amazing are the glorious new creatures and alien beings which are delightful. Yes, there is a definite ending to the tale but is it really the last installment? What about the little guy with the broom at the end of The Last Jedi? We shall have to see if this truly is the last hurrah or not. In the interim, go, go, go, go multiple times to Rise.

title: It's been emotional SPOILERS
review: Cards on the table: I think the sequel trilogy sucks donkey's. TFA is a lazy boring retread of ANH. TLJ is a very strange film riddled with: plot-holes, baffling character motivations, lore-breaking, terrible 'jokes'; and it holds a giant middle-finger up to a bulk of the fans. There was almost no way the final installment could be any good and so it proved. TROS is a poorly paced cluster that makes little to no sense. The pace of the film is so dizzying that I challenge anyone who has only seen the film once to recount the plot. About half the film is a tedious coupon chase that a video-game story-teller would be ashamed of. The other half seems to be obsessed with retcon-ing TLJ and the story told by episodes 1-6. There were at least 4 fake-out deaths - the laziness is strong in this one. I've given the film 5/10 because there were a few things I liked (e.g. it's very pretty). I'm gonna need to watch it again at least once (preferably on 3/4 speed) to decide how hate-able it is.

title: Very Good
review:
The reviews of this movie are per typical of Star Wars fan entitlement. The movie didn't go the direction you wanted it to so you're irritated and you rate it a 1-star. Really? This is among the worst movies you've ever seen? Extremely unlikely. Calm down. I've seen this movie twice now and it was definitely better the second time where you have more of a chance to take things in. I thought this movie was fun, interesting, full of twists, and great acting. I don't think J.J. Abrams ran course correction of The Last Jedi as many people are assuming. You really think Disney writes and plans the story arc one movie at a time? Come on now.

Anyways, I loved this movie and thought it was a great ending to a great trilogy.

title: Concluding the Skywalker Saga at Lightspeed
review: Director J.J. Abrams attempts to use The Rise of Skywalker as both a conclusion to the Skywalker Saga and as an apology for The Last Jedi. In doing so, Abrams forces the film to rush through much of its runtime and story, simply due to the bloat. If you are on board for the story and in-universe changes then the last third of the film still has something to offer. A few spectacular moments and nostalgia hits make the climax an enjoyable sendoff for the saga, but the pacing and patchwork nature of much of the film leaves a bad taste in the mouth.

title: Star wars .
review: This movie had it all , I can understand that it may piss some people off , but hot damn if it wasn't a hell of a ride . Far better than I hoped after TLJ . Make your own damn mind up and watch it , critics have been so off the last few years . It's like filmmakers have to check some artistic and social checklist for them to give it a thumbs up.

title: A recreation of the 6th One
review: This entire movie was pretty much the sixth one recreated. Poe was Han, Rey was Luke with Leia's personality, Chewbacca was Chewbacca, C3PO was himself as always, and same with Lando. Finn was pretty much the only new character. The 6th one however, is one of my favorite movies, and I think they ended the saga on a pretty good note. There were good characters and many Easter eggs. Also, the acting wasn't that bad for once. I found myself actually enjoying a movie. I'm only taking off one star because one of the scenes that happened at the end. (But no spoilers)

title: From a casual Star Wars fan...
review:
So rather than meticulously go through each film and how it got to this, I will say, I did enjoy this film. But in terms of story telling, it's lacking.

I was one of those that really liked The Last Jedi. What Rian Johnson did was different and I actually think it made for a really great watch. What frustrated me about Rise of Skywalker was that it was clear an hour in, it was trying to undo most of what had happened in TLJ. Scenes were cluttered together and would quickly move from one place to the next. The story itself didn't feel thought out, it felt like the quickest way to get the job done.

The story of Rey's past felt rushed. Admittedly, TLJ didn't delve too deep, but the reveal of who her parents were was a 'Oh, Ok' moment. And then, you'd move on.

Action wise, you get your fill of it. It looks beautiful. The actors in this film play their parts brilliantly.

If you're a die hard Star Wars fan, I think you'll be left disappointed. There are too many quick wins in this film for it to feel like someone has really taken their time with it. I enjoyed it, but I would have expected more for the end of such a saga.

title: Just so so
review:
To be honest. I feel a little disappointed when I come out of the cinema...
It's a good movie for free people who want to find a movie to watch. But it's not a perfect movie for a Star Wars fans...

title: Please Understand The Situation This Movie Was In Before Reviewing It!
review: If you don't live under a rock then you are aware and see all of the recent backlash and negative reviews for this movie. What baffles me is where was all this negativity when TLJ came out? In my opinion RoS is the best of the sequels. Sure there are plot holes and stories left unanswered but mainly only because of the mess TLJ has created. If JJ had the time to sit down with Lucas and actually fully plan these three movies out and was given more time I truly believe these could have surpassed the prequels. You have to understand Disney really messed with Lucasfilms and Star Wars in general. These films were rushed and handled poorly. BUT BUT BUT! JJ fully recovered from the disaster we seen in 2017 from the dark lord Rian Johnson. Writing was improved, I hated Poe and Finn in the last two movies and this movie I believe redeemed those characters. While Rey and Kylo Absolutely stole the show. Every seen with Kylo was so memorable and will be imprinted into your heads for ever. JJ made the best of a bad situation and that is sadly what we have to accept with this movie. I'm not gonna go into the movie so much because of all the spoilers. Who knows, the prequels got here doin reviews when they came out and now they are being praised by all. Give it some time. Let Star Wars rest a bit, the way this was left off I really believe We can have a new trilogy in the Future. We need Fioloni from clone wars and Deborah Chow from mandalorian to take over fully for lucasfilms. We have the Obi-Wan show to look forward to and the finale for mandalorian. Don't blame JJ for this, go in open minded like I did and truly Understand the situation this movie was in before reviewing it. May the Force be with you always

title: Not a good movie but enjoyable nonetheless
review: The story is a rushed, point A to point B nothing in between with some plot hole-causing fanservice thrown in and a villain that literally just shows up out of nowhere. Some of the writing is cringeworthy. It's almost entirely focused on Rey, Poe and Kylo with everything else falling extremely flat. On the good side, it's got all the usual Star Wars awesomeness like epic space battles, plenty of saber fights etc plus some good character development for the 3 it does spend all its time on, but that and the um...very distracting Daisy Ridley don't make it a good movie. Regardless, I'd still watch it if you're a Star Wars fan. The ending especially has some pretty impressive visual sequences. Despite the issues I still managed to enjoy it.

title: Really good for what they had to work with
review:
What I was most afraid of going into RoS:

1. That JJ would feel compelled to stay true to Rian Johnson's terrible vision.

2. That Rey would still have no backstory and her insane force powers would not be explained.

3. That the Emperor's return would be laughable and make no sense.

4. That Luke (my favorite character) would still have no respect for the Force and be completely lame.

5. That Leia's force abilities would not be explained and her character would be wasted like it was in TLJ.

6. That Finn and Poe would be totally wasted again.

7. That we'd be given more new characters who aren't well developed and who make infuriating decisions (Rose and Holdo).

8. That JJ would continue to ignore the rules of the Force the way Johnson did (I cannot and will not get over Force Ghost Yoda's lightning abilities or Luke's ridiculous Force projection battle).

What RoS did:

1. JJ doesn't give a crap about Johnson's vision. He even snubs it a few times. For example, when Force Ghost Luke catches the lightsaber that Rey is trying to destroy and says, "A Jedi's weapon deserves more respect." Heck yes, it does! None of this, "Hi I'm Luke and I'm gonna toss my lightsaber over my shoulder like it's trash" nonsense.

2. Rey's powers are explained in more ways than one. Not only is she powerful because she's Palpatine's granddaughter but because she's had help from fallen Jedi all along. Some people may take issue with her backstory and with the help she receives. Maybe it doesn't completely make sense, but good grief, it's better than, "Rey's a total nobody from nowhere but somehow she's the most OP force user of all time." I thought what they did with her character in this film was inspiring. When Yoda says, "Alone, never have you been"...I'm not gonna lie, I cried. And the fact that she's the emperor's granddaughter, but for all intents and purposes, Luke and Leia are her real mom and dad and she takes their name: that's awesome. I mean, the Emperor turns Anakin to the dark side by promising the ability to cheat death. Anakin's offspring (Ben) dies, while Palpatine's offspring (Rey) lives. BUT she takes the Skywalker name, so who really lives on? It's just all very poetic and inspiring.

3. The emperor's return was a little off just because JJ didn't have enough screen time to fully set it up. But for what he had to work with, JJ did a great job bringing old wrinkle face back. I really liked that we got to see Exegol and a lot of stuff from Sith lore.

4. Luke is the amazing Luke we all know and love and he's who he should have been in TLJ. In my head-canon, lame hermit weirdo Luke never existed.

5. Leia's Force abilities are explained and she's given the credit and attention as a Force user that we've been waiting for since Yoda's line in RotJ, "No, there is another."

6. Finn and Poe are back. They're finally getting the frontmen treatment they deserve instead of clueless, helpless side characters.

7. The new characters are excellent. What I wouldn't give to have had Zorii, Babu Frik, little cone head droid, and Jannah in TLJ instead of Rose and Holdo. Nothing at all against the actresses who play Rose and Holdo. Unfortunately for them, their characters were simply not written well. These new characters are written well, and frankly, Babu Frik is so cute, I want to adopt him. I also really enjoyed the cameos of old characters, especially Han.

8. JJ does continue to ignore the rules of the Force the way Johnson did. This was probably my biggest complaint of the film. How do Rey and Ben pass physical objects between each other despite being far apart? How does Force Ghost Luke lift the x-wing? Whatever. Johnson already messed this up, so I guess if this is the only thing JJ didn't fix, I can get over it.

Was RoS perfect? No. It was too rushed because JJ had to fit in a lot of stuff that should have been in TLJ. Some of the Force use was questionable, but nothing here was as cringe as in TLJ. Was this trilogy pointless because Anakin was the chosen one and he brought balance to the Force in RotJ? Yeah, probably. But if you can look past all that and just want to have fun watching Star Wars, this is a really good film. Thank you, JJ, for salvaging this trilogy remarkably well.

title: Good for what it had to work with
review:
Okay, let me start by saying, I was not a fan of The Last Jedi. I understand why some people liked it, but I feel as though it derailed the momentum of this trilogy. So that put a lot of pressure on this installment to basically carry it through and finish strong. There are pros and cons to this movie like any other.

My biggest problem with the movie is that everything feels shoehorned. All of a sudden Palpatine is back and he's just been pulling the strings this entire time. It just seems lazy to me. It felt more like a tv show when they randomly bring back a villain from an earlier season.

Secondly, even if you do go ahead and make the decision to bring Palpatine back, do it more creatively. For starters, they should've completely leave him out of if the trailer (the one where he laughs at the end). The surprise that he's still alive would've been better served. Then, the entire resistance finds out he's still alive early in the movie because of some random spy. Imagine how much better it would've been if the resistance was confused the entire movie, wondering who's behind this given that snore was killed. They would just assume Kylo Ren was the mastermind and would've been completely taken aback when they see the emperor is still alive. And, they didn't even give him a lot to do. All he does is give a couple of "bad guy speeches" and shoot a little lightening. He is literally beaten because Rey blocks his lightening with two lightsabers instead of one.



Lastly, this movie simply lacks creativity. One of the things everyone was saying was "I hope they don't use another Death Star." Well, congratulations, instead of one big ship that can blow up a planet, we got thousands of smaller ships capable of blowing up planets. And, the way they executed it doesn't make any sense. They just randomly decide to blow up one planet for no reason, just to show the audience that they are capable of blowing up planets again. But why would the first order randomly send one star destroyer out to blow up a planet while the rest of the fleet can't even take off because they need some kind of navigation tower? And the whole reveal of Rey's lineage had no weight. I'm happy that Rey is important and not just the daughter of "nobodies," but the reveal had almost no significance. I think it's due to the whole back and forth between the three movies of the trilogy, but like I said, this movie had to go with what it had to work with.

Just some other random gripes I had before I move on to the pros: Give Finn more to do then just scream Rey every time there's a crisis. Poe is supposed to be some crazy good fighter pilot, as seen in TFA when he went off and destroyed like 20 tie fighters in 30 seconds. We literally get nothing like that in this movie. Finn tells Rey he has something to tell her that he never got a chance to say, and it's never actually said at any point in the movie. Why does every movie in this trilogy involve the entire resistance standing in a room talking about the enemies newest method of destruction and everyone stands around acting shocked and confused? Kylo Ren randomly decides to turn back to the light because his mom whispered his name right before she dies? He literally blew her up and sent her flying through space in the previous movie.

Okay, with all that being said, this movie does have pros. For one, I like how the cast gelled this movie. I like the decision to put them all together on one mission. The effects were really good once again, nothing seemed unreal. I like how Rey is not just some random scavenger but she fits into the puzzle. I like how the original trio makes an appearance in some way, shape or form. Despite all of my gripes, this movie isn't bad. I do believe that a majority of its problems come from having to make up for TLJ. In my opinion, I wouldn't even mind if Disney scratches this entire trilogy and start over. This trilogy brought nothing worth wild to the Star Wars lore. The end of Return of the Jedi serves as a much better wrap up to the Skywalker story. I had and still have no problem with wanting to continue the narrative, but do it more creatively and make it seem less like a money grab.

All in all, not a bad movie. I saw another review that describes it as "safe" and I think that's the perfect way to describe it. It's not trying to blow anyone's mind, it just wants to wrap up a franchise as seamlessly and uncontroversial as possible. I put 6/10 in my review above but I would say 6.5 is more accurate.

title: Has its ups and has its downs,
review:
I, like most people, love star wars. I'm not old enough to have seen the originals in their day. But I love the films and think each film is great in their own ways. (maybe not phantom). This film has great moments, action, surprises and emotional moments. To some extent I am very happy with it and I personally think it provides a somewhat fitting end to the Skywalker saga. The pacing of this movie isn't great, they've tried to fit a ridiculous amount of story into a couple of hours, and it just doesn't work very well. However it's a very enjoyable movie and provides a good amount of closure to the saga.

I really think that had the movie been the length of the last Jedi and they had some time to slow down and really feel the emotions of the characters and let the sense of danger sink in, this film would be one of the greats.

Either way, it has its problems and didn't live up to the hype of some of its predecessors, but I thoroughly enjoyed this film and would highly recommend it.

title: Makes You Appreciate The Last Jedi
review: This movie contains more plot holes than plot. Obnoxious amount of action sequences on such a large scale that it's inappropriate for even Star Wars standards. It's like they thought more noise and bright lights would divert our attention away from the missing plot lines or character development. Scene after scene jumps from one fight or chase to the next. Don't get me wrong, I love some action sequences! I love light saber fights. The more, the merrier. But this film lacks any real depth or substance. There is essential zero character development except for one main exception. It's like a two hour action sequence with no real order or sense among the madness. No cohesiveness. No sound explanations. No logic. No back story for the newbies just revival of the old. This entire film seems like an effort to repair damage and to appease fans following Rian Johnson's eccentric Episode VII. There are cheap fixes to every problem and some miracle solution beyond comprehension. There are way too many Easter eggs. The whole movie feels like an Easter egg. It's like a Hail Mary attempt to end a series that deserved so much better. We have lived and died with these characters for 40 years. Looking at the three films as a whole, it's obvious there was never a roadmap heading into Episodes 6, 7, 8 and it feels like JJ Abrams was making up new material on the go. He defied all rules and logic to tie up this epic story in a nicely wrapped package. This is entertaining, yes. It's just not great. Not even close. Nothing compared to the Star Wars greatness of the past.

title: The ENDING tore me to shreds....and I'm not ok
review:
I've been watching Star Wars since I was 10 year's old. When you talk about a finale it better be one helluva finale.

The last two episodes TFA & TLJ have become some of my favorites and I was really looking forward to this film. From start to finish the action is great, the storyline of Rey being the granddaughter of Palpatine was an interesting twist, loved the way Leia's character was honored, and I have long awaited for the day Kylo gets redemption and turns back to Ben Solo and boy do we get it! Adam Driver truly has made this character one of my personal favorites whether he's Kylo or Ben, I love how Driver brought this character to life....and the emotion....good grief it just makes me cry. (I feel the same with the way Ridley has done this with Rey). But I was utterly destroyed that Ben dies at the end saving Rey!

If Rey and Ben are a complete convergence of the force (force dyad) and the Emperor was able to drain some of this force to restore himself, I think the storyline could have gone an entirely different direction!! Both Rey and Ben should have destroyed the Emperor once and for all using this force dyad TOGETHER (that we've been seeing since the Force Awakens between these two), bringing that balance TOGETHER & starting a new lineage of Skywalkers TOGETHER! Because they do LOVE EACH OTHER!!! This ending killed me, for real! Finally the moment a lot of us have been waiting for and it's literally snatched away. Can't a character who gets redeemed have more than 15 minutes? Maybe in a way Ben Solo is the Rise of the Skywalker because HE IS A SKYWALKER!!! Did anyone think about that? Maybe his welcome to the Resistance wouldn't have been a warm one if he had lived and returned with Rey, but they would get over it! After all, he is Leia's son and she believed in him. There are so many layers here but Ben Solo deserved better!

I'm also terribly confused as to why Rey did not become one with the Force when she defeats Palps & just disappear when she died if she was a Jedi?! WTH?? Also, no cameo of Anakin, Obiwan, Yoda, etc being with Rey when she is being encouraged to rise to defeat the Emperor....these characters needed a cameo...not having them was a bad idea! BAD IDEA!!

Bottom line, Ben and Rey should have defeated the Emperor once and for all and Disney would have had one of the greatest love stories along with a great story line to go off of in this franchise for a long time in my opinion. Of course I understand this is my opinion but my heart won't go on after this.

title: Why so much hate?
review:
As many have pointed out, nothing will EVER compare to the original trilogy. Plus for many who watched them in their younger years, the impact made in watching those movies at younger age also has huge impact on the way you look upon them too. Regardless the original can never be compared to. The prequel trilogy had its approach to explain all that led to the movies so many loved, and they did a good job and they were well done. The only flaw in the prequel was Jar-Jar being used too much, but as much as that was a slight annoyance, it didn't ruin the overall experience and they were fun enjoyable trilogy.
Here is the truth to it all, even though the recent trilogy obviously connects to the original trilogy with characters, the truth of the matter is, these are truly more of a new trilogy and new direction of telling of the story, so in a way all the original Luke Skywalker story line told in episode 4, 5 & 6 had a start & finish. So in episodes 7, 8 & 9, the story still has Luke within the story, however he isn't the main focus of this trilogy. Think back to the prequel trilogy, who was that entire trilogy about? It wasn't really about Anikan Skywalker, but it was more about Obi-wan Kenobi showing his journey through all 3 prequels as he was the focus and biggest character in all 3 of those movies. What happens when you go to episode 4, Obi-wan (old Ben), is a small part and it was all about Luke now. Well this new trilogy basically did the exact thing, Luke had been reduced to small character and now was about Rei and all the new characters. If you watch these 3 new movies as more of a new direction of stories and still including old characters to connect together, then you are able to enjoy these movies much better. This final episode 9: Rise of Skywalker closes off this trilogy with connection to the original trilogy with lots of nostalgic visuals, (or voices), and at the end you have a very exciting and enjoyable trilogy new series. Are there flaws, yes there are, but a big part is because of the constant comparison and/or expectations everyone has! Just enjoy these for what they are and understand nothing could EVER come close to getting the same feeling majority of people got when they saw the original Star Wars Trilogy and nothing will ever be able to match that! "Luke, I am your father" can never come close to matching the feelings you had at that moment if you watched it for the first time, so instead of trying to capture something that can NEVER be recaptured again, best to enjoy these new set for what they are.

review:

title: Two viewings Two senate standing ovations
review:
I love the fan base of Star Wars, they span over multiple decades and generations. How could we not be divided and how could we not be so mad and so thrilled at the same time? Make a new Saga installment to much like the originals and it's a rip-off, make anything new and progressive it's blasphemous. The Force Awakens was a lot like the originals and that wasn't a bad thing if the next movie was properly progressive. However, in my opinion, the last Jedi was trying but was not successful and was the worst star wars movie to date, this movie is right in the middle. I loved so much of this movie but there were many obvious flaws I'm gonna on this movie and then but some praise on its name. This movie failed the Knights of Ren, teased since before THe Force Awakens to be slaughtered with ease two movies later in their first fight. They used a Sword with a pull-out map, would work for like a side clue, maybe but not the main element. The acting wasn't bad but was nothing better or more evolved than the last few with these same characters. They still don't feel completely comfortable in the roles like they should, given the chemistry, they showed in the Force Awakens they had to rebuild everyone almost. The Last Jedi messed up even if you liked the music, the CGI, the sets, everything like that.. it destroyed most character development and hurt the story going forward in so many ways. There are some other flaws but those are the bigger ones I have so far or maybe for now. I've seen this movie two times and the first time i liked the pacing and I loved it on the second viewing it had two points where I was like okay let's go. mostly the second act still really really good. The force was incredible to see so strong and powerful and used in the proper ways, now that we can show its UNLIMITED POWER!
I liked how Princess Leia passed away and how Kylo now Ben solo and her were so strongly connected given she is his mother. Kylo seeing Han and him having that moment like Han always wanted to give them both that rest was incredible and helped Ben become okay and see he has to most likely die to bring peace. I liked how they kissed but him just falling after that was a bit much and Rey not becoming a force ghost like he did was interesting. Kylo was the best part of this entire new trilogy in a lot of ways. I believe the third act was one of the more thought out element bringing and refreshing of the entire Saga. The ending was very good in my opinion Rey was always searching for a mother and father to call her own and finding out she was a Palpatine she wanted a better name and what better than Skywalker, this is the Rise of Skywalker.
Critics loved The Last Jedi and this movie was fixing a lot of in their eyes positives but in most fan's eyes mistakes. so obviously critics dislike it and since they do many people feel uncomfortable saying its a good movie.

title: Too much crap going on
review: A lot of things that are either "too powerful", "too lucky" or "too surprising" going on all the time. It's simply not reasonable. Contradicts the nature of the universe and the previous storyline. It's like they're trying to create a Marvel-copycat.

title: Mixed feelings
review:
I was excited and nervous for this film. So just want to say first of all this is a good film if it wasn't tied to a story that I and so many others love...



First of all, the Skywalker saga. Anakin Skywalker was the chosen one. He was to bring balance to the force. You could argue that he did in episode XI. But in my opinion they almost completely ignored that and brought back the emperor which conflicts with Anakins contribution to bring balance to the force. They try to remedy it by having him say in the film bring balance to the force, as I did". (Not exact quote) This is not what anyone wanted

This film was just chaos until the end. It's like someone doing their Christmas shopping last minute, everyone running around.

The story was too thin. I kinda liked the end because I realized that they, as mentioned before, ignored Anakin's saga. So if they had to ignore him then this ending was OK.

The use of force in this film was not like any of the other trilogies. They once again ignored the logic of the other films. Too OP.

I am not a super hardcore Star Wars fan. I haven't read that much (Star Wars) but Star Wars is and always will be my favorite saga. The movies and TV shows that I have watched are my favorites. So I don't have the knowledge to tell you everything they did wrong compared to George Lucas's vision but these are my first thoughts after thinking about it w while.

title: A mediocre film with a predictable plot
review:
This film is definitely not the strongest instalment in the trilogy and franchise, but it manages to meet its own expectations and tell its own story.

Contains Spoilers:

The film's plot relies excessively on its predecessors, particularly Episode VI: Return of the Jedi, and introduces nothing new and fresh to the Skywalker Saga. The film also suffers from a lack of character development for the newly introduced villain, Emperor Palpatine, and his new organization, the Final Order.

Despite its flaws, the film is still a relatively enjoyable film to watch, especially for many Star Wars fans, and contains many references to other story arcs in the franchise. The first half of the film definitely added a great sense of suspense, while the middle of the film may be confusing to some viewers, due to its rather complex scenes.

In conclusion, this film manages to embrace the vision and scope of the Star Wars saga, however it is limited by its unclear storyline and lack of originality.

title: Not bad not good

Trust me ignore those posts, my guess is those people didn't go to the original movies and/or were too young to understand what they were watching.

A few scenes left me scratching my head and didn't seem "realistic" (I know it is Star Wars nothing is real but you'll see what I mean) but take those away and the movie would have been great. The ending of the movie (not the saga because let's face it there will be more) was very well done and conceived. I personally wish they would have built up Reys past in the last movie because the reveal left me scratching my head a little. Honestly it would have been better to do that in the last Jedi and maybe explore it a little in this one but what ever that is knit picky. The movie is great, it brings back some fan favorites and also has a good story line. You will like it if you are a true fan.

As for me this is my 9th Star Wars that I have seen on opening weekend the first when I was just 8 years old. I am thankful for Disney and George Lucas for allowing me to be part of the Star Wars world for so long. I was able to take my kids to 1 - 3 and my grand kids to 7-9 (well really only 9 on opening weekend). It has been a great a 40 years and I look forward to seeing the what they have in mind for the next ones.

title: Loved it. A perfect end to the saga.
review: Ignore the bad reviews, if you like Star Wars you will love this final installment. Like Avenger's Endgame, it fills every moment with action, loving references to all the earlier films and neatly ties up lots of loose ends, leeving this genuine die hard fan totally satisfied. Sure, if you want to apply logic to the plot you can pull it apart in seconds, but Star Wars was never Shakespeare and was never a documentary series, so why start worrying about the "how" and the "why" now? Enjoy it for the fun, the spectacle and seeing old friends. There are some very strong performances especially from most of the leading characters. I have two criticisms: there are a few cheesy moments, especially noticeable in the big crowd scenes (if you want to see how to direct big crowd scenes, watch early Frank Capra films). Also, the character of Poe Dameron, is naff and underwritten, and not particularly well acted; it is trying to replace Han Solo's character but without any of the wit and charisma. But these criticisms never spoil the film which, like episodes IV and V I will happily watch again and again.

title: Everything and Nothing
review:
When I read reviews the day before the release, I saw a mixed bag. Consequently I came into today with muted expectations. But when a trusted "Star Wars Friend" friend told me that it was "EPIC", I held out with a glimmer of hope.

The truth was, this film was somewhere in between. As a die hard Star Wars fanatic, it's hard to be realistic about what the film can actually deliver (and for that reason I've learned to be forgiving). However, this movie gave me everything that I could have ever wanted. Perhaps therein lies the problem. In an attempt to finish many things, it finished nothing.

Big moments in the series that should have delivered an emotional punch were rushed as if they were just another point in a checklist of things the film hoped to accomplish. The result was that there weren't any moments to let the plot breathe, or to deeply connect with the characters... be it in death, victory, or romance. Nothing illustrates this so clearly as with Palpatine. It will hardly count as a spoiler (since the trailers built up the laugh of Palpatine as a hint that he would play a part in this film), but the film makers elect to immediately reference this in the opening roll as if his participation was a foregone conclusion that didn't require any explanation. Often I find myself critiquing the nature of thin plots spread across excessive run times, but in this case it was a rich storyline that should have been an hour longer.

However, this wasn't the only reason it was difficult to connect with the characters. It was clear that they were looking to create a grand close to the series. In some respects it was too grand. The force transforms from an ability that stretches little beyond the interpersonal contact between two dueling characters in past trilogies to the augmented nature of its power seen in this film, where it is seen bringing down spaceships instead of merely choking insubordinate members of the empire. I get it. We want to see big explosions and impressive CGI-but I can't help but feel that this overwhelming power causes the characters to lose some of what makes them relatable. Especially when this grand ability comes without any of the struggle that we've seen past characters in the series confront. The result is a cast of bodies performing supernatural actions instead of people that we see ourselves in. Even when trying to connect, it ends up being a forced caricature of human experience that doesn't create any dynamic sentimental nuance. It's emotion for the sake of emotion... and it's hyperbolic display makes that pretty clear. It feels as if the characters are in a constant state of panic and urgency, and never have a vulnerable moment. It is almost as if vulnerability was explicitly avoided, and the characters are as rushed to respond to constantly arising conflict as the filmmakers were to get to the credits. What charming emotion might have been developed feels like little more than a ploy to reminisce on past character qualities that worked-like Poe and Rey mimicking the bickering banter of Han and Leia. It's like watching a magician try to perform the same tricks and expecting the same results. It lacks originality. To be fair, that seemed to be the case for this entire trilogy though.

For that reason, I give it an "ehhh". If you're looking for a movie that will tie a nice bow on the end of the series, and one that will come with tons of action, this flic will definitely give you what you're looking for. Heck! There were even a few good laughs. Of course, it's entertaining-and maybe that's what people are looking for. But if you are hoping to see a movie that will stay with you for life as an indelible climax to one of histories greatest chain of films, it may be a little short of your expectations. It will likely be forgotten in a way that Return of the Jedi wasn't... and that just seems like a shame. I wonder what George Lucas thinks.

title: The Circle of Mediocrity is Now Complete
review:
Oh Disney, what have you done to Star Wars? It's crazy to think how I went from being incredibly excited to watch episode seven to completely indifferent going into episode nine. I've always thought that it would be nigh impossible to botch up Star Wars, but congrats Jar Jar Abrams and company, you did it with this movie!

Of course, I didn't think it was bad per say. Just painfully mediocre. The visual effects and soundtrack are top notch, and original characters like C-3PO actually had some really solid moments. I also like how an attempt seemed to have been made to actually care about Star Wars lore by including Sith holocrons and the like. And yes, adding Palpatine was a terrible decision, but I did enjoy seeing him again, even if his actions were...questionable.

Unfortunately, there was just too much that held this film back. It felt rushed, especially at the beginning, and the movie thought it would be a good idea to randomly include two new girls who contributed next to nothing. I mean, were we supposed to care about them or something? Speaking of not caring, I never really felt a connection with the main cast. They just remain stagnant and never develop. Watching characters grow throughout a movie can be what really draws audiences in, but this saga utterly fails in that regard. Rey is the best example of this, and her omnipotent Mary Sue powers really reduce the stakes and tension in the movie since you know she will kick everyone's butt. And I'm sure Kylo's behind has been sore for the past two movies now.

Unlike The Last Jedi, I don't think that this movie did anything egregious (like ruining Luke's character), but it didn't do anything great either. It still had it's moments, but sadly fails to live up to the Star Wars name.

And that's quite disappointing.

title: as a Star Wars film, this is a letdown!
review:
If this was a standalone SciFi movie, it wouldn't have been half bad. Sure, the story has a "straight-to-dvd" feel and some of the plot is not well thought out, but the visuals, the score and yes, even the acting is pretty good. But this isn't a random holiday movie, this is an installment of the biggest franchise in the world, Star Wars. And taking that into consideration, this movie goes from decently average, to a whole lot worse.

This is the last part of a trilogy, and yet it feels like nothing has happened yet. The characters that were introduced in the Force Awakens are still as flat three movies later. We hardly know anything about them, and due to the lack of character development I just can't get myself to care about them (compare them to the original characters, who people to this day still love). The lack of a coherent story throughout the three movies make it painfully obvious that there was no plan about an overarching story. And the idea to bring an old foe back from the dead just to kill him again is just a cheap way to get sympathy points from nostalgic fans. But one that backfired in my opinion. Not only was the "reason" iffy at best, it also ruins the entire premise of the previous six films. Disney not only made a bad series, they also tarnished the old ones.

This terrible trilogy is exactly what happens when you make a movie solely for the intent of making money, without any vision or interesest to tell a good story. I'm sure some people enjoy it, as casuals usually do when given something flashy, but hardcore fans will end up with a wounded soul from these movies. And that's a damn shame.

Ask me in 40 years though after watching it 400 times if it's as good as the original trilogy because right now I've only seen it once :) Thank you to Disney for making my dreams come true and making this new trilogy. I do wish it had been done 20 years ago with Han Leia and Luke together in their prime, but they didn't, so this to me is as good as it could get in 2019 without those 3 characters together leading the roles, they're like family to me those 3. C3PO was back to his best in this. I did feel the last two lacked so much 3PO.

Alright I will shut up now. Just so hyped up. Cannot wait to see it in 4D next week!!

title: A long review for long term Star Wars fans
review:
As a fan of Star Wars since seeing the first movie as a child in 1977, this review is for the long term, true 'die hard' fans of Star Wars, who remember if from the first film.

Having loved the original trilogy, but really disliked the prequels, I was happy when 'The Force Awakens' turned out to be quite good. However, as I'm sure many will agree, 'The Last Jedi' was simply terrible! So terrible, that I was starting to fall out of love with Star Wars completely. It really was that bad, and it was almost as if it was written to deliberately disappoint and annoy fans like myself. I don't really want to mention the directors name of that film, but we all know who he was and hope he's never let near the franchise again. He did a lot of damage!

So when it came to watching 'The Rise of Skywalker' I was apprehensive, as it had an awful lot of repair work to carry out to fix the Saga.. Add to that this is the end of the Saga, and the pressure is even higher.

I have my own all metal R2D2 which I take to events, and this has got me on Disney's radar due to the work I do for the Astromech club, and I was fortunate to be invited to the premiere of the new movie in Leicester Square London on Wed 18th. I then watched it again the following night with two of my children. Therefore, having already seen the film twice, I feel I'm able to give a good review.

So, onto the film!

The first thing I want to say, is that for the first time in years, this really does 'feel' like a Star Wars film. A combination of sets, battles, droids, and the music score by John Williams come together in a way that makes the movie feel so 'Star Wars'. That may be a strange thing to say, but with many new characters, locations and ships.. the newer movies were not really that familiar to the original fans. This movie reaches out to everyone. There are various cameos in the film, some of which are easier to spot than others. I won't spoil any of them, apart from to say they are done well, appropriately, and really add to the excitement and thrill. Given this is the last film in the Saga, the cameos really help glue everything together.

The storyline is really, really good. Questions that have been left open are finally answered, and things that seemed to make no sense at all now make perfect sense, and boy are there some great surprises! You start to wonder if The Last Jedi was actually written so badly in order to allow there to be so many questions left to be answered in this movie.. or if J J Abrams has just done a brilliant job bringing things back into line with some excellent writing! I suspect the latter.

The action if superb in this film. It really does have a feel of 'Return of the Jedi' about it, going between several different storylines that are all in their own right fast moving, exciting, and gripping. As can be expected there are lightsabre battles, space battles and lots of use of The Force. All are simply amazing and stunning. All the characters have now developed their personalities and relationships with each other, and have all developed their own various skills that the action sequences are totally on another level than they were in the previous episodes.

During the previous movies we have endured some really cheesy moments, such as Leia's 'spacewalk'(!!) and the terrible 'Casino' scene in The Last Jedi. Even the prequels had some terrible moments and characters (Jar Jar!). Happily, The Rise of Skywalker seems to have done away with all of this. There are a few moments that are amusing for sure, but nothing that makes you cringe. Overall, there is a darker, more serious tone to events that really works with the overall style of the movie.

As the movie draws on, you are pulled more and more into the various stories happening in front of you. Great acting, stunning visuals, and well choreographed action scenes mean that although a long film, it seems to fly by in minutes. I didn't look at my watch once during the entire showing. And I've seen it twice within 24 hours!

As far as ending the Saga, I feel it does do this really well. I'm giving nothing away, but as a long term fan, I was more than happy with the way things draw to a close. And I have to admit that at various times during the film, I did tear up a bit, some happy, some sad. But mostly happy.

Star Wars has always tried to portray a positive image of good triumphing over evil. Wrongs being put right, and loyalty and love being able to conquer everything. J J Abrams gets this. He really does, as do the scriptwriters.

Don't listen to the press reviews by people who probably never even watched the original films or aren't fans, trying to outdo each other with their pretentious analysis of the acting, while concentrating on any flaw they can find to try and justify what they do for a living. If you're a fan of Star Wars, like I am, then you're going to love this movie. Put aside your dislike of 'The Last Jedi', and keep an open mind. I assure you, It's a masterpiece, and a fitting ending to a truly epic saga. J J Abrams.. we salute you!

title: I really enjoyed it! (Make me feel confused as to the bad reviews)
review:
I really liked this movie, I'm going to try and keep it spoiler free. So I am for sure a Star Wars fan through and through, I have watched them since I was probably about 2 years of ages when I had the originals on VHS.

I like most of you love the Original Trilogy, I probably am aligned with what I feel is the concensus on the Prequel Trilogy too, ish, I mean I don't HATE it, I think that the first film is a bad film saved by a great ending (Maul) Attack of the Clones has good parts but is broadly a 6/10 or perhaps 5/10. I feel Revenge if the Sith is 100% the best of the prequels, I actually really enjoyed a lot of that movie save for some bad acting etc.

The new ones, I loved Force Awakens, I feel there was a dip in quality with Last Jedi but I don't think it was a BAD movie, I feel like a lot of people look at that film as though it isn't part of a bigger trilogy, by that meteric, it's not amazing no, but I feel it is a good movie on the whole, probably 6.5-7/10.

I thought it would be helpful as you can see where i'm at in terms of the others and hopefully that will help you work out whether to entirely disregard my opinion or read on.

So, Before I went to the cinema I read about 3 spoiler free reviews, It seemed like the reasons the film was quite divisive in the was done to one of three or maybe things,

An Apparent "disrespect" towards Rian Johnson by reversing work in Last Jedi

They tried to fit in too much

Too much SJW content (ah yes 2019's favourite internet compliant)

The end is not satisfying?

So to address these, There is a lot going on in this movie sure, and on the way to these things happening there a lot of twists and turns, but if you are to write down the actual synopsis of this film, it really isnt complicated, I really don't get this piece of criticism, If you ask me, Attack of the Clones is there or there abouts in terms of complexity and i've never heard the same complaint aimed at that.

In terms of whether the ending is satisfying, Well that's hard to go into without spoilers but going into this movie, I wanted Snoke addressed, I wanted Reys heritage addressed and I wanted an ending that was fairly complete and unambigous. Honestly we get all of those, I'm really happy with the ending, My wife came out (not at all a Star Wars fan really) and she said " All i could think about was Game of Thrones could learn about endings from this movie"

The SJW thing, I mean if you haven't got to terms with the main character being a female by now then, I don't know what to tell you. There are plenty of female characters in the cartoons etc and no one complains about that....

As far as the Rian Johnson stuff, Again, What exactly? What part of this film does that? the fact that one character introduced by him has only a little screentime? Is that it? Because that particular character was only ever minor anyway.... (hey Bossk seems to have made a name for himself with all of 3 seconds of screentime and no dialogue in the original movies...)

I loved this movie, I love how it ends, it was truly visual masterpiece and the performances from all of the main four actors (Poe, Finn, Rey, Kylo) were frankly a huge step up from the previous entries.

All in all it's probably my 3rd favourite Star Wars movie, (I think it beats ROTJ) and I can't wait to watch it again.

title: Tries to clean up a mess called Last Jedi, but it was too big a mess to clean up.
review:
Please note there are spoilers ahead.

I shall start by pointing out the positives first, visually if you watch it in a decent cinema (and not VUE that at 90s prices offers 90s technology ) it is good, the acting is good and moments here and there are good. Now the bad points and spoilers.. We are introduced within the first 5 minutes to Palpatine, I am confident that neither of the previous 2 movies mentioned any greater being than Snoke. Miraculously they learn of the a beacon / tracker that can lead them to the First Orders massive army. Everything is conveniently placed, they find a dagger that reveals the location of a tracker. C3PO can read it, but cant translate it but can cause his memory to wipe, they d it for the greater good, but all it takes is R2D2s finger in C3POs butt to get his memory back up to the point before they went on that mission? Why did Chewie run after Rey and how easily he got caught? Then his so called death feels so anti-dramatic, this is a character you have an attachment to since 1977 but even that fake death feels cheap. Kylo Ren is chasing Rey and catches up to her, they have a farting face force fight, blow up a ship and the Kylo Ren just lets her go?? The reveal of the spy within the first order was just random, why all of sudden has this person decided to help? it has to be more than just hating Kylo Ren? Horse on a Star Destroyer up high in the atmosphere?? And the biggest ridiculous thing of all, Jedi healing, for 8 movies we hear nothing about it (and unless you have been watching the Mandalorian where it has come up, which is set before this) its not only used easily but mastered by 2 people?? Clearly you can see they tried to do damage control and I have a feeling for what was planned with episode 8 alot of the plot holes would have been covered but this is a total mess. Oh and the last line in the film... clearly by now you are aware that Rey is a Palpatine, (wont even go into there was no mention or indication that Palpatine had any family) who are you? I am Rey.... Skywalker. Might as well had said I am Batman... it had no impact. Also the scenes with Leia in them you can see she was CGI'd into her scenes and her death felt cheap too, but cant really blame anyone for that as Carrie Fisher passed away. Rian Johnson messed up this trilogy.

title: I understand the 1s and 10s
review:
People who rate this movie a 10 I think saw a fun, non-consequential movie that was a good and entertaining ride. Sure, that's what this it. However, this movie didn't come to us without any context. It's meant to be part of a story arc decades in the making. This is where the 1s come in, to them this movie doesn't stand on its own two feet but on top of 8 other movies. And in that context, it is worthy of only a 1 star rating.
Here's the thing: for all their flaws, the prequels added an enormous depth to the original movies. They complimented them. Darth Vader being the best example. Where he previously was just the evil guy with a twist and eventual redemption, the prequels added depth to this character and turned him into the pivotal tragic hero of the saga.
Enter the sequels. They do just the opposite. They add no new depth to the story, nothing that could compliment and enhance the previous movies. Instead, for a lack of genuinely new ideas, they make use of existing material whenever it suits to drive their chaotic plot and since it is chaotic indeed, the use turns into misuse and abuse. Best example is before mentioned Darth Vader. While the prequels added depth and drama to his character, this newest installment of the sequels basically negates a central part of his identity within Star Wars lore. For what? To serve as a cheap and easy fix to a messy plot.
In that context, I rate this movie a 3 out of 10. If it were one of those unaffiliated SW movies like Rogue One it might have been worth a 6.

title: An Honest Review From A Lifetime Star Wars Fan
review:
(Skip the first part if you wanna get straight to the review, this is just background information about me so you can understand my rational behind the score and review I'm giving you)

I'm going to be as fair and as honest as I possibly can with this review. A little background before I get into this, I've been a Star Wars fan for over 20 years. I loved the original trilogy. Although the prequels weren't the best (especially with that cringe dialogue), I still enjoyed them for what they were. I was entertained by the lightsaber battles and great character additions such as Darth Maul, Jango Fett, and Christopher Reeves as Dooku. I enjoyed the Star Wars: The Clone Wars TV series. I enjoyed Rebels for what it was. When The Force Awakens came out, I was satisfied. That movie kinda played it safe and redid some of the stuff from A New Hope, I didn't like how Rey beat Kylo with literally zero training; However, overall, I was satisfied. I thought there were a lot of good things set up for the sequel. Then we got the Last Jedi, and i'll be honest I borderline hate that movie. I can barely find the strength the rewatch it. Just everything I loved, or whatever hope I had for the sequel to Force Awakens was utterly crapped on and destroyed just for the sake of subverting expectation. I enjoyed Rouge One, hell I even enjoyed Solo for what it was worth. Sure It felt weird because it wasn't Harrison Ford; but nevertheless, I didn't feel offended by it as a Star Wars fan like The Last Jedi did to me. That being said, let me give you my honest take for Rise of Skywalker.

Honestly? It wasn't THAT bad. I was actually expecting this movie to be WAY WAY WORSE. Some parts made say "What the hell?!" and confused me, but after a rewatch i'll probably enjoy or be at least entertained by those initial "What the hell?!" moments. This movie could've been way better, The big reason this movie suffers so much is because NOT ONLY is it trying to be it's own stand alone film, it's doing it's very best to course correct all the things fans (including myself) didn't like about The Last Jedi. The Pacing for this movie is very very fast. It's trying to cram a lot of information, AGAIN, because not only is trying to do it's own thing, this movie is one big course correction. Okay now for some NITTY GRITTY details that I disliked or got (at least) confused by. Rey is SUPER powerful in this movie. I'm talking CRAZY powerful. This movie is supposed to take place a year after Last Jedi and she uses the force like a full blown master. Granted, she does get training from Leia (It is established in this movie, that Leia was trained by Luke to be a Jedi at some point in time. She was a Jedi Master in the EU). And IF YOU'VE READ THE LEAKS YOU SHOULD KNOW THIS, Rey is the granddaughter of Emperor Palpatine. So her year long training from Master Leia, plus her lineage, could suspend my disbelief a little to how she could have gotten so power in so short of a time. However, if you wanna just call a spade a spade, and say "That's bullcrap. She shouldn't be this powerful despite her heritage." Then I would say that is some fair criticism. At least Rey got some training. That made me at least a little satisfied knowing she got some training if at all. She does some really cool things with the force in this movie. Some great Jedi power action in this movie. It's like The Force Unleashed type of crazy badass force powers. However, The lightsaber combat in this is kinda mediocre. It's nothing like the prequel lightsaber battles. It's more just angry hack-n-slash rather than a display of master swordsmanship. But its okay I suppose. Leia dies. And the way she dies is by saying her sons name. She's laying in bed and using the force to connect to her son, she say's "Ben" and dies. Kind of a lack luster way to go out imo. Chewie breaks down and gets super emotional after finding out too. Which seemed silly, because he didn't act nearly as emotionally when Han Solo died. The battle with Palpatine was a little lack luster. Sure the force powers were cool, but idk. It just seemed so simple or not much of a thrill. Idk you'd think with all the money they put into the production for these things, they'd at least make the Jedi Sith battles just absolutely out of this world, but they don't and they didn't. There were plenty of great nostalgic moments. Plenty of great star wars feel good moments. But when it gets to brass tax, I'd have to give the movie maybe a 4-6/10. It was a tad underwhelming. However, it made me personally feel good because it wasn't as bad as i thought. And certainly wasn't as bad as the last Jedi. I'd probably rank this movie somewhere with The Phantom Menace and Attack of the Clones. I enjoy those movies too, but i can recognize aspects that make them critically not as great as others. I Hope my review was helpful to you. If you're a Star Wars fan, you'll mildly dislike it, hate it, but maybe you'll enjoy a little too, kinda like me.
