The connections to other movies were well placed and meaningful. The ending really did give a sense of closure and excitement. The now 40 year old men who sat in a theater and saw Luke Skywalker for the first time. They will never relive that. If that's what you are expecting, you will be disappointed. So put yourself in the mind of a young girl, a young boy. Look for the hope. The unity. The adventure and battles. A story in a galaxy far far away, a tale told a long time ago. Lessons that are eternal, morals that are universal, packaged neatly in our favorite characters submerged in plots that move and excite us. That is what Star Wars is about. title: Best Star Wars Movie Ever!
review:
Rey (Daisy Ridley) is a 20 year old Jedi, she's the main character in the last and final movie in the Star Wars Movies, she's going on an amazing adventure with Poe (Oscar Isaac) and Finn (John Boyega) to find the planet Exegol, the secret world of the sith, and right against them, there's Kylo Ren (Adam Driver) and Emperor Palpatine (Ian McDiaemid).

Throught their adventure, they meet older characters from older movies, like Lando calrissian (Billy Dee Williams) from the "Empire Strikes Back" and "Return of the Jedi".

If I had to describe this movie in one single word, it will have to be "Epic", Especially the ending when Rey and Kylo Ren joined forces and defeated the evil Emperor once and for all. For me "Rise of Skywalker" is the best Star Wars movie ever made and one of the best movies of 2019.

The chemistry between the actors is amazing and is really rare to find, the new characters that's been added are fitting perfectly into the film and adds more into it. The Soundtrack from John Williams is brilliant, with the normal "Main Theme" and the splendid "Finale".

The Movie is great, it has everything you could have asked for, and a lot more! I recommend it to any Sci-fi movies fan and especially any Star Wars fan, this movie is a must watch.

title: Everything you wanted to see and MORE!
review: I did not feel like there was anything left undone or unexplained. I loved this entire movie. I've never felt so excited about a movie in my life. The atmosphere of Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker was an absolutely amazing film. Thank you JJ and cast. I also enjoyed seeing a yellow lightsaber at the very end. I loved the scene between Rey and Ben when they were fighting on the same side, side by side...Just as Ben had seen before in his vision. Look there was nothing in the movie that I anticipated. I didn't expect to see Harrison Ford at all. I didn't expect to hear the force ghost voices; the Jedi who had died before. I didn't expect to see Force healing. I didn't expect to see Ben or Rey passing objects through the Force to one another, and it would later serve them in the battle against Palpatine. I didn't expect to see so many scenes with Carrie Fisher. And the way they wrapped up the ending for her was beautiful. She held the gold medallion in her hand and gave all she could to reach Ben. What energy she could muster to reach him drained her of her life and along with Rey's healing of Ben which gave him exposure to the Light Side of the Force and Leia's Love to reach him. The scene with Harrison Ford was even more poignant with the lines which came from Force Awakens. Having Palpatine in it was perfect to explain why there was still so much darkness in the universe. But the hope came from Kylo Ren when he told Palpatine he would kill him also. And while Kylo was busy getting his strength to face the Emporer, Rey was getting her strength to reach Ben. Finally, the kiss between Ben and Rey. Was amazing. We had seen them fight using the Force so long. When they were fighting on the sea I couldn't believe how much energy they put into their fight. It was astonishing. It seemed they were fighting themselves. And they were. Because they were a dyad. And together they could win but not on the dark side of the force but the light side. All the things I witnessed to wrap it up happened. I hated to see Ben die. But it made sense. He showed genuine proof that he had changed by giving his life for Rey. She deserved to live. And he knew that. You could see it in his eyes when he held her close to him. I could just see him saying, it should be me dead and not you. So I thought his sacrifice was just as beautiful as Leia's sacrifice to reach Ben...or her death would have been in vain. Palpatine was destroyed, this time melting down into nothing. And all the Sith were killed as the giant cave came down. Rey was brought back by Ben. The metal medallion was given to Chewie just as it should. None of the rest of the cast died. They lived to see a happy ending. I couldn't have imagined it any better than this. This movie was the biggest treat. I saw 3 generations come together to watch the film. There were tears of joy. For all the naysayers crying boohoo because that is all that they do, they are not real Star Wars fans. A real Star Wars fans love all Star Wars movies ever made. Believe me, I know people who cannot get enough of the world of Star Wars. So while there are the pitiful few disgruntled naysayers there are many more of us who LOVED this film and watched it numerous times. Thank you so much to JJ Abrams and to the cast of all the Star Wars films. Thank you to George Lucas for bringing us the world of Star Wars.

title: A Good Ending
review:
So, up until today, I had no intentions of ever seeing this movie, but due to self-isolation, I decided to give it a go.
And, surprisingly, it was a very good and mostly satisfying ending.
I won't go into the plot as I suck at plot descriptions and I think it's better if you all see it instead of me trying to explain it.
It had great special effects - some were so real it was really chilling.
It had AWESOME music; fantastically choreographed action scenes - in fact, this movie is one of the most jam-packed of the whole franchises and one of the most epic ones.
It had great themes, awesome emotion (one of the best emotional ones I've seen, considering how we all know that character development and ewwwy-gooey emotional stuff aren't Star Wars strongest suits).
It's not as bad as all the Star Wars haters make out, but I can see why people hate it. It's certainly not a movie for everyone, and keep in mind that there are always going to be haters, so just watch it for yourself and don't be afraid to like it if you want to - whether a movie's good or bad is ultimately simply a matter of opinion. If you want to hate this movie, go ahead. If you want to like this movie, go ahead. Ignore the haters, the ones that say nonsensical things about it - each new Star Wars movie is always going to be the new one for someone to spread nonsensical, overboard hatred and nonsense for it.
There were a couple scenes early on that I thought could have had more depth to, but since this is Star Wars, I wasn't about to let that stop me from enjoying it. They were just minor complaints and it is a very epic finale to the Skywalker saga with some amazing twists and turns. Very happy that I decided to give it a go.
It's not for everyone, but since it is the end to the Skywalker saga, I recommend that you watch it.

title: Did the best they could with what they had
review:
This film got an incredibly bad rep. Naturally it was not as good as the original trilogy, but of course it's not. There are such high standards for Star Wars films now because most fans want the new films to make them feel like the originals. Part of that 'feeling' is the fact that both the original and the prequels came out a while ago, and as a result people would have seen star wars, this huge extravagant sci-fi adventure, as children, when everything you saw would be mind blowing. My mum for instance (who i saw the film with) hated all the prequels because they didn't feel like the originals she saw as a child, whereas i loved them, because they came out as i was a kid.

But then again, part of the problem with this film is the fact that Rian Johnson just threw out JJ Abram's plan and characters arcs from Force Awakens, did his edgy little multi-million dollar student film project and then disappeared, leaving behind plot holes, destroyed character arcs (I think Fyn could haven been so much more than comic relief) and millions of angry fans.

I personally believe that this film is the best in the trilogy, I know many people will disagree but i went to see this and had such a fun time, almost made me sad that i don't have a new star wars to look forward to. Graphics are great (that's where the money went), story could be better, brilliant redemption for Ben Solo with one of if not the best lightsaber battles in the three films, but most importantly, a pleasing way to end this strange roller coaster of a trilogy.

I hope the next star wars in 10-20 years time can top this, cause let's face it. They played it pretty safe.

title: Best film this year so far
review:
A long time ago, in a galaxy far, far away......alright maybe not that far away, back in 1977, amongst the films of "Close Encounters of the Third Kind" and "The Spy Who Loved Me", a relatively unknown director called George Lucas created a vast leap forward in the world of special effects by creating the film we all know and love "Star Wars". Ever since then, along with advances in special effects, the universe of "Star Wars" has advanced leaps and bounds in what we understand a great movie to be.

Travel forward, 42 years, OMG I'm starting to feel old now, and the "Skywalker Saga" has taken it's final bow, fired off the 21 gun salute, in what has become the most wildly anticipated film of the year, "The Rise of Skywalker"

Now, as a fellow cinema lover, I despise, with a hatred induced passion, almost reminiscent of the dark side itself of spoilers and leaks about up coming films, so I will keep this review spoiler free, and only refer to scenes we have seen in the trailers.

Ever since Disney produced the first, new film in "The Sequel Trilogy" back in 2015, die hard fans have had mixed feelings about what these films are really about, and do they still hold their own against the original trilogy, and are they just being made for the profits from the franchise. The new turn has not been welcomed with universal open arms, with fans being split on love or hate for the "Disney Trilogy" and people loosing hope on the franchise being recovered any time soon.

But luckily along comes J.J Abrams to direct, produce and part write this final installment, with hope to bring "...the spark to light the fire which will take the First Order down" (Po Dameron, Oscar Isaac, The Last Jedi) so sorry, couldn't help myself....along with film composer royalty John Williams, excellent as always music to hark back to film gone by, this film is one that is made for the fans as well as the "none believers" alike. So this is a film for all.

The storyline can be a bit slow at the start, there was massive hype after the first trailer as we are given a fleeting thought of the return of Emperor Palpatine, played to perfection by Ian McDiarmid, following other trailers and media interviews, it's no surprise that "HE" will return, as the hype was so large, I was expecting some large scene that will lead on the the unveiling of the thought dead Emperor, but it was all tied up in the first few scenes, so a small disappointment there. Another possible one that fans may see, is from the trailers, the words of Luke Skywalker (Mark Hamill) "A Thousand Generations of Jedi Live in Your Now" a possible scene where all Jedi would come back in one form or another would be shown, but sadly it was not in the version I watched, maybe in the deleted scenes, I don't know.

Of course the films production was shadowed by the loss of Carrie Fisher, a much loved actress who's talent will live on in her films, much like the loss of Leonard Nimoy who played Spock in the series Star Trek and later films, both him and his character had a tribute on screen, and thankfully, TROS also had a touching tribute to both Fisher and Leia, one which, in my opinion done them both justice.

My final thoughts on the film, it was a fantastic final installment to a much loved franchise, with some excellent inclusions from all the sage, though, I think there could be many more questions on Rey (Daisy Ridley) back story, with her true lineage unveiled, the questions of what happens next will start to circulate.

title: Star Wars By Way of Marvel/Disney
review:
I wanted to love this film. I really did. I had my doubts, though, heading in. I'm not the world's biggest J.J. Abrams fan, although I enjoyed "The Force Awakens" quite thoroughly. He just never seems to stick the landing for me.

All in all, "Rise of Skywalker" was pretty much exactly what I thought it was going to be: an OK movie with some good action, fun ideas, and a messy ending. The film starts off a bit messy. The opening scrawl is incredibly poorly written and hearkens back to the silly exclamation at the beginning of "Ep III's" scrawl, "WAR!" After that we get Kylo Ren's, Poe & the Gang's, and Rey's stories kick off to varying degrees of success. I found Ren's stuff engaging, especially as it is the sort of thing we haven't seen in the movies before; an unaffiliated Force Power User seeking to hunt down the Emperor because of the challenge to his power. It would be like "RotJ" opening with Darth Vader trying to hunt down the Emperor. Awesome.

Unfortunately the same cannot be said of Rey and Poe & Gang's openings. Rey is basically doing an amped up version of Luke's training on Dagobah but all of it crammed into one scene rather than spread out over the course of time in-depth martial arts and mindfulness training actually takes. Poe & Gang's intro is even worse as they play courier for yet another secret message that has to be transported via astromech. It felt more like the opening of "Solo" than one of the actual Saga movies.

After that, the movie actually started to click for me. It's rare that I find the middle of a film to be more engaging than the opening of ending but this is a rare exception.

The middle action of the film is full of exactly what I want from Star Wars; under-dog adventure, uncovering the past, fighting for the future, a power struggle for our hero's heart, and a healthy dash of humor. They travel to new planets and old but the film never feels like just a 'look-at-my-cool-cgi-world-I-built' extravaganza till the end of the film.

Unfortunately, as Rey and Ren get closer to Palpatine and the climax of the film, much of what is to come become extremely predictable, less moving emotionally, and more of an apparent attempt at CGI one upmanship, even by the standards of the prequels. The fingers of a MARVEL bloated Disney are all over the ending of "Rise of Skywalker." Specific moments of the film had me flashing back to "Avengers: Endgame" more than "Return of the Jedi."

That's a real shame because on its surface, I have no problem with plot points like Emperor Palpatine returning from the dead, Kylo Ren and Rey in a power triangle with the Emperor, or voice from the past speaking hope into a character but, in each of these instances, the scenes in which these things happen are stripped of their emotional import and relegated to a sort or 'look-how-clever-we-were' reveal. Frankly, nothing in this movie is so clever that anyone needs to hang a lantern on it.

Unfortunately, J.J seems to have taken his best shot with "The Force Awakens" with an awareness that the series had suffered a blow under George Lucas's prequels that Abrams knew he had to overcome by making a film that rang so true to what Star Wars is that the studio could be sure it was going to be a huge success. With "Rise of Skywalker" we have his 'prequel moment" where he thinks he has everyone's good will and can let loose with what he can really do with a property, which as any fan of "Star Trek" will tell you, is gut a series of its heart and replace it with action sequences that are fun the first time but mean very little and have no staying power.

title: The Rise of Skywalker is a product of The Last Jedi's failure.
review:
While I enjoyed myself watching The Rise of Skywalker, it is not a great movie. Most of the complaints I have heard have been about how ridiculous, fast-paced, and messy this movie is. But the more I consider these issues, none of them would have been an issue had Rian Johnson progressed J. J. Abrams's story. Instead, Johnson tried to make what a Star Wars movie was in his opinion instead of what the fans wanted. The Last Jedi did not progress anything, in fact the story is back at square one by the end; Rey has barely learned anything, Luke barely did anything except show that Johnson does not understand his character, the Casino planet was a waste of time, Holdo could have saved so much time and panic had she just told everyone they were going to seek refuge on the nearest base, and Snoke (the supposed new big villain) is killed without any story to his character.

J. J. Abrams had almost nothing to work with, just the death of Luke and Rey & Kylo Ren's force connection. Who else would be the villain other than Palpatine? Who else could train Rey but Leia? The only things I found truly dumb were the dagger that perfectly aligned with the Death Star remains, and Rey & Kylo's ridiculous use of the force (i.e: grabbing a ship from the sky and magically making a lightsaber disappear into the other's hands).

This was a 4 hour movie crammed into 2. I hope that Disney will allow for a Director's Cut so we can see a more clear, but still fairly flawed movie. If IMDb allowed for decimals in my rating, I'd give it a 6.7/10

title: Don't get me wrong... it's a fun flick! But....
review:
Although I don't consider myself to be a hardcore Star Wars fan - I haven't watched any of the TV series (yet) or read any of the books - I do enjoy the cinematic releases, and have watched them all. With that in mind, I must start off by saying that I consider all three films -- episodes 7, 8, and 9 -- to be a million times better than the prequels (which were just cringe-worthy in so many ways).

The new films are simply better made. The dialogue is leaps ahead of the dialogue in the prequels; the acting is far better; the "world" is much more real; and the effects are far more believable. (It is my understanding that The Phantom Menace was one of the first films to be shot completely digitally and made heavy use of green screens. That shows in the film's overly-glossy appearance.)

Part of what made the original trilogy (episodes 4, 5, and 6) work so well was that, despite their setting, they felt grounded in a sense of reality; the world felt real. The new trilogy's reliance upon real sets and improved effects (especially the fantastic lightsaber effects, which, from what I've read, used a combination of the more traditional "low-tech" techniques used in the original films and the fancier "high-tech" ones used in the prequels, resulting in far more realistic light reflections) makes the films a pleasure to experience and "live in."

However.

When I was watching The Rise of Skywalker in the theatre, I found myself of two minds. On the one hand, it was a fantastically fun film. And watching it with family made it all the more so. This is why I initially gave it a slightly higher rating (8/10). However, there were several occasions -- including one major, fundamental one -- when I found myself thinking, "Wait... what?"

The first such occasion -- which was also the "major, fundamental one" -- happened right off the bat, as soon as the crawl began! Yes, I'd seen the trailers that teased the return of Palpatine. But having the very first words of the film suddenly parachute him back into existence made for a rather... jarring experience. There was no buildup! There was no suspense! He was suddenly... back! So much lost opportunity....

Don't get me wrong. I'm not saying that he shouldn't have been in the film! I'm just saying that it wasn't handled well. And the same can be said for much of the film. It felt like it was trying to cram too much in. And it had some rather silly turns. For example, having the heroes literally *fall* into the solution to one of their problems (through that quicksand-like stuff) just undermined the journey that we're told Luke went on to try to achieve the same result.

Plus, why does Rey have to be a Skywalker at the end of the film? Her parents gave their lives for her; why wouldn't she want to honour them and restore the Palpatine name? Did the filmmakers start off by giving the film the title The Rise of Skywalker and then write themselves into a corner? It just felt forced. (No pun intended.)

And it felt, unfortunately, like the film was undermining the film that came before it. The Rise of Skywalker undoes a lot of what was fascinating about where The Last Jedi was going. I know that many, many fans would disagree with me, but, to me, The Last Jedi was a far better movie. It was an exciting movie. It was a movie that made me want to find out what happened next. Like, what does it mean that those young people have Force powers? Where could that take us? It was a movie with depth.

The Rise of Skywalker, on the other hand, despite being a fun blockbuster, just played things too safe. Sure, it brought closure to many aspects of the story... but it didn't bring closure to *all* aspects. In fact, it left a lot questions unanswered. And didn't answer all of the questions it *did* answer in as satisfying a way as it might have. Watching it made me wonder if a proper, well-thought-out story arc had been written in advance of the writing and filming of these new films.

Again, I enjoyed the movie. It was a heck of a lot of fun. J.J. Abrams is, indeed, a fun filmmaker! But to say that I was happy to find out he was coming back would be a lie. The Force Awakens, despite also being a heck of a lot of fun, was also incredibly derivative of A New Hope. The Last Jedi's plot wasn't perfect. (I also didn't think that the film's name was entirely appropriate... but, then again, that could be said for all three of the new ones. But that's a whole other story!) However, I still feel it was the most original and interesting of the new films. (Other than Rogue One, which isn't part of the main series.)

So.... The Rise of Skywalker.... A missed opportunity in some ways? Perhaps. On the other hand, would it have truly been possible to make a film that wrapped everything up according to every fan's desires? Of course not. Which is why I still give this film a 7 out of 10. 7 ain't bad, folks!

I still have the imagine of looking through the car windows and seeing the Death Star blowing up, and remember the exhilaration I felt at the time.

That all being said, I had hopes for this movie, and I also knew it was going to be flawed.

As I sat and watch the ending credits I silently said Thank You. Of course it's not perfect, it has plot holes, and some things just weren't needed. But while I was sitting in the theater I was engaged in every scene, the music, the characters and the story. And my emotions rode the roller-coaster through each scene. I didn't analyze the crap out of it. I didn't question the plot holes. As I do with most movies, I allowed myself to watch, listen and feel. I just took it in and thoroughly enjoyed it.

review:

review: First off I do not get why people hate on the new trilogy. It has soooooo many great things. It might have some bad but the great overshadows it. We get this new protagonist,Rey,who is one of my favorite characters in anything. I also think Daisy Ridley is a great actor. She especially shines in this one, and so does Jon Boyega as Finn. Rey is a great character for many reasons. She is smart, crafty, and very powerful! Its what this world needs to see. To keep it short because I could go on forever, this movie brings so much cool action, fun, adventure, drama, comedy, and general suspense! review:

It seems the fan base and critics are still divided by the left turn The Last Jedi took and the right turn The Rise of Skywalker took as if J.J and crew wanted to course correct the actions from The Last Jedi. As a fan I very much enjoyed this film.Once the wheels (or jets) started half an hour in The Rise of Skywalker was a fun rewarding ride. My advice is to go into this movie looking for one last adventure to the Skywalker saga without trying to pick it apart and your experience will be sweet.

review:

Many plot lines were destroyed, my favourite characters from the old movies acted and died in ways I don't believe they would..and over all it didn't feel like the beloved Star Wars I saw for the first time in front of our old Tv in the winter on a sunday rerun with my christmas socks still on as a 10 year old..

The last movie, pays respect to Star wars. It shows characters the way I remember them and it shows new things mixed with the old in a fun and hopefull way. Thats Star Wars for me..hope..and it is in this last movie! I can only commend J.J. and recommend this movie wholeheartedly. title: A Good Movie With Tons of Flaws

title: An enjoyable romp
review: Having been a Star Wars fan for over 4 decades I entered the cinema with high hopes and those hopes were not dashed. This is a great conclusion to a not very well planned trilogy. Lucasfilm seem to have had no plan going into this other than let's have 3 filmmakers make a film each. This does seem like a strange plan for a trilogy. Although there clearly was no story plan J.J. and Rian have delivered 3 highly enjoyable and entertaining movies culminating in TROS. This film first and foremost is a great piece of entertainment aimed at healing some of the divisions from TLJ, which I loved by the way. I have read many a review on here basically trashing the movie saying once again it has killed the franchise, but I can honestly say the franchise has never been healthier I for one will be waiting with baited breath to see where in this galaxy far far away we get to go next. title: Had it's problems, but still a great movie and a powerful ending to the saga. (no spoilers)
review:
This movie has been out for a week and I can already say it's extremely underrated. First let me explain the issues with this movie- 1 The plot in the first act was really rushed and could have fared much better with an extra maybe even 30 minutes. 2 The movie would have been much more cohesive had there been no change in directors for the last jedi, it could be focused on Abrams' POV rather than jumping ideas. 3 This should have been planned out from the start. Something I never understood with the sequels is that they made the plot as they went along. It would have made much more sense to have a preplanned idea where we could see certain characters grow and theorize in different ways.

That being said, I feel that this was the strongest movie of the sequels. Reasons? 1 Instead of copying old movies (Force Awakens) and wasting time and cool characters with random/boring side stories and character changes (the last jedi), this movie was focused on one main storyline and one main villain with other new characters showing up to help out. The entire movie was focused on Rey, Finn, Poe, Chewbacca, and C3PO's group, plus Ben Solo. This is what should have been done from the start instead of all these characters having out-of-the-blue storylines from previous movies. This movie also brought its own feel while still connecting to previous movies.

2 The fan service was good and greatly brought nostalgia. There are a lot of critics upset about the nostalgia this movie brought with it, but isn't that the whole point of Star Wars? Laser swords fighting, giant evil empires, a classic battle of good and evil, all mixed with imaginative stories and sci-fi greatness? That is what Star Wars is and is what Star Wars fans what, so why is the nostalgia so hated? This is the END of the Skywalker saga so bringing in all the past is essential to have a strong ending.

3 It did its best considering the disappointments that came with TFA and TLJ. They strongly used all of the sequel's original main characters in a perfect attempt to have a new story while also spending time to fix the mistakes made in the previous movies. The emotion is extremely strong, actors performances are amazing, showed a lot of potential new stories for Star Wars to follow.

4 Again, it fixed a lot of TLJ (which made people really angry?), I don't want to say what changed in risk of spoilers, but I'm happy that there was change. And a lot of people are against this, saying that Abrams' ruined the sequel that Rian Johnson helped bring to a high, but really, TLJ ruined TFA. Abrams' started and ended this trilogy and its only fair that he ends it with his vision.

5 Most characters got to play their own role in one way or another. So many reviewers state that Finn and Poe were extremely useless throughout the movie, but really, I feel as if each of the main characters did something important in various parts of the movie. Of course the main focus was Rey as she is the Jedi, but that doesn't mean the other characters didn't get enough time. The only character that was sidelined completely was Rose (the directors do explain why, but still). I never liked her character, thought she was boring, random, wanted Finn to be with Rey,etc. but the way she was sort of shooed out of most of he movie was a bit ehhhh to me. Sure, she really wouldn't bring that much to the story (and she really wouldn't have), but you could have at least somewhat included her.

6 We see that Rey is becoming stronger due to training and not "wow i can fight out of nowhere" (which a lot of people and me were upset about in TFA). A lot of questions and confusions are answered and resolved (again, no spoilers), and a lot is clear if you watched the Clone Wars and Rebels to see how certain characters are able to do certain things.

7 This is supposed to be the end of a whole saga AND a trilogy, after having a change of directors for the previous movie. That's a lot of work and a lot of pressure to be put for one movie, and a 2h20min time slot just makes that so much harder. I do feel that they could have done with maybe and extra 40-60 minutes but given the time they had, the writers did the best they could and tried to fit everything they could into the movie, and that is respectable. This did cause an extremely fast paced movie though.

8 Predictability. I've seen so many comments hating on how predictable the movie was, but I felt that was important. With the fast pace, it was pretty needed to have a predictable movie so that people aren't completely lost behind in the first act.

Overall rating. This movie was honestly great and did everything it could have done, but it suffered from the pacing. It still concluded the Skywalker saga in a way that was incredibly satisfying to me and tied in so much of what we have seen in Star Wars canon, even including little VOICE cameos (this is so small that it isn't even a spoiler) from Clone Wars and Rebels characters.

title: Upon 2nd viewing...up from 4 to 8
review:
My initial reaction was not good. I was upset by how the potentially great movie was ruined by bad execution and meaningless first half. The pacing made it impossible to feel anything or process anything before moving on to the next scene. So I felt really cheated of the emotional scenes that should of but didn't land.
But after seeing it again and taking the time to process it, I've come to appreciate it a lot more. Given the toxic fandom he had to work with, and studio up his back I think he did the best he could. We need to remember what it's like to see the originals. Go in with a sense of wonder and let the story unfold and let them tell us the story. Not go in intending to nit pick every detail. Allow yourself to enjoy the story that unfolds before you. That is why you remember the originals as so great. You allowed the story to be told. You allowed yourself to enjoy it.
That is why there is such a disparity in fandom. The younger generation love these movies because they are watching it the same way you watched the originals. Allowing them to tell us the story not vice versus.
I don't want to be part of the fandom that chooses to find the worse and complain about it and choose to hate it. When I let go of my own expectations and watched it from a new perspective then I really loved what JJ was able to do. The ben arc was better then anything I could up with and it was beautifully written. I have racked my brain since TFA on how in the world could they pull off a redemption that we would buy and I honestly couldn't think of anything myself. And this was beautiful. For those last moments alone gave me enough movie magic feels to make me now love this movie. Execution could of been better but they gave me the story. And It's the story that'll stand the rest of time not the techniqualities. So I changed my rating from 4 to an 8

title: Fairly good with unfortunate "Game of Thrones" ending.
review: First I like to point out that I am a fan of the Star Wars enterprise. The visual effects are of the scale with every new episode that came out the last couple of years. However that being said Its my opinion that the soul and heart of the whole franchise has last its touch. Call it nostalgia but nowadays its like a "Dada" thing for scriptwriters to end a seemingly good movie with a a-typical ending. I call this new phenomena " a game of thrones ending ". You read the books you follow the movies and in doing so you automatically feel which endings are going to do the storyline good. Did "The Rise of Skywalker" disappoint? Not entirely. It has all the ingredients it needs and even if it was rated 4 I would still go see it in the movie theater. So why didn't I like the ending? Well unless I missed the entire "Ménage à Trois" thing I do not understand why Kylo Ren is evaporating at the end just after the movie finally reveals that Rey has strong feelings for him. Where does the character of Finn suddenly fit into all of this? Obviously he is madly in love with Rey but that's about all that there is to it. No real interaction between him and Rey in that area. So finally its about Ben And Rey or the ying and yang of the Force. What greater ending for the Star Wars saga could it have been if the scriptwriters would have put in a little bit more "Romeo and Juliet" in that storyline and topped it off with a happy ending for a change meaning Ren and Rey lived happily ever after being parents of little Skywalker's and finn maybe being their godparent together with Jannah because those 2 seem to be getting off of real good at the end they would have been destined to fall in love had this been the previous and not the last star wars movie. I will rate this 7 despite some serious plot holes but it could have been so much better. Let this be a shout out to other movie makers. The world is a pretty "crappy" place already and at least in the movies for just a brief moment I like to think that their can also be a happy ending to life. After the movies credits I can always snap back to reality.

title: Best yet!
review: Ok, I remember being in awe of the very first Star Wars film when it first came out and I must say this is the best one since the original. It really had me on the edge of my seat the whole way through and I had a few tears at the end.

review:
I remember being disappointed by Episode 7 because i felt the exact story repeated. I remember being utterly mad of seeing Episode 8 and how much fake ratings went into it (rotten tomatoes: 91%) to pump up this disgrace of a star wars movie. I went into episode 9 with no expectations, just to put my mind at rest and avoid being spoilered everywhere.
I think for what has been left to work with after Episode 8, J.J. Abrams has done a good job. Not a great though but a good one. There are still major logical issues such as teleportation solid matter or reviving the dead (2 times!), among many others I don't want to spoiler. If you are a fan of raw force power than you may get satisfied though. I understand why Rose was ditched and I generally agree with the decision although a little more screen time would have been less humiliating. Compared to others who felt the movie to fast paced and jumping I actually followed along and managed to not get confused too much.
I still rate this movie with a 7 because overall it is a good movie. If there wouldn't be such great predecessors (and yes I count the prequels among them) than I am sure many fans wouldn't rate the movie that low.

title: It feels as if all the previous SW movies were a training run for this one.
review:
Episode IX was better than I thought it would be, and the best since the Original Trilogy. It really does attempt to be the promised big, satisfying wind-up to the whole series of 9 (11?) SW films. My pros and cons:

  • I'm guessing that "and I am all the Jedi" is going to join "and I am Iron Man" as a tagline that will live on for years to come.


  • Bravo to Daisy Ridley! Her character Rey was almost sidelined in The Last Jedi (boo) but, thank goodness, she's back center stage for this one. Ridley really committed to this role and brought a nuance and maturity to it that made it stand head and shoulders above the rest of the cast. Like Luke in the Original Trilogy, Rey develops continuously in character from the beginning of A Force Awakens to the end of Rise of Skywalker. Her acting goes well beyond what's necessary for a movie that is essentially a splashy spectacle.


  • The visual spectacle is extraordinary. I saw this on an IMAX screen and that's certainly the way to do it; all the incredible detail in the background pops out and gives the whole thing a level of texture that no previous SW film has had. When you add in the thunderous score, the 2.5-hour experience is a sensory assault that might leave you wired for hours afterwards. But isn't that why people come out to see it?


  • The obligatory "cute droid" scenes were there, but thank goodness they were minimal. There's only so much I can take of R2D2 vibrating and beeping.


  • Many scenes act as callbacks to the Original Trilogy (Episodes IV-VI) or replays of the same events with new players. This could be thought of as lazy storytelling if it's done badly or mechanically, but by and large I thought these were effectively done. It made the frenetic planet-jumping travelog structure of the plot a little easier to deal with.


  • Once in a while, the dialog actually rises to the level of normal adult conversation. (This is NOT meant as a compliment.) Most of it is very, very predictable. With all the money spent on making this film, why can't they afford scriptwriters who can actually do something complex, witty, engaging? The kids in the audience would enjoy it just as much and the adults would get a lot more.


  • Like the previous films, a lot of first-rate actors in the cast are colossally underused: Richard E. Grant, Lupita Nyong'o, Dohmnall Gleeson, are little more than cameos. Even Adam Driver himself. who plays Kylo Ren, didn't use anything like the full range of what he can do.


  • And just like the previous outings, certain scenes just tip over into being ludicrous. Cavalry riding over top of a spaceship --- guys, really? (How do you even get all those horses there?) and bows and arrows against a Star Destroyer?


But the bottom line is that you get your money's worth. There's loads to occupy your eye, the plot makes enough sense to carry things along, and the ending is pretty much just what it should be.

title: True fans will love it for what it is.......
review:
So I'll just lay out something first. There are three types of SW fans: 1. The casual fan who seen the movies. 2. The hardcore fan who seen the movies, maybe played some games..etc. 3. The super nerds who seen the movies a bazillion times, read the all books, played all the games....basically obsess over it. They can tell exactly how to build a lightsaber and likely tell you how many hairs were on Yoda's body.

Group 3 SHOULD be the ones appreciating this movie but instead 1 and 2 seem to be loving it more. I am part of group 3 and am disappointed by my group.

The movie was amazing in my mind. Were there things that contradict some past SW things? Yes. Were there things that left you asking "But how...?", yes. Is this movie perfect? No. No movie is. But I accept it for what is and always was supposed to be. A series of movies for all types of people that was meant to be enjoyed.

I also remember JJ (who did Force Awakens) had to recover the story since Rian (Last Jedi) really went crazy with the story and messed up JJ's plans. So it does sort of leave this movie in a frenzied state. Often times rushing things to fill in some plot holes due to Rise of the Jedi messing up alot.

And if you talk to me in person I can tell you ALOT of problems with the movie in terms of lure and storyline. But I put that aside and accept this is now how it ends. Can't change it and no complaining will change anything. I gave it a 9 despite all of this because I thought it still wrapped up things well.

I'd lastly point out that this movie would be more near a 9 out of 10 (for overall IMDB score) if not for the "group 3" people who just gave it on a 1. This is why I ignore any review that gives a movie a 1 or a 10. No such movie that can be a movie that is either score.

No matter what group you belong to when it comes to the series, go see this. Put aside the nerdier side of you and just accept it the movie as it is. It will make enjoying it much easier.

title: Storytelling at its best!
review: Star Wars fans are toxic. There is no pleasing them no matter how great the movie is. I was on the edge of my seat during this whole film. There was not a dull moment. J.J. Abrams is a master of cinematic arts. The Star Wars saga is supposed to mirror itself and this is exactly what it did with for return of the Jedi. Also bringing palpatine back was genius because in the prequels he talks of the Sith Lord that had discovered how to come back from the dead. The story came full circle, and was a great conclusion to the saga. I laughed, sweated, and even teared up a few times throughout the film. Star Wars has been a part of my life since i was a child and getting to see the stories continue has been a great pleasure. All of the films have amazing and awesome aspects while they all have things that might be questionable as well, but to think that George Lucas came up with all of these characters and worlds so long ago, and that the legacy has continued this long is amazing to me. J.J. Abrams grew up with these movies, and if I'm not mistaken are a major reason he got into film making. To say he didn't do it justice is ridiculous. We live in a time where everyone can be a critic, so i say watch the movie, and decide for yourself. I feel it deserves a much better rating than it has, but that's my opinion. I will rewatch this along with the other Star Wars films for years to come. The formula for fanboys is Empire strikes Back, and have issues with all the other films. Ewoks were dumb in return. Prequels had too much cgi, medaclorines, and jar jar, so they all suck, force awakens was the same as a new hope, last Jedi threw away all the important questions, Luke drank milk from a sea cow, and was bad. Kylo ren is emo........ i dare anyone else to do better than the new trilogy. I'm sure everyone would criticize them just as harshly.

Luke was strange in the role too; just didn't seem like Luke. Didn't like Leia in the last 3 though either. She's a good character and there were some touching, heart-warming parts as well.

title: A Decent Ending That is Getting Way Too Much Crap
review: I honestly don't understand why there are so many ridiculously negative reviews about this movie. No, I don't think it was as good as the original trilogy, but it certainly was nowhere near as bad as "The Last Jedi" or any of the prequels. title: Not the worst action movie, best of the new trilogy - yet still only avarage
review:
The Force is not strong - even in this one - but it is the best of the new trilogy. Funny though, this being the best makes the 2 before even worse. I am not writing here about breaking Star Wars lore. If you are a fan of lore, you may take away a star or two from the rating I gave. I have a feeling that the makers of the films just dont care bat-crap whether the movies actually follow rules set by the other SW films. Its as if they want to give sad reacts to fans. Or they just dont care. I cannot know. Its just dumb.

Compared to previous titles, Rise of Skyw. has some storyline. However, the new old villain popping out of the blue (or sith dark?) is really cheap trick to fill the fact that Last jedi and FA had no proper storyline whatsoever. Just running around and things happening wearing plot armour does not account as a story. A good story has characters - villains, heroes and in-betweens - developing and interacting each other. Thats what is the interesting stuff. Not explosions and pew-pews but the reasons "why this and that happens", and "what significance it has" and "is the psychology behind characters believable".

The new trilogy had only one character who had any sort of emotionally and otherwise satisfactory character development. Kylo Ren, that is. His character development carries the trilogy and managed to be even touching in this movie.

Im not saying other characters are trash, but they are shallow enough to resemble something picked up from a tourist beach trash can. All the other characters have no character whatsoever, though i did like Finn throughout the movies. The Hackerman who was introduced in Last Jedi does not appear in this one, which is a huge disappointment. With the few minutes of screen time he had in Last Jedi, he showed more character than Poe, Finn and Rey combined.

Questions that made me wonder: A) in the beginning of the movie it is told that Empire Strikes back in 16 hours. This never happened. Why? Why make star destroyers wait in strategically crap position? Why not move them few kilometers up so their shields would work, or have them hidden somewhere nearby? B) if Force ghosts can do whatever they please now, why Anakin Skywalker - the most loved jedi/Sith by Kylo - never pops up to tell Kylo that being evil is not worth it? Or Luke? He was Kylos mentor. Why would he not torment Kylo as force ghost? I mean, Luke practically promised to haunt Kylo in the Last Jedi but in the end did not. C) the knights of Ren are showed menacingly pose throughout the movie, yet they do nothing. Bummer. D) the first part of the movie is chasing a macguffin to get another macguffing, yet the macguffin is found miracuously rolling on the spaceship floor. Do you know what fetch quests are considered in story telling, in video games, literature and so on? Crap. Thats what they are.

title: Fine as a Stand Alone, Just Ok in the Trilogy
review:
Star Wars: Episode IX- The Rise of Skywalker Review:

Returning director J. J. Abrams cowrites and directs this finale to the Skywalker saga. Here, Palpatine mysteriously returns and the Resistance faces the First Order once more to bring peace to the galaxy. I'm a Star Wars fan. Any Star Wars fan was excited to see this finale. The original trilogy (4-6) is just amazing and nothing beats it. The prequels (1-3) are ok but not great. The only one I actually like is Revenge of the Sith. Now they decided to do the sequel trilogy (7-9), I just have to say I hate that they call it that but that's what it is I guess, and I like it. The Force Awakens was pretty good and showed a promising trilogy. Now this will anger many people: I think The Last Jedi is one of the best films in the whole saga and I wish Rian Johnson would have directed the whole sequel trilogy. Despite people saying how I shouldn't like The Last Jedi and it's not right, I thought it was just great. Now here's the thing: J. J. Abrams had The Force Awakens be setup for the trilogy. He started it off and handed it over to Rian Johnson. There's a great analogy that I watched for this and I'm going to use it. At the end of The Force Awakens, Rey holding out the lightsaber for Luke to take is Abrams handing over the trilogy to Johnson. Then in The Last Jedi Luke throws the lightsaber and that's Johnson basically saying "I don't really like this setup so I'm going to change it up." People really didn't like that and just trashed the film. The problem now with The Last Jedi is it's a different setup so we have two films with two setups. Abrams came back for the finale and has to find a way to complete a trilogy with two different setups. Since Snoke is dead Abrams had to find a different threat so he decides Palpatine. This is my biggest issue with the movie. I personally didn't like the addition of Palpatine. It felt forced and there wasn't much exposition for the whole thing. The first three paragraphs we read at the beginning were just so confusing at the beginning and we're just supposed to except it all. The writing was just jumbled to me. There wasn't a whole definitive for the whole trilogy which didn't help. The prequels had a plan. The originals didn't have a plan at first, but then George Lucas mapped out the whole thing after he saw the success from the first. This trilogy was a free for all. My problem is that they needed consistency with the writing and direction throughout all of this. The first hour is all trying to setup all of this and I thought it was slow. The very beginning had a cool sequence and then it just slowed down. After the hour I think it found it's footing and took off. The action scenes were all fantastic. There's a specific one where it's Rey and Kylo on this wreck surrounded by water. The whole battle there had to be my favorite part of the movie. Most of that is due to the marvelous visual effects and the acting. The acting has never been just good in the sequel trilogy, it's always great. Daisy Ridley is such a fantastic actress and there isn't a better actress that could play Rey. Personally, Rey isn't my favorite character but I do like the conflicts with her and how much of a badass she is. Now Kylo is the best. I hated him in The Force Awakens. We used to call him "a pussy in a mask". Then during The Last Jedi he got a shit ton of development and I loved him. He's the highlight of The Rise of Skywalker. I praised Adam Driver in my review for Marriage Story so you can read more about that in there. He's also the perfect Kylo and couldn't get anyone better. There's even more of a turning point with him in this and I proved to be probably my favorite character in the whole saga. It's been decided just now that he's my favorite character. The Rise of Skywalker is mostly good with characters. There's an addition of characters that didn't really effect the plot that much. They may have done little things but nothing super major. As we all know Carrie Fisher has been dead for a while. They decided to recycle some footage and add Leia to this which was cool, but I don't think she should've been in this much. It's not their fault but everything she said was an inspirational quote and didn't flow well. Personally I think they should've just said she died or just have a funeral for her at the beginning. They tried what they could, however it didn't flow well. Without spoiling the movie this is all I can say really. I have a lot more things to say but if you'd like to know more of my opinions, come and talk to me. As a stand alone movie it's good. In the context of the trilogy it's a disappointment. I totally understand if you really liked it or really didn't. I think this is fine. I wasn't a fan of how the finale went. My mother even said "As a fan of Star Wars for 42 years, I was let down." There's many mixed feelings on this movie, just about as much as The Last Jedi. So don't get mad at me for having opinion. There's no correct opinion. I just thought this was fine. It took me two watches and six days of thinking to actually write this. If you're going to comment stuff trying to claim it's the best or worst I will probably not comment back. Really it's just all opinions.

My Grade: B-

My Ranking of Star Wars (Best to Worst)

1. Empire Strikes Back 2. A New Hope 3. The Last Jedi 4. Return of the Jedi (Rogue One) 5. The Force Awakens 6. The Rise of Skywalker 7. Revenge of the Sith (Solo) 8. The Phantom Menace 9. Attack of the Clones

title: Great final
review:
I grew up with Star Wars (Ep IV - VI) and watched the originals and the prequels literally more than a hundred times.
Of course I loved the originals and most parts of the prequels (despite Jar Jar Binks, some cheesy dialogues in Ep. II).
I had mixed expectations about Ep VII ( I personally think it was quite an impossible project to - one the one hand - satisfy the die hard fans and - on the other other hand - attract the (younger and new) audience at the same time.
But in the end the result was quite ok despite the recycling of the story line of Ep. IV...
Ep. VIII was quite disappointing. I watched it twice in the theatres. The story was not good at all and I was wondering why Rey thought she needed training at all since you got the impression that she is already a fully-trained Jedi.
Well, I watched Ep. IX today the second time within one week.
After watching it the first time I honestly wasn't sure how to rate it.
But today I can honestly say it is worth 8/10 in my opinion.
Of course it's for sure not the perfect Star Wars movie at all. I had very low expectations after Ep. VIII. Actually I wasn't even looking forward to watching it. I just wanted to see the result of Disney's approach to put and end of one of the greatest movie sagas in history.
Personally I think it delivers a fast paced story. Ok, Palpatine's revival wasn't convincing at all in the trailers. But the first 5 minutes into the movie I felt like - wow, ok let's see where this going to...
I still think that Adam Driver wasn't the perfect joice for the (young) villain. He seemed more to be a spoiled boy who desperately needed more guidance when it comes to his education.
But the way he finally turned back to the light side - I really pitied him in a certain way - and the part with him talking to his dad - it somehow reminded me of Clark Kent talking to his late father.
I loved the way they brought all the (old) characters back for this grande finale (visually and aurally).
I honestly had no clue that Rey was a Palpatine. The final scene between Ben and her was - well at first I hoped it wouldn't end like Romeo and Juliet - authentic. It would have been more awkward when Ben would have survived but in the end he proved he is a true Skywalker (Solo) by giving up his own life in order to rescue the one he had feelings for.
And Rey: I liked the way she finally became a Skywalker. She never asked for it. She never knew who she really was until she encountered the force...
The Star Wars saga for me is like family: You grew up with it, you love it, you got disappointed by it and you thought that life goes on without it but in the end you realize that it is part of your life and you are just happy to experience all the not so good times and better times with it.

title: Not Perfect, But A Surprise that Solved (some of) The Last Jedi's Problems
review:
Walking into the theater to watch this film felt more like a chore than anything. The first 2 films in the new trilogy were incredible disappointments for me, especially The Last Jedi, so sitting down in my seat hurt inside. After all these years, I was positive that this film would only poor salt into the wound and would deal the final blow that would kill Star Wars as a franchise.
I can't believe I'm saying this... but I was wrong. This movie brought the franchise back. It actually felt like I was watching a Star Wars film.
They finally brought back what Star Wars was originally about: the importance of teamwork and family, good's rise over evil, and how your bloodline doesn't dictate your destiny. This film was filled to the brim in order to wrap up the story, and by the end it felt complete. It felt good. I was bawling, not out of anger, but out of satisfaction. They finally did it right and made it come full circle.
Of course this film didn't come without flaws. From the beginning of the new trilogy, there were problems sewn into the story. They downgraded the power of the lightsaber, made Rey a sort of a Mary Sue, changed the power of the Force, and ruined Luke as a character. The new trilogy's problems had to inevitably bleed into this movie too. The pacing is atrocious and super fast paced. The editing was quick and needed constant attention from the audience in order to follow the story. In the end, I think this is forgivable. The Last Jedi was- in my opinion- terrible, with almost no use to the trilogy. The time it wasted had to be made up for, so TROS had to be stuffed to finish the story.
I also think that this film solved some of the problems in the Last Jedi. Questions were answered, and some things were redeemed and fixed. It is such a relief. JJ built the foundation with TFA, Rian knocked it down with TLJ, and JJ picked up the pieces and filled in the blanks with TROS.
There were some odd moments and some weird dialogue. But we shouldn't act like the people whi make Star Wars films must be gods. Even the original trilogy had script issues.
So... to those who are overwhelmed with the negativity surrounding this film: don't listen to it. Go in blind, without expectations. Have an open mind and interpret it how you want to.
It might seem impossible, but you just might like this one. It happened to me, and I'm happy. Trust me, as someone that avoids The Last Jedi like the plague I am surprised I liked The Rise of Skywalker. I hope that despite the hate, you like it too.

title: Needs a second viewing to be appreciated
review: This movie had a phenomenal task. It had to conclude a story 42 years in the making. We can watch it and criticize it by pointing out the plot holes (of which there are many) or the "insufficiently powerful" story and so on, or we can just sit back, enjoy it, and appreciate the enormous effort and attention to detail that was poured into telling a story about family, friends and choices that we all make in life, regardless of us being on this planet or in a galaxy far, far away. Seeing it for the first time is much like a first date that you've been looking forward to for far too long: there is tension, expectations are high, not everything goes as smoothly as you've hoped and you can even get a bit disappointed. But then...you decide to go on a second date only to discover that you want to be with that person more and more. The acting is solid, Daisy Ridley knocks it out of the park, the entire dynamic between Rey and Kylo/Ben is one of the movie's strongest points, without question. The whole Palpatine thing was the weakest aspect of the movie, but hearing the great Ian McDiarmid was enjoyable nonetheless, he can play the phonebook if he wanted to. Yes, it's a roller coaster ride, a lot of characters, not enough time to establish things, but somehow it all comes together. Best of all, a lot of heart was poured in this movie, so it deserves at least "a second date".

title: Well, it's Star Wars...and not the worst of the bunch!
review:
If you're a Star Wars fan like me, and have seen all of the movies, you probably have your favorite installment. Many love Empire Strikes Back, many detest Phantom Menace. Well, this movie, for me, falls somewhere in between. At the very least it didn't knock A New Hope, Empire Strikes back and The Force Awakens as my top 3 Star Wars films off the list. My apologies to those who have said this is the best of ALL the Star Wars films, in my opinion it wasn't. I even struggled with giving this film a 6 or an 8, so I settled on a 7 (which is probably too generous).

The good news is J.J. Abrams corrected what many didn't like about The Last Jedi, much like George Lucas course corrected in his follow up to The Phantom Menace. That said, Abrams introduced a few faults at the same time. Specifically, Abrams experimented a bit with the story line, and with things that we already know about (like the force) in a way that doesn't quite add up when seeing this together with the other films. It was a risky move, but one that I think was worth taking.

Now for the bad news. Critics have suggested this film tries to hard to please everyone. Fan Service seems to be a term that keeps popping up with this film. Perhaps. But for me the bad news is that while the first and last 30-or-so minutes of the film was cinematically spectacular, I found myself bored through much of the body of the film. I think that could be because this Disney installment used a lot of the same devices we are used to seeing like an old crutch...or Yoda's walking stick. Or, It could be because I was too distracted by the way Carrie Fisher's old footage of Princess Leia interacted with the characters to focus on the story line so that I could follow along. Or, more likely, the story was just plain weak and ill-conceived. Whatever it was that bored me, being a die-hard fan, I stuck with it for the big pay-off at the movie's climax. And, Rise of Skywalker certainly delivered in the end.

So here's the bottom line. To enjoy this film, you need to:
  • be a die-hard Star Wars fan to stick it, thick and thin.
  • check all the logic at the door
  • be open to a new story line, even if it doesn't quite fit with what we've seen before


If this sounds like something you can do, then you just might rise up and have a good time by the time you leave the theatre, like I did.

title: New thinking, but still true to the old stories.
review:
I've seen a lot of bad comments about this movie, and... I just don't get them.

People complain about things not being true to Star Wars when a LOT of things in this movies were obvious nudges, hints, and even direct links to Legends (formerly known as Expanded Universe, which I will write as EU from now on in this review).

Yes, Palpatine is back. Ooooh so weird, such a stuoid Disney movie, that came from no where, so desperate... But is it really? No.. In the old books of EU, that is exactly what happened. Palpatine foresaw Vader's betrayal and started working on clones and an old sith technique from way before the old republic era called Transfer Essence where your soul upon death is transferred into a target body. Your old body is destroyed, and if the mind of the new body is stronger than so is your soul, in which case it's sent to Chaos... Therefor those using this alternative path of immortality used clone bodies, because it was a blank slate to plant their essence/soul into. In the EU Darth Sidious was one of the practitioners of this technique. The emperor who died at the Death Star was one of those clones, and his first official death. His second death was by his own hands after conjuring an enormous force storm, which is an alternative much stronger variant of force lighting, which exists in two forms. A much bigger and stronger one that Sidious mastered, where you raise your hands up in the air and the lighing embraces a WIDE LARGE area hitting MANY... just like in the movie. The other version is even stronger, and more or a rare occasion, and has the potential of causing wormholes and decimating entire planets. In the Dark Empire books from 1991-1992 this happened, and he lost control upon which the storm engulfed his ship and destroyed him. All in all Sidious died 4 times before he was ultimately destroyed for last. So having him return with clone bodies in the movies... not weird at all. it's a DIRECT nudge to the old books.

Now, in addition to that there were a lot of hints to the old EU, and probably a lot that even I didn't catch. Abrams does read up a lot on the EU. Rian however, not so much. Rian messed up big time with the Last Jedi... I am not a fan of that movie, and Abrams was given that train wreck to try to save, and he did as best as he could by trying to recover the plotlines that Rian discarded in the former movie. Also, Abrams was given a very short time to make the movie, so that's sad, and I'm sure it would have been better if he was allowed more time. That IS a problem, and does explain the rushed scenes now and then. But I still think Abrams did a great job with what he was handed.

Having Rey cast away her birth surname (Palpatine) and taking a new one (Skywalker) was also a great take to show that if your blood family is truly bad, you can cast that away and stick to your chosen family. I mean, it's the future, and we can change names and surnames in real life as well.

I also love all the cameos, Wedge for instance, but many many others. And... something that made me real happy. You know that ceremony in A New Hope where Luke and Han gets medals, but Chewbacca did not get one for some unknown reason. Yeah.. that is the medal Chewie got after Leia died. Check the pictures, it's that one. I think that was a nice way of rectifying old mistakes.

And yes, the movie is not perfect, it does have flaws. But so foes every movie ever. Where are the wartorn, sad and mourning and wounded people in the ending party scene? However, that was the case in episode 6 as well. Problem? Yes, but not just this movie, also the old movies.

And to the people saying that this movie is not Star Wars because it just crams a lot of new stuff in it.... well... episode 5 and 6 did a LOT of new stuff as well.. and episode 4 was also very new in general and they thought it would flop at first. Star Wars IS about new mystical space stuff. Both new and old, and this movie added a lot of old stuff from the old EU, but also added new stuff, and some thing might even be new but inspired from the EU.

I personally think (not confirmed by authors but just my guess) that the complicated navigation to Exagol, and the super weapon producing Exagol,,, well...... the Maw Installation was a research station that worked on super weapons, and was located in the Maw Cluster which was an extremely difficult cluster of black holes to navigate through. I do see a very clear hint there that it might very well have been inspired by it. At least that's my guess. They also made the Sun Crusher... so... if you think it's unreasonable that they made tons of planet killing star destroyers at Exagol...... Well... the Sun Crusher was a superweapon that literally made suns go super nova, obliterating entire solar systems... So yeah.

I did want to see more about Jennah and the other ex-stormtroopers, Zorii, and other stuff. I also wanted Finn to dig more into the "I was redeemed, and so were they, so what if we try to talk more troopers out of it"... i did want more of that. I also think the kiss was slighty out of tune with the movie in the end. but at the same time, it does kinda embrace the whole "we're kinda toxic for eachothers but we still do this" which does actually happen in real life very often, so it worked, even if I would prefer it without the kiss. I did like that they downplayed the very forced romances from Last Jedi, like Finn and Rose, with just the shoulder pat, that was good, because the Last Jedi romance was.... very shoehorned and came from nowhere with no build up (Rian!!!).

There are some more problems, but also a lot more positives, and I'm already writing a convoluted novella here, but yes... the movie had a few problem, but it did as best as it could to save the trilogy from the trainwreck that Rian did with 8th, and I am VERY happy about the movie, and loved that they added so much from the EU and actually did their research.

title: A Good Movie with Some Bad Executions
review:
As a start I would like to say that I'm a fan of The Last Jedi and I think it's one of the best Star Wars movies. However, I anticipated that The Rise of Skywalker would retcon the ideas and themes of its predecessor in order to appeal to the fans who, to say the least, have problems with it, and that disturbs me a little bit. I wrote what I liked the most about that movie and then some other thoughts I have.

Ben Solo - Oh My God, I LOVE this character so much! His arc in this trilogy is absolutely amazing. In the beginning of the film we find him protecting the one thing he has left: power, but his heart is full with guilt and doubt. I was so hoping for his redemption in this movie, and oh boy it delivered it. I took Liea's sacrifice and Rey's healing to make Ben realize that there's is still good in the galaxy, that there is still good in HIM. But only when he has his conversation with his memory of Han, he finally ACCEPTS the good in him. When the threw his lightsaber to the ocean, I screamed with joy. His sacrifice to save Rey and the disappearance of his body felt so earned, truly the ultimate closure in my opinion. Great story of a great character.

My ONLY problem with it, however, is the execution. There is not enough time with him after Ben's return to the Light. We only see him killing the Knights of Ren, getting thrown into a pit and saving Rey's life. I wish we have more time to see him. Ah, and also, why Ben and Rey had to kiss? It didn't fit to their story at all.

I also enjoyed the plot a lot, I thought the returning of Palpatin was cool, I only wish they would have setting it earlier so it wouldn't feel like out of place. The action was very nice, I liked the long takes they made, the characters were even more interesting and seeing them all together was very enjoyable. The expansion of the Force Teleportation was brilliant, Rey and Ben relationship was, as in The Last Jedi, a powerful aspect. Overall I liked most of the things in that movie and I returned home from the theater satisfied.

However, there were some things that bothered me. As I said, I loved The Last Jedi, I loved that Rey was a nobody and I didn't care who Snoke was. So by telling us that Rey was the Emperor's granddaughter and Snoke was some kind of a clone or whatever, makes The Last Jedi, overall, unimportant. The Snoke reveal didn't effect the story so I could live with that, but making Rey's a Palpatin just disappointed me. The great thing about her was she was a nobody, a proof that you could become great even though we came from noting, as a contrast to Ben who came from greatness and became evil. The right to choose your identity theme is nice but it's not like we haven't seen it before, so that just sad.

In conclusion, as a long time fan of Star Wars, a series that has a special place in my heart, I enjoyed the film. It has a satisfying end and I can't wait to watch it again. Sure it has problems, but that's what makes Star Wars so great. Like our loved ones, we have issues with them when they disappoint us, but that's because we see them as inspiration. That is Star Wars for me.

title: Not too great but not too bad. The Ending saved it
review:
I'm someone who has been very critical of Disney Star Wars. Force Awakens was decent but The Last Jedi was trash. But what was truly bad was not the film, but how Rian Johnson, Kennedy and Disney handled the criticism. Honestly, I had no interest in this film, in the new trilogy or in Disney Star Wars. I wasn't even planning to see it, but eventually went anyway JUST to see how badly they made it up.I had zero expectations.

Where to begin? Let's go over the bad parts, then the good parts (because the film ultimately left me on a high note)

The film is messy. Unlike the Last Jedi, which divided fans, Rise of Skywalker has much more fundamental problems. It will be very obvious even to someone who doesn't watch many films or isn't a Star Wars fan that the film is messy. The first half is very, very bad. It's rushed, and barely gives you time to react as it jumps from place to place. I cannot help but feel that everything in the first half was originally supposed to be in The Last Jedi, and JJ Abrams is desperately trying to cover ground. There's a lot of settings and themes that were obviously meant to be explored in more depth, but couldn't be. But still, some of these parts could have been cut, or the films could have been 3 hours long. The way it turned out is just sad.

Secondly, the performances from Adam Driver and Daisy Ridley are bad. When you put them up against legendary actors like Ian McDiarmud and talented people like John Boyega, it's a stark contrast. It's a shame that these two are the protagonists, and the plot hinges on their emotional growth. We STILL never get to see any growth or development in them.

Although people accuse this film of pandering to audiences, it leaves a LOT to be desired. A lot of potential was wasted due to bad storytelling. (No Spoiler) For example, the Sith and their history plays a big role in this film. However, NONE of that is explored. There's an area in the film where we see what I can only assume are statues of all the Sith Lords that came before Palpatine. Wouldn't it have been kind of cool to show their faces? Or drop some references for the fans? But nope, we neither see or hear anything about anything. Or perhaps the Knights of Ren? They're there for like 5 scenes, but set up as these big and important figures. And then waht? Nothing. They just die, and there isn't even a dialogue of narrative about who or what they are. Why even include them in the film? The Sith Troopers, or Poe's former girl friend. It's like they're props, but key plot points rely on them. Not everyone is following the Disney comics or reading the film novelizations. Rey is STILL a Mary Sue, and any attempts at giving her pretentious obstacles fail miserably. All in all, watching this film felt like a bunch of different people made it with no unified vision.

I could go on and on, so let me cut it short and move to the good parts.

Except the protagonists, many of the actors do a very good job. Ian McDiarmus practically melts into the character of Palpatinem, and he's one of the best parts of the film. The film is very visually accomplished. The special effects are stunning, and the design for characters, costumes, props and locations is extremely detailed and well done. Props to every designer and artist who worked on this film.

JJ Abrams does go out of his way to address many of the criticisms of The Last Jedi. There's some comedy in this, and I think it works some times.

There's a lot of very deep and meaningful themes and concepts that I like, especially regarding the political struggle of the Resistance, Unity, Propaganda and the importance of standing together. The second half is better paced and actually interesting. The ending, which I should point out was written by George Lucas (after 4 failed attempts by Disney), is phenomenal. It's everything Star Wars should be, as Lucas brings the circle to a close and firmly establishes this as the ending of the saga started 40 years ago.

I also like the fact that, thanks to some new lore books about this film, characters like Darth Andeddu, Revan and a few other Sith are now cannon. Finally, they are tying Legends to new Canon. Many aspects of this film are reminiscent of the Dark Empire comics.

Finally, and this is what I like the most, this film is sure to have an impact on kids. In order to be a Star Wars fan, you need to be exposed to it at a very young age. Revenge of the Sith, despite all it's problems, did that for me when I was 6. This second half, particularly the climax and ending, is spectacular enough that it will stay with young children, who will grow up to be the next generation of Star Wars fans. Let's just hope that when THEY grow up, Disney doesn't spit in their face and spend two years screeching about how Star Wars doesn't belong to them. Star Wars is for EVERYONE. It's for ALL 3 generations of fans, and just because they're meant to impact kids doesn't mean you can alienate fans who came before. Let's hope they remember that 10 years later when they make Ep X, XI and XII.

title: One word: Disjointed.....
review:
Here's a more honest review, since most people are so hell-bent on exaggerating their point and rating this either a 1 or a 10 which is wrong on both counts. First of all, i think these new movies with 'Rey' are horrible when compared to the original saga. Not because i'm a die-hard fan or because i think the canon story-line should be preserved; rather it's because the core template or formula that made the first few movies successful does not apply to the recent movies; These movies have no coherent plot and the audience is not fully invested in the characters.

I do think this movie is marginally better than the previous two, but that's not saying much. Some small scenes do work well, and the small occasional fragments of coherent plot are quite good, but the buck stops there. In terms of the negative aspects of the movie; It's hard to make sense of the storyline, it's incredinly disjointed. One commentor summarized it perfectly by saying it feels like a 2 hour trailer. I can almost imagine the writer's room throwing a bunch of ideas into a basket and just collecting as many of them as possible and forcing them into the movie. It has way too much fan-service. Its clear they tried so hard to appease fans that they gave them whatever they thought they wanted, but it fails spectacularly.

In short, is it terrible? No. Is it a good Star Wars movie? Not by a long shot, and anyone who says otherwise is easily amused by special effects regardless of plot line
