title: A 'good' star wars film
review:
I usually don't write reviews for movies because i never feel over passionate about a film to do so, however after seeing the flack this film is getting alongside its positive impact on its fans i couldnt help but air my opinions regardless.

This film had a lot to make up for when recovering from 'the last jedi' and many like me, didnt think it could possibly do so after Rian Johnson's massive blunder of a film. However, even though Rise of skywalker is not perfect, it manages to do so in a way which pleases the audience to the best possible extent without alienating them by over compensating. This film in many ways can be seen as a safe way to end the skywalker saga (like many have stated) But, it fufilled its purpose which is whats important.

My analogy for star wars usually comes down to two things, storyline and action/choreography I.e if the storyline is coherent but not overfilled with subliminal messages and conotations and the action is engaging, believable and has enough sci fi elemnts to fill the audience with wonder the film will be good. These two elemts are ultimatly whats important to the fans, obviously cinematograpghy, sound design , editing and mise en scene is important in terms of technicallity but when making an impression on the audience to get a postive response these two aspects are paramount. Futhermore only one of them have to be good for the film to be good, the original trilogy had very good storyline and sub par choreograpghy, wilst the pequals was the opposite. If a star wars film does both of these well it will make the film increasingly better; if the director choses to pay attention to the small details which fans are (understandably) known to nit pick on, then the star wars film has the patential to even be perfect. Overall, star wars is heavily reliant on the fans for sucess, if you alienate them such as the last jedi did then your film will fail, so whats important is to have a fun action packed film with a stroyline which suits the canon yet is cohenrent enough to make sense to everyone.

The rise of skywalker has one clear goal in mind, to make a good star wars film that safely concludes the saga in a way that everyone will be happy with. Of course if it had enough time and effort, it could have small little edits and story choices to be perfect but overall both the stroyline and choreorgrapghy was to a standard which made the film a 'good star wars film' not amazing, not perfect but good . As i watched the film i did find many glaring plot holes and little issues which bugged me, and im sure hardcore fans could find several issues which doesnt fit with some sought of canon. And yes there are some moments where we want answers to events or that just seem plain lazy. But truth be told anyone who watches this film coud do so and could do so for hours, but thats not important. This film knew what it had to do, JJ abrams knew what he had to do and they did it. A star wars fim which was fun, had choreograpghy which was fun to watch and story which made everyone feel a number of feelings and made sense and, thank , did not have little to any mad. This film was good, 7/10 maybe a push but im happy with this ending, and just because its not perfect doesnt mean its bad, just enjoy it for what it is and be done with it is the attitude i Have with this film. I may be critiscised for this review one way or another, and im open to it as long as its constructive, but its just a film dude, not that deep XD

Cinematography: 9.5/10 Let's get real here. This movie is filmed by one of the best in the business. It's not any more over the top than RoTJ. I challenge anyone else to portray on screen the events that were occurring in a more entertaining method. Haters hate people who at the top for nonsensical reasons.

Sound: 10/10 This will be a benchmark in my home theater going forward.

Story: 8.5/10 This story made up for all the confusion in the first two movies. This may be partially do to JJs style of story telling. But he did not leave us hanging with this finally. All questions were answered and many doors were closed appropriately.

The only thing I didn't like was how corny Luke was. Just as corny as he was in the last film which turned me off greatly.

Overall: 9/10 There is so much Star Wars in our family life and this experience only made it better. Join the light side of the force... ignore the haters... appreciate the effort and service that went into this film. It's a feel good movie that any true Star Wars fan should enjoy.

And by the way... my entire theater clapped at the end. People appeared very pleased when leaving. Every stranger around me seemed pleased.

title: Don't understand all the hate
review: Star Wars represents different things to different people. It's the brands strength, and glaring weakness. Critics and a lot of fans seem to be maligning this movie, because it didn't line up with their personal expectations. The ability in our time to get exactly what you want, when you want it, is IMHO making everyone into a higher critic these days. The bottom line is no one is happy with a plain cup of coffee anymore, they want a "triple grande decaf two pump soy latte with no whip" " oh I didnt get my third pump" "I think this is almond milk" " this movie wasn't new enough" "Rey is too perfect" blah blah blah. New is not always good (see Episodes I and II) being content with things IS always good. Star Wars- A New Hope was not new. It borrowed from countless things, and put them in a new package. Despite what people say, TLJ was not that groundbreaking, or new either. If you want new, watch a new movie franchise. If we don't hold that movie to a standard of what's new, why do we have to hold this one to it. That being said, THERE IS A LOT OF NEW IN THIS MOVIE. I have consumed a lot of Star Wars, (books, movies, tv shows, games) There is a lot of new, a lot of old, a lot of good, and a lot of bad. What some people like, others seem to hate. I go in with low expectations, (It will probably be closer to Episode I than KOTOR) and see how I feel at the end of the movie. I left "The Last Jedi" feeling flat, and disappointed. Because I did not give into visceral hate for it, I have come to appreciate it more. This one made me feel a lot of things. If Episode IV and V are the standards to judge all Star Wars against, which I think personally is the case, this one holds up to me. It was fun, the humor was right, which is something the last one got wrong to me. The stakes were high, the emotions were raw, I left feeling great. See it for yourself, and it may line up with what you want, but don't expect perfection, and be open. And please, don't hate someone because they enjoy their coffee a certain way.

Leia just dies, in a hurry.., for no important reason.

title: A solid B
review:
There were a few things to criticize about The Last Jedi, the main 1 being making Luke bitter and killing him off. So first Han, now Luke? Prop up the stars of the new trilogy by killing the stars of the first one? Really?

Oh, and if these are spoilers for anyone, here is another 1: Darth Vader is Anakin Skywalker, Luke's father. Seriously? The Last Jedi came out 2 years ago. Catch up.

Still, no one can say The Last Jedi didn't take chances. It introduced the character Rose Tico, played by Kelly Mary Tran. She is Asian, and she doesn't die in the movie. Beautiful. There was love brewing between her and Finn. Beautiful.

The question I had at the end of The Last Jedi was who was going to end up with Rey. Poe or Finn? Love triangle. Nice. Adam Driver's Kylo Ren also wanted to hook up with Rey. So love pyramid, with Rey at the top? Nice.

Or maybe Finn was going to end up with Rose, and either Poe or Kylo with Rey? So love here, and love triangle there. Nice. Not that Rey needs to hook up with any man, by the way, but the potential for romance was there on the screen. Nothin' wrong with a little lovin'.

Rise of Skywalker gets rid of all that, basically gets rid of Rose (and Princess Leia for obvious reasons, RIP Carrie Fisher), and focuses on the feelings between Kylo Ren and Rey. The movie is fast and full of action, but it is safe. It is going to make a billion dollars. I saw it once, and I am going to see it again.

But does it measure up to Empire Strikes Back or Return of the Jedi? Hell no! Is it better than The Force Awakens? No. Without all of the additional, emotional stuff that was in The Last Jedi, the love pyramid that could have lifted the movie to another level, Rise of Skywalker is almost paint by numbers.

It is a big movie. It is fast and full of action, as previously stated, and I am going to see it again. I guess I'm part of the problem. But for me, the film is just... lacking.

Here is the thing, at the very end, when everyone is celebrating, J.J. Abrams shows us two women kissing, a lesbian kiss. Great! Fantastic! For 1 second. In the entire almost 3 hour movie, no one is gay, except for that 1 example at the end, that flash moment. That is all that is needed to be inclusive?

I understand playing it SAFE, not wanting to upset the hetero mass, which I am a part of, and all the religious folk who hate gays. However, if you're going to put something on the screen, do something with it.

review:

title: A mediocre ending to a badly planned trilogy
review:
George Lucas famously wrote his script for Star Wars, then realised it was too long for a single movie and split the script into three parts. What J.J. Abrams did was the opposite. He planned to make a trilogy but only wrote the script for the first episode (along with Lawrence Kasdan). This ill-advised approach was made only worse by when Rian Johnson was given more or less free reign over the next movie.

When Lucasfilm asked Abrams back on the writer/director-seat on The Rise of Skywalker, it was time to reap what had been sown. The Last Jedi had killed off a lot of the mystery boxes (a favourite plot device of Abrams') set up in order to continue the plot from The Force Awakens. Among these were the main villain and the mystery of Rey's parentage.

The result is a movie that is filled to its brim with events to make up for the lost time and plot development of the previous two movies. Things that were introduced only in the previous scene already got a payoff in the next. Probably in an attempt to please everyone -- as well as to come up with ideas in order to salvage the trilogy -- a lot of known fan theories seem to have found themselves on the writers table.

As has recently come to light, multiple endings for this movie were made and shown to test-audiences. The one we got to see on the big screen was undoubtedly the safest and the least controversial ending. It ticked all the boxes for suspense, saving grace at the last moment, some fan-service in the form of certain events and characters. There is nothing controversial about this movie, which is of course the intention after The last Jedi.

Not much needs to be said about the visuals, they are what you would expect from a movie of this magnitude. The music is okay, even though the only really memorable themes (apart from reused music from the older movies) are Rey's and Ren's leitmotifs.

title: I thought it was fine.
review:
It wasn't great, but it wasn't god-awful. I followed the plot along just fine, the actors were great, the effects were something beyond this world, but yes, there are many flaws. That doesn't mean it was terrible. Is it the worse of the sequel trilogy? Probably. I'll have to watch all three of them again to get the full effect. Is it the worse Star Wars film? Far from it. Unlike other Star Wars films, I was not even considering clocking out of the film. I did not get bored for a second while watching this film. I cannot say the same for Episode II.
I will admit it when I say I'm a recent viewer of the Star Wars series. I never read the "Extended Universe," I've only watched the films. I understand that if I did, maybe my review would look a lot different, but as it stands, I like the movie just fine. Is it a satisfying ending? Eh...
It has its moments, but something is missing. It does feel like an ending, but something about it just seems...incomplete. Like there are way more questions that need to be answered.
Speaking of answering questions, it does answer a few of them. I won't spoil the answers, but a question of lineage is finally answered. Quite abruptly at that. I was expecting the answer but not to have it just sprung up like that. Other than that, the fights are cool, the sad moments are sad (except for one at the end of the end fight, I do agree with people about that), and Star Wars still feels like Star Wars to me.

title: Worthy addition to the Star Wars sega
review:
The Rise of Skywalker does not match the magic and freshness of A New Hope or The Empire Strikes Back. Then again, I am not sure it is possible for any movie to live up to those two episodes.

That being said, it has a compelling plot that was well acted. Sadly, it felt rushed, and JJ Abrams was clearly not at his directorial best here. The first half was sloppy and on the whole, this movie had enough substance for three hours of screen time. Overall, I wish it flowed better, but it is what it is!

Those who think that Episode 9 was an attempt at appeasing/pleasing the fan base, for better or worse, missed the point of episode 8. Rian Johnson never went against the Star Wars cannon. Episode 8 was predominantly Lucas' vision for Episode 7. Luke was meant to give up and withdraw, as have virtually all others before him, from Qui Gon to Anakin to Yoda to Obi Wan. Every single gave up at one point or another.

Episode 9 was not meant to be a big FU to Rian, as many critics and fans seem to think. Luke returned to accepting his duty as a Jedi at the end of episode 8 and he was meant to play a more positive role in Episode 9. Like Obi Wan chose to do in the end of A New Hope, Luke chose to become one with the force at the end of The Last Jedi. This is a choice many a Jedi had taken, so Luke was no exception.

review:

I found the best way to watch this film is to watch it not thinking to much about the previous two and it becomes quite enjoyable. The story line I actually felt was good, everybody keeps saying it was a to similar to the return of the jedi but I felt that was one of the reasons why it worked for me.

Perhaps the most disappointing bit is the knights or Ren they didnt really do much for a formidable group of killers. The other thing that annoyed me was Disney's political crap that they have to put in. Best example was the two lesbian fighter pilots at the end hugging and kissing!? Why was that needed? The fact that they felt that it was needed to be put in is quite worrying. Maybe what they should have been more concerned about was making this trilogy a masterpiece.

I give this film an 8/10. It is by far the best one out of the three and well worth a watch. No where near as good as the originals but how many films can you say are? Go watch it and put aside all of these negative reviews and enjoy it for the film in front of you.

review:

It was everything these new films could have been, after the average-but-fun, fan pleasing TFA and god awfulll Last Jedi. Destroyed my expectation of a terrible follow up and was some of the most stunning storytelling Star Wars has seen since Empire. There's so much I loved about this film I wish I could leave a list of spoilers.

The only things I didn't like were problems I have with ALL Star Wars films, and I'm always happy to let those slide tbh... it's not exactly an art movie is it. But this is as close as it comes to a dark, intense and stunning chapter of the Star Wars story (in a messy trilogy) with depth that both gutted me at moments and left me with such resolve at the end.

Basically, couldn't have been more surprised with how much I loved it. It was near perfect to me. So,Disney obviously, but...don't believe the negative reviews and go see it and let John Williams, Adam Driver and Carrie Fischer break your heart.

Just for context, since this review is already super geeky - here's how I'd rank all the main films:

1. Empire Strikes Back 2. Rise Of Skywalker ?! 3. A New Hope 4. Return Of The Jedi 5. Attack Of The Clones 6. Phantom Menace (this would lower but I have weird love for it) 6. Revenge Of The Sith (this would be higher but THE DIALOGUE) 7. Force Awakens (meh) 8. by a mile Last Jedi

title: I was there at the start
review:
On May 25, 1977 I saw Star Wars, Episode VI. It was a wonder. Yesterday I saw The Last Skywalker. It was billed as the end of the what started all those years ago. It was.

The opening was the original Star Wars graphic and John Williams' music thrilled right on queue. From there it just got better.

No movie is perfect, and there are points where I wasn't sure where it was going. There were more twists that a typical Star Wars movie. I think it was necessary, not just because Ms. Fischer had died, but because a lot needed to happen to pull it all off (read the credits to see how hard this movie was to make).

Rey HAD to be a Skywalker in the end. That was never going to be an easy task. Do I think it was slightly cheesey she chose to be the last Skywalker? Yes, and no. Yes, because it is part of the all old westerns, but no because SHE had to choose. Star Wars has always been about the choices the characters make.

Every choice this time was more difficult that any in the previous movies. More was at stake and death is a part of taking risks. I give the writers an A-, they could have done better. They still did a good job with a tough assignment.

If you are old enough to have been there for the first movie, then you will understand why the feeling of wonder still exists. The CGI was flawless, almost. The ghost scence has Ms. Fischer looking a little strange. Other than that, the CGI was fantastic. The physics of motion (I am a physicist) left a lot to be desired, but all CGI movies have the problem, so I forgive it.

Star Wars changed a generation. I am proud to be one of those it impacted. This was a good film, not great, good. I may see it again to review scenes that moved too fast to take in everything. I had to do that three times with the first Star Wars.

If you did not live though them all, I invite you to understand the journey. Lucas started something fantastic. True, Disney finished it, but it has been a great, and bumpy ride. I am glad it is done and happy to have been a part of it.

May the Force be with You.

title: Don't believe the 1s nor the 10s.
review:
First off, is by no means a bad film, sure it's flawed mostly from a story point of view, which is where most fans attack this film. Despite some inconsistencies within the framework of the story's saga, I recall some unexplained elements from the first trilogy and none of these fans are nitpicking like they do with these films, purely because most of them saw them when they were kids/teenagers and were so enthralled by them that they omit some of these "flaws". My point is that it is almost as if they want to hate the sequel trilogy for whatever reason, minutiously ripping every small detail to shreds without giving it the slightest chance. The 1, 2 or 3 star ratings are absolutely disgraceful, as they only increase the poor conception this trilogy has without actually being deserving of such shaming. These whiny fans seem like they want to have everything served in a silver platter, asking for huge send-offs with big pompous displays to major characters but it is not always the case to do that, nor it should be. This film already gives much fan-service so as to please every generation but it is still impossible to satisfy every single viewer.

Having covered the disruptive venom toxic fandom spreads, I would say The Rise of Skywalker is arguably the better one from the whole trilogy. But first some displeasing aspects: some jokes and one-liners are oddly placed, and seem rather forced instead of coming up with more clever ways to throw them in. Some clichÃ© "Disney moments" also appear in many parts of the film but for some reason are a bit cringe-worthy, perhaps not coming off as sincere as one would expect, which is a bit detrimental to the nurturing essence of togetherness, hope and fellowship heavily present in the first trilogy.

In the acting spectrum, Daisy Ridley and Adam Driver make up for the pairing with most given screen time, mainly because they both represent good and evil, Jedi and Sith, and they are both inevitably fearful of and torn between switching to the other side, which is a fantastic dynamic in my book. They both give great performances, that suit the bond they have created with one another.

The most impressive aspect is its visual setting, and the well-crafted CGI, which proves that in that department, these are definitely great times for Star Wars films being made. There are some exquisite shots that could delight even some of the most die-hard fans of the franchise.

When it comes to action and fighting choreographies, the stunts are fairly good, although nothing truly spectacular, which is a shame, because great efforts could be done in order to achieve something truly majestic and of a more enduring quality.

I won't get into plot details or issues, I will leave that to your own discovery, all I will say is that I hope future Star Wars installments don't suffer the fierceful and unjust scrutiny and tiresome comparisons these films had. Although I understand the comparisons to some extent because it is the sequel to the original story, but enough already, when does it end? It's extremely hard to live up to such a glorious cinematic achievement and cultural global phenomenon as it is, so newer films should be viewed and analyze under their own light so that they don't become a mere shadow of the original, or maybe even less. We have to give them a chance to stand on their own.

The Rise of Skywalker might not be the best SW film, but it is definitively an entertaining one, and the closing chapter of the mighty saga that has enamoured million fans all over the world. I believe this film will gain more acceptance as the years pass by. Or at least I hope so, because it would be a step forward.

title: Has anyone ever told you the tragedy of episodes 7-9?
review:
The Rise of Skywalker is the ultimate byproduct of two competing visions. In episode 8, Rian Johnson obliterated much of what JJ Abrams had built up in episode 7. And now in episode 9, JJ Abrams had to retcon much of what Rian destroyed in episode 8.

The emperor returns thankfully not in some idiotic way that I feared (time travel via force disturbance), but rather by the unnatural powers of the sith to control life. His existence serves as a motivation for Kylo Ren, which was sorely needed after Rian Johnson turned his character into some second rate Dick Van Dyke show. Kylo is hesitant to trust the emperor, and immediately begins plotting against him.

After that opening sequence, the movie is slow to gain momentum with the jarring Leia scenes that are clearly dialogue from Carrie Fisher meant for different purposes. And TROS doesn't really pick up speed until Kajimi, nearly an hour into the film, when we meet Zorii and Babu Frik. Though one exception is the explosive power of Rey's force lightning that gives us a taste of her dark side.

And that's the real strength of the movie: Rey's dark side, and Kylo Ren goading it out of her. This has always been their story, and the (only) genius thing Rian Johnson wrote in ep 8 was connecting them by the force. JJ employs that several times in TROS to delightful effect, and even expands on the capabilities of that force connection. Kylo and Rey receive an extremely satisfying arc by the ending moments.

There are several questionable moments, as in, "Are you sure the force can do that JJ?" The tragedy is that JJ had little else place to go. The main villain (Snoke) was quickly merked without even a single lightsaber battle in episode 8, so the emperor really had to ratchet up the sith powers. However, the reliance on the history of the sith, and the portrayal of them as a cultish religion, was extremely faithful to source material. So even the parts that made me question what I was watching still felt like Star Wars.

title: Forget the critics and the haters, this movie is good!
review:
I've been a Star Wars fan since I was a kid. I grew up on the original trilogy, and my parents were fans before I even came along. In recent years I've grown dismayed by the wrath that so many other Star Wars fans have vented on not just the prequels, but especially the new trilogy. In fact, the venom others have expended on these films has left me feeling very frustrated; in a story arc this big, spanning over 40 years and with so many flavors (from Clone Wars to The Clone Wars to Rebels to Rogue One to IV, to II, to IX) you just can't please everyone. But the hatred is just shocking.

I LOVED VII. Loved it. I enjoyed VIII--although there were a few quibbles I had with it and some of the complaints others registered were either justified, or should have been anticipated by the filmmakers in advance.

I thought that this movie is, overall, fantastic. Forget the critics, I hardly ever agree with them anyways. They love movies I hate, and hate movies I love. Almost universally.

Spoiler free: the movie packs a lot into its storyline. For the first hour, or thereabouts, I thought some of the scene transitions were a little choppy. And it was very fast-paced throughout. But it nicely tied the newest trilogy back into the originals, I felt, while completing the story arc for the new characters. A few twists and turns... some neat throwbacks... overall a cool story. I can't wait to see it again and again.

One thing that struck me is a number of "course corrections" from VIII that I thought addressed many of the most viable complaints others had with that film. Things that were odd or left feeling useless in VIII were explained or made useful in IX. I wish VIII hadn't been so divisive to fans. I don't think the SW fan base will ever recover from that schism. But for a moderate fan who loves the genre yet doesn't cling to the original laserdisc copies of IV-VI as the "only" true Star Wars, or whine endlessly about who shot first, I loved IX. Our whole multigenerational group did.

Don't listen to critics or haters. Go in, watch the movie with an open mind, and lose yourself in a galaxy far, far away while you consume some popcorn.

The movie has very few emotive moments, when quite frankly (being the conclusion) it should have many. The plot has more holes than swiss cheese.

It seemed to me to be a "by the numbers" kind of movie. A sort of going through the motions just to get to the end point. That said it was overall enjoyable enough but for me it is a case of "been there, seen that".

The movie does not compare with something like Endgame. They are just not in the same league at all.

The more I think on it, I would have to say that my 7 rating is generous. I really wanted it to be great. Sadly, it is not. "great" isn't even in the rear-view mirror.

title: Egregious pacing and plot issues aside....it's not all bad
review:
I went in with low expectations given the reviews so maybe that coloured how I saw it. I agree with a comment I saw, that this feels like both of JJ's planned sequels squashed into one movie, while ignoring one of the major points of the previous film. The pacing is just awful. The first 10 minutes could have been half a movie and from there we're taken on a tour of a few new planets including an interplanetary Burning Man. After a while of feeling angry at the pacing, I calmed down and started paying attention to what was good. Rey and Kylo's arc is continues in a satisfactory manner and concludes almost as well. The emperor, all things considered, was an interesting addition. He was clearly meant to be the big reveal at the end of the previous film, which could have been cool. Everything looks great obviously and the set pieces are as fun as usual.

I would put the blame for this trilogy's severe lack of direction, on both JJ Abrams and Rian Johnson equally. Say what you will about JJ Abrams' mystery box theory. It is silly, but you don't ret-con previously established intrigue simply because "it doesn't matter". Alright then Rian Johnson, what does matter? I think The Last Jedi failed to answer that. All it did was dump what had been set up in the first film but it didn't replace it with anything. That said, I would expect someone like JJ Abrams to be more than up to the challenge of building something meaningful from that point. Rather than that, he simply ret-cons the ret-con and says "so this stuff that the previous film said didn't matter, yeah it matters".

title: A basic guide on enjoying a legendary movie franchise
review: Instead of writing a movie review per se, and having read all the hatred disguised as movie reviews here, I decided to write a simple guide on enjoying not only Star Wars, but absolutely any movie at all. That said, whenever a sequel of a legendary franchise such as Star Wars comes out, there are two things I usually do. 1. I do not open my IMDB app or visit any website containing movie "reviews" in order to completely ignore the usual hatred that befalls an all-time favorite flick. 2. I avoid those meme-based apps which are rife with spoilers at all cost. Unfortunately, when it comes to Star Wars, some "fans" act as extreme traditionalists who will never accept Disney Studios as the legitimate owner of Star Wars and to them, it doesn't really matter if they come with an epic flick. They will always wear their keyboard warrior armour and loathe it at all costs. Such people would rather see Star Wars being written with the same Apple 1 computer George Lucas used when writing the script for Star Wars: A New Hope back in 77. Hell, they probably resent the fact that 35 mm PANAVISION cameras weren't used in episode IX. I like to compare what's been happening to Star Wars to what's been happening to Formula 1. There's this group of people who call themselves "fans" who insist on ignoring the fact that Liberty Media has been gathering more F1 fans around the world by making this motorsport more enjoyable too by introducing "modern" entertainment such as a T-shirt gun/launcher and Bruno Mars concerts on race weekends. Despite the fact that I hate Bruno Mars (or that type of music), it is undeniable that F1 has got itself into a more modern, sophisticated Era, just like Star Wars. There are legions, believe it or not, who stopped following F1 because those extreme fuel-efficient, lower-emission Power Units are being used instead of gas-guzzling, oil-spilling V10s from the 80s. Believe it or not, there are legions who stopped following the Star Wars franchise because Rey, Finn, Poe and Kylo Ren aren't like Luke, Leia, Han and Vader. So, what are you waiting for? Go and enjoy another excellent Star Wars installment if you can ignore the bad "reviews" in here. And if you, like me, grew up watching A New Hope, Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi, don't forget to bring your tissues (yes, there will be crying in the theater, I guarantee it).

title: Put yourself in Abrams' shoes

title: Fixes what The Last Jedi broke
review:
The split in Star Wars fandom won't heal as a result of this final episode of the nine movie series. That goal would be beyond the skill level of any director in history. But, what JJ Abrams did was fix the damage done to the Star Wars lore wrought by Rian Johnson's alternate universe effort The Last Jedi. And that goal was plenty ambitious.

For those who like to see heroes torn down, this movie will anger. Nothing else can be said for that.

For those who like to see odes to heroism overcoming great evil, and a message of hope to build upon, then this movie strikes the right balance.

That said, there are some cringe worthy lines in the script, as the syrupy rhetoric piles on a bit too thick in places. That truth, combined with the alteration of the true path of the Chosen One, and there is plenty here to upset a segment of the fandom, and the polarized movie reviews posted is plenty proof of that.

Still, judged on the merits that ultimately all movies should be judged upon, JJ Abrams does an admirable job here, correcting the deliberate efforts to destroy much of what George Lucas created, while at the same time reaching deep into the canon lore to bring out nuggets previously explored only in the deeper treatments of the novel series.

This is especially true in the climatic revelation of the Sith legend of what true eternal life for the Sith master looks like, and more importantly how it is carried out. Turns out that Palpatine's statements to Luke Skywalker that implied "striking him down" would secure Luke's path to the Dark Side, was not metaphorical after all!

Ultimately, the nine movie story arc is carried back to its very beginnings, and without question the effort was to send a valentine to the many fans who watched the story unfold over nearly five decades. In that, Abrams finished it off in likely the best way that was achievable.

title: Enjoyable but flawed - but this trilogy went wrong with Last Jedi
review:
Let's start with the positives (in what will be a negatives-heavy review). I enjoyed this movie. It was good to see the (cloned) Emperor who has real menace and Rey and Ren/Ben elevate the film whenever the focus shifts to them.

But The Rise of Skywalker is overlong which resulted in several lulls/pacing issues. Part of the problem is that these sequels have far too many characters that are nonentities. Rose, anyone? She should be an extra as she adds nothing. (This has nothing to do with this being a female character - Rey is an excellent character and worthy of centre-stage). Another example is Poe. It seems like they have made him out to be a Han Solo equivalent but he has none of the charm. He's a Wedge Antilles equivalent but with way too much screen time over the three films. There are many other examples of characters who could have been minimised or foregone entirely.

As we have come to expect, The Rise of Skywalker takes liberties with the force, building on the rubbish we saw from the Last Jedi such as communicating with each other over huge distances. Using the Force to teleport physical items like lightsabers? Give me a break. Heeling with the force was another new one. I went with it for the giant snake thing, and even when Rey saved Ren/Ben, but when he saved her it was a step too far. Why did Rey actually need to be brought back to life anyway? Why did her final confrontation with the Emperor kill her? She repelled his lightning blasts with her two lightsabers. What did she die of? Exhaustion? This seems to be a very stupid way for Jedi to die in the sequels. In the original films a Jedi could die from old age, lightsaber, Force lightning bolts or being thrown to their death. But in the sequels Luke, Leia and Rey all die of Force exhaustion. As does Ren/Ben. He gives his life Force to bring her back from the dead and expires doing so. A shoddy ending made worse by the fact that he is not given a proper redemption conclusion. Why was he not a Force Ghost at the end? It happened to Anakin - why not Ben? One of many inconsistencies that have plagued the prequels and sequels.

Luke gets yet another derisory cameo. He's the saviour of the Galaxy, the hero of the original trilogy, and yet it feels like he gets less screen time than anyone. He's been given the Alec Guinness role but with a tenth of the screen time. Given how little we have seen of him this trilogy - and The Rise of Skywalker is no different - I was expecting to see him make a defining appearance at the end of the film but, alas, no. I hope poor Mark Hamill wasn't paid by the word! The writers of the sequels cannot have liked Luke in the originals - (especially Rian Johnson). Is there another explanation for the character's shoddy treatment?

Finally, what about those big planet-killer guns underneath the Star Destroyers? They looked like great big (dogs). Amazed nobody pointed that out at the design stage.

After the promise of The Force Awakens this trilogy was then made disposable. That's Rian Johnson's fault with his abysmal The Last Jedi. One is left wondering what might have been had JJ Abrams overseen Episode VIII. This sequel trilogy should have had one writer in charge of the storyline across the three films. It is clear that when they began they had not worked out what the purpose of this trilogy was. It is hard to fathom why Disney allowed Johnson to depart so much from Abrams' initial direction. Johnson has no understanding of what makes a Star Wars film. Given the very poor card Abrams was dealt he has done well to do what he has with The Rise of Skywalker. Despite the many flaws I have listed above, this is still worth a watch. It's just not a patch on the originals.

How I rate the nine films:

* The Empire Strikes Back (10/10 - perfect) * A New Hope / Return of the Jedi (9 - superb films from the original trilogy) * The Force Awakens (8 - It's not perfect, the Force comes far too easily to Rey and its story covers familiar storylines but the new cast of characters are good, it has Solo, it's the least bloated of the sequels, has fewer non-entity characters and still holds out promise of what could come. You just have to do your best to forget that what happens next is The Last Jedi) * The Rise of Skywalker (7.5 - Needs a repeat viewing but possibly edges Revenge) * Revenge of the Sith (7 - The best of the prequels although that's a low bar to clear. Palpatine reveals himself and we have the birth of Vader) * The Phantom Menace (6 - Darth Maul a highlight; Jar Jar the lowest of low points) * Attack of the Clones (5 - A bit too much like a computer game and with shoddy acting but a couple of highlights - Dooku decent and Anakin showing signs of shifting to the Darkside although Yoda with a lightsaber bouncing around like a pinball is not for me). * The Last Jedi (3 - Woeful. I have never watched a Star Wars film that left me so disappointed and angry as this one as I left the cinema. It poured a bucket of manure on what Star Wars was about. Ridiculous liberties with the Force, ruined Luke's character, built Snoke up and then disposed of him cheaply, ships running out of fuel, Marvel-esque jokes, and it was overlong - to name just a few of its problems).

title: They did the best they could with what they had to work with.
review:
First let me say that, like all Star Wars movies, I enjoyed this movie while watching it and was on my Star Wars high immediately after seeing it. "Star Wars High" is that great feeling you get after watching a Star Wars movie that allows you to ignore all the "fridge logic" that will make you question whether the movie was actually good or not after seeing it. If you don't know what "fridge logic" is, just google the term, you'll laugh. Star Wars movies have always had a lot of fridge logic, but episodes 8 and 9 were particularly bad when it came to plot holes, unanswered questions and things that just didn't make sense.

This trilogy had the same problem Lost did. JJ Abrams wrote the beginning and the end but let other writers take over for the middle and the ending didn't fit anymore, but it was still awkwardly tacked on. The biggest problem this film had was that it had to continue the story where episode 8 left off. Rian Johnson didn't leave JJ Abrams with much to work with. Episode 8 ended on a dead end, not a cliff hanger. Johnson had written the trilogy into a corner and Abrams had the unenviable task of undoing a lot of what Johnson had written so that he could conclude the story in a satisfying way. He wasn't entirely successful unfortunately, and as a result it seemed more like two movies crammed into one. It was so fast paced that it was hard to follow the plot, and what I was able to follow just seemed like a retelling of "Return of the Jedi" with different characters. But this was the problem I had with all the movies in this trilogy. Ep7 was basically an inferior remake of Ep4, Ep8 an inferior remake of Ep 5 and this one an inferior remake of Ep6. Could they have made something more original and satisfying? Let's examine how this trilogy could have been improved.

There was that great moment in Ep8 where Rey was about to join with Kylo. This was the best moment of that film, and I think if they had the balls to have her join with him it would have saved that movie. It would have truly been "subverting expectations". Rey could have become a powerful villain who continued being tempted by the dark side and then in this film they could have had Kylo save her from the Dark Side. This would have made these movies a lot better ... but I'm not sure it's enough to make it a great trilogy.

The root of the problem goes back to Ep7. The worst part of Ep7 wasn't so much that it was a total rehash of Ep4, it was the fact that everything the good guys accomplished in the original trilogy had been undone by the start of Ep7. The Empire had risen again as The First Order and had more powerful weapons than before. The "New Republic" was in ashes and was reduced to an even weaker resistance than the earlier rebellion. As much as it tried to honor the OT, it took a dump on it.

The Empire was basically the Third Reich in space. Like the nazis, they lost the big war and were forever seen as a force of pure evil. Neo-nazis are a joke today and anyone who tries to revive their hateful ideology is pretty much universally shunned. The idea that Neo-Nazis could rise again to the same level the actual Nazis had, a la The First Order, just isn't realistic. BUT, it is a lot more likely that a different group could unknowingly become just as fascist even while claiming that they are fighting fascism.

Perhaps what they should have done is, instead of a First Order that tries to continue where the Empire left off, there should have been a separatist faction that split off because they felt the New Republic was becoming just as totalitarian as the Empire. Meanwhile, the New Republic sees the separatists as fascist and under control of a Palpatine like figure that is misleading them. Both sides see each other as evil and under control of the dark side, and perhaps it turns out both are correct (Palpatine is leading both sides to war with each other behind the scenes, like he did in the prequels).

It would have been more similar to the prequels in this regard, yes, but the one good thing about the prequels was that the overall story and themes were very good, original, and an excellent allegory to what is going on today even if the execution was poor. They would have retold a story that needed to be retold in an improved way, not one that was already done to near perfection.

Perhaps I am wrong and these changes would have made things worse. After all, I did enjoy these films while watching them. But in order for new Star Wars movies to have a lasting impact in the same way the original trilogy did, they need to have a strong story in addition to great execution. This trilogy delivered, for the most part, on the latter, but not so much on the former ... sort of the opposite of the prequel trilogy that had a great overall story, but missed the mark in many regards on the execution.

title: Hating this movie will not make you one of the cool kids.
review:
Dear Jedis, Sith lords and Rebels,

Basically this movie, in my opinion, is more than perfect and fits for THIS trilogy, not the whole Saga.

  • Palpatine's return is more than predictable. If you go deep into his life and his journey to the dark side and becoming the great sith lord he is, you'd know that he wouldn't go and die with a fall just like that. I mean even Darth Maul who was cut in half with a lightsaber is still alive in the comics.
What bothered me with bringing back Palpatine is the fast rush. The whole movie was rushed and obviously because they needed to get a closure and because of TLJ. TLJ was a waste of time. Imagine if they included Palpatine's return at the end of TLJ instead of wasting time with stupid Fin and his useless journey with Rose, that would have been awesome and thrilling at the same time. One more thing about Palpatine. Okay i get it Rey is his grandchild. But Palpatine had a.. SON? This is huge! The Sith lord himself has a kid and we don't know about it? So one honest opinion about Palpatine's return: they did him wrong.

  • Kylo:
Kylo is a vey interesting character. Ever since he appeared in TFA it was more than obvious that J.J. was trying to give us some Darth Vader vibes and obviously he succeeded. I really felt like he was there, all the way till the end. Kylo was that good. The important question here is: was it necessary to kill him off? The answer in my opinion is: of course. He didn't 'die' btw, the force took him. What's nice about all of this is the connection between Kylo and Leia. Yes Leia, not Rey. it's amazingly strong. All the way from TLJ they prepared us and gave us a hint that they have a strong connection and we might see it again in ROS. Brilliantly done, Leia made us all cry with this connection.

Fin/Rose/Poe/whoever: I seriously do not give one slightly tiny about any of them. Waste of time and cheesy Disney moments. Especially Fin.

Rey: I have nothing but respect to my queen. Nothing to add on her journey except for DAMN she's good. Sith blood and Jedi soul in one person. Akh!

Returning to Tatooine: I cried. Like a little girl, i cried a lot. That was it, that was the end of the Skywalker Family. Amazing ending, i loved it so much. They appreciated Luke and Leia a lot. Would've been epic if they showed the whole Skywalker family, from Anakin and PadmÃ© all the way to Kylo. But we take what we get.

A lot to discuss but I personally loved it, wouldn't want it to have another ending at all.



May the force be with you all, always.

title: A happy fan!
review:
I have always loved the star wars films. The fundamental theme of the films is good verses evil. Heros rising to meet challenges and characters working together to beat the bad guys. This film had a huge job to do, to finish a 9 film saga and please all the fans. The latter was never going to happen. There will always be fans who have imagined the direction they would want the films to take and are upset when it didn't pan out that way. I had no idea what was going to happen. I wanted to go in and be entertained, I wanted a tied up finish and questions answered. I wanted nods to the fans and to see characters old and new come
together to beat evil - I got that, so I am a happy fan.
The film was exciting, emotional (especially the Leia scenes) and tense. I loved the new characters in the series and loved seeing the old ones one last time. I'm looking forward to watching it again.

title: What a great way to end it
review:
As a fan of Star Wars, what I really like about it is it is a three-act play. I was impressed with how Lucas wrote it and his direction. It was refreshing to start the play with act two (original trilogy) and then go to act one (prequels) and end with act three (Final trilogy).

It was important to see this not only as a single movie, but as part of the play as a whole. For anyone who has read, and follow this story, it is a story of Hope and facing giants. For some, it would be like David and Goliath. Darth side - seeming to be larger and strong, but all self-seeking, focused and fueled on hate/fear. While the Light side - seeming to be smaller, but determined, fighting for the good of all, and self-sacrificing. A fight to destroy evil.

This ended made sense, and in my opinion fit quite well with the vision of George Lucas. I congratulate JJ Abrams for keeping true all the way to the end. I am looking forward to see it again and enjoying watching all nine movies in order.

title: Connect the dots. It's a fun fun time
review:
Arm chair critics are harsh and i would like to see them do a better job and not get blasted. I've been a huge fan all my life and I've read so many of the stories. I don't just like Star Wars I love Star Wars! But to go into this movie thinking that everything was going to be perfect is pure crud. But, in my opinion it all works. I see connections that others say came out of now where. I think it was more emotional and feeling than analytical story telling. Some of the negatives I'm reading... 1) Rey is a palpatine all of a sudden. "What?!" Come on, like, you couldn't feel that there was more after TLJ? You really thought that her parents were nobody and accepted that?

2)Palpatines sudden emergence as the driving force. For anyone who knows about sith, they can be immensely powerful...more powerful than Jedi even, and the power of life and death was how palpatine lured Anakin away in the first place. He wasn't lying. He could have saved padme. He didn't so he could tap into the anger. Sith feed of the negative energies and there is so much more of that in the universe. That's why there is never more than two!! Master and apprentice with apprentice the majority of the time killing the master to gain power. There's always a host of Jedi. And remember the force is always trying to balance itself. In the prequels, palpatine arose from an over abundance of Jedi... i feel and why he is so powerful. Upon wiping out the Jedi and the death of powerful light siders like yoda, the universe kept feeding us more powerful force users to counter act each other. Also why they came from the same two blood lines. Trying to consolidate and find harmony.

3) Rey being so powerful...again balance I feel and Anakin had the same sensitivity at a very young age. Reys emergence gave me the feeling of a neutral and why her saber is gold. It was a theme Ben was trying to push on her but he was to Dark. She felt the dark side as well. I don't feel she is committed fully to the light and will be a balance the force is looking for until of course newer generations arise.

4) Huxley being a spy just bc he hates Ben. Well, duh. How is this a problem? The highest ranking military man has been embarrassed and bullied at every turn by Ben, add his failures which he also blames Ben for and now he is demoted. Pettiness is a very real human reaction to having everything and then nothing. He's spoiled and a brat and wants "revenge".

5)The huge fleet. It's palpatine. He showed himself to be a good strategist with extreme patience and cunning. He didn't overthrow the republic overnight. He also seems to have prescience or a type of vision, as Rey was showing as well. So 25 or so years in a huge galaxy full of a gazillion people. I'm not looking that hard.

6)The only problem I ever have, ever, is just the empires sole plan is always a weapon that can destroy a planet. Other than that.....JUST ENJOY IT! ITS FANTASY and FUN! I can connect in my mind so many more dots but the passing of and era hit me in the feels. It was a good run. I absolutely loved Bens conflict and his and Reys connection was a huge build up.

title: Good, but fitting for a finale? No.
review: Good not great is the theme I kept coming back to for this film. Was this passable as we recieved the material that led to the close of a 40+ year long saga, arguable. For the finale though, leaves a bit of a bitter taste. Seems like if anywhere they needed to get it right, it was here, which is not to say this fact makes the movie bad, just Disney's capabilities.

title: Hard to rate it on its own
review:
All in all, I consider TRoS nothing short of a miracle. They had to squish two movies in one, as Johnson decided to make TLJ more of a standalone movie than the middle chapter of the trilogy and the penultimate of a saga. TLJ did nothing for character or plot development and only caused trouble by ruining every possible lead TFA left behind, including killing the villain and the main mentor just for "subverted expectations" sake. Plus Carrie Fisher's death further complicated the script.

I can't help but wonder just how much better this whole thing could have been. I don't think TFA was the best Star Wars movie ever, but it certainly entertained and felt like a faster paced Star Wars, with its main sin being that it felt too much like Star Wars. But it set really interesting characters, specially Finn and Kylo, and set all sorts of mysteries that could (and should) have been explored in 8. But they were not.

Considering all it had to deal with, TRoS manages to make a decent movie and save the trilogy somewhat, but at the same time falls really short of delivering a better ending to the saga, letting us wondering if the new trilogy was needed at all. Scratch that: I think we can all agree that it was not.

title: what people are saying about it
review: Alright now I get why hardcore fans are mad about it and keep in mind that I walked into this with somewhat low expectations considering all the mixed feelings people are having but I still very much enjoyed it! Sure it has its flaws as all movies do and one of them being that the first half feels pretty rushed, pretty much every line of dialogue in the first 30 minutes is of exposition but despite that I still think it had a satisfying conclusion to the Skywalker saga

title: Solid and utterly entertaining finale to the saga!
review:
Not quite sure why there a complaints about plot holes in the film that completes a saga consisting of plot holes? It is certainly nowhere close to the GOT final season, otherwise Rey would have taken the Sith throne ...

The acting (specifically Driver and Riddle) exceeds everything that we have seen in prior Star Wars installments. And this is certainly true of the chemistry between protagonist and antagonist.

Visuals are breathtaking and the story line basically focused on the main characters without silly extended subplots.

9 (should be 10), just to off all these haters and trolls on this platform. Once upon a time in a galaxy far, far away, there lived snowflakes also, not just on Hoth.

title: Why the hate? I loved it
review:
This is a great final installment in the Star Wars "Skywalker" movies. To all those who think it's too complicated, it falls on its face, it's made only for money or toys because DISNEY, it's just stupid and cheesy, or it's just BAD, I do not, I repeat, DO NOT see what they mean. This is a movie series about space battles and ninja laser sword people that actually has a following on global scale. All these nerds sweating too much because Star Wars isn't how they wanted it to be gotta calm the down. Let me give you some examples of why I rated this 9/10

Daisy Ridley as Rey: Fantastic. Absolutely fantastic. Her struggle with the dark side and being afraid of who she is (or who's she's descended from) is tied with the best part of this movie (along with Kyle Ren's storyline). Daisy Ridley literally made this struggle feel so real and human. You can imagine someone who does not want to be the same as their parent or grandparent and would do anything to run from that. "BUT HOW IS SHE DESCENDED FROM PALPATINE?! THATS SUCH A CLICHE!"

Ummmm how? The same people saying it's dumb that she's descended from palpatine are the same people wanting her to be a skywalker. Come on people. She can be descended from a powerful sith and want to fight against that. Give it a break.

Anyway, Rey is fantastic. I found her real and relatable, and more than that, a badass. And what's this about a Mary Sue? Shut up, seriously.

another plus: KYLO REN Full disclaimer, my brother and I totally called that he would either 1. Die evil 2. Turn good and either die or live

That was an easy prediction. But nonetheless, I loved the way it happened. He finally gave into the light. And it was powerful the way he sacrificed himself. I loved his entire story arc.

I'll say that I didn't really know why the emperor would tell Rey about his plan to have her kill him?? Why not just let her do it and your plan be fulfilled? So that was a little dumb. I'm going to be honest, other than that, I'd love to hear some criticism that is legitimate. Here's some criteria

1. It's not criticism based on silly space physics incongruity. It's a space movie. Be quite please nerds. 2. It's not criticism based solely upon what YOU would think is a creative way to end this series. Newsflash nerds. There is literally like 3 and a half million people that could have an opinion on how this movie ends. Let them end it without you complaining about it, good lord. 3. It's not criticism based on "the plot is convoluted and I'm confused!" Seriously. How? It's good vs bad, and good person feels pull to bad, but ultimately doesn't go bad.... huh? Like, are you serious? The original series was just the same. Come oooonnnn people.

Final verdict: I like this movie. A lot. A lot of these complaints are REALLY nit picky. Like REALLY. As a movie production, I quite literally see (or hear) zero flaws in HOW this movie was made. It's cliche, it's basic in story, and it's about space ninjas. But it's also FUN, it's inspiring, it's hopeful, and it's about SPACE NINJAS.

Don't be an old fart thinking this movie should be "serious" or "break the mold". Be a kid for gods sake. Enjoy this while you have it.

title: If you are looking for entertainment you will not be disappointed...
review:
...but if you are looking for a SCIENCE FICTION plot line to finalize a story never meant to be explained you will be disappointed.

I grew up watching Star Wars. My first one in the theater was ROTJ when I was six years old. I've always been a fan. I went in to this movie with low expectations based on everything I read and was entertained enjoying myself with the humor, wonderful sight saber action, and cinematography. Isn't that what movies are for? Entertainment? They don't explain your life existence and aren't mean to give you joy.

The original trilogy will forever be my favorite. I thought the sequels were better than episodes 1-3 - the development of Darth Vader was ridiculous! TLJ was not my favorite so this one surpassed my low expectation from the last movie.

I gave it 7 from 10 because there were some laughable and hokey scenes but I think all in all it was great entertainment. I will forever be a Star Wars fan and this movie will eventually be on my shelf like all the others.

title: Good but a little indulgent
review:
Some of the reviews are a little extreme. It's not a great film, but it's not bad. It's probably not a good film. It's certainly at least okay.

It's definitely indulgent and certain scenes don't at all feel earned. I'm generally quite emotionally involved with films, so it's telling I didn't really feel emotionally impacted even in massive moments of the film.

The action scenes weren't up to much unfortunately, with nothing new and creative. At times so much happened that I didn't real feel anything had much impact.

There was very little development through the film and somehow, despite massive opportunities, it wasn't at all particularly creative.

It was still fun though, it still had some likable characters, lots of references and nods. It at least ends a story we've been following for decades. It was never going to live up to the journey. After all, it's never really about the end, it's about the journey.

title: Not perfection but still good
review:
I am not one to usually write a review of a movie or TV show but I wanted to express my option on The Rise of Skywalker and the sequel trilogy in general. A lot of people are comparing it to the original, which is ok if you do that. I want to compare it as a completion of the last 3 movies, not as an overall.

I took my children to see this and tried to remember how I say the original as a kid. Looking at it with the eyes of my son and daughter gives it another perspective. Most people are looking at it as adults, but let us remember that the children are the ones that will be inspired by what they see.

I spoke with my children after and they enjoyed it, for the most part. I will start with my daughter's reaction first. She enjoyed it and loved a female playing the lead role. She was super excited to see what the lead female character did and how she was able to do by herself, along with the help of her friends. She now wants to learn how to do some of the stunts that were done. From a little girls view, she gives it an awesome rating and loved how it came out.

My son was a little different. He says there was a lot of good in the movie but some parts of the story seemed rushed. He wanted a pivotal scene to be expanded more to showcase how it happened and would not have minded if it was longer to further explain some areas. He also made a comment that the main characters, not the ones from previous movies, showed a growth in their acting abilities over the course of the trilogy. He thinks their confidence increased and they were more comfortable in what they were doing. These factors led him to think the acting quality became was better in this movie, when compared to the previous two. From a teenagers view, he was pleased.

I think we look at this too fondly from childhood memories and do not want to have a beloved part of it ruined. People have their own opinions on what was good or bad and everyone is correct. At the end of the day this movie was fun. No need to over analyze every single piece. Have fun, enjoy the movie, think how children will feel about it.

title: Good enough for me
review:
I'm easily entertained so I thoroughly enjoyed most of this. The first twenty minutes or so felt a bit rushed and choppy but once it got going it improved.
I managed to avoid spoilers beforehand except for one about "First LGBT kiss in Star Wars Franchise"
I mean, I immediately assumed it was between Poe and Finn, of course, and spent the entire movie waiting for it.
It was .... between two female extras, in the final scene, and I don't think the camera was even entirely focused on them.
Would've preferred something much more, but at least it was better than Endgame's attempt at LGBT representation.

title: Not bad, but not great
review:
I've grown up with Star Wars, and to put it simply nothing will ever come close to the original trilogy, it was ground breaking in so many ways. I walked into the theatre with trepidation, will they ruin a large part of my life.

No they didn't ruin it, but did they make it better? No they didn't, was it breaking new ground ? No it wasn't. There was some nice moments, Chewie getting his medal at last, I think what they did with Carrie Fisher was very well done, you would be hard pressed to know that it was old footage they used, although you could tell if you looked for it.

I said to my friend, when they were rescuing Chewie, that if they end up in a trash compactor I'm walking out. They didn't do that thank god, but I do think that they tried to shoehorn in too many Easter Eggs for the original films.

Marvel knows how to spend Mickey Mouses's money wisely, Star Wars I'm not so sure, although The Mandalorian does give me hope that it might turn into a universe that we are all are dying to see more of.

And where was baby yoda ?

title: one of the funniest movies ive ever seen
review: This movie goes out of its way to retcon all the major plot points of the worst movie in the saga, the last jedi, and for that reason i found it highly entertaining.

title: Not terrible, not great.
review:
So, there was Star Wars number 9.
Not impressive, not memorable, not terrible either. The series wasn't killed with an awful ending, like Games of Thrones, but it was left to rest on her former glory. Just like Star Wars number 7 and 8, the 9th was a tribute to the past, to the former glory.
The censorship and Disney's wise men guidance could be felt in any dialogue and twist of the plot. The lasts were exceptionally tiresome and predictable. I liked the Sith world and their Armada that was supposed to whip out the Resistance fighters. It amused me how the mightiest fleet of the galaxy ended up destroyed by lack of elementary safety features like redundant guiding antennas. The countless script logic flows make it less disturbing.
What buttered me most was the lack of good storytelling. Every crew member acted like they were there for a 9 to 5 job, and the director was just a name on the screen. It will never be remembered as J.J. Abrams Star Wars but rather like Disney's SW9. The same can be said about Carrie Fisher and Adam Driver. They are the most meretricious antagonistic couple in the history of the series.
But in the end, it's Star Wars, not Dune. I think it's my fault that I aspected more.

title: Excellent and satisfying
review:
I'm a HUGE SW fan.

I thought episode IX was really fun, awe inducing and ultimately satisfying. The action was great and effects very well done. The story surprised and delighted. I laughed, gasped and cheered. It hit lots of good emotional notes. The music was stellar as always.

I look forward to watching again and again over the years! Well done!

Still it is well made just not a true Star Wars film but still a very entertaining SCI FI film

title: Wonderfull ...with faults
review:
I was very impressed by the strong display of The Force in The Rise of Skywalker. In real life though, highly advanced practitioners of Chi or Qi will quickly excuse themselves rather than pay the price for the misuse of chi force.

I enjoyed the overall story, but the entire film seems rushed. JJ Abrams may have done a good job, but whosoever slapped and edited the film together spoiled it.

Some of the graphics of the space ships seemed toy like. I know we're not back in the 70's when the first Star Wars came out, but even then the space ships were larger than life.

title: Mixed feelings
review:
Ok, I watched this. Just came from the cinema. And I would say that this film is strange. Really strange.

JJ Abrams had a very difficult task: to fix mistakes from TLJ, introduce the new story and end the saga. Unfortunately, he couldn't do this. Let's go and see why.

CGI It is perfect here! Explosions, huge amount of starships, lightsaber duels - everything is amazing and fascinating. Disney CAN do special effects, but at the same time this is the only good part of the film.

Plot Oh my god this was truly idiotic. I think this is the worst thing about the film. Characters do stupid things. Really stupid. Film makers don't introduce us anything new, they even don't answer any questions from The Last Jedi and Force Awakens. There are even more questions. So wash your hands before watching because you will facepalm every 10 minutes.

Characters Well, Ray has become an unbreakable, immortal Jedi. Kylo is like a teenager: he can't choose his side and darts from Dark side and back. Finn and Po played acceptable, their duet is not bad. Po will become a new Solo in next trilogy, I suppose. All the actors are great, but the plot doesn't allow their characters to develop.

Music This is the last John Williams film. There are some nostalgia notes in soundtrack, but not more. That's my own opinion but the music from trailer and teaser was more epic.

The Force I know that in all saga the Force was the main magic thing that anyone couldn't explain but in that part it brakes every common sense. For example now you can lift the ships or heal the wounds with it. And now when the character makes one more stupid move it explains that it was "an instinct". WTF? In previous episode every hero had a motive. Every his move had consequences and was meaningful. In this film you won't see any smart move.

Conclusion I have really mixed feelings about this film. He has lots of easter eggs to other episodes, great CGI, but the plot kills everything. I can give filmmakers my own plot, and I assure you it will be 10000 times better then this. 6/10, not more

title: Good Movie, Bad Ending
review:
I enjoyed watching The Rise of Skywalker it was a fun movie with mostly good CGI but I hated the Ending and here is why:

From the Moment on where Rey uses lightning I knew one thing and hoped for another. I knew that the movie was setting her up to be a Palpatine.

I hoped that the End would consist of her accepting who she is and using the Lightning to defeat Palpatine. Then she and Ben would recognise the worth of both The Light and the Dark Side and found a new order: The Skywalkers.

But what instead happend is that Palpatine stood for all Sith and Rey for all Jedi and as quick as that we are back to the basic white Vs dark fight without grey areas. At least I had a neat Lightsaber Duel to look forward to in which Ben and Rey have to fight a repowered Palpatine, but Ben gets Force Pushed in a pit and Rey deflects Lightning, which Palpatine still hasn't learned to turn off, until he is only dust.

Although their last Scene together (Ben & Rey) was Sweet I don't get why Rey even died and I would have preferred if they both lived to raise the next generation.

I know that's a personal preference but I think it would have been nice.

title: A terrific movie on it's own merits
review:
I sincerely enjoyed this film from start to finish. Entertaining, engaging, beautifully staged, film-craft at the cutting edge of what is possible. The story and character lines felt very satisfying and emotionally grounded within the fantastical world(s) and atmosphere we've come to expect and enjoy from the Star Wars movies.

Daisy Ridley's Rey and Adam Driver's Kylo Ren are, of course, the most remarkable characters to emerge from the latest films and their mutual story's arc shapes this final movie - it's the necessary heartfelt and grounded relationship needed in a film series which orbits so furiously around the mechanics and set-pieces which make the films so dazzling. What happens to them in this film is worth the wait.

(IMDb critique) I don't claim to be a fan at all but I've enjoyed every release in theaters since the very first film. This release and it's user reviews have been a tipping point for me. Reading user reviews has been interesting and engaging over the years as IMDb has found itself providing a great service to filmgoers and cinema fans alike. For whatever reason, this film's release (and perhaps "The Last Jedi") have made me recognize the destructive influence of the "Twitter-reflex" approach to social media. Instead of measure, there is an entitled, emotion-based gesture which is interpreted as thought or idea. It's a profound misunderstanding of why communication can be interesting at all. The Trump-Tweetfart doesn't bring insight To bear, but it rather assumes every emotional reaction to anything seems worthy of print. I wish users would try to actually be helpful with reviews rather than mistake their most subjective, undigested and unedited response as insight.

title: The best of Episodes IV-IX
review:
I have more than 40 years invested in this series, and I've been selective in seeing only the original trilogy and the newest trilogy. And only in theaters where the full effects can be felt. No prequels, no odd rip-offs, no watching on TV with commercials. And only showings when school is still in session so I can enjoy the movie with just adults. So, yeah, I'm a big fan.

I think Episode IX is the best of the six. It was exciting, satisfying, and kept me interested every moment. (Except when some idiot's cell phone rang. Twice.) The story was gripping and progressed well. No slow moments that make you lose your concentration. There were a very few moments that seemed to have odd direction for the characters, but not enough to ruin the storyline.

If you are a Star Wars fan, you will enjoy IX and leave the theater satisfied. Even though it is billed as the "last", the conclusion seems to leave plenty of room for future installments. I hope we don't have to wait too long, because we original fans are in the Medicare age group now.

title: Better but not great: 7.3
review:
First off wow, this movie is chaos, not persé in a bad way. But so much happens, and I shared this thought with the others I went to see this with in theaters.

Do I think this was a decent ending to the ST? I do, it stays in theme of the ST, good and bad. But once again it tries to connect with the OT (and ignore PT) but it fails to do so for me.

Things I liked: 1. Toned down the ridiculous amount of (bad) comedy and silly stuff in TLJ. 2. Rose, the ''crazed finn stalker fan'' has been toned down and is pretty much friendzoned in the movie. 3. Kylo dies, although personally still is an irredeemable character and his death was too ''good''. 4. Finn finally doesn't feel utterly useless, but the suggested love plot with the other deserter FO trooper is a bit weird with Rose still ''in the picture''. 5. Visuals, just stunning all around. 6. Rey and Kylo's relation and struggle, yes it has many faults, but it was good...before the kiss, let's forget about that.

What I did not like: 1. May be surprising but the MUSIC, felt... weak. The only emotion throughout this movie I got was adventure and *star wars*. The entire movie felt so lighthearted, even though it had a lot of dark moments. I felt so much more sadness during Padmé's funeral than I did at Leia, nor Kylo.. And that was the prequels, and Padmé wasn't as instrumental as Leia, nor as charismatic/lovable. Rey's theme and Palpatine's theme were the only ones that stuck out, because they are amazing, but for the rest...not much.

2. Kylo dies, of course he climbs out of the endless pit, used his ''lightside'' to heal Rey, give his life and die. (Darth Plagueis reveal? ;)... I guess thats fine, personally I'm not sure on this yet.

3. Palpatine.... he's back, ofcourse. No I did not like this, and I felt like his voice didn't match up either. So what we are to assume is that he cloned himself, (as we see a snoke clone(?) in some fluid tank) and then raised an army from...somewhere. Like how does this work, did force palpatine clone himself? But how can you then ever kill the sith? He can just do this again?

4. In the end the story felt weaker, it was more about the personal individual journey of each character, but they never had a focused pay off, why does Rey fail training at the start of the movie, but minutes later gets handed the lightsaber back (with some odd dialog from Leia) and thats it..she's good I guess?

5. Rey and Kylo kiss, hmm. For someone that killed Han, Luke, Leia (indirectly) and countless rebels + planets he seems easily forgiven, he should have faded away before the kiss.

6. I don't know why they try to keep making unique characters and troopers if they don't differentiate them. Zori Bliss, badass looking bounty hunter type, nope, just a cheesy love plot. Okay. What about these badass looking red stormtroopers? Exactly, they are storm troopers....but RED! Cool right?! (+extra sith jet troopers). Seriously I was so looking forward to a unique stormtrooper(s) and we got actually nothing! + Deserter horse girl wit bow and arrow, she was okay, but again, love-ish plot. Where are just the downright bad characters.

7. Knights of ''who cares'', so Kylo trained these guys I guess by the name? Elite warriors, who.. walk around, always one step behind, and get killed by Kylo at the end because for some reason they are on Palp's planet.

8. Almost FORGET, WTF HUX?! This plot twist is so damn weird. I feel like he just wanted out, and the writers had no clue what to do with him.

9. Personally too much goddamn nostalgia callbacks. And I'm happy this saga is over so that they can CREATE the future nostalgia because half of this movie is OT characters doing their OT thing.

Well.. thats it so far. More negative things than I thought but all in all I stand by my 7.3, for what I expected, it managed to surprise me in some good, and bad ways, but it was fun.

title: The film is "ok" and that's good and bad at the same time

title: It was pretty allright
review: Polarized world these days. Lots of 1s and 10s. Objectivity and being reasonable seems to be a lost thing. I'm 47, saw the first one ever in the cinema 1980, as it was rereleased before Empire. Was hooked before that, as I saw glimpses on TV. Even wrote love letters to Carrie Fisher as a 5 year old. Is a big fan of SW, but not uncritical. Loved OT, still do. Prequels where pretty stale, though ROTS was OK. TFA was pretty good imo, R1 was fine, even liked Solo, and thought it got way worse reception than it deserved. TLJ was the worst ever. Rian Johnson is an OK director, but giving him story carte blanche was really stupid. How Disney could go into full production on a close to a billion dollar trilogy, without clearing a complete storyline is mindboggling. Don't think they will make that mistake again. So the new one: Messy. JJ had an almost impossible task, but almost pulled it off, imo. Lots of stuff to complain about, if you want to. But several moving scenes, and the heart seems like it is in the right place, even if it's all committe in the end. Not great, not bad. Could have been waaaaay worse. Star Wars is not dead in my book, and Mandalorian's first three episodes makes me even more sure about that.

title: Almost Mission Impossible to Win
review: Great movie, double great special effects. The only problem is that, how do you wrap up a series that is 40 years old, think James Bond dieing. J J A did a very good job and I was..... satisfied. The Force Awakens remains the best of the trilogy.... just!

title: Good
review: Kinda fan service but I enjoyed it better than the previous 2 movies of the trilogy.

title: "I don't know how it happened but it did"

title: An OK End to a Messy Trilogy
review: 'Star Wars: Episode IX - The Rise of Skywalker' is the film fans have been anticipating since the announcement of a sequel trilogy. For nearly half a decade we had no idea what was to come of a sequel trilogy. 'The Force Awakens' introduced us to many new characters and hardships, and of course continued the stories of the original trilogy. There was hope for the continuation of the Star Wars franchise until 'The Last Jedi', which practically had nothing to offer to the story as a whole. Director Rian Johnson scrapped many of the ideas from the previous movie, and tried to go in a different direction. Now we have JJ Abrams back in the directors chair for episode 9 trying to wrap everything up. The full story is a mess due to two directors trying to go two different directions with the characters. These films are tied between paying homage to the original trilogy and bringing something entirely new to the table. They can't please everyone. 'The Rise of Skywalker' is a very visually pleasing movie. Many of shots are beautifully done, and the action sequences are exciting. John Williams' score is wonderfully done. The music, along with the visuals, are really breathtaking at times. The film falls flat with the character development in the end. It's no secret that Palpatine is back. This is a bold move for director JJ Abrams. Fans loved the idea of Anakin saving his son and bringing balance to the force in the end of episode 6 by killing The Emperor. What does that all mean now that we know Palpatine was alive the whole time? Either way, the film isn't absolutely awful. It's fine and worth watching if you've followed the sequel trilogy so far. Nothing will ever be like the original trilogy and fans need to accept that.
