title: Disaster!
review:
Disney's arrogance and lazy handling of this movie (trilogy) - as if simply buying the rights to Star Wars would guarantee George Lucas' genius - is extremely arrogant & disappointing.

The movie in a rush to be relevant, completely undoes the first 6 episodes and renders episode 7-8 pointless. All powerful Rey (Palpatine's granddaughter) comes along and simply destroys the emporer by holding up 2 lightsabers... That's it, dead. Something master Yoda, mace windu, all the most powerful Jedi before her couldn't do, even without having the force energy sucked out of them. It completely cheapens his power and undoes all the deep story telling about the characters you love/loathe from before. The hero is only as good as the villian he fights.

What happened to Anakin being the chosen one? No, that doesn't matter. You see, the emporer's daughter comes along and is actually the chosen one to bring balance to the force because Disney needs to milk the Star Wars teet for a little more money. They tried to have an Avengers endgane moment with all the Jedi from before showing up to help her, but it was so poorly executed and such a missed opportunity. At the very least they should've done cameos by all, but opted to simply whisper in her ear and now she's all powerful. Yikes! These movies should not have been made.

There are more plot holes in this movie than plot. How in the heck did the emporer come back to life? He only mentions it in episode 3 but how did he do it? Who's to say he's really dead this time either? According to this movie's own plot, we can assume that he's still alive waiting for the time Disney needs a little more cash again, so basically the climatic conclusion can't even be enjoyed. How did he build an army of star destroyers, 10,000 larger than the army he could before with the full might and resources of the empire and Darth Vader backing him? Who built them? Who manned them? How in the heck did he fit the super large Death Star planet destroying tech on them - once again diminishing the terror of what came before (The Death Star). Who were the audience in his chamber? If Luke can use the force to raise his ship and grab lightsabers in death, why doesn't he just come back and fight the emporer himself? There is zero sense, backstory or effort put into this mess. It felt so extremely rushed - like a cliff notes version of 5 movies slammed into this disaster.

This is to say nothing of the ZERO character development or chemistry between the cast. The original cast had so much chemistry you could taste it. You cared about the characters. You cared about what happened to them. This new trilogy just felt like the kid who stays at a party 3 hours after it ended. It felt awkward and sad. Say what you will about episodes 1-3, but there was at least a story in them that made sense and tied them to the original trilogy. The awkward love story of those is nothing to this. I could go on and on, but others have written far better reviews touching these issues.

Disney expects you to like this crap because they put it in a box that said Star Wars on it. Nothing about this felt like the epic conclusion of episode 6. My take away from all of this is it shouldn't have been made. The Skywalker saga actually ends with episode 6 as it should've done. The emporer died at that time. Anakin WAS the chosen one who brought balance to the force at that climactic moment when everything came to fruition and the emporer destroyed by his most trusted and dangerous Darth Vader. George Lucas was and is the father of Star Wars. His ability to convert his ideas into a palpable story on screen are simply genius, made more evident by the catastrophic failure of this movie (trilogy). Disney should be outright ashamed at this nonsensical tripe.

title: Entertaining, but a missed opportunity
review: The best thing about this movie was Kylo/Rey connection, and their struggle to pick a side. I couldn't help but wonder while in the cinema: why the bloated, rushed plot? Couldn't they have made Kylo the main villain, started the movie by showing that he has only lost to Rey before because he was still torn between light/dark side and was holding back? Establish him as a real threat by making him defeat Rey and almost kill her in the beginning. Then the plot will be about the resistance trying to stop Kylo and kill him, while Rey, being trained by Luke and Anakin force ghosts, is torn between giving up on him and trying to save him, because she feels she owe Han and Leia. This could have given plenty of time for us to connect with Kylo and Rey, and plenty of time for them to form a sort of a bond. I see a wasted opportunity to make a character-driven movie that focused on the struggle of characters and their connections to each other. They chose to go down the route of a thousand spaceships firing at each other, was lame for me. Anyway, no, wasn't a bad movie, was an average one with some rare good moments.

title: This is the end of Skywalker saga even if it is not a fitting one.
review:
After the debacle that was The Last Jedi, I had little to no hope from The Rise of Skywalker. Still I became a little optimistic knowing JJ was going to direct it. It is very clear that Disney had no idea from the get go that what they are actually going for. JJ and Rian both had different visions and it shows.
There are so many WTF questions in this movie that I stopped thinking about "how and why this just happened" in the middle.
To correct the mistakes that the last Jedi made, JJ have made some questionable choices and very few of them have paid off.
The plot holes in this movie are so big that you could fit an entire star killer base through them. How can a master planer like Palpatine, who is plotting for 70 years suddenly does things off the cuff. There are so many things that don't make sense. There are some editing mistakes too.
Now to the good stuff:
Adam Driver's Kylo Ren really shines in this movie. He has given a brilliant performance. Even though Carrie Fisher is dead, they have done a good job showing her on screen using previously unused footage. Cinematography is spectacular, as expected form JJ backed by equally spectacular John Williams score. Some of the lightsaber battles and force "miracles" look so freaking awesome that I unknowingly let out a loud cheer. Speaking of new force powers, I would recommend you watch 7th episode of The Mandalorian to get a better sense of it all. There are so many scenes and callbacks and easter eggs deliberately added just for fanservice and it works. Lets just say everything from canon can be found if you look closely enough. I really liked that.
This is the end of Skywalker saga even if it is not a fitting one.

title: Why are there so many negative reviews? Don't listen to Them!
review:
As the credits began to roll, the theater audience bursted into a standing ovation for the conclusion to this trilogy. I was one of them. I never thought so many people disliked this movie with the initial response it seemed to get from an actual audience. That's why everyone needs to disregard any review less than 6/10. At the end of the day most, if you go into the the movie with an open and unaltered mind, then you will enjoy the movie.

Was the film perfect? No, not at all, but what would the fun be if ever movie on the planet was perfect in the eyes of everyone? We are only human. Yet the movie still is getting so much hate from people who go in with their own idea of a plot and story in mind rather than enjoy the world of the movie unfold around them.

10/10-Production/Cinematography: Personally I thought the production of the movie was the highlight. There were so many scene that literally took my breath away, the cgi was on a god tier level. I had so many chills!

10/10 - Score: The music was also brilliant! It was a well done rendition of the old score and incorporated flawlessly!

7/10 - The story is the only thing that can have some critiquing. In my opinion, the plot seemed a little rushed at times. In fact the pacing was all over the place. But overall it was still pretty solid. Maybe a few random plot holes here and there, but again, just go into it without any expectations! The story is definitely there, even thought so many people seem to disagree. There were many parts in the plot that gave me chills and so many moments of nostalgia, that make it perfect for any die-hard star wars fan!

Again, please do not listen to any of the negative reviews, as they are ridiculous and absolute nonsense. Go into the movie with a fresh and relaxed mind and you will be taken on an amazing adventure!

title: Awful conclusion for an lame trilogy
review:
Ok, I understand that they had to get the attention of the fans, especially after the great failure that was TLJ. However, there are ways to do things, but with this movie they showed us that they are not clear about what they are doing and apparently it's really difficult to come up with a great plot that respects their own canon and the work that it's already done.

As you probably have already read, the main antagonist is Palpatine again, I know he is a great villain for the saga, but the way he returns in this movie does not make the slightest sense, it is simply because it has to be, just like his fleet which as always has the power to destroy planets and was built with who knows what resources.

The film happens at an impressive speed, with a change of scenes so fast that it becomes very difficult to keep up with the film. The protagonists will find the way to the search for Palpatine by chance and with events that are very convenient for the protagonists, such as finding Lando out of nowhere or falling into a pit of quicksand to find the dagger.

Some things also happen in the film that become completely inconsequential, such as the sacrifice of C3PO, which it was meant to be an emotional moment (it didn't matter too much to the protagonists) it no longer matters because R2 restores its memory. Chewbaca's supposed death does not make sense equally, because it turns out that in a zero explained way by the film, that he survived because he was in different ship to the one that exploded.

We have been explained on multiple occasions that Rey has a very strong connection with the force, I still think that his abilities are exaggerated and it does seem that at any time that the character requires, it new powers are removed from the sleeve to give the character the strength to handle a certain situation.

Finally, I would like to say that the film seen individually is bad, but if it's seen as part of a trilogy it's even worse, because the connection with its predecessors is practically nil, it seems that they decided to finish it and try to make it largest possible fan service in the world to try to win over fans, which was a serious mistake. This film leaves me a great dissatisfaction as a lifelong Star Wars fan, because it leaves the remaining 8 films in the trash, since the sacrifice of all the characters to reach the destruction of the empire and its leader are not worth it.

title: The hardest job in the world
review:
As the title states, J.J. Abrams had the hardest job in the world having the responsibility of wrapping up 8 movies of story arc. I believe he does this masterfully.

Whether you were bothered by the pace of the film or not (I was not) I felt that Abrams and producers wrote a very cohesive and magnetic story while answering many peoples lingering burning questions from previous films as well as putting finality and closure to just about all character arcs.

Similar to how rogue one makes episode 4 feel like a better movie I feel rise of skywalker does a brilliant job at making some of the directions took in last Jedi feel more grounded, explained and enjoyable in future playbacks.

Coming from an avid die hard fan of this franchise, this film for me was a nonstop rollercoaster ride of emotions, action and satisfaction.

title: PTSD!
review:
Like most of you I am suffering from PTSD (Post Traumatic Starwars Disorder) right now. But we go it for different reasons. 42 years in the making. Just think about it! But let me start from the beginning. When we first heard that it would be a new trilogy coming, most of us went YAY! When we heard that some of the original cast was going to be in it we went DOUBLE YAY! But then for som unfathomable reason Disney decided that the three movies were goning to have three different directors, and more unbelivable three different script writers! Imagine some one ordering a book to be written, and then assigning three different writers. One to do the beginning, one to do the middle, and one to do the end. With no or very little discussion between them. Ofcourse this would be a problem in the upcoming trillogy. Despite this unbelivable hurdle these three movies comes out pretty darn well. It hits all those cordes in us fans that we want in a Star Wars movie. No matter the scattershot plot, it is unmistakeable, with out a doubt, a full-on Star Wars experience! And that is what we all long for!

The actors are cast perfectly on all places. Daisy Ridley and Adam Driver are excellent in their roles. And please, for those of you with the Mary-sue complex please note that in cinema history that have been littrally 100's of characters with the same effect with no-one complaing. Why? Because it was guys! :) And just one note for all the haters out there. If it's really that bad, just stop watching. There is MILLONS of Star Wars fans, you will not be missed!

But what about TROS then? Well, it's much like a 100 meter-runner that got late out of the startingblocks, and then discovered it was a hurdle race, it went on an epic comeback win. The breakneck pace is dotted with homage to the other movies throughout the entire time. The dark setting of the Sith is a nailbiter and the spice of this one. For all it's flaws, missed opportunities, and out right gafs, I still walked out of the theatre feeling like Oliver Twist, "Please Disney, can I have some more?"

To all the rest of you Star Wars fans out there, I am glad to have been with you in this EPIC 42 year trip. And a I am looking forward to continue the this fantastic ride with you for the next 42 year!

Make the force be with you!

title: Watch it as we watched the first three films, with the soul of a visionary child, and you will enjoy it. I will miss all the characters we leave in this trilogy, just like in
review:
A movie from the Star Wars series. Not just one of them, but the finale. Sometime ago I watched many interviews and articles by Lucas. I was interested in where it all began. It turned out that the original idea was Star Wars to be a wonderful space fairy tale. And that was it! But the people saw in this tale an adventure, a friendship, a unity of good, so that evil could be defeated. After a while, Lucas created more parts of the great saga. Family, friends, love and the battle between good and evil. Our generations grew up with these wonderful films, but with the growth of their numbers, we grow up, and our expectations grown up with them. We began to notice some mistakes that we can see in the old films, but it was not important for us, because it was tale of our imagination. It's a cosmic tale, with a lot imagination and fantasy. As a children we didn't question anything , and that was the magic. Then we grow up...with a lot criticism and we lost the spell, the magic, that was in us...not in the new movies that we blame. Did we lose the magic? Not all of us.
It was time when it was not important how the stormtrupers that dies with almost a look and non of all this soldiers can stop 3 kids, but we doesn't care then that this is impossible. That's not the point. There're always mistakes if you're looking for them. A woman older than my parents with her husband came to me when I cosplayed Leia at one Star Wars concert and told me that they are fans of the old series and the new once. How the old movies changed the space movies world forever and how the new once are changing with the time , but they are still amazing. They can be never an innovation like the old once, but still a good legacy. My little 12-year-old cousin, loves all the new sequences and the old once too, but for exam he feels the new once closer to him. I have a feeling that the greatest criticism came from fans of our generation (25-40), cuz like I said we grow up and everything changed, we cant watch the new once the same sentiment and eyes of a child.
The films changed, fact. But I dare to say that in this last movie they tried to give us the end we had to see. Family and friendly story... The symbolism of the finale beyond the sci fi part.
Mistake for me was to put all these in the last part only, they should put some of it in the 8 movie, but however.
I think that was worthy finale of the film, followed all the basic principles and most important ideas of the movie. Watch it as we watched the first three films, with the soul of a visionary child, and you will enjoy it. I will miss all the characters we leave in this trilogy, just like in the previous ones. And I will finish with a cue from the film, which has won me, me and a lot people I know and this is the simple truth about 90% of the idea of all the movies SW

title: Better than TLJ
review:
Pros:

Solid movie (some dialogues felt a bit ham fisted) but overall cool and inventive story. I also loved the world building. The inclusion of cinemas probably biggest baddie, aka the emperor was brilliant.

Cons: Movie could have been a bit longer and taken some more time to build up/answer the twists and turns.

title: Perfect? NO! Enjoyable? YES
review: I totally understand how die hard fans were a let down. I'm a pretty big fan and I thought some of the "big reveal" was underwhelming. At times I felt like it was being told by my drunk uncle who kept back tracking and saying "Oh yeah, i forgot to tell you this character did that earlier". However, people giving it one or two stars, was it REALLY the worst movie you've ever seen, or were you just disappointed that an ending 42 years in the making wasnt perfect?? Its fun to watch. YES it's a bit Disney and the formula is the same as the past but it didnt drag! I wish I could rave about it but I CAN say it's worth the price of admission.

title: Does not deserve all the hate it is getting
review:
This movie is not nearly as bad as they say it is. I understand why all the fans are so upset at this point, but it's not because of this movie, it's because of the previous movie, how bad it was, how it didn't feel like a Star Wars movie, how the studio and the director treated fans like "man babies" instead of owning their mistakes, insulting their critics, instead of listening to them. So fans have lost their faith in the story, in the new characters. I think if that wouldn't have happened, this would be regarded as great Star Wars film. If they had done a different episode VIII, we wouldn't be here. It is not a perfect film, but it fixes most of what happened in The Last Jedi, that is a terrible Star Wars film, it's like the director didn't watch the original trilogy, it doesn't have world building, it doesn't even have a real lightsaber duel, it's awful. It makes Luke a Grumpy old man, after being the most optimistic person in the galaxy. Thus making The force awakens a worse movie. And It even kills the main villain of the trilogy, putting episode IX at an impossible position.
The Rise of Skywalker has great world building, it's action packed, the visuals are awesome, the plot picks up where they left it and course correct it, has to dig up another antagonist, it gives good arcs to the characters, mainly Rey, Kylo,C3P0 (that was cool) and maybe Finn (a little), there are new aliens. They didn't do a Holdo maneuver. If you go with fresh eyes, understand where the story is, you are going to enjoy it. I bet children are going to love it. Like I said, it's not perfect, and is easy to tear a movie apart, but it's also easy to enjoy.
The studio needs to learn from their mistakes, this movie tries to, so give it a chance. But there a bigger lesson for them, something Marvel has, a plan, a big big road map ahead, which allows them to put out 2 movies a year. There's no Star Wars fatigue, just bad movie fatigue, fans treated badly fatigue.

title: Come on people - Be fair... but not dumb
review:
There is so much in this movie that makes no sense... the plot reads like below average fan fiction... heck electronic arts and BioWare came up with better storylines than this movie.

But it's not s terrible movie... it is entertaining and fast paced... the fast pace may be by design so that you don't think for too long about the nonsense logic bombs dropped every 15 mins or so...

Visuals are great and so is the score.

A lot of the movie feels like damage control from the backlash of last Jedi....but it overcorrects and goes way too far in the over direction

So yeah... 6/10... enjoyable movie if you don't think too much about it

title: Nail to Fail...
review:
Of all the movies I have ever seen, none have ever left me on the edge of my seat like the rise of Skywalker. At times I was so impressed, I would thrust my weight up against the chair to resist from bursting out in excitement. But of course, there were other times where I was left baffled with a million questions hyper jumping through my mind all at once. As the questions boiled on the tip of my tongue, my respect for J.J Abrams slowly piped down hill. Nonetheless, a new hope rose and fought its way through the intolerable flaws; plot holes and unanswered questions that have left me somewhat riddled. That new hope was enough to reignite my spark of respect for J.J Abrams. With all been said, I am just another thoughtful critic with a long train of opinions.

The worst mistake u can make is to be misled by another persons view on the movie. Don't go in there with the desire to tear the movie apart and critisce it for every senceless action u may happen to come across. Go in there with an open mind. BE YOUR OWN JUDGE of how well u thought the movie played out. Do not fool yourself with the voices of the critics. Asides from all of that, enjoy the movie for what it is and may the force be with you!

title: Hating is trendy, but not fair!
review:
There are many people keep saying the story is bad and how better were the old movies. I think this is not true. The original movies had so simple story - those are the bad guys and those are the good guys and we all enjoyed the amazing worlds and Jedi/Sith.

This movie has to respect all the previous stories, all the fan ideas of how the old movies should have been. You realize that this is an impossible task right?!

I think this is the best episode from all Star wars movies so far. The story might look a bit chaotic, but that's the life - everyone is doing what's possible. Excellent work of the whole crew!

For haters, just don't watch it!

Abrams try to keep the pace fast.. no delay no break, he was in a rush to finiish this movie as fast as possible..

title: A beautiful ending
review: Spite the outcome we received from the last jedi, Rise of Skywalker really makes up for that. I would have expected a different ending to the movie as well as a better battle at the end but you can't have everything. Overall the movie was an absolute joyful and thrilling experience.

title: A sure footing finale!
review:
The unsure footings in the first two, esp much more so in TLJ are no more in this finale. We went to watch as a family and my teenager sons don't know Star Wars at all. But fans or not, one can surely feel the plot and enjoy the epic scenes. One can even feel the intricate relationships between the characters even if you did not watch a single Star Wars film before. That is no mean feat for the script writer and the director.
And Rey is just so telling with her eyes!
The film is just well balance between epic actions and storytelling! Well done!

title: Grand and Serviceable
review: A grand and serviceable end to this nostalgia fitted sequel trilogy. There is so much packed into this one that will probably take a while process. I loved the tech upgrades given to the various characters, Kylo Ren's journey and the grandeur of the final hour. I am inclined to up my rating because making a finale that meets at least some of the expectations of each one of the varied fanbase is a near impossible task and JJ Abrams, I think, has succeeded.

title: I found it really enjoyable.
review:
I'm going to start by saying that, even though I've watched all the Star Wars movies, I'm not a die-hard fan and I have a difficult time remembering who's who sometimes.

Having said that I really enjoyed this movie. It had me crying more than once, I was at the edge of my seat with the action scenes and I was swept off my feet with the whole Rey/Ben story.

title: Not the best, not the worst
review: I went into the movie not knowing what to expect. I had a completely open mind about it. I think it was okay, but still weaker than previous movies. I feel like the character development of Kylo Ren was what disappointed me the most as well as the fact I personally feel Rey had too much power. It just doesn't make sense to me how she would be able to defeat the whole First Order and Palpatine by herself with such little training (that we know of) when people such as Luke couldn't do it before. It wasn't a big let down, but I feel like it had more potential as a movie. I encourage you to see it yourself and formulate your own opinion.

title: OK, possibly even good but not really good.
review:
OK, possibly even good but not really good. I feel like a teacher who wants to write a school report on a pupil saying "Could do better". I can see what they were aiming for. I think they missed. Star Wars was always about seductive evil vs good. The original trilogy did it far better. This seemed to jump around. It wasn't bad in parts and I can see why some would love it and some hate it. Overall OK but not really good. Not enough characterization for me.

Also unfair to him but I can't see Richard E Grant as evil

But what are they going to do for movie ten? Or is it more inbetweenquels?

About #TROS/movies in general. If they're going to make every women and every non-white good and only white men can be buffoons or evil and given that they seem to have quotas it'll ruin any movie with a spy/traitor/turncoat in it because you'll know it can only be the white man

title: Could have been so much more... but ends up so weak tripping over itself.
review:
Honestly this is probably the second worst Star Wars. Ya, I am a die hard fan.. Episode 1 Phantom Menance and the Gungan mess takes the worst but the surprise for this movie failure is simply sloppy story.

You don't need to be a Star Wars fan to watch this movie, then realize the laziness of the writers and directors opened up so many unexplained can-of-worms and dead-end plot stories that only exist in this movie, yet serve no purpose. Where was the editor? Would you really have a story with 30% of the chapters being unrelated to the plot? Where is the depth of character development?

I liked many retro elements, guess that's why I still go.

The crazy part is the big plot twist does nothing to change Rey's character development nor gain new skills. Boooo

They could have linked Rey's past to the Mandalorian, baby yoda, anything of interest and instead it is just faces of nobodies with no new character growth or insight.

Prepare for multiple parts where it drags on so you almost are willing to reach for your phone, and they great jokes that lose all their humor cause they are glanced over.

Get rid of Abrams and hire someone to actually proof the movie and plot before going to theaters next time... glad I didn't wait hours in line for this one!

title: About a 7.5 out of 10/No spoilers in this review
review:
Movie was not as bad as the naysayers mentioned.

Characters were decent for the most part. Some were more/less likeable than the previous installments, and some unfortunately were brought down in importance. But movie overall had decent character development.

Plot and flow of the movie is debatable. There is so much going on screen(fast pacing); good for keeping you awake and fun to see at the Bigscreen and give you your money's worth. But with so many subplots and action sequences you may lose track of the main plot purpose. Movie is about 2:20 minutes but it feels like a 3:00-3:30 hour movie, dragged more than necessary. Plot twists were a mix of yays and nays.

Effects were great. So many of them and so many lights! Though with a few errors here and there.

Fixes/errors, extras, etc. Movie went on to fix issues that would carry on from episodes 7&8. Some fixes were done right while others just made things cringier or were down right scrapped for the better or worse. Fan service was there, reliving past Star Wars moments in its own special way. There was some leftist and gender agenda/propaganda going on that would make viewers role their eyes.

It was a fun and decent watch. Well worth to see at the theaters due to the effects and lights; characters were funny and lively. Plenty of action scenes. Some cringy moments and clitche' here and there but overall it was worth the ticket. My best one so far of the three latest numerical movies. Definitely walked out happier than I did with the Last Jedi.

title: 42 fabulous star wars years
review:
The best possible ending to a fairy tale.
it is entertaining fan service with beautiful emotional moments.

title: Reviews schmeviews.
review: Forget what you read from the critics and official reviews. This movie is a fantastic ending to the saga. I was there for the start in 1977, I am 100% happy with this. Action, flashbacks, musical callbacks, everything to tie it all together. JJ left one very small loose end for a main character, grr.

title: It was good, but was it necessary?
review:
First things first. Let us talk about the movie itself, without taking into consideration the big title "Star Wars". The movie begins with a slow rhythm. The first 30 minutes or so feel slow and maybe sleepy. Maybe it is the editing that makes it sort off boring. The editing in the first part of the movie feels odd. Weird cuts and transitions make the movie feel fast and at the same time slow. What do I mean? Simple. The story is slow, but weird cuts make it jump fast from one thing to another. So it is a story being told by several turtles. One second you are watching Ren doing some fancy stuff and the other second you are watching Rey doing some other fancy stuff.

But then, the movie gathers some power and becomes exiting. Once everything starts to fail for the Resistance, the movie begins to grow, and it ends with an epic climax. Basically, the movie is a crescendo, it starts with a low quiet sound, and it ends with such a powerful sound.

Speaking of which, the score of the movie is simply magnificent. John Williams is an amazing composer. The score of the movie makes it feel like you are watching a film from the old 80s. There is this scene in the movie where Ren and Rey are fighting in the Death Star, and the score makes it feel so epic. But again, what can you expect from such a master musician.

Now, let us talk about the plot of the movie, shall we? And solely from the movie, and not taking into consideration the Star Wars Saga. As I stated before, the movie feels like a crescendo. This translates into the plot, of course. The plot starts slowly, and if you have no idea about the Star Wars Saga, then you might not have any idea about what is happening at the beginning. Then the plot begins to be more interesting. But the thing is, it is a vague plot. What do I mean by this? Yes, of course the plot is good, and gets better within every minute that passes in the movie. But it is predictable. You know one of the swords will be for Kylo Ren at the end of the movie. You know that Kylo would be a good guy at the end of the story. You know that Chewy was alive after the big fight. There are no big surprises in the movie. The only mayor surprise is that Rey is a Palpatine. But, is it really a surprise? This is where the movie fails: plot.

Now, let us take into consideration the name. Star Wars. It was a good ending. It fits perfectly into the Star Wars Saga. It does not disappoint an average Star Wars Fan. But, was it really necessary? I mean, was this new trilogy really necessary? It is not a bad trilogy, I am not saying that, but, was it substantial for the whole saga? If we remove movies 7, 8 and 9, you can perfectly understand the saga. They really do not add anything to the original trilogy. Some might debate 1,2 and 3 do not as well add anything. But they are more related to the original saga. They follow the storyline. But the only thing that the last trilogy grabs from the original trilogy is the name of the characters. That´s it.

Let's talk about the failure of the saga overall. I do not consider the saga as a complete mess as everyone does, but, as I stated, it was unnecessary. But why did it fail? Circumstances. Disney. Death. Twenty first century. You know what I am talking about.

In conclusion, it is a good movie, it has amazing effects and an amazing score. Maybe the plot lacks power, but it fits the Saga, and it is not bad overall; it is enjoyable. Now, placing the movie in the Saga, was it necessary?

PD. Palpatine: "I am all of the Siths". Rey: "And I am... Ironman, I mean, all of the Jedis". Really, Disney? I really felt the Endgame vibes at the end there, but well, Disney´s formula.

title: Not as epic as I was hoping, but no cringe The Last Jedi moments
review: Overall good movie. So many Star Wars movie have those cringe moments that make you think 'what were u thinking' (ie jar jar, anakin and padme's entire storyline in ep2, leia Superman space scene etc), this movie didn't have any of that. I suppose there was a lack of emotional connection to some of the story unlike Rogue one. But anyone that gives this movie a 1/10 already had their mind made up before seeing the movie.

title: Not entirely perfect, but a heck of a great movie!
review:
Ok so most if you have seen Rise of Skywalker but I'm not into spoiling anyway. I thought the film was entertaining, I cared about what happened to the characters, I liked the new editions, I appreciate the humor involved and the story kept my attention.

Was it different than Last Jedi - YES.

Was there a lot of things that fans wanted to see - YES.

But why does making a movie that at least somewhat caters to what fans want sound like such a bad thing???? I watch Star Wars because I want to continue the stories I grew up with! And Episode IX checked all the boxes for me as a life long Star Wars fan!

title: Satisfying end to the Saga - in a bit rush
review:
First of all, I am a big fan, but not a die-hard one of Star Wars. I don't have big problems with the prequel triology as the Phantom Menace was the first movie that I watched as a 6-year-old boy and it made me interested in the whole Star Wars world. So my assumption is different from those who think that the only good Star Wars is the original triology.

Considering the circumstances including Carrie Fisher's sudden passing and the negativity that surrounded The Last Jedi I wasn't sure that the new triology can end in great way. It wasn't the great way that it could've been with Leia accomplishing her potential but that wasn't the production's fault. The Rise of Skywalker was a satisfying end, most probably the best within 142 minutes to this time line.

This movie declared the mission to somehow summarize the 8 movies and put an end to the whole story. This way it had to sideline some characters and ideas from TLJ, but I don't feel that everything landed in trash. I would say that it kept the good from it, including the complex attachment of Rey and Kylo Ren, and sidelined the less interesting parts (at least for me) like the Rose-Finn line.

The idea that Palpatine is still behind all that is evil is valid and a good explanation why Snoke could have been killed so easily. Daisy Ridley and Adam Driver give a great performance, they drive the whole story. Leia has a respectful ending, her efforts have a reason however we can't be really sad as the story doesn't let us. Maybe that's the most problematic part, that the plot is running so rapidly that sometimes it's not possible to get really involved and emphatise with the characters. But final was strong enough not to feel confused at the end.

It wasn't fantastic because it was simply not possible. But it was great, sometimes stunning and gave a decent end to the main characters.

title: GREAT MOVIE
review: Avoid the criticism. It is an excellent movie. Everything that was expected to happen has happened. The only one I didn't like was that Kylo disappeared (died) in the end. Probably had a reason, but I didn't realize what it was. Anyway this movie brings us a great story and I think it has regained the brilliance this saga has accustomed us since The New Hope.

title: Damage control at its best
review:
Without a doubt, The Rise of Skywalker is an outstanding technical achievement (and artistic, to some extent). Great visual and special effects, impressive locations and sets, lots of well-directed action scenes, mostly decent acting (with Adam Driver shining above all), and of course perfect stunts, lighting, props, make-up and sound design. Last but not least, TROS has an inspiring score, with John Williams heavily stealing from his old work and binding it all together in a beautiful and coherent musical structure that wraps up a saga of 9 epic movies.

Unlike Williams' score, J.J. Abrams' job was much more challenging and frustrating. Instead of simply having to tie up lose ends from the first two movies and bring everything to a climax, he had to reinvent an entire trilogy almost from scratch and condense it in one movie; or so it seems. Rian Johnson's arrogant experiment ruined everything for a lot of people, especially the scriptwriters of this final Skywalker chapter.

How do you deal with Snoke getting killed for the sake of plot twist in the middle of the second movie and without the slightest hint about his backstory ever revealed? Make him a puppet of a bigger villain, who lurks in utter darkness. How do you justify Rey has become so insanely powerful without any training? Make her the granddaughter of someone insanely powerful we already know. How do you explain the whole duality concept and the intimate bond between Rey and Kylo? Well, you don't really, but at least you have to find a way to make it work. A bit, which is a pity, because it could have been a nice idea to expand the myth of the Force to that direction (apologies to Jedists, I mean no offence to their religious beliefs).

Enter Palpatine. Whose middle name is Damage Control, and he excels at it, with the wonderful Ian McDiarmid delivering every single line with the frightful awe of the "one and only true emperor". Kylo Ren could not possibly carry so much burden as a villain alone, and let's not forget the murder of his father in TFA was meant to conclude with some sort of sacrificial redemption. With Snoke out of the picture, poor J.J. didn't have the option to invent a brand new threat and develop his (or her) ark in just one movie. So, Palpie had to be ressurected, and also connected to the bunch of nobodies we never got to care about as much as the main characters of the original trilogy. And if that wasn't enough, Abrams also had to work around the fact our beloved Princess has passed in real life but not in the story. Her lines from outtakes and deleted scenes had to be re-purposed to a totally new context. A real jigsaw puzzle that could drive mad anyone attempting to solve it under so much pressure. No way Disney would wait for a couple more years till the movie got released, or accepted to distribute a movie long enough to make the Irish seem average.

There are plot holes big enough for a whole Death Star to squeeze through. How did Palpatine use those "unnatural" abilities of the Dark Side and revived himself in a new body? We never learn, but we do get to see some Snoke clones hanging around. How did he manage to keep a secret he was building the most formidable fleet the galaxy has ever seen? With what allies and resources did he do it? Where did he recruit all those hundreds of thousands stormtroopers, officers, etc and how did he bring them to the unknown regions without anyone taking notice? Investigative journalism in the galaxy far far away sucks, same goes for Resistance intelligence.

Lots of crazy coincidences, heroes conveniently finding immediately what they're looking for in every world they briefly visit, a frantic pace (especially in the first half) in order to cover lost ground and set up a new narrative, not enough time to develop further any characters (while bringing on board new ones, who were basically extras with a few lines each). Sure, comic books (and possibly animated series) will somehow make some sense out of this chaos by filling the gaps, but the movies are supposed to be complete and self-contained stories, not bits and pieces of a Frankenstein monster on crack.

I honestly pity the people who watched this movie without having seen first any of the previous two Star Wars films; they must have left the theater sooo confused by what they just saw. But what a spectacle! And those rewarding moments, like the "I am all the Jedis" badassery of Rey (cool, but let's not analyse further if there's any logic to it). Kudos J.J., your job sucked and you still did the best anyone could to salvage this wreck of a trilogy.

title: It's definitely Star Wars
review:
Just as I was expecting. I read all the spoiler reviews before seeing this so I wouldn't be as disappointed.
This series of newer movies basically is pointless as exactly the same things happen and they just reuse all of the same plots. If you want to just be entertained it's a good movie. Just don't take it too seriously. The baddies always die in the end.

title: Watch it!
review:
The Last Jedi sucked soooo bad like probably a 2/10 or worse and The Force Awakens was about a 6/10. The new trilogy was just straight up crap before this last movie. Finally we can all move on from this new trilogy. This movie is good, because it is action packed, exciting, beautiful, ties up loose ends, and isn't stupid like TLJ. But if you are truly a Star Wars fan you are doomed. This trilogy missed on so many storylines and misused the Star Wars Universe over and over again. If this trilogy was left up to the fans to write their would have been a whole lot more Luke, Han, Leia, and Chewy together and their wouldn't be the stupid new additions that went against the natural rules set forth in the original 6 movies.

However, if you can all move on like I somehow did, I was able to appreciate how the story wrapped up the major issues that the TLJ left. It was cool and interesting and felt like a Star Wars movie. Unfortunately the writers felt the need to add too many grandiose concepts to this movie which made it over the top and on a SUPER level compared to the originals.

Just watch the movie and enjoy it! Do not expect it to be the most amazing star wars ever. Accept the trilogy as crap and don't recognize it as a true star wars film. If you do that it will be interesting, entertaining and enjoyable.

title: Best of the sequel trilogy
review: This is the best movie in the sequel trilogy. I could go on for a while about problems with the trilogy as a whole and the story arc from VII-IX, but if taken alone, this movie is a solid entry. It's fun and fast-paced with great sound and visuals. It fixes many of the problems with The Last Jedi. It concludes one saga while leaving plenty of space for future sequels with compelling stories. Some plot holes, some difficulties that come from trying to pick up the pieces from The Last Jedi, and a needless lesbian kiss ( don't try to teach my kids about human sexuality) knock it down to 9/10. But overall, if you like Star Wars, go see it, enjoy it for what it is, and hope that in the future, the lessons learned from this trilogy will pay off with stronger story arcs and better planned movie series. Star Wars could learn a lot from how Marvel plans their movies, and I think this trilogy will reinforce those lessons.

title: As expected
review:
Look, this movie is probably not going to change your mind about sequel trilogy, but if you just sit and wach the movie without any prejudice you will find out that it is quite good movie. JJ did best that he could do with story that he got, but to be honest he did play again safe with nostalgic phrases and characters... There are things that I expected to happen, but didn't and some things that I imagined differently, but that's life - you don't always get what you want. There was never chance for this movie to satisfy all SW fans. This movie is more of a damage control and it does that pretty well. At the end I don't feel sorry for spending money on a ticket.

Just go, watch it and don't pay too much attention on people who think that they would write story better then George Lucas himself.

title: An incoherent but very enjoyable film
review:
Absolute bonkers movie. This is partly because JJA was clearly briefed to reverse a lot of TLJ and create a new plot. It's also because he wanted to make this movie a celebration of SW, and I liked that. Liked the menace of the knights of Ren but would have liked to see more of them. Of course it would have been better if the story had been written for this trilogy in advance but given that it wasn't I think the three films, although not well connected, are all great for different reasons. Really liked the role of Leia, helping Rey in her epic fight on the Death Star against Ray. Amazing. Love the scene of Leia and Luke training. Explains why Leia didn't become a Jedi.
Overall I think the people making this thought, we can't please everyone so let's just have some fun with this.

title: The rise of Skywalker is ok in my humble opinion
review:
Im just back from the theatre. I feel ok with this movie. Im old enough to have seen the original trilogy back in the 80's as a kid. I love it and watch it regularly. I have also grown to love the prequels over the years. But Im not a fanboy who knows every detail about the SW universe. I just love the overall experience and escapism that it offers. I was ok with The force awakens. I was not fully satisfied, but the introduction of Luke at the end gave me hopes for The last jedi. But unfortunatly that movie left me feeling disappointed, like so many others (I never thought I would ever feel bored and disappointed watching a Star Wars movie). There are so many things I dislike about it.

And so I went into The rise of Skywalker with lowered expectations. Especially after having heard alot of negative things and rumours about it. But guess what...I actually enjoyed it for what it is. Technically the movie is great. It looks fantastic. There are alot of things going on in the movie...it might be difficult to keep up with everything during the first viewing, but there is certainly plenty to like. I decided to just go along with it as a 2 1/2 hours popcorn epic. I was mostly not bored. I especially liked the scenes involving the main antagonist. There are some really cool scenes. There is plenty of good action. The last 30 - 40 minutes are spectacular. The acting is ok for the most part. There is much less of the things that ruined The last jedi for me. I prefer JJ's style of directing to RJ's. I like the overall dark tone of the movie. The musical score is great. And Im ok with the story...Im ok with how the saga concludes. I think they were able to tie the loose ends together in a way that I can live with. I felt the saga came full circle in the end. Im sure there are many fans of the original trilogy and the prequels who will never find love for the disney trilogy. I understand that. But personally I have decided to accept it for what it is and focus on the positives and not the negatives. The rise of Skywalker is ok in my humble opinion.

title: Not the ones I grew up to......
review: What do all the people want that give the last 3 movies crap ratings?? Episodes 4,5 and 6 were fantastic, I think the last 3 were good and geared more towards our children. I took my 2 kids today and they absolutely loved it along with the force awakens and the last jedi. So the 'Star Wars' experts please leave the crap comments to yourselves......

title: Not as bad as I thought it would be.
review: The leaks were RIGHT! But that's okay. I wasn't happy about it when I read the leaks, how they would ruin Anakins story arc and what not. But all in all, a satisfying movie. I give a 9/10 because the music and cinematography made this movie. It was visually stunning and honestly don't agree with everyone on the bad story telling. It wasn't great story telling but it wasn't the worst. It seems rushed at times, but by the time Rey meets with ol PALPS I'm all in. The final scenes of the movie are not wasted. The crazy amount of power Palatine had was INSANE. I honestly loved this movie. But I feel like I'm in the minority, and I'm okay with that.

title: Closure
review: Does it go the way all the obsessed fans want. No but if you just go and watch and dont keep saying "Thats not what I wanted to happen" or nit pick the editing or the little things then its a great way to close the Skywalker saga. I feel bad for those who cant enjoy it because their closed minds can only picture things going the wy they want. Saw 1st one as an 8 year old and have like/loved all of them.

title: Good, but not like the originals.
review:
I saw the reviews a day before I went to watch it, and I was honestly surprised to see this movie ending up with a second-to-last rating. How could that be?

In every new movie (7, 8, 9) there have been some plotholes as well as weird storytelling. What angerred me about TFA was that the second half was extremely rushed. This traits I've seen in this movie. Beginning was great, but after all the shockers were delivered (Hux is a spy, Rey is a Palpatine etc), it began to be rushed again. The tempo went from intermediate to really fast.

Suddenly, Rey has had enough, goes to the wreckage on Endor, lands on Luke's Island, then magically rushes to meet her fate with the emperor and, oh, that goes quickly! It didn't seem honest, and I felt, just as I felt watching TFA, that it was a remake of the original trilogy. Nearly everything in the second half was adapted from Return of the Jedi. You could almost feel J.J.'s obsession with the original trilogy, up to a point where it didn't feel original. I also noticed that a lot of dialogue was recycled material from TFA, as well as a lot of important scenes, which actually lead nowhere. I give this a 6/10, because the second half takes away a lot of originality. Probably what annoyed me the most was Disney's forced garbage, like oh look they're gay, oh look, this character represents a minority so they should speak unnescessary for a minute. It doesn't matter, it isn't important to the story, so stop forcing it...

I wouldn't say this movie was bad, it just had a lot of smaller things that kept annoying me throughout the movie, soo yea, ergo 6/10.

title: Not perfect, but a fun ride
review:
It shared a lot of beats with Return of the Jedi, but it still had original elements that kept me engaged all the way though. It wasn't perfect, sure. Did I think it was a satisfying end to the JJ trilogy?
Yes. Yes, I did.

title: It's a good movie
review:
Star Wars is one of those franchises that can do no right. There are too many fans with strong fastidious opinions that will never be satisfied (lest they exclusively write, direct and produce the film themselves). Unsurprisingly, many rate this film poorly.

This is a good film. The production is the best of the latest three. There are nostalgic nods to the previous films and a good deal of originality. Catch it in the cinema if you can and ignore the fanatic rantings of the impossible to satisfy.

title: My second favorite Star Wars
review: Stop forcing people to leave comments...I'm not an influencer, no one cares what I think.

title: Rian Johnson ruins everything
review:
After the movie I couldn't stop wondering if JJ directed "the last Jedi" because in The beginning of "the rise of skywalker there are so many scenes which try to make sense what the last one caused

Because of them this movie is bound and could not show its all potential However as it gets closer to its end and starts focusing on what they really wanted to show us and we might expect to see from Star Wars film

I can say it succeeds to complete its job There are many scenes which bring me the feeling like "Yes this is what I'm here for"

It wipe all the worries I have about this trilogy out I wouldn't like to recognise the last Jedi as a Star Wars movie but this one, this one I am happy to count in

So I hope you to see it to see where the trilogy went, the all Star Wars series went

I'm sure you wouldn't feel so bad after the movie

title: Best Star Wars Movie...
review: This film is a success. I loved. There are beautiful moments of emotion. What a pity that we had to go through two rather average films to reach this conclusion rich in many ways.

title: Go see it
review: Cannot believe the negative reviews. Great story, great acting, and nostalgia to add. People trying to ruin everything and won't just enjoy something meant for enjoyment.

title: The sequel trilogy delivers!
review: I have seen TROS twice now. Once at the midnight screening and once with my family. I have two children. On first viewing I was shocked at the pace and reveals and a bit blindsided. I had mixed feelings and wasn't able to take it all in. On my second viewing I was ready to just enjoy it and had my seven year old son sitting next to me who was in Jedi costume. I loved so many scenes in this movie. It has a lot of heart and the scenery is beautiful. The action and effects are incredibly well done but it is the character moments for me that really work. Unfortunately because of the pace at which some of this is introduced you may need more than one viewing to really soak it in. A big shout out to what Daisy and Adam have done with their roles and to Abrams and Johnson for the interesting way they brought them together through the force. This was something truly unique in the Star Wars universe and gave the new films something memorable. I hope everyone sees this movie more than once, I think it really pays to do so.

title: HATERS WERE WRONG... SUCH A GREAT ENDING
review:
Not perfect but yet so satisfying. Was entertained all the way through.

So many interesting themes and aspects in this film that opens up for many new possibillities in future installments.

Not all things are explained directly but leaves one to speculate which I like. There are clues left here and there, though.

The acting was great, action was great too. Minor subplots gave the film a great flow despite being a little rushed. Many heartfelt moments and great humor without being too much.

All in all a solid Star Wars film!!!

title: Came in expecting to hate it. Came out satisfied.
review:
The plot feels a bit muddled up until the final act. However the movie does explain some plot holes while creating others.

The way they built up the characters felt better than both the previous movies and it felt like there was real conflict in the characters. Finn was constantly being left behind by Rey but still followed her up until the end where he himself went alone and let the troops escape. Poe's past was more looked into and before entering the final act we saw him moaning the death of Leia before leading the Resistance into battle as valiently as she would. Rey and Kylo were the most interesting. There characters were almost intwined. They would always speak with Kylo pushing Rey towards the dark side. It all came to a head after Rey nearly kills Kylo and he realises what he's done is wrong. He then has a final chat with his father before coming to save Rey from the Emporor. The conflict of Rey is from the dark side pulling at her. And at the end when the Emperor (her grandfather) gives her a chance to kill him, save her friends and become a Sith. With Kylos help she rejects him and gathers the strength to kill him. Then we see the conclusion of Kylos character as he gives his own life for Rey's completing his ark. Rey's ark finishes on Tatooine as she accepts herself as a Skywalker.

The action in the movie is great. But by the end of the movie there are still a few unanswered questions.

My main issue is the frequency of the movie tricking the audience giving the illusion that a fan favourite character is dead.

title: A fitting end to the saga
review:
JJ Abrams went into this film with the fallout of a fanbase that fell out of love with the franchise over the last jedi. title: Great, plain and simple
review:
Let me start off by saying this, I have been quite unimpressed with the direction of the new sequels so far. I found TFA to be dull and uninspired while TLJ was too brash and heavy handed. I must say that for this finale to the saga, JJ hit the perfect balance of everything Star Wars needs. I won't act like the movie wasn't predictable, but that's okay because personally I got everything I could have wanted out of this film. It addresses every question I was left scratching my head over after The Last Jedi and somehow ties the first two movies of the sequel (which seem to contradict each other so greatly) together in a way that makes sense for the story. I was very satisfied with the explanation of Rey's background, and even though I found her a bit hard to root for before, by the end of the film I felt really good about seeing her overcome her past and succeed. Daisy Ridley is absolutely beautiful in this movie, and I found myself very emotionally invested in seeing her close off her journey. Ben Solo' finally gets the treatment he deserves as a character, in a way he got the best possible outcome for a man who had done so much damage in the galaxy. Adam Driver gives a heartrending performance in this movie, I would even go on to call it the best I've seen in a Star Wars movie.
Overall I found this movie both breathtaking and satisfying, and I'm glad I went into it with an open mind rather than looking for things to hate. No it wasn't perfect, at times it felt rushed and almost methodical, and the majority outcomes were very easy to predict. But in my opinion, this film perfectly combines nostalgia and familiarity with interesting new concepts, does a good job of honouring past characters while giving a platform to the new ones.

title: Not great, but definitely not bad
review:
I went into this movie expecting the worst honestly, based on early reviews. It certainly wasn't bad. But there still could be more made of it. With that being said:
The good:The cinematography was flawless. This time, I somehow enjoyed all the characters? (I didn't like Finn at all before, especially in TLJ, but he somehow ended up being my favourite in this one). The music is, as always, perfect. And all the little things that reminded me of both the Original Trilogy and the Prequel one (watch out for certain voice cameos that got me really excited).
The bad: Some things seemed really forced plot wise. Actually, the plot was all over the place. Too much was happening. There also were some inconsistencies (I remember reading somewhere other things about Poe's background than what was revealed during this film?) Also the last scene. Oh boy. It made me angry.
All in all, I think this could have been a great trilogy. The ideas were certainly there, in all movies. What really killed it was the change of directors and the lack of a clear vision, in my opinion.
So, I think it's worth watching because it has some really cool moments, some really great character development for Finn (I still can't believe I'm saying that), and John Williams' music is full of throwbacks, which really made it a much more enjoyable experience. I honestly can't comprehend how some people are giving the movie 1/10 reviews. (7.5/10 for me actually, but let's round it up)

title: It is what Star Wars always has been
review:
I know lots of people are going to be analyzing this film frame by frame to point out all the faults, but why? This film is what Star Wars always has been: a kids movie. Even the original film didn't have Academy award winning acting or a complex story. It was made to wow 8-year-olds. That the story didn't somehow "mature" over 42 years isn't the fault of the movie or the writers. Take your kid or your grandkid, and you'll see that they are still doing what they did when we were kids: wowing 8-year-olds.

The first movie was a simple story and mediocre acting, albeit with groundbreaking special effects for the time. While the rest of the industry has caught up in the special effects department (but their job bringing Carrie Fisher back to life was amazing), this movie isn't really that much different. To the people giving this 1 or 2 stars, I'm not sure what you were really expecting, but it certainly says more about your expectations than the movie itself.

This was one last ride for the 8-year-old in me, to hang out with some old friends, as well as new acquaintances that have been picked up along the way. It was a satisfying conclusion to a 42-year journey.

title: "History doesn't repeat itself but it often rhymes," = Abrams' solid variation on the 'Return of the Jedi'
review:
It's an ENTERTAINING MOVIE - it's a GOOD STAR WARS MOVIE - It's a SOLID SKYWALKER SAGA MOVIE - It's the BEST POSSIBLE, given the circumstances, FINALISATION of DISNEY's STAR WARS TRILOGY - It's a PROBLEMATIC CONCLUSION of THE CENTRAL STAR WARS SAGA OF 9 MOVIES - It's TOO OVERLOADED WITH ALL KINDS OF THINGS that should have been DISTRIBUTED MORE EVENLY THROUGHOUT THE WHOLE DISNEY's TRILOGY. And YES, it is FULL OF SMALLER and BIGGER WINKS, NODS, HOMMAGES and TRIBUTES to Lucas' ORIGINAL SAGA and PREQUELS, but these elements and scenes are incorporated rather logically and rationally, so I would not, with all the respect to some reviewers, call it fan-service for the sake of fan-service or s comfort cinema food for STAR WARS hardcore fanbase. Okay, let us start with a statement that the biggest problems of the Rise of Skywalker are stemming from the fact, judging by the entire trilogy, there a tangible ABSENCE OF ONE COHERENT CREATIVE VISION underlying all three movies. In sum, Disney could hire different directors and scriptwriters to execute such project - there is no problem with such studio-system way of producing films, but there should have been ONE PERSON IN CHARGE OF THE PROJECT with ONE CLEAR IDEA ABOUT THE TRILOGY. Abrams, Johnson or somebody else, it matters not, but there should be ONE DEFINITVE CREATOR. Clearly, as shocking as it may be, there was no such thing at the beginning, and given that the movies had been executed by two almost contradicting voices in terms of the approach to the source material and film-making in general, it is then no surprise that Disney's trilogy and its conclusion does not hold together particularly well. Firstly, part of the problem lies in the fact that Disney wanted to do basically remakes of the original trilogy updated for 21st century audience as a safe bet in terms of economics and etc. However, Disney understandably did not want to confess this to STAR WARS fans looking for the continuation of the original trilogy, and therefore they somehow try to make a VARIATION ON THE ORIGINAL TRILOGY with SAME BACKBONE FOR THE STORY with new young generation of characters, while using reducing the old and iconic ones as a supporting cast to be killed throughout the trilogy, so they could be, in terms of movies, discarded forever, giving space to Disney's new generation of heroes. Okay, it does make sense and there is nothing wrong with such approach, but Disney did not play it fair with fans, explaining their new trilogy in these terms. Rather, Disney intentionally let people believe that they are making a genuine continuation and culmination of the Skywalker Saga. It's sad because some fans have been disappointed, and the Rise of Skywalker can be hardly perceived as something more than a variation on the Return of the Jedi. In terms of the Skywalker saga, Disney's trilogy does not deepen, extend or elaborate on previous 6 episodes of Skywalker saga, it rather frames the saga in the Rise of Skywalker. It's a shame because the Force Awakens was a promising start and, at the time, I truly believed that the connection of Disney and STAR WARS was capable of producing films of similar qualities like LOTR series, aspiring to snatch several Oscars for my beloved space opera. Nonetheless, as I suggested before, the Rise of Skywalker is a good STAR WARS movie, a good episode in Skywalker Saga and a good movie in general. The pivotal problem, however, is that much of its screen-time, the Rise of Skywalker is busy navigating the story back to the far far away galaxy of STAR WARS, so to speak. Let's face it - The Last Jedi was a very good movie and very good space-opera movie, but not a good STAR WARS movie and utterly bad and nonsensical movie in Skywalker Saga. Undoubtedly, Rian Johnson is a very good film-maker, but he was a right choice for the Last Jedi, which, does not mean that he was a wrong choice for STAR WARS franchise in general. But should have been tasked with doing something brand new within STAR WARS, perhaps a new trilogy from distant past with all his talent for twists, surprises and deconstructions. To put it differently, the screen-time of the Last Jedi largely used to show, do and solve things to venture into unexplored areas, while it should have been building bridges from the Force Awakens and extending its motifs to connect it smoothly with the Rise of Skywalker. Basically, trilogies does not work on the basis of thesis-antithesis-antithesis to previous antithesis, and the Empire Strikes Back or, say LOTR: Two Towers were not antitheses of their respective predecessors, buy they rather served as great second acts - thickening up both the story and world-building, preparing us for the ultimate ordeal and conclusion in third episode. So, if the second act does not play this role within the trilogy, you can hardly expect the Rise of Skywalker to do miracles, when, in fact, has to deal with largely missing second act, and is thus forced to use its precious screen-time to build ad hoc bridges, when, in fact, these bridges should have been constructed by the Last Jedi - and this has nothing to do with quality of the Last Jedi as a film in general sense. All in all, the Rise of Skywalker suffers, when it really suffers, from the failed function of the Last Jedi as a part of a trilogy - that is - being useful as a second act. THE GOOD
  • Ian McDiarmid is fantastic, delivering Palpatine's lines with gusto in his iconic voice. Indeed, truly captivating performance. It's obvious that he is enjoying himself in this role.
  • Dark and haunting, horror-like atmosphere of scenes with Palpatine
  • Luke is handled very well by Abrams, though it only shows that killing Luke in the Last Jedi was completely unnecessary and it robbed the trilogy of Luke's further interactions with Rey. Here, Luke is even allowed to DO SOMETHING MEANINGFUL that he was not able to accomplish in the original trilogy - watch for familiar tunes by John Williams....
  • Given Disney's final decision to use footage of Carrie Fisher, Leia's scene are handled with respect and sensitivity.
  • Abrams uses some force abilities both for Jedi and Sith that had been already established long ago, albeit in less powerful manifestation, in STAR WARS classic computer games such as Dark Forces, Jedi Outcast or Knights of the Old Republic.
  • Abrams, in my opinion, manages to somehow explain the force connection between Rey and Kylo and makes the use of it in terms of the film's climax.
  • While I am still not a fan of Rey-Kylo Force Video calling , recently mocked as 'Force-Skype', Abrams serves it in more aesthetically digestible and less cheesy/pulpy form compared to the Last Jedi.
  • New designs of some vehicles, droids + stormtroopers with jet-packs
  • Music by John Williams is amazing... as always.
  • Visuals are stunning and there is also a good balance of practical and visual effects
  • Some scenes are truly emotional, so despite all the limitations, it sort of works and somehow manages to ooze several tearful moments.
  • Very beautiful ending - aesthetically, narratively, cinematically - framing the Skywalker Saga with respect to the legacy.
  • New planets and environments look fantastic
  • Episodic appearance and short cameos of some original characters and familiar faces associated with STAR WARS.
  • The return of the king of galactic suave - one and only - Lando
THE BAD
  • Lightsaber duels and lightsaber fighting in general. Okay, I know that after all the fantastic choreography in the prequels and precision-like sparring moves in the original trilogy, it is very hard to come up with something new and breathtaking. On the other hand, Kylo Ren's physique, armour and new claymore-like lightsaber design had been promising in terms of new fighting style focused on long and heavy strikes like armoured knights, and to some extent, the Force Awakens demonstrated it quite well, though, the Last Jedi abandoned this potential, giving us practically no real lightsaber duels or sparring, and, maybe, more importantly, wasted its screen-time, which should have been used to give Rey her own distinct fighting style, moves and a type(s) of lightsaber(s) corresponding with her agile, fast and dynamic skills with that metal stick from the Force Awakens. I still think that she should have been equipped with double-bladed (Darth Maul type) lightsaber, but two lightsabers would have worked as well, and, at certain moments, fighting with double-bladed and single lightsaber at once (check out SW: Old Republic cinematic entitled 'Arrival'). The problem is, Abrams can hardly do something about it in the concluding episode of this trilogy, where the character of Rey, story-wise, must work with what she has or to put it differently - with what she and Abrams have been left after the Last Jedi.
-Underdeveloped secondary characters that are interesting, but they should have been introduced already in second movie - the Last Jedi, to make their actions, decisions and links to the main protagonists relevant and important. Okay, I really like both new characters of Jannah (Naomie Ackie) and Zorii Bliss (Kerry Russell), but both should have been introduced much earlier than in the third episode of Disney's trilogy, giving their presence on screen more reasons and their interactions with the main protagonists like Poe or Finn would have more narrative layers and their decisions would feel more organic in terms of the plot of the trilogy. Part of the problem is that the Last Jedi did not give us anything in terms of the backstories of the central characters of the trilogy. It only gave us more more information about Kylo Ren and, to some extent, few tiny details about Finn, but the backstories of Ren and Finn were properly established in the Force Awakens, so the Last Jedi should rather focused on giving us proper backstories of Poe and Rey, but it did not, and therefore we, in fact, knew nothing about Poe and his past life, motivations and etc.

title: How is it even possible that it's this good?!?
review:
Well, where do I begin? First up let's get one thing straight; it's a film. It's not something that's capable of creating world peace or curing cancer, so it shouldn't be on any kind of weird pedestal.
Of all the Star Wars films that have been made the pressure on anyone to make this one must have been phenomenal; the third of the new troubled trilogy, a major cast member who was not killed off in the previous film but has sadly passed away in real life, ludicrously over-the-top backlash from crazed and obsessed "fans" over the previous instalment to appease and somehow correct while avoiding creating a messy story, a film that specifically must include a whole list of things to even exist as a bonafide Star Wars film, enough plot twists to make it not entirely predictable, and to exist as the finale of 42 year old film saga that means so much to literally millions of people.
So it's fair to say that from the outset it's basically an impossible task, to create a film that achieves all of these things and in a good way. In fact just agreeing to make the movie deserves a big round of applause and a medal for bravery. If you disagree with me so far, you should stop reading now.
If you're still with me, you probably agree that the internet is sadly a place more people come to moan than to rejoice, and that alone is the explanation for the stupidly low score this film currently has (6.9 at the time of writing).
For me, a 10/10 film is something like Shawshank Redemption or Jaws. Basically flawless films, neither of which had faced anything like the challenges listed Rise of Skywalker did when they were being made. So there's no way it can realistically get a 10, the highest sensible score it could get is probably an 8 or a 9.
As a life-long Star Wars fan, I was really looking forward to this film, more than any previous Star Wars film.
And as a genuine film fan (by that I mean someone who goes in to films not knowing anything about it) I simply hoped that the film would at the very least be good, so that I can enjoy watching it with my son and daughter once it's available to own.
I'm so pleased to be writing now, 2 days after watching it, that it definitely exceeded my expectations. In fact I even found myself thinking "Wow, this has now exceeded my expectations" several times throughout the film. But that's probably because whilst I'm a big Star Wars fan, I also have a reasonable and balanced view of what's possible. And I also went in open minded and not knowing anything about it.
Most of the negative reviews seem to be from hardcore "fans" who, for some unknown reason, read all the spoilers and leaked information prior to seeing the film. If these idiots can't work out that if anything is going to ruin a film it's knowing what happens in advance then more fool them.
I was surprised several times throughout the film, pleased with how things were being wrapped up and moving towards its conclusion. And pleased that the story centres firmly around the characters that matter. It also did a good job of politely sidelining the less successful characters from previous films (Rose).
It also did something that genuinely surprised me by the end; made me fond of C3PO again! For some years now he's annoyed me but he was so well handled in this film it was a joy to watch, he even managed to get me emotional at one point!
In fact I cried three or four times throughout the film, once from an emotional moment of fan service, the others all from emotional moments relating to the story itself.
Thinking back on it now it really only fails on one level; to make critics, hardcore obsessed fans and the general film-going public all happy. But seriously, was that ever going to happen?
Well done JJ and the team. In my opinion, a huge success, given the immense uphill battle you and the team faced when undertaking the challenge of making this film.

review:
I was born in 1971. I was 7 or 8 when I saw A New Hope in theaters, me and my older brother saw the original trilogy (ep. 4-6) with our dad. It was something that "formed" us... we grew up with this. Then 16 years later, as a young man, I saw the second trilogy (ep. 1-3) with my friends and I was much more developed as a film fan than as a young boy.
